|---|---|---|---|
| `chat_ignore_categories` | channels | `[]` | Settings page · Chat page → SETTINGS · `/settings` ▸ A setting group… ▸ chat · `/chat` ▸ **Settings** reads it back |
| `chat_home_channel_id` | channel | blank | the same four |
| `chat_staff_can_ping_roles` | bool | `true` | the same four |
| `chat_escalation_names` | int, 0–10 | `2` | the same four |

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ **RENDERED, not reasoned about (2026-09-01)** | Both pages were driven in a browser against `site/mock/server.mjs`: all four keys appear in the Chat page's SETTINGS panel and on the Settings page, each with the control its type asks for — a multi-select for `chat_ignore_categories`, a single channel select for `chat_home_channel_id`, On/Off for `chat_staff_can_ping_roles`, a number box for `chat_escalation_names`. **`chat_escalation_names` was actually EDITED to 3 through the Chat page's docked Save Changes bar and read back from `/api/settings` as `3`** — the round trip, not just the pixels. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/chat.py:187` | Nothing was added to the router: `chat_settings` already returns every key whose namespace is `chat`, so a new `chat_*` key reaches the page by being registered. `site/public/assets/page-chat.js:33` is the curated subset the CHAT page shows, and all four were added there; the Settings page shows every key regardless. |
| `site/public/assets/labels.js:328` | Each key gets a human label, because the fallback (`derived`) would render `chat_home_channel_id` as "Home channel" — losing the "when the bot names a channel that is not real" that is the whole reason it exists. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:368` | The mock's rows are hand-maintained and there is no parity test between them and `KEY_TYPES`, so a key added to the registry and not to the mock simply does not appear in a mock render. Both were changed in the same commit as each key. |

# Chat follow-up (2026-09-01) — the four things a live evening found

> **Every item traces to something the owner or a member saw the armed chat do
> on 2026-09-01.** Built on a branch cut from `main` @ `ed2710c`, one commit per
> item. ⚠️ **Still no verification against a real model call** — every test here
> drives fakes, and what a prompt change does to a real answer cannot be
> measured from this tree at all.

## 1. Only a STRONG hit is worth the dear tier

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ **MEASURED first, and it found a second cause** | The live ledger: **8 calls, every one `anthropic` / `important` / `ok`, zero Groq attempts.** Reproduced here over a realistic note set, which showed something the ledger could not: **the bot's own mention tokenises into a WORD.** `<@1234567890>` splits to `1234567890`, which lands in no note, so the every-token pass could never answer a real @-mention and *every* live call fell through to the loose pass — where 29 server notes match nearly anything. `any hit → IMPORTANT` was therefore not merely generous, it was unconditional. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/chat_llm.py:461` | **The fix that makes the rest possible: the notes are searched on `spoken(text)`, not on the raw message.** The id was never a search term anybody wanted; it is an accident of `tokenize` splitting on non-word characters. Everything else in this section is dead code while the id is still in the query. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/knowledge.py:252` | **`is_strong` lives in `knowledge.py` rather than in `tier_for`, because the search is the thing that knows how it answered.** Three conditions, each for a measured failure: the **every-token pass** answered (the loose pass is "closest matches" and always finds something); the top hit reaches **`STRONG_SCORE`** (a body-only coincidence scores 1, a note actually about the question scores 8 or more); and every term lands on a **whole word** — `hi` is inside `this`, so `<@bot> hi` scored a title hit of 8 against "Channels in **this** server" and would have passed a bare AND-pass test. |
| `black_bloc/knowledge.py:238` | `whole_word` bounds on `[a-z0-9]` only, so a token that already carries punctuation (`off-topic`, which `tokenize` deliberately keeps whole) still matches at its hyphen. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/knowledge.py:108` | `Found.strong` is a property over the same function rather than a stored field: strength is derived from the hits and the pass, and a copy in the row would be a second thing to keep true. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/chat_llm.py:156` | **A bare list of hits is never strong, on purpose.** The one caller that matters passes a `Found`; anything else carries no record of which pass answered, and assuming "probably strong" is exactly how the original bug read. |
| **The accepted cost, said plainly (item 1)** | Stopwords are not stripped, so the every-token pass is brittle against ordinary sentences: `cookout hours` is strong, `when is the cookout` is not, because `when` lands in no note. That second question goes to **Groq with the note attached** rather than to Haiku. That is the design's own trade — weak hits still ride as grounding — and the lever if it reads badly in practice is a stopword list in `tokenize`, not a looser threshold, which is the bug this replaced. |

## 2. The bot knows what it can do itself

> Live, 2026-09-01: *"i want to host an event, can you show me how to do that"* →
> **"hit up @Admin"**. It owns the event form and did not know. (⚠️ The command it names became `/event` alone on 2026-09-03 — the form is the panel's **Propose an event** button, and `chat.py`'s lines were rewritten to say so.)

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/chat.py:388` | **The four new intents sit between `need_a_mod` and the data intents, and that band is the whole ordering argument.** Above them, `about_member` and `need_a_mod` keep the two questions that are genuinely about people. Below them, `birthdays`, `whats_next` and `who_is_live` keep *"whose birthday is it"* and *"whats the next event"* — none of which contains a self-service phrase, which is what the ordering test pins. `help` and `what_can_you_do` stay last, so the generic `how do i` never swallows `how do i host an event`. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/chat.py:1012` | **A NEW built-in reaches a guild that was seeded months ago for free**, because `seed_defaults` creates the rows it does not find and only those. New *triggers on an existing row* are the hard case, and that is `top_up_triggers`' job — which is why the role-menu phrasings could be added to `my_roles` at `:287` rather than needing a sixth intent. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/chat_data.py:449` | **The role-menu channel is appended as `extra`, not put in the line as a token**, for the reason `need_a_mod` already documents: `my_roles`' row already exists in every live guild and `seed_defaults` never rewrites one, so a `{where}` token added to the code table would render for a guild seeded tomorrow and be invisible in the guild that asked. Blank when no channel is set — the sentence simply is not there, rather than pointing nowhere. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:155` | **`FEATURES` is a hand-kept table and NOT derived from the live command tree, which is a deliberate loss.** `/help` walks `bot.tree`, and the tree needs a built bot and a guild; this block has to be a **constant** so it can sit inside the `cache_control` prefix and be byte-identical on every call. The honesty tax is `tests/test_personas.py`, which builds the real bot, takes every top-level command with no `default_permissions`, and fails when one of them is missing from the block — so the table cannot silently fall behind the tree. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:155` | The wording avoids `limit`, `cap`, `spend`, `budget`, `quota` and `credit` — `/voice` "sets how many people can join" rather than "limits" them — because `says_a_budget_word` is asserted over the whole stable core. That test caught the first draft. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:155` | **The instruction lives in CORE and the list in `FEATURES`, and the split is on purpose.** A rule in the core cannot be displaced by a mood (the file's standing structural argument); the list is data that changes when a command is added. The rule reads *before you send anybody to staff*, because the measured failure was not ignorance of the command — it was reaching for staff first. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:311` | The block joins `stable_core`, so **both tiers get it**: `system_blocks` (Haiku) and `system_text` (Groq) are built from the same function, and a fact only one provider knew would be the worst kind of drift. |

## 3. The Costs card — THE one home for money

> Owner, 2026-09-01: *"on the dashboard somewhere can put a cost breakdown for
> the hosting, apis keys, models, etc. so we can track spend"*.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/costs.py:96` | **The key inventory is DERIVED from `config.py`'s own fields, not hand-listed** — every field whose name ends `_token`, `_secret`, `_key` or `_client_id`. A hand list is a list that goes stale the first time somebody adds a key, and this is exactly the page where a missing one matters. A test pins the derivation against `Settings.model_fields` and pins that every derived name has a sentence. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/costs.py:101` | **`secret_rows` reads `bool(getattr(...))` and nothing else, so a VALUE cannot reach the page even by accident.** Two tests attack it from both sides: one asserts each row has exactly `name`/`set`/`what`, another builds a `Settings` with real-looking values and asserts neither string appears anywhere in the rows. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/costs.py:113` | **`outcome = 'ok'` is in the WHERE clause, and the ledger's other reader deliberately leaves it out.** The fuses in `chat_llm` count failed calls too — a failed attempt still spends the allowance — but a failed call cost no money, so the bill must not carry it. Same table, two questions, two filters. `COUNT(DISTINCT turn)` for the same reason the fuses use it: a Groq failure falling through to Haiku is two rows and one answer. |
| `black_bloc/api/costs.py:82` | The prior month is computed by walking the day-1 boundary back one, rather than by subtracting 30 days — a 30-day step lands inside the same month in March. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/costs.py:159` | **Zero hosting means UNFILLED, not free, and the wording is what carries that.** `cost_hosting_usd` defaults to 0 because there is no honest default: Fly exposes no billing without a token on the machine (the same risk class as the parked deploy button). So the row says nobody has filled it in, the total says the same, and neither pretends the bill is zero. |
| `black_bloc/api/costs.py:169` | Discord, the Twitch API and Groq's free tier are listed **at $0 rather than left out**, because a costs page that omits the free things reads as a costs page that forgot them. Groq's line says the ledger already records its real token counts, so the day the tier stops being free the figure is there. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/costs.py` (the notes list) | The unfilled-hosting sentence is the hosting ROW's own `word` and is **not** repeated in `notes` — one card must not print one fact twice. A test pins that no note mentions the invoice. |
| ⚠️ `site/public/assets/page-health.js:151` | **The section is given an EXPLICIT count.** Left alone the shared rail counts `.log-table tbody` rows, which here is two model rows plus nine key names — a card headed "Costs 11" when there are four cost lines. Measured in a browser, not reasoned about: it read 11 before the count was passed. |
| ⚠️ `site/public/assets/page-chat.js:71` | **The Chat page's dollar figure is an `<a>` to `#sect-costs`, and the section note says the money lives on Health.** One number, one home: the Chat page keeps tier liveness (which is a chat fact) and hands the money to the page that also knows hosting and the keys. `a.spend-figure` drops the underline so it still reads as the number. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`cost_hosting_usd`) | A key whose namespace is its own — `namespace_of` splits on the first underscore, so it lands in a **Costs** group on the Settings page with no override needed, and `page-settings.js` gives that group a name and a note pointing back at the Health card. |
| ⚠️ **RENDERED, not reasoned about (2026-09-01)** | Driven in a browser against `site/mock/server.mjs`: the Costs card renders the total, the four cost lines, the two model rows with this month and the month before, and the nine key names behind a fold. **`cost_hosting_usd` was actually EDITED to 12 through the Settings page's docked Save Changes bar**, and the Health card then read **$12.34** with the hosting row green and the "Fill it in" prompt gone — the round trip, not just the pixels. The Chat page's figure was clicked and landed on `/health.html#sect-costs` with the card open. No console errors. |

## 4. Play, do not deflect

> Live 2026-09-01, member PT: *"who is the strongest DBZ character"* → *"way
> outside my wheelhouse… you'd get better arguments in #off-topic… Who's your
> pick?"*, and the member said to have the bot at least pick a character.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:35` | **A CORE section, not a mood, because a mood can be off and every mood is appended after the core anyway** — the file's standing structural argument. The failing answer was in the HOUSE voice with no mood on it at all, so a mood could never have fixed it. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:35` | **The rule names the three shapes of the failure separately, because the live answer did all three:** it said the topic was outside its wheelhouse, it pointed at a channel *instead of* answering, and it handed the question straight back. So the text forbids each one by name and allows the two that are fine in their place — "what's your pick?" AFTER a pick, a channel as an aside at the end. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:35` | **Placed between "What is true" and "What you may name", and the surrounding rules were not touched.** The new paragraph restates their boundary in its own words — do not invent a fact about the server or a member to back a pick up; keep the ducking for personal details, moderation decisions and real harm — so a model reading only this section cannot read it as permission to make things up. A test asserts both old rules are still in the core beside the new one. |
| ⚠️ **What was NOT verified** | **Everything about the effect.** No real model has read this text, so whether it actually stops the deflection is unmeasurable from this tree. What is tested is that the sentences are in the stack, that they are in the core rather than in a mood, that the two rules they sit between survive intact, and that no forbidden budget word crept in. The check that matters is the owner asking a live opinion question after the next deploy. |


# Phase 15 (F14) — ping roles

> Keyed against the Phase 15 branch (`37407bd` + this commit). Nothing below has
> met a real Discord role: role creation, panel refresh and the Manage Roles
> ordering are test-suite evidence only.

## `black_bloc/pings.py` — the decisions, with the Discord calls at the edge

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/pings.py:528` | ⚠️ **`kind_via(...)` is why one helper serves both doors.** `/pingroles streamer add` and `POST /api/pings/streamers` write the SAME row and the SAME log line; the only difference the log should show is where it came from, so the `web.` head is built from the caller's `via` instead of being a second literal in a second module. This file used to own a private `head(via)`; 2026-09-03 replaced it (and four other copies) with the one `logkinds.kind_via` — see `black_bloc/logkinds.py:530`. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:156` | ⚠️ **Checklist 17.** `pings_fan_role_template` is staff-editable text going into `str.format`, so a stray `{game}` raises `KeyError` — the fallback catches every exception, logs it, and uses `{name} pings`. The result is then whitespace-collapsed and cut to **100** characters, which is Discord's role-name ceiling (checklist 22); a template that renders to nothing at all falls back rather than asking Discord to make a nameless role. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:222` | ⚠️ **The `notice` flag exists so the missing-role line is logged ONCE per stream, not twice.** `_go_live_once` calls this with `notice=True` and `_mark_ended` with `notice=False`: an announcement and its end-of-stream edit are the same session, and a role somebody deleted by hand would otherwise leave two `pings.fan_role_missing` rows for one event. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:221` | The whole read is skipped while `pings_mode` is off, so turning the feature off costs the announcement path one settings lookup and no query at all. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:273` | ⚠️ **`wear` catches bare `Exception`, not `discord.Forbidden`.** discord.py raises `Forbidden`, `HTTPException` and plain `TypeError`/`ValueError` out of `add_roles` depending on what went wrong (checklist 29), and every one of them means the same thing to the member: the role did not move. The sentence names the permission AND the ordering, because "Manage Roles" alone is the half of the answer that does not fix it. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:312` | **25 is Discord's cap on options in one select**, taken from `role_menus.py:OPTIONS_MAX` rather than written again here (checklist 15). Page 0 keeps the name `streamers` so the panel staff already posted survives a 26th streamer arriving. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:327` | The label is the ROLE's name, not the member's, because that is what a member reads on the panel and it survives a nickname change. A row whose role has gone falls back to the member, and `sync_streamer_menus` drops those rows before they ever reach a menu. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:343` | ⚠️ **Every option is removed before any is added, and that is deliberate twice over.** `add_option` keeps an existing row's `position`, so adding without clearing first leaves the menu in insertion order rather than sorted by label; and a full page of 25 replaced by a different 25 would trip `check_option_count` on the 26th insert. Removing first makes both problems impossible. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:358` | Trailing menus are un-posted before they are deleted, so a `streamers-2` panel does not sit in a channel pointing at a menu row that no longer exists (`MENU_IS_GONE` is the sentence a click on one would get). |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:375` | ⚠️ **`staff=True` is the ONLY way past `pings_mode off`** — the design's D1 says staff can always do it for anyone, and the mode is a member-facing switch, not a lock on the console. Everything else — `/pings fans on`, the `auto` path on `/twitch link` — goes through the same helper with `staff=False` and gets the words. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:375` | A row whose Discord role has been deleted by hand is treated as no row at all, so the next ask makes a fresh role and `INSERT OR REPLACE` overwrites it. The alternative — refusing because a row exists — would wedge a streamer whose role somebody tidied away. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:459` | **D4 `keep` is the default and it says nothing.** `on_streamer_left` returns `None` unless the setting is `delete`, so `/twitch unlink` and `/golive optout` read exactly as they did before this phase for everybody who has not opted into a role. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:470` | **D1 `auto` is the only setting that makes a role from a link** — and it still asks `pings_mode`, so a server that has not turned pings on cannot accumulate roles nobody can use. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:502` | ⚠️ **Setup is allowed while `pings_mode` is off, and SAYS SO.** Staff have to be able to make the role and post the panel before anybody can opt in; refusing here would make the feature impossible to prepare. The reply ends with the sentence naming the switch rather than leaving the owner to wonder why nothing happens. |
| `black_bloc/pings.py:502` | **D3: one role, two keys.** `golive_ping_role_id` and `events_ping_role_id` are both pointed at it and both stay separate keys, so the owner can split the feeds later from the Go-live and Events pages without a migration. The panel is created but **never posted** — posting is `/rolemenu post notifications`, which is the path the TEST_MODE guard already refuses correctly. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` — the two doors

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/pings.py:816` | `role.members` is Discord's own view of who wears a role; a role that has gone reads as the WORDS "the role is gone from the server", never 0. A zero would say "nobody follows them", which is a different and wrong fact. (Moved out of the cog by the wave-2 panel — both doors read it now.) |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py:1140` | ⚠️ **The command is `pings`, the method is `pings_panel`.** The module `black_bloc.pings` is imported as `pings` in this file, and a class attribute or method of that name would make `pings.is_on` inside the class mean two different objects — legal Python, and exactly the trap that costs an hour. The wave-2 panel retired the `ping = Group(name="pings", …)` attribute that used to carry this note; the trap did not go with it, because the one `@app_commands.command(name="pings")` still lives beside the import. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py:138` | `pages_under_limit` lost its `/pings list` caller when the panel replaced the paged list — the embed's own `clamped()` cuts at Discord's 4000-character description limit instead. ⚠️ **`pages_under_limit` itself is NOT deleted**: `/rolemenu showall` and `/help` still call it. (GONE) |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py:138` | ⚠️ **"Is this person a streamer" has two answers, and both count.** A linked Twitch channel is the obvious one; a session Black Bloc has already announced covers the presence-only streamer who never linked — which, per the design, is most of them. This stayed in the COG on purpose: `get_link` / `latest_session` live in `cogs/content/golive.py`, which already does `from ... import pings`, so querying them from `black_bloc/pings.py` would be an import cycle. `start_own_fan_role` takes the boolean as an argument instead. (GONE) |

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/golive.py:394` | ⚠️ **`ping_prefix` deduplicates, and the order is load-bearing.** One role may legitimately be both the shared Events role and a streamer's own; mentioning it twice would ping everybody twice for one stream. The shared role goes first because that is the one most readers are in. |

Before, so the id is in the `details` dict the `golive.announce` line carries whether the post lands or not. |

The end-of-stream edit passes the SAME list: an edit does not re-ping, and the guard is there so a mention can never be ADDED by one. |

## `black_bloc/api/tools/pings.py` and the Pings section

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/api/tools/pings.py:33` | ⚠️ **`followers` is `null`, never `0`, when the role has gone** — the same honesty rule as `open_counts` on the status route. The page draws a dash for null and the count for a number, so "nobody follows them" and "there is nothing to count" are never the same pixel. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/pings.py` (the whole router) | Every route calls the `pings.py` helpers with `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and lets THEM write the log line, rather than calling `writes.note()` after the fact. One write, one line, one home — and a helper that refuses mid-way cannot leave a log row saying it worked. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:152` | The Set-up button sits in the Pings section rather than beside the `golive_ping_role_id` field, and that field is NOT duplicated: the design's "do not duplicate it" note is why the section shows the mode switch and the button and leaves the role picker where it already lived. |

(GONE) |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (the F14 block) | ⚠️ **A role the mock "makes" is remembered on the fan-role ROW, never pushed into the module-level `ROLES`.** `check.mjs` re-seeds `state` between every route, and `ROLES` is not part of `state` — a push there would outlive the reset and make the run order-dependent. Found by reasoning about the reset, not by a failing run. |

# Phase 16 (F3) — YouTube: the LINKS (the uploads half was REMOVED 2026-09-18)

> ⚠️ **Most of this section is GONE.** The uploads half — the feed poll loop, the Atom
> parser, `fetch_feed`, `classify`, `render`, the seed-on-link, the announcement path, the
> Setup sub-panel and the seven `youtube_*` upload keys — was removed on branch
> `youtube-uploads-removal` (owner, 2026-09-18: *"the youtube uploader we should just fully
> trash"*; design `info/youtube-uploads-removal-design.md`). Its notes were DELETED with it
> rather than left pointing at nothing. What survives below is the half Phase 16 built that
> the LIVE feature still stands on: the channel LINKS, `resolve`, and the `/youtube` panel.
> The removal's own notes are the *YouTube uploads removed* section at the foot of this file.
> Keys here are CONSTRUCT NAMES, not `path:N` — nothing for the re-key pass to move.
> ⚠️ **Nothing in it has met live Discord.**

## `black_bloc/youtube.py` — the client and what a channel reference can be

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `youtube.BROWSER_AGENT` | A browser-ish `User-Agent` is sent because a default library UA is the classic WAF trip (the estate has been bitten before). ⚠️ Honest note: it was measured NOT to matter for the feed — a bare `python-urllib` UA and a Chrome UA got the same 404/200 mix — so this is belt and braces, not a fix. It is still sent on the handle page and on the `/live` probe. |
| `youtube.CANONICAL` | ⚠️ **The canonical link is the ONLY reliable way to turn a handle into a channel id**, and the design's suggested `"channelId":"UC…"` scrape is actively wrong. Measured 2026-09-02: on `youtube.com/@Kurzgesagt` that pattern matched **four ids, none of them the channel's own**; on `@GoogleDevelopers` it matched **nothing at all**. `<link rel="canonical">` was correct on both. |
| `youtube.CANNOT_RESOLVE` | The refusal names the exact thing to paste (`youtube.com/channel/UC…`) AND the way a Lead can make handles work. A refusal that says only "I could not resolve that" leaves somebody with no next move. |
| `youtube.YouTubeClient.resolve` | `resolve` answers a bare id or a `/channel/` address **without any network call at all** where there is no key — checked by `tests/test_youtube.py`, which asserts no request was made. That is the path the panel's **Link for somebody…** and the dashboard take most often, and it costs nothing and cannot flake. |
| `youtube.YouTubeClient._resolve_with_key` | With a key, `forHandle` is tried, then `forUsername`, and **then it still falls back to the page scrape**. Google's own API does not resolve every legacy `/c/` name, so the keyless path is not dead code once a key exists — it is the last rung of the same ladder. |
| `youtube.YouTubeClient._title_of` | ⚠️ **A title that cannot be fetched is blank, and the link still succeeds.** The channel id is the thing that matters; the title is decoration, and the panel falls back to the id. Refusing a link because YouTube would not hand over a display name would make an outage into a user-facing failure for no gain. |
| `youtube.YouTubeError` | ⚠️ **`YouTubeError.network` is set at the RAISE SITE, never inferred from the message.** The transport wrapper, `_api`'s non-200 and `probe_live`'s non-200 set it; `CANNOT_RESOLVE` does not. The log row carries it, so "YouTube was down" and "that paste is not a channel" are told apart even though both share the `youtube.resolve_failed` kind. String-matching the message would break the day somebody rewords a sentence. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` — the links and the panel (wave 2, 2026-09-03)

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `cogs/content/youtube.LinkRefused` | ⚠️ **`LinkRefused` exists so ONE resolve serves both doors.** The web route needs `400 bad_channel` and `409 link_taken` as distinct HTTP answers; a `(said, row)` tuple with `row=None` cannot carry that, and the alternative — the route re-running `client.resolve` — is a second network call. The exception carries `status` and `code`; the panel just prints `str(exc)`. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.link_channel` | ⚠️ **One write, one log row, both doors** (checklist 34). `link_channel` builds its kind with `kind_via`, so the website's row is `web.youtube.link` and Discord's is `youtube.link`, and the route no longer `note()`s a second one on top. The same shape as `unlink_channel` and `set_live_mode`. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.tell_unlinked` | The unlink DM is best-effort and WRAPPED: a member with DMs closed must not make a staff move fail. A failure becomes `details["dm_failed"]` on the row that already exists — never a second row, which is the trap checklist 34 names. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.unlink_channel` | A member unlinking their own channel is never DMed; the DM is only for the case where somebody else did it to them (staff-final-say, owner 2026-09-03), and even then only while `youtube_unlink_dms_them` is on. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.add_site_button` | No origin, no **Open on the site** button. A link button with an empty URL is a Discord API error, and one pointing at `/golive.html` on nothing is worse than an absent button. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.staff_lines` | The staff half prints the linked list as LINES as well as offering the picker. A select's options are invisible until it is opened, so the picker alone would lose what the list actually showed. The lines are data, the picker is the control — not two spellings of one move (P3), and the same shape `/request` ships. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.MoveButton.callback` | Every staff branch re-asks `still_staff` BEFORE it defers, and `db_up` before any `send_modal` — `db_ready` is for after a defer and answers a followup, `db_up` for before one and answers the response. Using the wrong one leaves the caller with a permanent spinner. |
| `cogs/content/youtube._handle_of` | `_handle_of` stores the handle ONLY when the input was a handle — a `UC…` id is not a handle, and writing one into that column would make the dashboard show a fake `@name`. |
| `cogs/content/youtube._pollable` | Two members who link the same channel: the first is probed, the second is warned about in the log and skipped — the same shape as the Twitch poller's double-link warning. `link_channel` refuses this outright (checklist 16); `_pollable` is the belt for a row that got in some other way. |
| `youtube.card_buttons` | The button table is a dict keyed on `(mine, linked)` plus a staff tail, and `tests/test_youtube.py` walks the whole product. It lives in the PURE module, not the cog, so the parametrised cog test can compare what rendered against the table itself rather than against a second hand-written list — two copies of the table would agree until the day they did not. |
| `youtube.CARD_BUTTONS` | The `(mine=False, linked=False)` cell is reachable even though the picker only lists linked rows: a member can unlink between the render and the click. It returns `Refresh · Back` rather than raising. |
| `youtube.where_words` | A member reading the panel must never see a bare "no". `where_words` gives the reasons a live stream is not being announced — the live mode, no go-live channel, go-live itself not on, or it is genuinely on — four different sentences, and the mode ones name the mode so they can quote it to a Lead. |

## `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py` and the Go-live page

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `api/tools/youtube.youtube_link` | ⚠️ **The POST no longer does its own resolve or its own owner check** (2026-09-03). It calls `link_channel`, which does both, writes ONE `web.youtube.link` row through `kind_via` and raises `LinkRefused` carrying the status and code — so the route's worded 400/409 survive without a second call to YouTube and without the route `note()`ing a row the shared path already wrote (checklist 34). |
| `api/tools/youtube.youtube_status` | The status route answers even with the cog unloaded (`api_key_set: false`, `live_running: false`) rather than 503ing, because a Health-style panel that vanishes when the thing it monitors is down is the opposite of useful. The WRITE route does refuse in that state, through `require_cog`. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js` ▸ `channelsSection` | ⚠️ **The section is on the Go-live page, not a page of its own** — the same ownership answer as F14's Pings section. A linked YouTube channel going live is announced through go-live, shares the fan roles, and is about the same people; a second page would split one question across two surfaces. |

## Where else Phase 16 touched

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `storage/db.py` ▸ `youtube_links` | Schema **22** at the time, additive only. The table survives the uploads removal untouched; `youtube_videos` survives too and is now **orphaned** — nothing reads or writes it (see the removal section at the foot). |

The same pressure now lands on `settings_panel.editable_options`, which caps at 25 per group and offers **Find a setting…** past it rather than dropping anything. |

# Phase 17 — chat long-term memory, and the requests state machine

> Keyed against the Phase 17 branch `worktree-agent-a268aa7fa2979dd4a` (the docs
> commit carries this section). The phase ADDED `black_bloc/chat_memory.py`,
> `black_bloc/chat_distil.py`, `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py`,
> `black_bloc/api/tools/chat_memory.py` and their four mirrored test files, and touched
> `requests.py`, `cogs/community/requests.py`, `api/tools/requests.py`, `chat_llm.py`,
> `groq.py`, `settings_store.py`, `logkinds.py`, `personas.py`, `storage/db.py`
> (schema **23**), `api/status.py`, `api/server.py`, `bot.py`, `site/mock/*` and
> `site/public/assets/{page-requests,page-chat,labels}.js`. ⚠️ **No key above this
> section was re-keyed** — the phase appended to `settings_store.py`, `logkinds.py` and
> `storage/db.py` rather than editing them in place, but `requests.py`,
> `cogs/community/requests.py` and `api/tools/requests.py` WERE edited in place, so any
> older key into those three should be trusted by anchor text, not by number.

## `black_bloc/chat_memory.py` — the rules, the shapes and the storage

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:278` | ⚠️ **`normalise` and `has_phrase` are wrappers around `chat.py`'s, imported LATE inside the function on purpose.** `settings_store.py` imports this module for its choice tuples, and `chat.py → chat_data.py → settings_store.py` is a cycle at module level. `chat_data.py` already uses the same late-import trick; duplicating the two functions would have broken checklist 15 instead. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:71` | Only the DOUBLE-quote family and the backtick are banned. An apostrophe is not a quote mark in English, and banning it would drop "they're", "don't" and half the legitimate notes. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:90` | The availability list is the GABI rule made mechanical: the bot must never claim somebody is online, free, or anywhere. `lives in` and `based in` are here rather than under sensitive because location is an availability claim first. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:162` | ⚠️ **`OUTCOMES` is checked against THREADS as well as notes, and §J is why.** Run 1 of the measurement had the model return the thread `"namu quitting the server"`; `quit` was already on the list and did not match `quitting`, because `has_phrase` is word-boundary exact. The departure family (`quitting`, `quits`, `leaving`, `departure(s)`) plus `banned`/`kicked`/`muted`/`warned`/`timed out` were added for that one measured leak, and run 2 dropped all three attempts. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:185` | `straight` was REMOVED from the sensitive list after §J: it collided with "likes straight answers", which §D2-definition names as a KEEP example. A false positive costs one note; that one would have cost a whole class of legitimate ones. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:319` | ⚠️ **`other_names` is the only guard that can catch an arbitrary third-person name**, because a phrase list cannot enumerate the server's members. The cog passes it, so it is guild-aware; a note naming any other member is dropped. It is not a proof — see `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:332` | `why_dropped` returns the rule's NAME rather than a bool so the log and the tests can say which rule fired, and so `Distilled.dropped` can carry rule names and never the text. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:389` | ⚠️ **`Profile.visible` is the D4 guard at the DATA level, not the prompt level.** GABI relies on telling the model not to use DM notes in public; here a `where = dm` note is filtered out of both the reply block AND the prompt the next distillation sees, so it cannot be re-emitted into the server scope by a model that ignores an instruction. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:504` | The distil prompt states the KEEP list and the THROW AWAY list in the model's own terms, and `parse_distilled` re-checks every one of them. The prompt is the cheap filter; the parser is the one that is load-bearing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:488` | A code fence is the one wrapper tolerated. §J saw none in 29 calls with JSON mode on, but the cost of tolerating one is three lines and the cost of not is a whole conversation's distillation. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:504` | ⚠️ **Structural problems are a no-op; one bad ITEM is a dropped item.** Bad JSON, an unknown key, a non-string note or an over-long `call_me` all return `None` and write nothing — never a partial profile. A note that breaks a privacy rule is dropped on its own and the rest of the profile still saves, which is what §D2-definition rule 2 asks for. An over-long NOTE is treated as a dropped item rather than a whole-profile reject; the design's "over-length fields → None" is read as the top-level fields. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:546` | `widest` is why a note learned in a DM and then again in the server ends up `server`: dedupe would otherwise let the newer (DM) copy NARROW an existing public note, silently losing it from public replies. Widening is the safe direction and loses nothing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:578` | `merge` caps AFTER merging, so a newly learned preference always survives and the oldest drops off. The caps are `chat_memory_notes_max` / `_threads_max`, not constants. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:619` | `drop_matching` matches on NORMALISED substrings, because the **Forget by words…** modal asks a person to type a few of the words they just read, not to quote a line exactly. It drops EVERY line that contains them, which is right for typed words and wrong for a line picked off a select — hence `drop_fact` beside it, which drops exactly one by identity. Both exist; neither replaces the other. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:656` | ⚠️ **The `Fact` layer touches only `Profile` and `Note` and imports NOTHING new, and that is a hard requirement rather than tidiness.** `settings_store.py:18` imports this module for its choice tuples, so it may not import `settings_store`, `actionlog`, `panels` or `chat` at module level — see the `:278` note. Everything the panel needs that WOULD need those imports lives in the cog instead. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:665` | `facts_of` orders name → notes → threads, which is the order `profile_words` prints them, so a select option's `#3` and the embed's `**#3**` are the same line. The panel is the only reason a fact needs an identity at all. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:684` | ⚠️ **`fact_at` returning `None` is the whole staleness guard.** A select option identifies a line by KIND + INDEX, and the hourly distillation can rewrite a profile between the render and the click; `drop_picked` re-reads the fact and compares its TEXT against the one the view rendered, so a shifted index drops nothing instead of dropping the wrong line. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:837` | ⚠️ **One table, one meaning: a row in `chat_memory_optout` means "this person is NOT on the server's default".** Under `optout` consent a row means do-not-remember; under `optin` it means remember-me. That is what lets D1 be a settings key rather than a schema change — the alternatives were a second table or a `choice` column the design's schema does not have. `set_remembered` is the only writer, so no caller has to think about which way round it is. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:793` | `overridden` returns `None` on a read failure and `remembered(None)` is `False`, so an unreadable table means nobody is remembered. Failing towards forgetting is the only safe direction for a privacy feature. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:773` | `forget_everywhere` is keyed on the member alone, not on the guild: `on_member_remove` fires for one guild, and D3 says leaving clears the profile at once. A single-guild bot makes the difference academic today, and the wider delete is the one that stays right if that changes. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:848` | `expire(days=0)` returns 0 rather than deleting everything — `chat_memory_retention_days = 0` means FOREVER, and the read that makes that true has to be here rather than at the caller. |

| Key | Note |
|---|---|

| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:195` | A capped or fused month BREAKS the loop rather than continuing: the allowance is a global fact, so re-checking it per conversation would spend the rest of the sweep proving the same thing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:195` | A DM has no guild, so it files under `dev_guild_id` with `where = dm`. One profile per person, two scopes inside it — D4. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:240` | Expiry runs on the same sweep rather than a loop of its own, for the same reason the window sweep does: a bot that restarts weekly would otherwise never reach a timer that only fires monthly. |

# Phase 18 (F19) — raid trains

> Keyed against the Phase 18 branch tip (`worktree-agent-a1c38e3df0f71fa7e`, the
> docs commit that carries this section). ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live
> Discord.** No lineup has been posted, no reminder DM has ever arrived, and no
> member has claimed an hour. Everything here is test-suite evidence.

## What section J actually measured, and what it changed

The design told the builder to read `events.py`'s scheduled-event helper FIRST
and only ship `raidtrain_scheduled_event` on if it was reusable **without
editing `events.py`** (which is read-only in a parallel build).

**Finding: it is importable, and it is still not reusable.**
`cogs/community/events.py:570 create_scheduled_event(bot, guild, row)` is a
module-level function, so `from ..community.events import create_scheduled_event`
would compile. It is disqualified by what it does, not by where it lives:

1. It ends with `set_scheduled(bot.db, row["id"], made.id)`, which runs
   `UPDATE events SET scheduled_event_id = ? WHERE id = ?`. Passing it a raid
   train would stamp a Discord event id onto **whatever `events` row happens to
   share that id** — silent cross-table corruption, and exactly the class of bug
   this file exists to stop somebody re-introducing.
2. It gates on the `events_create_scheduled` setting, so raid trains would
   inherit the events feature's switch and D13's own key would be dead.
3. Every line it logs is `event.*`, so a raid train's calendar entry would never
   appear under `/raidtrains logs` or the Raid trains section's log filter.

**So D13 ships `raidtrain_scheduled_event = false`**, per §J's instruction, and
the key is NOT a dead switch: `_maybe_scheduled_event` is twenty lines of this
cog's own that call `guild.create_scheduled_event` directly, with raid-train log
kinds and no writes outside `raid_trains`. `find_scheduled_event` — the one
genuinely reusable piece, a pure cache-then-fetch lookup with no table in it —
IS imported from `events.py` for the cancel path (checklist 15).

⚠️ A second reason the default would be academic today: `create_scheduled_event`
refuses outright while `bot.guard` exists, and so does ours. Under TEST_MODE no
scheduled event can be made at all, whichever way the key is set.

## `black_bloc/raidtrain.py` — the pure half

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:31` | ⚠️ **`SLOT_COUNT_MAX = 24` is a Discord limit, not a taste.** A slot line renders at roughly 85 characters (`#12 <t:…:t>–<t:…:t> — <@700000000000000002> (https://twitch.tv/somelogin)`), and a message is capped at 2000, so 24 lines plus the header is the last size that certainly fits in ONE message. It has to be one message because the lineup is edited in place rather than reposted. r3dlabs runs 50-slot trains; ours refuses in words and says why. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:35` | `REMINDER_LATE_MINUTES` is checklist 31: a due-row sweep must age rows out. A slot whose start is more than this far past does not get a late DM telling somebody to go live for an hour that has gone — `missed_reminders` stamps it instead, so it also stops being carried by every future sweep. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:227` | The transition table is the ONE place a status move is decided; `may_move` and `allowed_moves` are both derived from it, and `allowed_moves` exists so a refusal can say what IS possible in words rather than printing a status list at somebody. `cancelled` is reachable only from `open`/`locked` — the design's rule, so a train that has already started is finished rather than un-run. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:188` | `_value` reads a sqlite `Row`, a plain dict or an object with attributes. That is what keeps every helper in this file testable with dict fixtures while the cog hands it real rows — the same trick `render_lineup` needs to be a pure function. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:108` | ⚠️ **Times belong to the POSITION, never to the person.** Slots are created eagerly at `create` with their times already in them, so `swap` moves five holder columns and touches no timestamp. A design that stored times on the claim would have to rewrite them on every reorder, and a half-finished reorder would leave a lineup with two 8pm slots. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:223` | `ends_at` prefers the SLOT rows' own `ends_at` over `starts_at + minutes × count`. The arithmetic is the fallback for a train whose rows are unreadable; the rows are the truth, because they are what a swap and a future per-slot length would move. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:252` | `caps_ok` treats **0 as no ceiling**, which is why the settings validator lets the key go to 0 and its max-reason sentence says so. An organizer's `assign` never calls this — D10 says the cap is for self-service claims only. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:321` | A holder is written `<@id>`, and every send/edit of this text goes out under `AllowedMentions(users=False)` (see the cog's `_mentions`). The mention RENDERS as their name and pings nobody — which matters because the lineup is edited on every claim and a pinging edit would notify twenty people twenty times. Checklist 11. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:315` | ⚠️ **`render_lineup` is the whole post, and it is re-rendered from the rows every time rather than patched.** One function means the Discord post, `/raidtrain status` and the dashboard's `lineup` field can never disagree about what the lineup says. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:280` | The reminder names BOTH neighbours with their twitch.tv links, because the thing a slot holder actually needs at T-30 is not "your slot is soon" — it is who to watch for the incoming raid and who to send the audience to. That is the request's own wording ("who they will be raided by and the person they raid next"). |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:383` | ⚠️ **`due_reminders` deliberately excludes a slot whose start has already gone by** (`start <= floor`), and `missed_reminders` picks exactly those up. They are two functions rather than one flag because the two outcomes are different actions — send, versus stamp and stay quiet — and the cog must be able to do the second without the first. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:419` | `due_checkins` takes the live user ids as an ARGUMENT rather than reaching for `golive.open_sessions` itself. That keeps this module Discord-free and database-free, and it is what makes the check-in window testable without a session table. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py` — the cog

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:190` | `create_train` writes the train AND every slot in one commit. Slots-on-create is what makes `position` meaningful from the first second: `/raidtrain list` can say which hours are free before anybody has claimed anything, which is half of what the request asked for ("slot availability"). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:235` | ⚠️ **`take_slot`'s `WHERE id = ? AND user_id IS NULL` is the race guard, and `rowcount` is how the caller learns it lost.** Checklist 6 wants a lock AND a database constraint; the lock is `_lock(train_id)`, and this conditional UPDATE is the constraint — a partial unique index could not be used here because the per-member ceiling is a SETTING (0 = unlimited), and a schema cannot encode a value the owner may change. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:294` | `swap_holders` moves five columns and no time (see `raidtrain.py:95`). `reminded_at` travels WITH the person, so somebody already reminded for 8pm who is moved to 9pm is not reminded again — the alternative, clearing it, would DM them twice about one train. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:334` | `stamp_slot` interpolates a column name into SQL, so it validates against a three-item allowlist first and raises otherwise. The allowlist form is deliberate (default-deny, per the estate's export rule); an exclusion list would leak the moment a column was added. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:343` | The DM helper is this cog's own rather than an import from `cogs/community/requests.py`, which was being rewritten in parallel by Phase 17. It is six lines and it catches everything, because a member with DMs closed is a normal state, not an error — the CALLER turns that into a `raidtrain.dm_failed` line so silence is never silent. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:416` | One `asyncio.Lock` per train. The contended path is two members claiming the same open slot in the same second, and the second half of that guard is the conditional UPDATE above. The sweep takes the same lock, so a claim cannot land between "read the slots" and "promote the train to live". |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1974` | Checklist 28: discord.py re-raises a non-HTTP exception out of a `tasks.loop` and the loop then stays dead for the life of the process. `@sweep.error` restarts it and records the failure where `/api/raidtrains/status` and the Health tab can see it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1979` | `_retime` re-reads `raidtrain_poll_minutes` every tick instead of freezing the boot value, so changing the gap on the dashboard takes effect without a restart. Same shape as the YouTube poller. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:482` | ⚠️ **Checklist 32: `guild.unavailable` is skipped.** An outage that hides a guild must not be read as "this train has no slots" — nothing is promoted, nothing is finished, nothing is stamped for a guild Discord is not currently telling us about. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:495` | The clock does all three moves and the poller owns all of them: auto-lock at the start (D11 — fixed, deliberately not a key: a train that keeps taking sign-ups while it runs cannot have a raid order), `→ live`, then `→ done` once the last slot's own `ends_at` has passed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:523` | ⚠️ **`reminded_at` is stamped BEFORE the DM is attempted, and that order is the whole point.** A crash between the two loses ONE reminder; the other order would re-send on every sweep for as long as the failure lasted. The same rule as `youtube.record_video` returning False for a duplicate. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:540` | Checklist 2: `raidtrain.remind` (sent), `raidtrain.would_remind` (shadow) and `raidtrain.dm_failed` (tried and refused) are three different kinds, because the owner's verification method is reading the log and those three must be distinguishable at a glance. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:574` | Check-in reads `golive.open_sessions` — the one signal, not a second detector. It is also why **KI-16** exists: a holder whose presence is hidden and who is not Twitch-linked is never seen. Accepted, same limit as F1. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:619` | D7: blank `raidtrain_channel_id` borrows `events_announce_channel_id`, so a server sets up ONE place rather than two. Same pattern as `youtube_channel_id` borrowing `golive_channel_id`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:2192` | ⚠️ **The only role that may be mentioned is the configured ping role.** `users=False` is what makes the in-place edits safe (see `raidtrain.py:189`), and `everyone=False` is what stops a train titled `@everyone` from doing anything. Checklist 11. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:645` | The one guarded path to a channel. A channel TEST_MODE refuses is logged as `raidtrain.post_skipped_test_mode` and returns None — never raised, so a refused post can never abort the state change that preceded it (checklist 12: the important thing first, cosmetics last). `no_channel_configured` and `channel_not_visible` are separate named reasons because the fixes differ. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:727` | The thread is opened on the message that was actually posted, and the guard is told it owns the thread (`own_channel`) so the "train moves" lines may be sent into it while test mode is on — the same allowance temp voice uses for the rooms it makes itself. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:2330` | See §J above: this is the raid-train-owned scheduled-event creator. It refuses under TEST_MODE with `raidtrain.would_create_scheduled` (checklist 1: a side effect the HTTP guard cannot see checks `bot.guard` itself), and it never writes outside `raid_trains`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:788` | ⚠️ **The lineup is EDITED, never reposted.** One message is the whole public record of a train, so a member who bookmarked it keeps a live view; a repost would leave a trail of stale lineups and would ping the ping role again each time. A failed edit is a logged `raidtrain.post_failed`, not an exception — the claim that caused it has already been committed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:829` | ⚠️ **Mode `off` refuses EVERY member command in words**, naming `/raidtrains mode` — not a hidden command and not a dead one. The staff group deliberately keeps working while off, because `mode` is how you turn it on. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:851` | D2: organizer = the configured role OR staff. It is not `default_permissions`, because Discord's permission lock cannot express "or this role"; the gate is at runtime and the refusal NAMES who may do it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:2400` | ⚠️ **Every command that ends up editing the lineup DEFERS first, and every refusal that can be decided without touching Discord answers BEFORE the defer.** Checklist 8 and 24: `_refresh_lineup` fetches and edits a message, message edits are rate-limited, and discord.py sleeps through a 429 — so the 3-second interaction window would expire and the member would see "The application did not respond". `tests/cogs/content/test_raidtrain.py` asserts `response.deferred` on all seven, so removing a defer fails by name. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:978` | The order of the refusals is the order they cost: the train's status, then the per-member ceiling, then whether the slot exists, then the race. Each returns a sentence, and the last one is the only one that can be reached by two people at once. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1098` | `submit_train` reuses `events.py`'s `start_error` and `START_IN_THE_PAST` rather than writing a second pair of date sentences (checklist 15). The zone is the member's own `/timezone`, so nothing new about time was invented for this phase (D15). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1161` | `_numbers` refuses out-of-range sizes BEFORE a row is written, and its sentence names Discord's one-message limit as the reason rather than just quoting a number. |

## `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py` and the Events page

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:104` | Every id leaves as a STRING. A Discord snowflake is bigger than a JavaScript safe integer, and a number that quietly loses its last digits on the page is the worst kind of bug — it looks like it worked. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:153` | ⚠️ **`/status` is declared BEFORE `/{train_id}`.** FastAPI takes the first route that matches and `{train_id}` is typed `int`, so the other order would answer `/api/raidtrains/status` with a 422 about a path parameter — a bare status code in front of a person, which the estate rule forbids. | `site/public/assets/page-events.js:302` | ⚠️ **Raid trains are a SECTION on the Events page, not a page of their own** — the Events page already owns "what is scheduled", and a second surface answering the same question is the duplicate-surface bug the docs standard names. The mode warning sits at the top of the section, above the table, for the same reason the YouTube sweep card does: it decides how to read everything below it. |

Checklist item 6. `tests/test_applications.py::test_the_unique_index_catches_a_second_application_the_check_did_not_see` stubs the read out so the INSERT really is the thing that loses; it fails if the `except` is removed. |
