## One web write, one log row (owner report, 2026-09-03)

> Keyed against `df393ab` (the `fix/web-write-double-log` merge), then re-keyed by
> the requests third pass to `feat/requests-third-pass`. ⚠️ The original header
> line here said "commit **HEADSHA**" — a placeholder that was never filled in;
> `df393ab` is the merge and `19d2f7d` is the docs commit that carries this
> section. Owner: *"The app double posted all messages with a web.request and a
> request"*.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:523` | ⚠️ **`kind_via` is `bare()` read backwards, and the ONLY place the `web.` head is put on.** Six modules used to build `f"{WEB}." if via == VIA_WEBSITE else ""` for themselves (pings, rolemenu_panels, applications twice, role_menus, tempvoice); six copies of an inverse is how one of them drifts from `bare()` and a kind stops classifying. `test_no_module_builds_the_web_head_for_itself` fails if a seventh appears. |
| `black_bloc/api/writes.py:203` | `note()` survives, but only for events **the route is the sole logger of** — `web.request.filed`, `web.request.updated`, the comments, the withdraw, the raid-train and role-menu CRUD. Where a shared bot function already logs, the route passes `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and notes nothing: that pairing was the 2026-09-03 double post, two rows and two embeds for one click. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:760` | `via` is **keyword-only with a Discord default** so the four slash callers keep writing bare `request.*` kinds untouched, and only the dashboard's `_decide` opts into the `web.` head. (Third pass: `mark_ready`, `accept` and `send_back` take the same keyword and pass it straight through.) The same shape is on `resume_request`, `events.apply_decision`, `events.cancel_event`, `polls.store_poll`/`apply_decision`/`close_poll`/`cancel_poll`, `role_menus.apply_request_decision`, `modmail.close_ticket`, `honeypot.ban_hit`/`make_trap_channel`, `tempvoice.make_creator_channel`/`forget_creator`, `automod.save_rule`/`apply_case`/`punish` and the six `modcmds` punishers. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:768` | `details["via"] = via` is written even though the kind already carries the head, because `via_of()` prefers what the writer recorded over what the kind says. Belt and braces: a row keeps saying "Website" even if somebody later renames the kind. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:594` | The route's whole job here is now `via=VIA_WEBSITE` — the deleted `note(f"web.request.{status}")` was the defect. `request_status` still notes `web.request.updated` beside it, because assignee/priority/notes are a **different** change from the status move and nothing else logs them. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modcmds.py:233` | `refuse_in_test_mode` takes `via` too, so a dashboard punish refused by TEST_MODE leaves `web.mod.would_ban` rather than a bare one that reads as a Discord action. It is the actor's row, not a bot-emitted consequence — the `mod.*_failed` and `request.dm_failed` family deliberately stay bare. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/automod.py:310` | `punish` heads every row it leaves, not just the successful one: delete/warn/timeout and their `would_`/`_failed` twins are all outcomes of one actor's click, so they belong to the same Via. This is why the dashboard's Apply-now now leaves `web.automod.*` and no `web.mod.apply` — the automod rows ARE the event, and `mod.apply` was a second framing of it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1326` | `send_reply` was a **false positive** in the survey that found these: it logs only `modmail.dm_failed`, nothing on success, so `web.modmail.reply` is the route's own and stays. `close_ticket` next to it did double, and does not. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:466` | `_branches` unwraps `kind_via(...)` so the dynamic-kind table does not need forty new entries: a literal inside it yields BOTH the bare and the `web.` form. An f-string inside it still needs `KNOWN_DYNAMIC`, keyed on the INNER expression — which is why the pre-existing keys like `f'request.{wanted}'` kept working and just grew their `web.` twins. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:50` | The mechanical guard for checklist 34. It resolves each route's imports to real module files, asks what kinds those functions log (following helpers within their own module, and reading `KNOWN_DYNAMIC` for the f-strings), and fails on any `note()` whose `bare()` kind is in that set. ⚠️ Helpers under `api/` are excluded (`API`) — `note` itself logs whatever it is handed, so without that filter every route matches itself. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:537` | `DOUBLE_LOG_ALLOWED` is **empty and should stay that way**. It exists so a genuine exception is written down with its reason rather than the guard being loosened; an entry here means "these two rows are different events", never "this one is fine". |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:763` | The default matters more than the call sites: one shared function defaulting to `VIA_WEBSITE` would silently turn every slash command's kind into a `web.` one. A private helper with a REQUIRED `via` is fine — it is always handed one. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:556` | `one_web_row` is the per-route half of the same guard, and it is behavioural where the AST walk is structural: it asserts the write left exactly ONE `web.*` row, of the named kind, with `details.via == "website"`. Counting is the point — the old tests asserted both kinds were *present*, which is exactly what a double post looks like. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:222` | Eight kinds left `ROUTINE` with this change (`event.cancel`, `honeypot.ban`, `mod.apply`, `mod.rule`, `modmail.close`, `poll.cancel`, `poll.end`, `tempvoice.forget`): each was only ever produced by a deleted `note()`, and `test_no_classification_entry_is_dead` refuses a table entry nothing emits. ⚠️ Legacy rows keep their kind and classify the same, with ONE exception — `honeypot.ban` ends in `.ban`, an `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` entry, so old `web.honeypot.ban` rows now read as important. That matches the new `honeypot.banned`, so it was left. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:5724` (`MOD_KIND_DONE`) | The mock has to lie the same way the real API does: the punish helpers log what HAPPENED (`warned`, `timed_out`, `banned`), not what was asked for (`warn`, `timeout`, `ban`), so the mock maps the route name to the outcome word rather than logging the route name. `contract.json`'s `action_kinds` was updated in the same commit; `check.mjs` only checks emitted ⊆ listed, so a stale mock would have passed silently. |

# Requests — third pass: the review state, the embeds and the site link

> Keyed against `feat/requests-third-pass` at the commit named in the header
> line above. Owner, 2026-09-03: *"a standard appealing template … one of the
> discord info boxes"*, *"Do we need an acceptance pending so a staffer can check
> if something is done?"*. Design: [`requests-embeds-design.md`](requests-embeds-design.md).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/requests.py:54` | ⚠️ **A LOOK is not a STATUS.** `LOOKS` has seven entries; `STATUSES` has seven too and they are **different sets**: `filed` and `sent_back` are looks with no state behind them, and `open` and `withdrawn` are states with no card. Everything downstream — the log kind, the colour, the fields, who is DMed, whether a card posts at all — reads the look, never the status. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:456` | `look_of` is the whole of that distinction in three lines: `in_progress` arrived at **from `review`** is `sent_back`. Storing a `sent_back` flag would have been a second home for a fact the `was:` already carries, and it would drift the first time somebody moved a row by hand. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:462` | `checked_move` grew two keyword-only text arguments rather than two new functions, because a move is judged in ONE place and the site, the slash commands and the tests all ask this. `TEXT_NEEDED` is keyed by LOOK (`review` needs `built`, `sent_back` needs `note`), which is why the required-text rule fires on a send-back and not on an ordinary pick-up — same target state, different look. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:174` | `DONE_NEEDS_A_CHECK` fires only from `OPEN_STATUSES`. From `declined` or `withdrawn` the generic "is where a request finishes" sentence is still right, and pointing somebody at `/request ready` there would be a lie. The refusal names both the slash path AND the site button, because the person reading it may be on either. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:309` | The colours are DATA (`EMBED_COLOURS`), and so are the titles, the field lists and the inline flags. Seven looks by four properties as literals inside one builder is how the sixth one quietly gets the fifth one's colour. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:752` | `moment` reads `created_at` for the filed card and `decided_at` for every other, so a card is stamped **when the move happened**. A row read back before `decided_at` is written (or a naive ISO string from an older row) falls back to now rather than raising — a card with a slightly wrong timestamp beats no card. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:785` | ⚠️ **`field_value` returning `""` is what leaves a field OFF the card.** Discord refuses an empty field value outright, so "How to test" on a review with none, "Assignee" on an unassigned row and "Due" with no date are absent rather than blank. Every value goes through `clamp(…, 1024)` here and nowhere else — §J measured the worst look at 2004 of Discord's 6000, entirely because of this line. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:849` | `site_view` answers `None` when there is no origin, and `post_line`/`dm` pass `view=None` straight through. A link button with a broken URL is worse than no button; `bot.settings.origin` is always set in practice, so this is the belt to the braces. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:858` | `move_line` is the plain one-liner that REPLACED the sent message — it is now only ever written to the server log, in `post_line`'s two `log.warning` calls, so a card the guard skipped still says in the log what it would have said. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:1028` | `set_status` builds its `UPDATE` from a dict because five columns now have per-move rules and "leave this one alone" was already being faked with `COALESCE`. **A column with no rule for this move is not in the statement at all** — which is how `ready_by` survives a hold-and-resume and how `decided_by` survives a withdrawal. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:717` | `may_accept` answers True when nothing is recorded in `ready_by`. A row moved to `review` by the landing one-off, or by a `/status` write before this shipped, must not become unacceptable by anybody. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:768` | ⚠️ **`kind_via(f"request.{look}", via)` — LOOK, not status.** This is the line that makes `request.sent_back` exist at all; the row's status is `in_progress`. `tests/test_logkinds.py:KNOWN_DYNAMIC` is keyed on the source of that expression, so renaming the variable breaks the build loudly rather than silently dropping six kinds out of the classification check. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:260` | `person_told` is the ONE place that decides who gets a DM, and it is the reason `tell_requester` was renamed: on `sent_back` the person told is the staffer in `ready_by`, not the requester. Nobody is DMed on `review` — it is staff-facing and the channel card is its notice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:281` | The `request_dm_on_decision` gate applies to `DM_LOOKS` only, so the send-back DM to `ready_by` is NOT gated by it. That key is documented as the **requester's** switch; widening it to staff notices would give one key two meanings and there would be no way to want one without the other. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:296` | `post_line` keeps its name and its `line` argument even though the line is never sent — the embed is the message and `content` is `None`. ⚠️ **The guard check is unmoved and unchanged**: TEST_MODE still refuses every channel but the test one and logs `request.notify_skipped_test_mode`, and a mutation that removes the check turns `test_the_review_card_is_skipped_and_logged_while_test_mode_holds_the_channel` red. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:696` | `apply_decision` passes `ready_by` and `sent_back_reason` on EVERY call and lets `set_status` decide whether this move writes them — the alternative, each caller working out which columns its move touches, is the same rule in five places. The `request_review_by_other` check lives here and not in `accept`, so `POST /{id}/status {"status":"done"}` cannot walk around it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:760` | `send_back` is the only one of the three wrappers with a guard of its own: `accept` and `mark_ready` are refused by `TRANSITIONS` when the row is in the wrong state, but `review` → `in_progress` is legal from `open` too, so without this a `/request sendback` on an untouched request would quietly pick it up. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1531` | `ReadyModal` prefills from the row, so a request sent back and marked ready again does not need retyping. `built` is `required=True` at the Discord level AND refused in words by `checked_move` — the client-side one is a courtesy, the server-side one is the rule. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1679` | `/request ready` is two interactions: the command opens the modal, the modal does the move. ⚠️ A modal can only be the FIRST response, so `_wanted_id` must not `defer()` — `require_staff` answers without deferring, which is why it can be called before `send_modal`. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:518` | The three routes' whole job is `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and **no `note()`** — checklist 34. `tests/api/conftest.py:one_web_row` asserts exactly one `web.*` row per write, which is the assertion the pre-fix tests were missing (they asserted presence, which is what a double post looks like). |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:591` | `/status` takes `built` and `how_to_test` as plain fields through `set_fields`, so fixing a typo in how-to-test is a partial save that leaves one `web.request.updated` row and moves nothing. It ALSO forwards them to `apply_decision` when a status is present, so `{"status":"review","built":…}` is a legal, if unused, second path into review. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:914` | Schema **26**: four nullable columns on `requests` (`built`, `how_to_test`, `ready_by`, `sent_back_reason`), added to the `CREATE TABLE` and to `ADDED_COLUMNS`. No backfill — a row that was `done` before this stays `done` with four nulls, and `requests.py:row_value` reads a missing column as nothing on an older file. The landing move of #1 and #2 into `review` is a one-off in the design doc, **not** a migration: `done` → `review` is not a staff move and must not become one. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2996` | `enums` is a NEW registry type — "any of these words", where `enum` is "one of" and `channels`/`roles` are lists of ids. `coerce_value` returns the picked set **in `KEY_CHOICES` order**, so the stored value is stable no matter what order the checkboxes were ticked in and two identical settings never diff. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:47` (`CONTROLS`) — the `enums` row | `VALUE_KEYS` had to learn `enums` or `request_channel_moves` would have been a **dashboard-only** key — exactly half of checklist 33, and the half that is invisible until somebody tries to change it from Discord and finds no way to. ⚠️ **Superseded 2026-09-05 by the settings panel:** the guard is no longer a membership test against a hand-built list: `CONTROLS` maps all eleven registry types, a parametrised test walks every key, and `test_every_registry_key_is_reachable_from_the_panel_as_well_as_the_dashboard` asserts the panel's reach **equals** `KEY_TYPES`. A new registry TYPE with no control is what goes red now, not merely a new key. |
| `site/public/assets/ui.js:938` | The `enums` control is a checkbox per choice, not a segment: a segment says "one of these", and the answer here is a SET. `read` walks the DOM rather than a captured array, so the value saved is what is actually ticked. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:376` | `REQUEST_ANCHOR` takes its page from `logkinds.FEATURE_PAGES["request"]` — **`requests.html`, with the extension.** The design said `{origin}/requests#r-N` and the build shipped that; the site is a `StaticFiles(html=True)` mount (`api/assets.py`), which resolves `/requests` to a file called `requests` or `requests/index.html` and nothing else — live it answered `{"detail":"Not Found"}` (measured 2026-09-03 06:19, before the merge deployed). One home for the page name, so the log-embed links and the card button cannot drift apart. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:245` | ⚠️ **`anchored()` is what makes every Discord card's link button work.** Each card carries `id="r-{id}"`, and `{origin}/requests.html#r-{id}` is built in `black_bloc/requests.py:request_url`. The two halves are in different languages and nothing type-checks between them — `tests/test_requests.py::test_every_card_carries_one_link_button_to_the_request_on_the_site` pins the URL shape, and this is the other end of it. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:flashLinked` | ⚠️ **TWO things break a deep link into a shut section, and neither raises anything.** (1) A card inside a shut section or foldout — Done and Declined both are — sits in a `.card` with `overflow: hidden` and a **clientHeight of 32**, so `scrollIntoView` does nothing at all. (2) Opening the `<details>` is not enough on its own: the scroll must wait a **frame** for layout to settle, or it measures the collapsed height and stays put. Opening and scrolling in the same tick left the reader at the top of the page with nothing in the console. Measured against the mock: with the section open and one frame elapsed, `.content` (the real scroller — the body never scrolls) goes 0 → 3019 and the card lands mid-viewport. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:cardFor` | The pinned card is drawn as whatever the row actually IS. Drawing every one as a review card would put Accept and Send back on an open request, and the API would then refuse the click — the page's own rule is that a control which would be refused is never drawn. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:1141` | The off-page case: staff fetch `/api/requests/N`, a member scans their own `/mine`, and the result is PINNED above the sections with Back to all rather than paging the reader around. ⚠️ A 404 or a 403 here is "that number is not one you can read", **not** an outage — the two get different sentences, because the fixes are different. `pinned` is set before the fetch so a refresh mid-flight cannot pin twice. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:684` | The review card filters `done` and `in_progress` out of `row.moves` and draws Accept and Send back as its own buttons — those two moves need a dialog and a distinct label, which a generic move button cannot carry. `MOVES` lost its `done` entry entirely, so no card anywhere can draw a Done button. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:621` | `writtenRow` is a partial `/status` save, not a move: the owner asked that a typo in "how to test" not need a state change to fix. It is on the review card and on the done card, which is why `shutCard` builds a `notice()` only when the row is `done`. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:6860` (`askDecide`) | The mock enforces the SAME three refusals the API does (no `built`, no send-back note, the second-pair-of-eyes rule) because `check.mjs` only checks that emitted kinds are a subset of the listed ones — a mock that accepted anything would pass while the real API refused. ⚠️ Its `/accept` and `/sendback` read the row AFTER the move; the pre-existing `/hold`, `/decline` and `/status` entries do not, and answer with the state the row was in. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs:21` (`IDS`) | `review_request_id` (11) is a row the SEED already has ready to check, so `/accept` and `/sendback` reach it without walking the machine first — every contract entry runs against a fresh seed. `progress_request_id` (12) is where `/ready` is legal from. |
| `site/public/assets/labels.js:7` | ⚠️ **This file did not parse between `7b1c592` and the fix on this branch**, so `LABELS` never loaded and **every dashboard page rendered blank**. The Phase 19 merge pasted the applications block after the object's closing brace and after `NAMESPACES`, leaving seven orphaned properties and a second `};`. `node --check site/public/assets/labels.js` is the whole test, and it is worth running after any merge that touches this file — nothing else in the suite reads it. |

# Requests, fourth pass — `/request` is ONE command that opens a panel

> ⚠️ **Re-keyed again 2026-09-03 at the wave-0 merge (`1861923`)** — seven rows whose code moved to
> `black_bloc/panels.py` now carry that path with a "was … until wave 0" note, and the cog keys
> moved UP (the library imports replaced ~60 lines of the cog). Before that,
> ⚠️ **re-keyed 2026-09-03 against `feat/requests-panel-own-list` (`dd7c788`)**, which made the
> panel's own-request list staff-only: every key in THIS section was shifted by anchor — the
> `requests.py` ones by **+1** (`PANEL_OWN_LIST_KEY` above them) or **+5** (`withdraw_request`,
> below `panel_shows_own_list` too), and the `cogs/community/requests.py` ones by **+1** above
> `build_panel` and **+2** below it (one import line, one `if`). `settings_store.py` +5;
> `api/tools/requests.py` unmoved. Two rows were ADDED (the gate at `:511`, the helper at
> `requests.py:512`); none was rewritten, because nothing they describe changed.
> Before that, keyed against `feat/requests-panel` at the commit this section was written in.
> Owner, 2026-09-03: *"Let's also have /request open a menu maybe. Let's try and
> minimize slash commands and maximize interactive windows."* Design:
> [`requests-panel-design.md`](requests-panel-design.md). ⚠️ **Not re-keyed against
> earlier sections** — this build deleted the nine `request_*` slash commands and every
> earlier note that describes them (the two "Requests — third pass" rows about
> `/request ready`'s two-interaction shape and `ReadyModal` prefilling, the Phase 13 row
> about `/request create` needing the group) now describes code that is **GONE**, not
> moved; they are left as historical record rather than rewritten, per the standing rule
> that only the conductor re-keys the whole file at merge.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/requests.py:511` | ⚠️ **`CARD_BUTTONS` is DATA, not a chain of `if status ==`.** Every earlier request state-machine bug in this file (`TRANSITIONS`, `EMBED_TITLES`, `MOVE_LINE`) was a table for the same reason: a table is one thing to get wrong, and `tests/test_requests.py::test_every_status_maps_to_the_move_buttons_the_panel_design_names` is parametrised over all seven statuses, so a status the table forgets fails by name instead of silently rendering no buttons. `card_buttons()` is the only reader; the cog never branches on status by hand. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:75` | **`SELECT_CAP = 25` is Discord's own hard limit on a select's options, not a decision.** It caps BOTH selects — the staff "Pick a request…" (which also says "N of M — the rest are on the site" past the cap, per the design) and the member's own "Take one back…" (which silently truncates with no such message, because a member realistically never has 25 requests open at once; noted here since it is the one place the two selects behave differently for the same reason). |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:1156` | ⚠️ **`withdraw_request` deliberately widens checklist item 34's own wording.** That item's own text lists "withdraw" among the routes where `note()` is the sole logger — true when it was written, that morning, before withdraw had a shared function to call. This build gives withdraw one (the panel's confirm and the site's `POST …/withdraw` both call it), so the route's `note("web.request.withdrawn", …)` became the SAME double-post shape checklist 34 exists to catch — `kind_via("request.withdrawn", via)` replaces it, and `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_a_route_never_notes_an_event_its_shared_path_already_logged` is what would have failed if the route had kept its own line. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1325` (`RequestView(Panel)`) | ⚠️ **Views are not persistent, and every render creates a FRESH one with the FULL `request_panel_minutes` timeout — the clock is inactivity, not wall time from when `/request` was first opened.** `RequestView(minutes)` is constructed by `build_panel`/`build_card`/`open_withdraw_confirm` on every single render; clicking anything resets the countdown rather than merely extending a single running one. ⚠️ **This note used to end "only the LAST view nobody touches ever reaches `on_timeout`", and that was WRONG** — see `retire` (now `black_bloc/panels.py:66`) and the design doc's deviation 9. A displaced view keeps its own timeout task; nothing in the library stops it. See KI-20 for why persistence (`bot.add_view`, the `TempVoicePanel` pattern) was not used instead. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:66` (`retire` — was `cogs/community/requests.py:168` until wave 0) | ⚠️ **Every re-render MUST stop the view it replaces, or that view's timeout will overwrite the card that replaced it with a stale disabled copy.** `ViewStore.add_view` (installed `discord/ui/view.py:940–968`) merely overwrites `_synced_message_views[message_id]`; it never touches the displaced view's `__timeout_task`, so that task keeps running and `_dispatch_timeout` (`view.py:611–620`) eventually calls the OLD view's `on_timeout`. `retire` is called in the cog at `:607` (`render_panel`), `:632` (`finish_card`), `:656` (`open_card`) and `:695` (`open_withdraw_confirm`), always immediately BEFORE the edit; every item callback passes its own `self.view` down as `previous`, and `CardMoveButton` (`:811`) hands it to `ReadyModal`/`NoteModal` so the modal's submit path retires it too. `RequestModal` (filing) never re-renders and carries nothing. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:229` (`Panel.on_timeout` — was `cogs/community/requests.py:685` until wave 0) | ⚠️ **The guard is `self.replaced`, NOT `self.is_finished()` — the obvious spelling would have disabled the footer entirely.** Measured against the installed library: `_dispatch_timeout` does `__stopped.set_result(True)` (`view.py:619`) and only THEN `create_task(self.on_timeout())` (`:620`), so `is_finished()` is **already True inside a genuine timeout** — proved by running a real `discord.ui.View` with a 0.05s timeout and reading the flag from inside `on_timeout`. `stop()` alone is what actually prevents the timeout in production (`_dispatch_timeout` returns early on a done future); the `replaced` flag is the belt-and-braces half, and it is the only one that can tell "replaced" apart from "expired". |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:225` (`interaction_check`) / `:92` (`went_quiet`) — were `cogs/community/requests.py:681`/`:696` until wave 0 | ⚠️ **`view.message` is an `InteractionMessage` bound to ONE interaction token, and Discord kills that token 15 minutes after the interaction — so at the old 15-minute default the "gone quiet" footer essentially never got written.** `View._refresh_timeout` (`view.py:315–317`, from `_scheduled_task` at `:596–597`) extends the timeout on EVERY interaction with the view, including ones that do not re-render at all (`Logs`, opening a modal), so by the time it fires the message's token is at least `request_panel_minutes` old and usually older. `interaction_check` therefore records `self.last_interaction` (and always returns True — it gates nothing), and `went_quiet` tries `last_interaction.edit_original_response` first, falling back to `self.message.edit` when there is no recorded interaction OR when the recorded one is refused. Both are wrapped: an `HTTPException` is logged at info, never raised. The other half of the fix is the default dropping to **10** (`settings_store.py:1315`). |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:59` (`still_staff` — was `cogs/community/requests.py:159` until wave 0) | ⚠️ **The panel checks `is_staff` when it RENDERS; a staffer demoted while their card is open would keep moving requests until the panel timed out — so every move re-asks.** `still_staff` runs in the cog's `CardMoveButton.callback` (`:110`, before any defer or modal) and at the top of `Requests.ready_submit` (`:1021`) and `Requests.note_submit` (`:1045`, before their defers), refusing in words with `store.staff_refusal(guild.id)` through `answer()`. ⚠️ **`settings_store.require_staff` is deliberately NOT reused**: it calls `interaction.response.send_message` directly, so it only works where nothing has been deferred — one shape (`still_staff` + `answer()`) at all three sites beats two. `LogsButton` needs nothing, because `send_logs` (`actionlog.py:295–297`) calls `require_staff` itself before it has responded to anything. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:973` (`MOVE_FUNCS`) | ⚠️ **`MOVE_FUNCS`'s three entries are ALL lambdas, not two lambdas and one direct reference.** `{"accept": accept, "resume": resume_request}` would have baked in the function OBJECT at dict-creation time (module import), and `monkeypatch.setattr(requests_cog, "accept", fake)` afterward would silently not affect what `run_move` calls — a lambda body does a NAME lookup in the module's globals at call time, so it is the one shape both a test's mock and a future call-through actually see. Found by writing `test_a_direct_move_button_calls_its_shared_function_and_leaves_via_alone` and watching the "accept" case call the real function anyway. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:74` (`db_ready` — was `cogs/community/requests.py:465` until wave 0) | `db_ready` assumes the caller already `defer()`'d — every component/modal callback in this file does `interaction.response.defer()` first BECAUSE, per `discord/interactions.py`'s own `InteractionResponse.defer`, a component or modal-submit interaction's default (non-`thinking`) defer is `deferred_message_update` (type 6): an ack that edits the SAME message in place, never a new one. `interaction.edit_original_response(...)` is what actually changes it afterward, and `interaction.followup.send(...)` is what puts the returned sentence beside it — checked against the installed library source (checklist 29), not memory. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:999` (`build_panel`) / `:530` (`build_card`) | `build_panel`/`build_card` are free functions taking `bot`/`guild`/`actor`, not `Requests` cog methods, so every `discord.ui.Item` subclass can call them via `interaction.client` without holding a `self.cog` reference. Only `submit`, `ready_submit` and `note_submit` stay cog methods, because `RequestModal`/`ReadyModal`/`NoteModal` already take a `cog` argument (existing shape for the first two; matched for the third) and fetch it with `interaction.client.get_cog("Requests")` at the point a modal is opened. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1128` (`open_withdraw_confirm`) | `open_withdraw_confirm` reuses `look_for_status` (open → `filed`, everything else itself) for the PREVIEW card too, not only the staff card — one status→look mapping, one place it can drift. The confirm view carries only "Yes, take it back" / "Keep it", never a `Back`, because the design lists exactly those two. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:260` (`NoteModal.__init__`, the label mutation — was `cogs/community/requests.py:909` until wave 0; the cog's thin subclass is at `:916`) | `NoteModal.note.label` is mutated per-instance in `__init__`, the same way `ReadyModal.built.default` already was — one `discord.ui.TextInput` field, three labels (`hold`/`decline`/`sendback`), each naming who the note is sent to inside Discord's 45-character label cap. ⚠️ This discord.py version deprecates the `.label` setter in favour of `discord.ui.Label` (Components V2) — it still works, and nothing else in this codebase needs a per-instance label yet, so the migration is left for whoever adopts Components V2 wholesale rather than done piecemeal here. |

The value is still NOT clamped — the `KEY_HELP` sentence is the warning, and KI-20 carries the same one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:999` (the own-list gate) | ⚠️ **Only the RENDERING of a member's own requests is gated — `own_rows` is still fetched for every caller, on purpose.** Owner, 2026-09-03: *"We need to make the view request thing staff only"* → *"Viewing requests on the panel"*. `if staff or panel_shows_own_list(store, guild.id):` wraps the `summary_line` block AND the `PANEL_EMPTY` line, and nothing else in `build_panel` moved. See deviation 12 in [`requests-panel-design.md`](requests-panel-design.md). |
