This should be in website logs only". The gate already existed (`requests.py:696` `posts_a_card`, checklist 33 both ways since the third pass), and the live DB held NO stored `request_*` row, so a default change is the whole fix and a server can tick `done` back on from the Settings page. Two tuples, not one edited: `KEY_CHOICES` must keep `done` or the Settings checkbox and the panel's own multi-select would REFUSE it. The requester's DM on done (`DM_LOOKS`, `request_dm_on_decision`) is untouched — it goes to the person who asked, not to the channel, so it is not the duplicate the owner named. `test_every_card_but_done_posts_and_one_pair_of_eyes_is_enough_until_a_lead_says_otherwise` pins both tuples. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:608` (`panel_shows_own_list`) / `:52` (`PANEL_OWN_LIST_KEY`) | The helper and its key sit beside `panel_minutes`/`PANEL_MINUTES_KEY` rather than in the cog, so the cog holds no `store.get(..., "request_panel_own_list")` string of its own — the same shape `channel_moves`, `review_by_other` and `panel_minutes` already use, and the reason `tests/test_requests.py` can pin the default (`Store()` with no value at all → `False`) without building a `SettingsStore`. `bool(store.get(...))` rather than `is True`, because the registry coerces the key to a real bool before it is ever stored and a `None` from an unconfigured guild must read as off. Registered in the three places `request_panel_minutes` is: `settings_store.py:294` (`KEY_TYPES`, `"bool"`), `:904` (`KEY_HELP`) and `:1322` (`default()` → `False`) — which is all checklist 33 needs, since the panel reaches every registry key by construction (it was `VALUE_KEYS` in `cogs/core.py:27`) derives the `/settings set-value` list from `KEY_TYPES` and the Settings page reads the same registry. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:663` (`request_withdraw`) | The route keeps its own `NOT_YOURS` check (whose row is this?) and hands the rest to `withdraw_request` — identity belongs to the caller, because the panel and the route each already know their caller a different way (a Discord `User` versus a signed-in session), and `withdraw_request` takes a `row` it trusts is already the actor's own. |

# Panels library (wave 0, 2026-09-03)

> Keyed against `feat/panels-library` at the wave-0 build commit `5da0081`. This section is
> NEW. The older `Requests, fourth pass` rows above WERE re-keyed at the merge (`1861923`,
> 2026-09-03): the seven whose code moved here — `retire`, `on_timeout`,
> `interaction_check`/`went_quiet`, `still_staff`, `db_ready` and `NoteModal.note.label` —
> now name their `panels.py` line with a "was … until wave 0" note. Nothing in this wave
> changed behaviour; the 163 requests tests passed **unchanged in assertion**.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/panels.py` (the module) | ⚠️ **This file exists so seventeen feature panels do not re-implement three defects seventeen times.** `/request` took four passes and a review that found exactly three (a replaced view's timeout clock overwriting the live card; a "gone quiet" footer that could never be written at 15 minutes; a staff check that only ran at render time) — deviations 9, 10 and 11 in [`requests-panel-design.md`](requests-panel-design.md). Every one of them lives here now, fixed once. [`panels-program.md`](panels-program.md) §2 is the invariant list every later panel is reviewed against; its §4 is this wave. The module imports `command_errors` and `settings_store` only — it knows nothing about requests, and `tests/test_panels.py::test_the_library_says_what_it_offers_and_knows_nothing_about_requests` pins that. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:203` (`Panel`) | **Was `RequestView` (`cogs/community/requests.py:674–713` before this wave), moved verbatim except that the gone-quiet sentence is now the `footer` constructor argument** instead of a module constant read out of `requests.py`. `AnswersErrors` stays FIRST in the bases (checklist 30 — a view that defers without an `on_error` leaves a permanent spinner). Invariant P7. The cog's `RequestView(Panel)` (`cogs/community/requests.py:1325`) keeps its name and its `__init__(minutes)` so `build_card`, `build_panel`, `open_withdraw_confirm` and every requests test are untouched. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:229` (`on_timeout`) | ⚠️ **The guard is `self.replaced`, NOT `self.is_finished()` — the obvious spelling would disable the footer entirely.** Measured against the installed library: `_dispatch_timeout` does `__stopped.set_result(True)` (`discord/ui/view.py:619`) and only THEN `create_task(self.on_timeout())` (`:620`), so `is_finished()` is **already True inside a genuine timeout**. Deviation 9; invariant P6. This is the single most important line in the file to leave alone. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:66` (`retire`) | ⚠️ **Every re-render MUST stop the view it replaces**, or that view's timeout overwrites the card that replaced it with a stale disabled copy. `ViewStore.add_view` (`discord/ui/view.py:940–968`) merely overwrites `_synced_message_views[message_id]`; it never touches the displaced view's `__timeout_task`, so that task keeps running and `_dispatch_timeout` (`view.py:611–620`) eventually calls the OLD view's `on_timeout`. Deviation 9; invariant P6. Called immediately BEFORE every edit — in the requests cog at `render_panel`, `finish_card`, `open_card` and `open_withdraw_confirm`; every later panel does the same. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:225` (`interaction_check`) / `:92` (`went_quiet`) | ⚠️ **`view.message` is an `InteractionMessage` bound to ONE interaction token, which Discord kills 15 minutes after that interaction — so a panel whose `<feature>_panel_minutes` is 15+ silently loses its footer.** `View._refresh_timeout` (`view.py:315–317`, from `_scheduled_task` at `:596–597`) extends the timeout on EVERY interaction with the view, including ones that do not re-render at all (a Logs button, opening a modal). So `interaction_check` records `self.last_interaction` (and always returns True — it gates nothing), and `went_quiet` tries `last_interaction.edit_original_response` first, falling back to `self.message.edit` when there is no recorded interaction OR when the recorded one is refused. Both wrapped: an `HTTPException` is logged at info, never raised. Deviation 10; invariant P7, whose "default 10, and the key's help text says why" half stays per-feature in each `settings_store` `default()` branch. ⚠️ The log line now reads `"panel: could not disable a timed-out panel: %s"` on `black_bloc.panels`'s own logger, not `"requests: …"` — a grep for the old sentence will miss it. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:51` (`still_allowed`) | Wave-3 conductor prep (raidtrain design §F, added 2026-09-04 on `main` before any wave-3 build): the re-ask with the gate FACTORED OUT. `still_staff` became a two-line call to it, so raid trains (`is_organizer` = configured role OR staff), role menus and automod can re-ask their own gate without copying `still_staff`'s body — checklist 15. Takes the verdict and the refusal already computed, not a callable, so callers that need the guild or a row to decide keep that logic in their own module. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:40` (`still_staff`) | ⚠️ **A panel checks `is_staff` when it RENDERS; a staffer demoted while their card is open would keep moving things until the panel timed out — so every staff move re-asks.** Refuses in words with `store.staff_refusal(guild.id)` through `answer()`. ⚠️ **`settings_store.require_staff` is deliberately NOT reused**: it calls `interaction.response.send_message` directly, so it only works where nothing has been deferred. Deviation 11; invariant P8. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:40` (`answer`) | The one refusal shape that copes with responded-or-not: `followup.send` once `interaction.response.is_done()`, `response.send_message` otherwise, always `ephemeral=True` and `AllowedMentions.none()` (checklist 11). It is what makes `still_staff` usable after a defer, which is the whole reason deviation 11 did not reuse `require_staff`. ⚠️ Distinct from `command_errors.answer`, which is the generic unhandled-error sentence and swallows its own failure; this one is a deliberate reply and lets an `HTTPException` reach `AnswersErrors`. Two functions, one name, on purpose — they are NOT interchangeable. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:74` (`db_ready`) | ⚠️ **Assumes the caller already `defer()`'d** — it answers a followup, never `response.send_message`. Every component/modal callback defers first BECAUSE, per `discord/interactions.py`'s own `InteractionResponse.defer`, a component or modal-submit interaction's default (non-`thinking`) defer is `deferred_message_update` (type 6): an ack that edits the SAME message in place. Deviations 1 and 6; invariant P5 ("every click re-checks `db_ready`"). It imports `DB_UNAVAILABLE` from `settings_store` at module level, which is the ONE new import edge this wave adds (`requests` → `panels` → `settings_store`); no cycle, because nothing under `black_bloc/*.py` or `black_bloc/storage/` imports `black_bloc.requests`. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:151` (`capped_placeholder`) / `:14` (`CAPPED_PLACEHOLDER`) | Invariant P10 — Discord's 25-option select cap, with a placeholder saying what was left off. `CAPPED_PLACEHOLDER` is the sentence's ONE home (checklist 15): `requests.py:230` `PICK_CAPPED = CAPPED_PLACEHOLDER` reads it rather than restating it, and `requests.pick_placeholder` (`:488`) is now a one-line call passing `PICK_A_REQUEST`. The `pick` word stays per-feature ("Pick a request…", "Pick a poll…"); only the capped wording is shared. `capped` is still a parameter so a feature whose list is NOT on the site can say something else. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:191` (`panel_minutes`) | Takes the settings KEY, so each feature keeps its own `<feature>_panel_minutes` registry entry (checklist 33 / invariant P13) while the read is one function. `requests.panel_minutes(store, guild_id)` (`:191`) is now a one-liner over it with `PANEL_MINUTES_KEY`; it is imported into `requests.py` as `library_panel_minutes` purely so that module's own two-argument public name does not shadow it. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:260` (`NoteModal`) | Invariant P12 — one paragraph field whose label names what the note is for and who is sent it. Generic on `title`/`label`/`max_length`/`on_submit`. ⚠️ **The callback is stored as `self.takes_note`, NOT `self.on_submit`** — an instance attribute named `on_submit` would shadow `discord.ui.Modal.on_submit`, which Discord calls with `(interaction)` alone, and the arity mismatch would surface only at click time in production. ⚠️ The inherited class-level `note = discord.ui.TextInput(...)` works in a SUBCLASS because `Modal.__init_subclass__` (`discord/ui/modal.py:111–121`) walks the full `__mro__` collecting `Item`s, and `_init_children` (`:123–129`) `deepcopy`s each one per instance — checked against the installed library (checklist 29), pinned by `tests/test_panels.py::test_two_note_modals_do_not_share_one_field`. That same `deepcopy` is why a test must compare `note.style` with `==` and not `is`. This discord.py version deprecates the `.label` setter in favour of `discord.ui.Label` (Components V2); it still works, and the migration stays for whoever adopts Components V2 wholesale. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1559` (`NoteModal`) | The requests note modal is now a **thin subclass** of the library's, keeping its `(cog, request_id, kind, previous)` signature and its `NOTE_TITLES`/`NOTE_LABELS`/`NOTE_LIMITS` lookups, so `Requests.note_submit`, `CardMoveButton` and all six existing tests are untouched. ⚠️ **The `self.cog`/`self.request_id`/`self.kind`/`self.previous` assignments come BEFORE `super().__init__(...)` on purpose**: the `on_submit=self.note_submit` bound method it hands up is called later, but it must exist as an argument now, and the state it closes over is this instance's. The bound method is named `note_submit` to match the cog method it forwards to. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:973` (the two `panels` imports) — wave 0 | ⚠️ **`retire`, `answer`, `db_ready` and `still_staff` are imported to MODULE level in the cog on purpose, not called as `panels.retire(...)`.** The cog's own code resolves them through its module namespace, so `requests_cog.retire(view)` in `tests/cogs/community/test_requests.py` and any future `monkeypatch.setattr(requests_cog, "still_staff", …)` keep working exactly as they did — the same call-time name-lookup reasoning as `MOVE_FUNCS`'s lambdas one section above. `NoteModal` is imported `as PanelNoteModal` because the cog exports its own `NoteModal` under that name. |

# Requests, sixth pass — "Ask them to check" (2026-09-03)

> Keyed against `feat/requests-check` at its fourth commit. This section is NEW; nothing above
> it was re-keyed, because the sixth pass only INSERTS into `requests.py` and the cog — but the
> insertions shift every `Requests — third pass` and `Requests, fourth pass` key below the
> insertion point, so re-key those two sections at the merge (the standing rule). The design and
> its 11 deviations are [`requests-check-design.md`](requests-check-design.md).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1110` (`BackButton`, `row=1`) | ⚠️ **A review card is now FIVE moves wide, which is exactly Discord's action-row cap — Back had to leave row 0, and this is a crash fix, not a layout preference.** `discord/ui/view.py:193` raises `ValueError: item would not fit at row 0 (6 > 5 width)` while the view is being BUILT, so every review card in the panel would have failed to render, not merely looked wrong. Found by running the parametrised `test_the_card_renders_exactly_the_buttons_the_table_says[review]`, which is now also the guard: it asserts `len([item for item in view.children if item.row == 0]) <= 5` and that Back is on row 1, so the sixth move somebody adds later fails in a test instead of in production. Deviation 1. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:53` (`LOOKS`) / `:46` (`CHECK_ASKED`) | ⚠️ **`check_asked` is a LOOK, never a status, and deliberately NOT in `DM_LOOKS`.** The states say who HOLDS a request (staff working / staff checking / waiting / finished); "the requester has been asked" is a fact ABOUT the review, so the row stays `review` and `TRANSITIONS` is untouched — §B of the design says why a `checking_by_requester` state would double every review button and every test for no new transition. It is out of `DM_LOOKS` because `DM_LOOKS` is the table `tell_person` (`cogs/community/requests.py:282`) reads on a MOVE; `ask_check` sends its own DM at a moment no move happened, and putting the look in that tuple would have made a `request_dm_on_decision=false` server silently skip the one DM this feature exists to send. Added LAST in `LOOKS` so `MOVE_LOOKS` (`cogs/community/requests.py:152`) and `channel_moves` (`:689`) pick it up with no edit. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:813` (`request_embed`, the `if look == CHECK_ASKED`) / `:191` (`CHECK_ASKED_DESCRIPTION`) | The ONE `if` in an otherwise table-driven builder. Title, colour and fields stay in `EMBED_TITLES`/`EMBED_COLOURS`/`EMBED_FIELDS`; only this look sets `embed.description`, and a fourth table with one populated row would cost more than the branch. `mention(check_asked_by) or "staff"` — a row whose asker is unknown (an auto-ask by a bot actor with no id) still reads as a sentence rather than as `Try it and tell  how it went`. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:763` (`asked_stamp`) / `:273` (`FIELD_LABELS["asked"]`) | The "Asked to check · @who · 3 minutes ago" field on review and done cards. ⚠️ **An empty string is the whole point**: `request_embed` skips a field whose value is empty, so a card nobody has asked on simply has no such field — no "not asked yet" line to read past. An unparseable `check_asked_at` falls back to the mention alone rather than raising, the same shape `moment` (`:752`) already uses; a stamp is cosmetic and must never be able to stop a card rendering. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:185` (`NOT_READY_TO_CHECK`) | ⚠️ **Its last sentence was stale from the moment the fourth pass landed** — it recommended `/request ready {id}`, a subcommand that build deleted, and nothing caught it because no test asserted the wording. It now names the **Ready to check** button on the card, which is what actually puts a request there from either surface. The mock carries the same sentence (`site/mock/server.mjs`, `REQUEST_NOT_READY`) and was fixed in the same commit; it also gained a `{doing}` placeholder, because two routes refuse with it now. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:861` (`ask_check`) | The one shared path, same `(what to say, row or None)` contract as `send_back` and `resume_request`, so the panel button and `POST /api/requests/{id}/check` differ only in the `via` they pass (checklist 34: `kind_via` builds the head, the route `note()`s nothing). ⚠️ **The order matters**: the fields are stamped BEFORE the DM is built, so the card the requester receives already carries its own "Asked by" line, and `told` is decided by what actually happened rather than by what was attempted. `request.dm_failed` on a refused DM is a SECOND row, not a substitute for the action row — today's contract for every look, not a new one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:296` (`post_line`, the `ping=` keyword) | ⚠️ **The only place this cog mentions anybody.** Every other send in the file is `AllowedMentions.none()` (checklist 11); this one narrows to exactly one user — `AllowedMentions(users=[discord.Object(id=ping)])` plus a `content` of that mention — so an `@everyone` in a `what` field still cannot ping, and neither can a role. Everything else in `post_line` (the guard check, the missing-channel warning, `NOTIFY_SKIPPED_KIND`, `NOTIFY_FAILED_KIND`) is unchanged and still applies to the fallback post, which is why test mode cannot leak one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:760` (`mark_ready`, the auto-ask) | `mark_ready` is no longer a pure delegation to `apply_decision`: with `request_check_on_ready` on it asks straight afterwards, and the ask is its OWN log row because it is its own thing that happened. ⚠️ **It returns `ask_check`'s fresh row, not `apply_decision`'s** — `finish_card` re-renders from the returned row, and the pre-ask row has no `check_asked_at`, so the new field would have been missing from the card until somebody refreshed. Deviation 6. The reply text stays `READY_SAID`; the ask's outcome is on the card, not in a second sentence. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:973` (`MOVE_FUNCS["check"]`) | A lambda like its three neighbours, for the same reason the wave-0 note above gives: a lambda body looks the name up in the module's globals at CALL time, so `monkeypatch.setattr(requests_cog, "ask_check", fake)` in `test_a_direct_move_button_calls_its_shared_function_and_leaves_via_alone[review-Ask them to check-ask_check]` reaches it. `CardMoveButton.callback` needed no change at all — `check` is neither `ready` nor `needs_modal`, so it falls through to `run_move`, which already does `still_staff` → defer → `db_ready` → `MOVE_FUNCS` → `finish_card`. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3790` (`REQUEST_CARD_DEFAULT`) / `:1324` (`default`) | `check_asked` is the eighth `request_channel_moves` CHOICE and, like `done`, is excluded from the DEFAULT — the DM is the point, and a channel copy is opt-in. Two tuples again, not one edited: `KEY_CHOICES` must keep both or the Settings checkbox and the panel's own multi-select would refuse them. `request_check_fallback_channel` defaults **on** (a closed DM should not silently mean nobody was told) and `request_check_on_ready` **off** (asking is a judgement about whether the work is worth a person's time). Both are `bool` registry keys, which is all checklist 33 needs. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:557` (`request_check`) | The `/accept` route's shape exactly, with `ask_check` behind it and `via=VIA_WEBSITE`; `fresh is None` is a 409 carrying the shared function's own sentence, so the site says the same words the panel does. ⚠️ **No `note()`** — checklist 34, guarded by `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_a_route_never_notes_an_event_its_shared_path_already_logged`, an AST walk of `api/tools/*.py`. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:657` (`askedChip`) | Added to the shared `headBlock` rather than copied onto the done card, because `readyChip` — the thing the design said to mirror — is not used in the finished list at all: `shutCard`, `boardCard`, `openCard` and `heldCard` all render `headBlock`. One call covers every card, and rows nobody has asked on return `null` from it. The text is "asked **by** X", not "asked X": `check_asked_by_name` is the staffer who asked, and without the preposition it reads as the name of the person being asked. Deviations 7 and 8. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs` (the review walk) | The action-kinds walk is the one pass that does NOT re-seed between calls, so its order is a state machine: `ready → check → sendback → ready → accept`. `check` goes FIRST of the four on the review row because it is the only one that leaves the row where it is — put anywhere else it would be asking a row that had already moved on. The contract table (`contract.json`) re-seeds per route, so its `/check` entry is order-independent. |

# Applications, no-role pass

> Keyed against `feat/applications-no-role` at the build's third commit (`df99135`), 2026-09-03.
> 3414 tests pass, ruff clean, `check.mjs` 17 pages / 141 routes. The design is
> [`applications-no-role-design.md`](applications-no-role-design.md); its `## Deviations` foot
> lists the five places the build departed from it. ⚠️ **Re-key this section after the merge**
> — the sibling `feat/requests-check` build touches `settings_store.py` and `storage/db.py`
> and will shift these numbers (standing merge-order rule in `CLAUDE.md`).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:1049` (`_loosen_application_form_roles`) | 🔴 **The one place in this build where a mistake destroys owner data, and the reason it is called at `:697` — BEFORE `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` at `:699` rather than beside the other migration steps.** `application_questions.form_id` carries `REFERENCES application_forms(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`db.py:595`). With foreign keys ON, `DROP TABLE application_forms` performs an implicit `DELETE FROM application_forms`, which cascades — **every question on every form would vanish silently**, and a form with no questions cannot be applied for. Run before the pragma, the drop is inert. `tests/storage/test_db.py::test_a_schema_26_file_lets_a_form_drop_its_role_and_keeps_every_question` builds a 26-shape file by hand (two forms, three questions, one application) and asserts all three questions survive. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:1013` (the `commit()` before the log line) | ⚠️ **Without it `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` two lines later becomes a SILENT no-op.** SQLite refuses to change `foreign_keys` inside a transaction and does not raise — it just ignores the pragma. The rebuild's `INSERT … SELECT` opens one under Python's legacy transaction control, so the connection is mid-transaction when `connect()` reaches the pragma. Found by running the test, not by reading the code: the first version passed every row-and-question assertion and failed only `PRAGMA foreign_keys == 1`. That assertion is the reason the test keeps it. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:13` (`APPLICATION_FORMS_COLUMNS`) / `:34` (`APPLICATION_FORMS_LOOSENED`) | One fact, one home (checklist 15): the column list is a module constant that the `SCHEMA` f-string interpolates AND the rebuild's `CREATE TABLE … ` reuses, so the copy cannot drift from the live shape and `INSERT INTO … SELECT *` cannot fall out of column order. ⚠️ `SCHEMA` became an **f-string** for this — it contains no other `{` or `}`, which was checked before the change; any SQL added to it that needs a literal brace must double it. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:1069` vs `:747` (`_set_aside_mod_cases_with_a_required_user`) | ⚠️ **Deliberately NOT the mod_cases rename-then-restore shape.** Renaming the LIVE table would make SQLite ≥ 3.26 rewrite `application_questions`' foreign key to point at the renamed copy (unless `legacy_alter_table` is on), leaving the fresh `application_forms` unreferenced. Create-copy-drop-rename renames only the new table, which nothing references, so the existing FK text keeps naming `application_forms` and resolves again the moment the rename lands. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:449` (`role_of`) | The ONE reader of a form's role. Returns `None` for missing, `NULL`, `0` and unparseable, so no caller ever formats `<@&None>` or `<@&0>` — the sentinel-zero design was rejected in §B5 precisely because `holds_role(member, 0)` is a silent lie. Every `form["role_id"]` read in the tree now goes through it (`render_card`, `decision_lines`, `_approve`, `remove`, `form_lines`, `form_row`). |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:41` (`NO_ROLE`) with `:785` (`CLEARABLE_IDS`), `:796` and `:816` (`update_form`) | ⚠️ **`role_id=None` means "leave it alone" and `role_id=NO_ROLE` (0) means "clear it" — they are NOT interchangeable, and the difference is invisible at the call site.** `update_form` drops `None` values (that is how every optional slash argument spells "unchanged"), so clearing needs its own word. `:606` turns the sentinel back into `None` AFTER that filter, and `:626` builds `SET role_id = NULL` as literal SQL for any surviving `None` rather than binding it — the parameter form works too, but the literal is what makes "this column is being cleared on purpose" visible in the statement. ⚠️ The same trick would fix the standing inability to clear `review_channel_id`/`approver_role_id`/`owner_user_id`; §E of the design keeps that OUT of scope, so do not widen it here without an item. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:540` (`decision_lines(granted=…)`) | ⚠️ **Three-valued on purpose: `True` handed over, `False` Discord refused, `None` there was nothing to hand over.** The old `if not granted` treated "nothing to hand over" as "the grant failed" and would have pasted "Discord refused to add the role — hand it over with `/role grant`" onto every no-role approval. Every test of it is `is False`, never falsy. `_approve` (`cogs/community/applications.py:451`) and `is_live` guard the same way. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:195` (`APPROVED_ON_RECORD`) | The no-role half of `APPROVED_SAID`. It names the form's HEADING rather than a role, and takes no `{extra}`: `EXPIRES_EXTRA` says "the role runs out …", which is a lie when there is no role, so the expiry line is suppressed on a list form even when `expires_days` is set. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:1038` (`remove_application`) | `APPROVED → REMOVED`, the owner's "staff always get the final say" rule (`CLAUDE.md`, 2026-09-03) applied to a list. ⚠️ **`status = 'approved'` is in the WHERE clause, not checked before it** — same one-writer-wins shape as `decide_application`, so two staff pressing the button at once produce one removal and one "not approved" sentence. The reason reuses the `deny_reason` column: the row's `status` says which kind of no it was, and a second column would have been two homes for one fact. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:959` (`last_decision`) | ⚠️ **`REMOVED` was added to the status list here, which is what makes `retry_days` bite after a removal.** Without it `cooling_until` would see no decision and somebody taken off the list could re-apply the same minute — the design says the wait applies "as it does after a denial", and this line is where that is true. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:968` (`twitch_logins_for`) | One `IN (…)` query for the whole roster, never one per row — `tests/test_applications.py::test_the_whole_roster_s_twitch_logins_come_back_in_one_query` counts the executes. De-duplicates ids before building the placeholders, and drops rows whose `twitch_login` is empty so the caller's `.get()` is the only emptiness check. Reads `golive_links`, which is per MEMBER and not per guild (`db.py:99`) — the roster is therefore as accurate as `/twitch link`, and §D3 keeps a hand-typed login out of scope. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:498` (`settle_approval`) | `until` is computed only when there IS a role, so a list form with `expires_days` set neither writes an expiry into the log nor mentions one in the DM. `details["role_id"]` is `None` rather than absent — the Logs page reads details as a flat map and a missing key would render as though the form had never had one. `_hand_over` is not called at all, so `application.granted`, `application.would_grant` and `application.grant_failed` simply never fire; `application.approved` with `granted: null` is the whole record (design §C6). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:638` (`remove`) | The web route and the button share this one function, which is why it takes `via` and logs `kind_via("application.removed", via)` itself — checklist 34, one write leaves ONE `action_log` row. `api/tools/applications.py:470` passes `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and does NOT `note()` on top of it. ⚠️ Refuses a form that HAS a role in words (`REMOVE_IS_FOR_LISTS`, `:95`) rather than removing the record and leaving the role on them: for a role form the role's own end IS the way off, and `/role revoke` is the sentence's answer. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:203` (`can_decide`) | ⚠️ **`may_decide` ANSWERS the interaction when it refuses, so it cannot be used to decide whether to draw a button.** `can_decide` is the same question with no side effect, used by `show_panel` at render time; the button's own callback still calls `may_decide` (`:1070`), so a staffer demoted while the panel is open is refused in words at click time (checklist / invariant P8). |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:291` (`card_buttons`) (was `cogs/community/applications.py:838 show_panel`) | ⚠️ **`show_panel` is GONE with `/applications show` (2026-09-03).** Its job — draw **Take off the list** only on an `approved` row of a form that keeps a LIST, and only for somebody who may decide it — is now three arguments of `card_buttons(status, has_role=…, may_decide=…)`, which the `/apply` panel's `build_card` calls. Same three conditions, expressed as data rather than as a `None`-returning factory, and `tests/test_applications.py` parametrises them |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:642` (`form_lines`) (was `cogs/community/applications.py:1405`) | The form line prints `list` instead of `<@&None>` — the old code interpolated `one['role_id']` straight into a role mention, which rendered as a broken chip on a no-role form. `role_of()` is asked first and the word `list` is the else. The line builder moved out of `/applications list` into the pure module when the panel took over (2026-09-03); the test that pins it moved with it |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:37` (`PANEL_MINUTES_KEY`) | `applications_panel_minutes`, the fourth `<feature>_panel_minutes` key (invariant P13 / checklist 33). Deviation 5 in the design doc: §C4 asked for ONE new setting and this is a second, because `Panel` takes a timeout and a hard-coded 10 would be a decided default the owner cannot reach. Its help text carries the same 15-minute warning `request_panel_minutes` does. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:89` (`form_row`) | ⚠️ **`resolve_one(guild, None)` must never be called** — it would name whatever the guild resolves for a null id (`@everyone` in practice) and the forms table would show a role chip for a form that has none. `role_name` is resolved inside the `if role` branch, and `tests/api/tools/test_applications.py::test_a_form_can_be_made_with_no_role_and_never_resolves_one` monkeypatches `resolve_one` and asserts it is never asked about `None`. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:257` (the PATCH `role_id` branch) | A blank `role_id` in the payload becomes `forms.NO_ROLE`, not `None` — see the `update_form` note above; `None` here would mean "the page did not send a role" and the clear would be dropped. The page sends `''` on PATCH and `null` on create for exactly this reason (`page-rolemenus.js:723`). |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:344` (`GET /roster`) | Declared BEFORE `GET /{application_id}` so `/roster` is not eaten by the id route. 404s in words when the form is unknown or belongs to another guild. Honours `applications_roster_shows_left` (default true, §D1): somebody who has left is listed with `in_server: false` rather than hidden, because the official team page may still list them and staff decide. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:782` (the blank role option) | Deviation 1: `roleSelect` ALREADY prepends a blank `not set` option, so the design's `allowNone: true` was not needed — the option is relabelled **"No role — keep a list"** in place. `:782` (`syncRole`) hides the whole **Role lasts, days** field while the select is blank, using `el.hidden` (the artifact reset and the site's CSS both honour it) rather than `style.display`. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:1010` (`rosterFoldout`) | The roster is fetched **on the fold's first open**, not with the page — a server with a dozen forms would otherwise make a dozen requests nobody asked for. The `toggle` listener is guarded by `asked` so re-opening does not re-fetch (press the page's own refresh for fresh rows). The count in the summary starts from the approved rows the section ALREADY has from `/api/applications` and is replaced with the roster's own length once it lands, because `applications_roster_shows_left` can make the two differ. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:105` (`ROSTER_LINE`) / `:936` (`copyLines`) | §D4: one line per member, `Name — twitch.tv/login`, `no Twitch linked` where there is none and ` (left the server)` appended where they have gone — the bridge to the official team page, which is not ours to write (§E). ⚠️ `navigator.clipboard.writeText` rejects in a page without clipboard permission, so the failure is caught and answered with a sentence telling the reader to select the rows by hand — never a silent no-op. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (`GONE_FROM_GUILD`) | The mock's one seeded member who is on a list but no longer in the server, so `in_server: false` and the roster's "left the server" flag are exercised by `check.mjs` rather than only by pytest. `nameFor` still knows them: the record outlives the membership, which is the whole point of the flag. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs` (`checkRoster`) | Deviation 4: the design asked for a DOM walk (open the fold, click the button, count rows). `check.mjs` has no DOM — it is a route-contract runner — so the same walk is done over the routes: roster lists 3, one carries a `twitch_login`, one is flagged as having left, a removal with a reason succeeds, a removal with a blank reason is a 400, the roster is then 2, and the removed row appears under `?status=removed`. |

# Birthdays panel (wave 1)

> Added 2026-09-03 by the birthdays panel build, branch `worktree-agent-a19bdce15408f8243`, keyed
> against that branch's tip. `/birthday` is ONE command that opens an ephemeral panel;
> the `birthday` `Group`, the nested `birthday role` group and all twelve subcommands are
> gone. The design is [`birthdays-panel-design.md`](birthdays-panel-design.md); the
> invariants it is built against are [`panels-program.md`](panels-program.md) §2.
>
> ⚠️ **The Phase 5 section above was re-keyed by ANCHOR in the same commit** — 30 keys in
> `## black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py — F6`, every one checked against the
> construct it names. Two of them now point at `black_bloc/birthdays.py` because the code
> moved there (`chunked`, and the confirmation sentence as `stored_sentence`), and one
> (`:250`) says out loud that the `/birthday import` command it was written for has not
> existed since 2026-08-27. The design doc's header called this drift out before the
> build: the old `:308` named `loop_health`, which was at `:300`, and the old `:624` lock
> note was at `:673`.
>
> NOT verified: anything against live Discord. No panel has been opened by a person; no
> boot was run (this build has no bot token). `commands synced` was read from
> `tests/test_bot.py::test_the_command_tree_stays_inside_discords_limits`, which measures
> the real tree with every cog loaded: **44, unchanged** — a `Group` already held one
> top-level slot, so retiring it frees nothing (requests deviation 7).

## `black_bloc/birthdays.py` — the panel's pure half

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:485` (the `panels` import) | The pure module now imports the wave-0 library for `panel_minutes` alone. That is the same edge `black_bloc/requests.py:608` has and it is not a cycle: `panels` imports `command_errors` and `settings_store`, neither of which imports this module. It does mean `black_bloc/birthdays.py` pulls `discord` in, which it did not before — the module is still free of Discord *objects*, which is what "no Discord in them" was ever about. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:37` (`MODE_WARNINGS`) | A member who sets a birthday deserves to know nothing will be posted, and the feature ships in `shadow`. Keyed on the mode string so `on` simply has no entry and the line disappears — an absent key, not an `if mode == …` chain that a fourth mode would silently fall through. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:418` (`DATE_PARTS`) | `-`, `/`, `.` and space, collapsed as one run, because people type `09-15`, `09/15` and `9 15` and none of them is wrong. Splitting on a character class rather than parsing a format string is what makes all four separators one rule instead of four. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:421` (`parse_birthday_input`) | ⚠️ **It never guesses a year.** Two parts means no year, full stop — a birthday typed `09-15` must not silently acquire one, because a stored year is what puts somebody's age on a public embed. Anything that is not two or three runs of digits is `None`, and the caller answers `DATE_UNREADABLE`; the month/day/year values themselves are NOT checked here, so `date_problem` and `year_problem` keep their existing sentences and their existing home. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:432` (`date_modal_title`) | Discord refuses a modal whose title is over 45 characters, and a display name is arbitrary attacker-controlled text — a nickname of 90 characters would have made `Set their birthday` fail with an HTTP error and no explanation. Only the "theirs" title is clamped; the "mine" one is a constant. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:439` (`stored_prefill`) | Zero-padded so the prefill round-trips through `parse_birthday_input` — the modal offers back exactly the shape it accepts, which is what makes "change my birthday" an edit rather than a re-type. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:459` (`PanelButton`) / `:473` (`PANEL_BUTTONS`) / `:480` (`panel_buttons`) | The button table is DATA (invariant P3), the shape of `requests.MoveButton`/`CARD_BUTTONS`/`card_buttons`. ⚠️ `(False, True)` is **unreachable** — `opted_out` is defined as `has_date and not opted_in` — so `panel_buttons` falls back to the nothing-stored row rather than raising: a hand-edited row or a future caller must not be able to crash the panel, and the parametrised test pins the fallback. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:485` (`panel_minutes`) / `:489` (`panel_shows_next`) / `:493` (`panel_allows_lookup`) | One helper per key, beside the key name, so no caller ever spells a settings key as a literal. Same shape as `requests.panel_minutes`/`panel_shows_own_list`. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:509` (`card_lines`) | ⚠️ **`mine` changes two things, and both matter.** The stored birth **year** is shown in brackets only on your own block — `birthday_show_age` already decides whether an *age* is public, and the year is the raw fact behind it, so somebody else's card renders exactly what `/birthday show` rendered before. And the opted-out sentence reads "You are" rather than "They are", because the same builder writes your panel and their card. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:557` (`stored_line`) | ONE home for the stored/opted-in/imported/self sentence, which the staff panel and `status_lines` both show. It was inline in `/birthday status` before and would otherwise have been typed twice, which is checklist 15. |
| `black_bloc/birthdays.py:564` (`status_lines`) | The cog gathers the values and this only words them, so the whole of the Status button's output is testable without a bot, a database or an interaction. The dict is deliberately flat and named — a positional signature of thirteen arguments is not readable at the call site. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py` — the panel

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:89` (`NOT_STORED`) etc. | Five strings named a command that no longer exists (`NOT_STORED`, `NOT_STORED_FOR`, `OPTED_OUT`, `NOBODY_YET`, and two lines inside `report_lines`). They name **buttons** now. ⚠️ `report_lines` is rendered by the WEBSITE too (`api/tools/birthdays.py:121`), so its two replacements name neither a button nor a slash command: "until the person corrects their own birthday", and "set these by hand, from the Birthdays page or the `/birthday` panel". `ROLE_CLEARED`/`ROLE_NOT_SET` were left alone at the time because `/settings set-role birthday_role_id` still existed; ⚠️ **2026-09-05 they were rewritten too** — that subcommand is gone and they name `/settings` ▸ **A setting group…** ▸ birthday. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:333` (`dm`) | Staff forgetting somebody else's birthday is the one move in this feature that affects a person who is not in the room, so they are told. A closed DM is logged at info and the move still succeeds — the row is gone either way, and failing the removal because a DM bounced would be worse. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:346` (`store_birthday`) | The one path a birthday is written by, for the member's own modal and staff's alike (P4). It returns the **sentence to show**, so the refusal and the confirmation come back the same way and the caller never decides wording. `date_problem`/`year_problem` run here rather than in the modal, so the two paths cannot drift. ⚠️ The retired `set` option was `Range[int, 1900, 2200]` while `year_problem` refuses anything after this year — the modal keeps `year_problem`, so the effective rule is unchanged and the dead 1901-year gap in the Range is gone. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:377` (`forget_birthday`) | Takes an optional `member`, which the design's `(cog, guild, actor)` signature did not: the person card's **Forget their birthday** is the Discord path to a move the website already had (`DELETE /api/birthdays/{user_id}`), and the owner's staff-final-say rule of 2026-09-03 requires it to exist somewhere in Discord. `source` rides into the log row's details so a staff removal is distinguishable from a member's own. The role still goes back before the row is deleted (Phase 5 review finding 3) and the whole thing is inside the per-user lock. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:408` (`change_opt`) | ⚠️ **Staff cannot opt somebody else out, and no surface offers it.** Opting out is the member's own privacy control; the card gives staff *set* and *forget*, which are both about the stored fact, never about somebody's choice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:483` (`build_panel`) | One command, two panels, split on `store.is_staff` (P2). Every block is a LINE, never a dead control (P9): a member with the coming-up list switched off is told it is for staff rather than shown an empty heading. The colour is the same `parse_color(birthday_color)` the wish embed uses, so the panel and the post are one look. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:525` (`build_card`) | The person card. **Forget their birthday** renders only when there is something to forget (P3), so staff never press a button that would answer "there is nothing stored". A non-staff caller gets `Back` and nothing else, which is the whole difference between looking somebody up and acting on them. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:592` (`open_confirm`) | ⚠️ **Since the confirm/opened fold (2026-09-05) this builds the embed and the view and hands both to `panels.confirm`; its six Button classes are gone, replaced by `panels.confirm_items` at the three call sites.** Three confirms — remove, forget-theirs, clear-the-role — share one builder because they differ only in their sentence and their two buttons. Each is a re-render in place with `retire(previous)`, so the confirm screen is the panel, not a second message. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:728` (`send_month`) / `:724` (`send_status`) | The two staff reads answer NEW ephemeral messages and never edit the panel, so the panel is still there when the list is read — the same shape as the Logs button (P11). They still `defer()` first, which is a `deferred_message_update` on a component: it acknowledges without changing anything. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:781` (`MoveButton`) | Row 0 is built from `panel_buttons`, and the button's `action` decides the shape of the click: `set` opens a modal (so it must NOT defer), `remove` opens the confirm, `refresh` re-renders, and the two opt actions run the shared function. One class for four moves rather than four near-identical classes. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:799` (`LookupSelect`) | A `UserSelect` rather than a name-matching select: it is not option-capped by us, so `capped_placeholder` (P10) has nothing to bite on here and its absence is deliberate, not an omission. `self.values[0]` is a real member object, so the card never has to resolve an id. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:807` (`MonthSelect`) | 13 options — `Every month` plus the twelve names — against Discord's 25, so no cap and no placeholder. Value `"0"` means every month; the alternative (a separate "all" button) would have been a sixth control on a panel that already fills all five rows. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:821` (`ModeSelect`) | The current mode is marked `default=True` so the select reads as a state, not a menu of two spellings of the same move (P3). It is rebuilt on every render, which is why flipping the mode makes the warning line and the select's own default change together. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:893` (`DateModal`) | ONE modal, one field, for both the self path and the staff path — the title and the `mine` flag are the only difference, and `mine` also decides whether the submit re-renders the panel or the person card. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:920` (`open_date_modal`) | ⚠️ **A modal cannot follow a `defer()`**, so the stored row is read BEFORE anything acknowledges the interaction, and a database that is down is answered in words here rather than raising. This is the one click in the panel that does not defer first, and the reason is Discord's, not ours. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:1254` (`/birthday`) | The whole command: `_ready` (guild + database), build, send ephemerally, keep the message on the view so `on_timeout` can write the gone-quiet footer. `MEMBER_COMMANDS` still contains `birthday` — the panel is a member command that grows a staff half, not a staff command. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:1266` (`date_submit`) | ⚠️ **`still_staff` runs BEFORE the defer** on the staff path (requests deviation 11): `require_staff` writes through `interaction.response.send_message` and cannot be used after one. A staffer demoted between opening the modal and submitting it moves nothing. |

## `settings_store.py` and `tests/test_bot.py` — what the panel changed

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3250` (the birthdays panel block) | Appended as its OWN `KEY_TYPES.update` / `KEY_HELP.update` pair rather than added to the existing `birthday_*` rows, so the three wave-1 branches merge textually instead of fighting over one dict literal. The `default()` branches go beside `birthday_show_age`, which is a different file region again. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3178` (`birthday_panel_minutes` default) | **10, not 15.** The "gone quiet" footer can only be written while Discord's 15-minute interaction window is open (KI-20), so 15 or more means the buttons stop with nothing to explain it. Nothing is clamped — the help text is the warning, exactly as `request_panel_minutes` does it. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3208` / `:1326` (the two member-visibility defaults) | Both **True**, which is today's behaviour: `/birthday next` and `/birthday show @user` were open to every member. That is fork **F-B1**, decided by the owner 2026-09-03 12:20 — the coming-up list already shows the next five to everyone and `Opt out` is the member's own control, so the lookup reveals nothing somebody did not choose to store. The owner made the analogous call the other way on requests; either way the key exists and the Settings page flips it. |
| `tests/test_bot.py:11` (`LOGS_GROUPS`) | Lost its `"birthday"` entry: `/birthday` is no longer a `Group` with a `logs` child, so both loops that walk this dict would `KeyError`. `LOG_LEVEL_COMMANDS["birthday"]` in `settings_store.py` was deliberately NOT touched — it still names a real command, and `/request` is carried the same way after its own panel landed. (GONE) |

# Events panel (wave 1) — `/event` is ONE command, `/timezone` is gone

> Written 2026-09-03 on `feat/events-panel`, keyed against that branch's own tree
> (`9a1beb4` + `d85274e`). ⚠️ **The whole shared layer moved out of the cog into
> `black_bloc/events.py`**, so every events key ABOVE this section was re-pointed by
> anchor text in the same commit — 55 keys moved, four of them across a rename
> (`_health_lines` → `health_lines`, `_post_review_card` → `post_review_card`,
> `_make_review_channel` → `make_review_channel`, `MODAL_ZONE_HINT` into the module).
> Re-key again after the merge.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/events.py:13` | ⚠️ **The import block is the whole reason this file is now bottom-heavy.** It was a pure module that knew only `discord`, `golive` and `timezones`; the move brought `actionlog`, `command_errors`, `panels` and `settings_store` in with it. That edge is real and one-way — `settings_store` does not import events, and never may, or the package stops importing. The import check in the design's §H exists for exactly this: it is what a boot would have caught. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:97` (`TRANSITIONS[DENIED]`) | ⚠️ **`denied` is no longer terminal.** The owner's standing staff-final-say rule (2026-09-03) says no stored state may be one staff cannot leave, so `denied → approved` is legal and the card renders **Approve after all**. Two consequences that are easy to miss: `TERMINAL_STATUSES` is derived from this table, so it lost `denied`, and `apply_decision` only drops an event's lock once the status is terminal — a denied event therefore **keeps** its `asyncio.Lock` until it is cancelled. That is correct (a row that can still move must still be raceable-safely) and it is pinned by `test_a_settled_event_stops_being_kept_a_lock`. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:127` (`ZONE_BUTTON`) | The button's label is a module constant because **eleven sentences name it** — `BAD_START`, `START_IN_THE_PAST`, `DST_GAP`, `TZ_SHOW`, `TZ_SHOW_DEFAULT` and the panel row itself. One home, so renaming the button cannot leave a refusal pointing at a control that no longer exists. Every one of those sentences used to say `/timezone set`, which is now a command that does not exist — a dead end inside the product, not just a stale doc. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2456` (`submit_event`) | ⚠️ **`review_view` is an argument, not an import.** This function ends by posting the review card, whose Approve/Deny buttons are a `DynamicItem` living in the cog; a pure module cannot reach it. Passing the builder in keeps the dependency stated and lets a future web door post no card at all (`view=None`) rather than crash. It returns `(sentence, row)` and answers no interaction — the caller owns the reply, which is what let the cog's `submit` shrink to modal wiring. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2532` (`may_cancel`) | The requester-or-staff rule, in ONE place, so the member's `Call one off…` select and the staff card's `Call it off` button both render exactly when `cancel_for` would succeed (P3). It also carries the "still open" half, which is why a `denied` card never offers to cancel. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2545` (`cancel_for`) | ⚠️ **The rename the website never did.** `cancel_event` cancels; the Discord path always renamed the review channel afterwards and the web route did not, so the same action left two different servers behind depending on which door you used. Both doors are on this function now. `reason` stays the LOOKUP KEY (`CANCEL_WHY`) the site passes free text into; `note` is the new thing — the one line a person is actually sent, appended to the DM. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2628` (`CARD_BUTTONS`) | §C's table AS DATA, and `MOVE_TARGETS` beside it is what lets a test check the table against `TRANSITIONS` rather than against a copy of itself. `room_resolves` is a third argument because "does the review channel still exist" is not derivable from a status, and the `denied` exit is only offered while the room is there to argue it in. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2725` (`set_zone`) | ⚠️ **A button cannot have autocomplete**, so the refusal has to do the work the dropdown used to. `suggest()` is the same function the old `/timezone set` autocomplete called; typing `Phoenix` now gets `America/Phoenix` offered back as "Did you mean…", which is strictly more help than a slash command that simply refused an unknown name. 598 zones on this machine against Discord's 25-option select cap is why this is a modal and not a picker. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2866` (`checked_numbers`) | The two numbers `/event settings` bounded with `app_commands.Range`, which a modal has no equivalent of. It reads the SAME `settings_store` constants, so the `/event` panel and the `/settings` panel's own number modal cannot drift, and it refuses in words naming the range rather than clamping silently — a clamp would tell somebody their 9999 was accepted. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:433` (`build_panel`) | ⚠️ **Staff get `list_lines`, not just the counts line.** The design's staff table named only counts + the select; built that way, the loudest sentence `/event list` ever said — `NO_STAFF_WARNING`, "nobody but admins can press Approve" — would have vanished with the subcommand. So the staff half of the embed IS `/event list`, and `event_panel_own_list` became purely a member key: staff see every open event, which is a superset of "staff always see theirs". |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:407` (the `on` branch) | P9 in two lines: with `events_mode off` neither **Propose an event** nor **My time zone** is rendered and the embed says why. The zone button is tied to Propose deliberately (owner, I2): a zone is only ever needed where a member TYPES a time, and DISPLAY needs none at all because `stamp()` emits `<t:…:F>`, which every reader's client renders in their own clock. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2352` (`Events.submit`) | The reply now carries `when_line` — "7:00 PM your time (America/Phoenix) · `<t:…:F>`" — both readings of the time that was typed. That is the second half of the owner's I2 exchange: the member sees what the bot understood AND what everybody else will see, in one line, so a wrong zone is visible at the moment it matters instead of on the day. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1146` (`CategorySelect`) | ⚠️ **`min_values=0` is the library's half of an unproven contract.** discord.py permits it (`discord/components.py`, `SelectMenu`); whether the *client* actually submits an empty select is the half nobody could check without Discord, and an empty submit is the only way a picker can mean "forget this". So the fallback was built beside it rather than instead of it: `ForgetButton` opens a three-option select over the same three keys and writes through the same `write_settings`. If the empty submit turns out to work, `Forget…` is a second door to one behaviour, not a second implementation. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:714` (`change_settings`) | Every settings control — four selects, a toggle, a modal and the forget list — funnels through one function, so there is one write path, one `event.settings` log row per press (checklist 34) and one re-render. `still_staff` runs BEFORE the defer, because `answer()` copes with both states and `require_staff` does not (requests deviation 11). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1729` (`NoteModal`) | Deny and Call-it-off share one modal class and differ by one dict lookup, including `required` — Deny needs its reason (the requester is told why), Call-it-off does not (an event called off with no explanation is still called off). `panels.NoteModal` gained `required=` for this rather than a private copy; it is a library-shaped need, and the library's own test pins both values. ⚠️ **The optional note IS the confirm** on the staff card: submit is yes, dismiss is keep, so a staff cancel is one click plus a line instead of a confirm and then a reason. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2247` (`_sweep_finished`) | Unchanged, but worth saying now that `denied` is not terminal: `SWEPT_STATUSES` still includes it, so a denied event's room is still deleted on the retention clock. That is what makes the `Approve after all` button conditional on the room resolving — after the sweep there is nowhere for the decision to be discussed, and the card says so in words instead of offering a move into a room that is gone. |


# Polls panel (wave 1, 2026-09-03)

`/poll` is ONE command that opens an ephemeral panel; the `poll` and `poll recur` groups and
all eleven subcommands are gone. Design: [`polls-panel-design.md`](polls-panel-design.md);
the invariants it is reviewed against are [`panels-program.md`](panels-program.md) §2.

### `black_bloc/polls.py` — the button table and the lines, still with no gateway in it

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/polls.py:101` | ⚠️ **`DENIED: (OPEN,)` — a denied poll is no longer the end of the line.** Owner's standing rule (`CLAUDE.md`): never a terminal state staff cannot leave. `TERMINAL_STATUSES` is derived from this table, so it collapsed to `(ARCHIVED,)` on its own, and `apply_decision`'s `drop_lock` branch followed — a denied poll keeps its lock because it can still move. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:871` | `MoveButton` mirrors the requests NamedTuple and adds ONE field: `staff_only`. `End` is the only move in this feature a non-staffer may make, so it is the only row that sets it False — the alternative was a second table for members, which is exactly the "two spellings of one move" P3 forbids. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:897` | `card_buttons` takes `creator_may_end` as well as the design's `staff`/`is_creator`, so the `poll_creator_may_end` key is answered in the pure module rather than by each caller pre-computing a misleading `is_creator=False`. A move nobody present may make is never returned, so P9's "not rendered" falls out of the table instead of being remembered at every call site. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:922` | `summary_line` and `recur_line` (`:931`) take the already-parsed datetime rather than calling `golive.parse_ts` themselves. ⚠️ **`polls.py` cannot import `golive`**: `golive` → `settings_store` → `polls` is a cycle, and `panels` → `settings_store` → `polls` is the same cycle. Leaving the parse with the caller is what keeps §H's promise that this module imports no database and no gateway. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:940` | `recurrence_card` is the one builder a template gets; `review_card` would have shown a poll's hours and options but nothing about when it comes round. The paused case writes `RECURRENCE_PAUSED` where the clock would be rather than dropping the field, so the card never looks half-rendered. |

### `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` — the panel, and five writes lifted out of it

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:1712` | `pause_recurrence` / `resume_recurrence` (`:1730`) / `delete_recurrence` (`:1757`) / `save_recurrence` (`:1776`) are the four recurrence writes, each `(what to say, the row)` and each taking `via`. They were inline in four subcommand bodies AND inline again in `api/tools/polls.py`; both callers now go through one copy, so one write leaves one `action_log` row (checklist 34) and the routes' `note()` calls were deleted rather than kept. `resume_recurrence` answers `(sentence, None)` when the stored cadence no longer reads, which is what the route turns into its 409. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:1816` | `apply_poll_settings` is the whole of the old `/poll settings` body: every `store.set`, every `store.clear`, and ONE `poll.settings` line per submit however many switches moved. It takes no `via` — no web route calls it, because the dashboard writes settings through the generic settings API, which logs `web.settings.set` itself. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:1834` | `counts_for` moved from a cog method to module level because `build_card` needs it and a card is not a command. `Polls.counts_for` stays as a one-line delegate so nothing holding a cog had to change. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:1848` | `post_now` and `send_for_review` (`:1865`) are the old `_post_now` / `_send_for_review` cog methods turned into `(said, row)` functions: the panel answers through a followup after its own defer, not through `answer()`, so the sentence has to come back rather than be sent. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2090` | ⚠️ **`PollDraft` holds the whole create flow and NOTHING is written until `Post it`** (design fork I-3). `draft_trouble` catches the one thing `poll_plan` cannot be handed — hours that are not a whole number, because `poll_plan` calls `int()` on them — while slots and step are passed through as typed text, so `date_trouble` can quote back what the person actually wrote. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2427` | `MOVE_FUNCS` and `RECUR_FUNCS` (`:2438`) are late-bound lambdas, so the shared function behind each button can be swapped in a test and every move is provably going through the one copy rather than a private path. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2475` | `may_end` is the panel's one non-staff gate and it re-asks at click time exactly as `still_staff` does (P8) — a `poll_creator_may_end` flipped off while a card is open takes the move away rather than letting a stale render through. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2491` | `write_draft` is the ONE write the panel makes: `store_poll`, then `save_recurrence` (repeating), `send_for_review` (review on) or `post_now`. Every refusal ahead of it re-renders the preview or the panel and answers in words, so a failed create never leaves half a poll behind. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:3135` | The create modal uses Discord's five-component cap exactly: question, options, hours, a `RadioGroup` of kinds, a `CheckboxGroup` of the two switches. ⚠️ **All five are wrapped in `discord.ui.Label`.** A bare `TextInput` still works in 2.7.1, but mixing bare inputs with labels produces a payload carrying both an action row and label components, and `TextInput(label=…)` is deprecated in favour of exactly this shape. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:3274` | `FindModal` is the panel's answer to the lost `poll_id` argument: the pick select carries `OPEN_STATUSES` only, so a closed, cancelled or archived poll is reachable by number and by nothing else. It is deliberately NOT the library's `NoteModal` — that is a paragraph box, and a paragraph box for `12` reads wrong. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:3399` | The settings panel is five rows of controls over `settings_lines`, and every one of them goes through `save_settings` → `apply_poll_settings`, so "one write, one log row" holds however a switch was flipped. `SettingsToggle` reads the current value at render time and writes the NEXT one, which is why its label says `Polls: on` rather than `Turn polls off`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:1229` | The cog's own `answer()` was a byte-for-byte second copy of `panels.answer` and is gone (it used to sit just above `dm`). `option_label` came out of `requests.py` into `panels.py` in the same commit — wave 0 deviation 2 said the first feature wave needing a second copy should extract it, and this is that wave; `requests.option_label` now delegates, so its tests stayed green unchanged. |

### `black_bloc/panels.py` — what wave 1 added to the library

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/panels.py:159` | `option_label(ident, status, text, limit)` is the generic form of `requests.option_label`: the id, an optional status word, then as much text as fits. It clamps the WHOLE label rather than only the text, so a caller handing it a long status word still gets something Discord will accept. |

The panel says the feature is off in words instead and renders no Apply control (P9). `tests/test_command_visibility.py` pins the absence, and sweeps row 53 now tests the opposite of what it used to |

| `black_bloc/applications.py:1054` (`restore_application`) | ⚠️ **The THIRD writer, beside `decide_application` (`WHERE status = 'pending'`) and `remove_application` (`WHERE status = 'approved'`).** Each hard-codes the state it may move FROM, which is what makes two clicks a millisecond apart settle once — a single wider writer would have to trust its caller's read. It also nulls `deny_reason`, because the reason belonged to a decision that has been reversed |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:493` (`settle_approval`) | Everything a yes owes once the row says `approved`: the role, the log, the DM, the edited card. Extracted so `reinstate` cannot drift from `_approve` — a denied application approved after the fact hands the role over and sends the approval DM through the same lines, and `decision_lines` already words `approved` for both role and list forms |

The log kind is `application.approved`, **not a new one** — the same event, so `tests/test_logkinds.py` needed no new entry |

| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:717` (`set_mode`) | The mode write goes through one function so `application.mode` is logged once **and** `bot.store.set` still fires the `command_visibility` on-change hook. # Operator read token — a bearer that may look and never change

> Written 2026-09-03 on `worktree-agent-aa960a4c8635193e0`, keyed against that branch.
> ⚠️ Re-key at the merge. The design and its `## Deviations` foot are in
> `operator-read-design.md`; how to mint and use it is
> `../access/operator-read.md`. Neither is repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/config.py:23` | `SHORT_OPERATOR_TOKEN` deliberately mirrors `SHORT_SECRET` word for word, because they are the same failure with a different name: a secret that is present but too short, treated as unset, saying so once at load rather than failing quietly at the first request |
| `black_bloc/config.py:142` | The validator only WARNS — it never raises. A short token must not stop the bot starting; `operator_read_enabled` is what actually closes the door, so a typo costs the feature and nothing else |
| `black_bloc/config.py:142` | ⚠️ **`operator_read_enabled` re-checks the length, so the minimum lives in ONE place.** It reuses `SESSION_SECRET_MIN` rather than growing a second constant: the name says `SESSION` and this is the deliberate exception — the two secrets have the same floor for the same reason, and two constants would be two homes for one number |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:41` | `OPERATOR_RATE` is **30**, not `LOGIN_RATE`'s 10, and it has its OWN bucket. Ten a minute is a sign-in rate; sharing the login bucket would also mean guessing at this door could lock a real person out of signing in |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:46` | `OPERATOR_WHO` carries **exactly** the keys `current_session` returns, plus `operator`. That is what lets `staff_dependency`, `reader_dependency` and every route consumer stay unchanged — nothing downstream knows this identity is unusual. `member: False` is a decision, not an oversight: `/api/requests/mine` is a person's own list and the operator is not a person |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:258` | `bearer_token` reads headers through `getattr` because `current_session` is called in tests with a bare `SimpleNamespace(cookies=…)` — the same shape the non-ASCII-cookie test uses. It also returns `None` for a scheme that is not `bearer`, so a `Basic` header falls through to the cookie path rather than being a refusal |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:284` | ⚠️ **The `request.state` guard is why one read leaves one row.** FastAPI caches a `Depends` by callable identity, and `staff_dependency(bot)` builds a NEW closure per call — so `/api/members`, which depends on staff AND reader, runs `current_session` twice. `tests/api/test_auth.py::test_a_route_whose_gate_runs_twice_still_leaves_one_row` is that route specifically |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:298` | A missing guild, a disconnected DB or `operator_read_log` off all mean "no row", never "no read". The log is a courtesy to the owner; refusing the read because it could not be logged would turn a sqlite blip into a dead door — the same reasoning `sessions.alive` uses when the database is down (KI-6's residual) |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:306` | The write is wrapped because `log_action` touches the DB and the log channel. A read that succeeded must not turn into a 500 because its audit line did not land — the warning is the record that it did not |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:314` | `compare_digest` on **UTF-8 bytes**, not on `str`: the str form raises `TypeError` on any non-ASCII character, which is the trap `state_matches` was already fixed for (F3). Encoding both sides makes a non-ASCII header a mismatch, which is what it is |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:331` | The method check is the WHOLE permission model, and it sits here — before `current_session` returns, so before any route body, any later dependency, or `actor_for`/`WebActor`. A test monkeypatches `WebActor` to fail on construction and asserts a valid-token `PUT` never reaches it |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:332` | ⚠️ **The bearer is read BEFORE `bot.settings.session_secret` is checked.** An operator read must work on a server whose sign-in is not configured at all — the two doors are independent, and putting this second would have made the read depend on a secret it does not use |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:11` | The third `via` word. `via_of` still answers `website` for a bare `web.operator.read`, because the `web.` head is all an old row has — only `details["via"]` makes it `operator`, and `actionlog.stamped` is what records it. `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_an_operator_read_says_so_only_because_the_writer_recorded_it` pins exactly that |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:222` | `operator.read` is listed in `ROUTINE` and `operator` is deliberately **NOT** added to `HEADS`: the fall-through in `feature_of` already lands it on `core`, and a `HEADS` entry would change `like_patterns("core")` — which is built backwards from every OTHER feature — for no gain |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2998` | `operator_read_log` is the ONLY registry key this feature has, and that is checklist 33 answered rather than dodged: the on/off IS the secret, because a settings key that could re-open a door the owner had `unset` would be a worse switch than the secret itself. The design doc's decision 12 is the written form of it |
| `black_bloc/api/settings_api.py:30` | It joins `CORE_KEYS` because `namespace_of` reads the first word of a key — left alone it would have invented a namespace called `operator` holding one bool (GONE) |
| `site/public/assets/logs.js:103` | The site keeps its own copy of `VIA_WORDS` (it always has). Without the third entry `viaCell` renders an em-dash for an unknown word, so an operator read would have shown as "—" rather than wrongly as Website — safe, but useless |
| `scripts/read.ps1:9` | The fallback to `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable(..., 'User')` is not belt-and-braces: a shell spawned by a parent that started BEFORE `setx` ran inherits the parent's environment block and never sees the variable. The registry read is the only way such a shell finds it, and it costs one line |


# Go-live panel (wave 2) — `/golive` is ONE command, `/twitch` is gone

> Written 2026-09-03 on `worktree-agent-a87a00d41b8dc47d1`, keyed against that branch.
> ⚠️ Re-key at the merge. Everything `panels-program.md` §2 (P1–P17) says is not repeated here.

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py:1551` | ⚠️ **ONE command, member-visible, carrying both halves** (owner, 2026-09-03 16:10: `/golive`, described as *"Your Twitch channel, and whether your streams get announced"* so the word Twitch is still on the card). A `Group` and a command cannot share a name in discord.py, so `golive` and `twitch` both had to go for this to exist. Eight subcommands over two top-level slots become one slot: `commands synced` **42 → 41**, measured by `tests/test_bot.py`, not asserted. It keeps **no `default_permissions`** because neither group had any; the staff half is gated at runtime by `still_staff`, exactly as `require_staff` gated `status`/`mode`/`test`. ⚠️ **`command_visibility.HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` was already silent about `golive_mode` and stays that way** — the panel says the feature is off in a LINE and still offers every member control, because linking does something with the mode off (raid trains read the link, fan roles are made from one). |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:654` (`PANEL_BUTTONS`) | The §B table AS DATA, keyed `(linked, opted_out)`, with the staff pair appended rather than interleaved. It is what makes P3 testable: eight rows, and the cog's parametrised test asserts the rendered labels ARE this table and nothing else. The two spellings of one move (`Link` / `Change`, `Stop announcing` / `Announce again`) can never both render, because they are alternatives inside one row rather than two entries filtered at render time. |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:634` (`PanelMove`) | ⚠️ **A LOCAL dataclass, not a move of `requests.MoveButton` into `panels.py`.** One-fact-one-home says fold them; five wave-2 builds editing `panels.py` at once is the conflict `panels-program.md` §5 exists to avoid. The fold is the conductor's job after wave 2 — the same call events and applications made. It carries `row` because a go-live move's row is fixed by the table, not by the order it is added in. |

# Automod panel (wave 3) — `/automod` is one command

> Keyed against `0b1b2bf` (the `--no-ff` merge of `worktree-agent-ae7bb4ba9c5540ad4`, clean, no
> conflicts; re-keyed 2026-09-04 at the merge — every key is an anchor, so nothing moved).
> ⚠️ **Live Discord has seen the BOOT only** (v74, 22:45Z: database ready / synced 38 / logged
> in, no Traceback): no panel opened, no button pressed, no message judged. The import check (`black_bloc.automod`, `cogs.moderation.automod`,
> `api.tools.mod`, `black_bloc.panels`) is the substitute, and it is the one that matters
> here because `api/tools/mod.py` imports `apply_case` and `save_rule` from the cog and
> neither moved.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/automod.py:213` (`_as_words`) | ⚠️ **The ONE engine-adjacent change in this build, and the only reason it is here.** The site's textarea joins and splits the word list on NEWLINES (`page-automod.js`), so a modal prefilled the way the site prefills it would have collapsed a whole list into one word on submit. `WORD_SEPARATORS` splits on `,`, `\r` and `\n`, so a comma list, a line list and a mixed one all produce the same words and no stored list changes. It changes how a list is TYPED, never which words are enforced — `matched_words` and `evaluate` are untouched. |
