# Chat panel (wave 3) — `/chat` is one staff command

> Written on `worktree-agent-ab33797d235cf0d96` against `e4304e1` and carried into `main` at the
> merge `251dd14` (v75, 2026-09-04) — the merge added nothing to the chat files themselves, so the
> keys still hold; ⚠️ trust the anchor text over the number where later merges shift lines. ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live Discord**: no boot, no panel
> opened, no note written, no model called. The import check
> (`black_bloc.chat_panel`, `cogs.content.chat`, `api.tools.chat`, `knowledge`, `personas`,
> `settings_store`) is the substitute, and `settings_store` is in it on purpose — it already
> imports `personas` and `chat_memory`, so a careless `chat_panel → settings_store → personas`
> edge is where a cycle would appear. It is clean.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:278` (`mood_refusal`) | ⚠️ **Fork F-C4's two guards live here and NOWHERE else**, which is the whole point of the fork: the website refused two moves the Discord command allowed, so the pool could be emptied from Discord and `pick_trope` would fall back to the cookout voice with a `log.warning` nobody reads. It returns a failed `Outcome` rather than a bare string so `mood_options` can filter on `is None` — the select offers exactly what `set_mood` would accept, which is P3 in one function rather than in two that can drift. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:293` (`mood_options`) | Returns `(may be turned off, may be turned on)` — two tuples, because the panel renders TWO selects and not one toggle. A single "pick a mood to flip it" control is P3's *two spellings of one move* in a disguise: its option label would have to say both what the mood is and what picking it does. `guarded_moods` is the third view of the same rule, for the embed line that says WHY a mood is missing — hiding a row with no explanation is the quiet-wrong the panels program exists to end. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:Outcome` | ⚠️ **A dataclass, not the bare string `pings.save_settings` returns.** The website door has to raise `Refused(status, code, message)`, and a string cannot carry a status or an error code; returning one object means the two doors cannot disagree about whether something was refused. `refusal()` is the only constructor for the failure case, so a new refusal cannot forget its status. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:404` (`wanted_note`) | The guild check and the `SERVER` refusal both doors need, in one place — it returns `(row, refusal)` rather than raising, so the note CARD can render a `server` row (with the refusal as a LINE) while `edit_note` and `remove_note` refuse it. That asymmetry is deliberate: the list is how staff see what the bot actually knows, so hiding the row would be worse than showing it locked. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:502` (`read_limits`) | Every one of the five fields is `parse_value`d and `coerce_value`d BEFORE the first write, so one bad field saves nothing — the pings `NamesModal` rule. It is separate from `save_settings` because a modal hands over STRINGS and the website would hand over numbers; `save_settings` re-validates either way, so neither door can write past the registry. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:kind_via(...)` call sites | Every kind inside `kind_via` is a string LITERAL, including the `"chat.trope_enabled" if enabled else "chat.trope_disabled"` pair. That is not a style choice: `tests/test_logkinds.py::_branches` unwraps `kind_via` and reads literals directly, so a literal needs no `KNOWN_DYNAMIC` entry while a named constant would. The five entries the old cog had were deleted in the same commit, and the stale half of `test_every_dynamic_kind_is_enumerated` is what caught them. |
| `black_bloc/chat_panel.py:240` (`status_lines`) | ⚠️ **The signature is `(store, guild_id, …)`, not the design's `(bot, guild, actor)`.** Nothing in the lines depends on WHO is looking — the admin gate decides whether `spend` is passed at all, and the caller passes `hidden=True` instead — so taking an actor would be an argument the function never reads. The tiers arrive as a tuple because `tier_words` needs `bot.settings` and `tier_errors`, which is cog knowledge, not settings knowledge. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:893` (`chat_panel_command`) | Calls `require_staff` before anything else, which is what `settings_store.is_staff_command` reads out of the callback — `tests/test_bot.py::test_nothing_a_member_can_run_is_hidden_behind_the_lock` walks every locked command and would fail without it. `still_staff` is the runtime gate on every MOVE after that (P8); the `default_permissions` lock is only UX. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:273` (`panel_lines`) | ⚠️ **The status block is written out ALWAYS, never behind a `Status` button** — the events build's deviation 10 precedent. `last_ingest_error` is exactly the kind of warning a button loses: a daily read that has been failing for a week is invisible if nobody presses anything. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:250` (`spend_readable`) | `chat_status_admin_only` used to refuse the whole `/chat status` command. A panel cannot refuse itself — the same command carries Knowledge and Personality, which a non-admin staffer may use — so the key now hides the spend BLOCK and the embed says so in a sentence (P9). The key, its default and the site's copy of its help text were all reworded in the same commit; its *meaning* changed, and a help string that still said "keeps `/chat status` to administrators" would be a lie. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:229` (`ingest_health`) | The `_ingest` loop's `last_ok_at` / `last_error` live on the cog instance and the panel's builders are module-level, so the cog is asked for by name through `get_cog` and every miss degrades to "not yet" / "none" rather than raising. That is also what keeps the test fakes simple — the same shape `tempvoice.voice_health` uses. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:810` (`NoteFieldsModal`) | ONE modal class for add and edit (fork F-C2 (a)): passing a `row` prefills the three fields and sets `note_id`, and `on_submit` picks `add_note` or `edit_note` off that. Two classes would be two places to keep `TITLE_LIMIT` / `BODY_LIMIT` / `TAG_LIMIT` in step, and those limits are imported from `knowledge.py` rather than retyped (checklist 22). ⚠️ `BODY_LIMIT` is exactly 4000, which is also Discord's `TextInput` maximum, so a note body fits a modal field with nothing lost. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:840` (`LimitsModal`) | Five fields is Discord's maximum, so nothing else can ever join it — that is the ceiling fork F-C1 (a) was chosen against, not a preference. A modal has no `app_commands.Range`, so `read_limits` is the bound, and it names the key and the range in words. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:1033` (`on_message`) | The local `answer` was renamed `said`: the module now imports `panels.answer`, and a local of the same name would shadow it inside the one function on the file's hot path. Nothing else about the listener, the cooldown, the wave or the staff note changed — the 72 existing tests that exercise them stayed green unedited, which is the proof. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat.py:887` (`usable_db`) | Survives only for the `_ingest` loop and `seed_guilds`, which have no interaction to answer through. Everything at the interaction boundary uses `panels.db_up` (before a defer) and `panels.db_ready` (after one) instead — the library's, never a fourth local copy (checklist 15/17). |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/chat.py:259` (`answered`) | The one place a shared function's refusal becomes a `Refused`. The routes keep their own `_wanted_section` / `_staff_row_only` pre-checks in front of it on purpose: those produce the site's OWN 404/409 wording (`SERVER_ROW_LOCKED` says "cannot be changed by hand"; the shared refusal says "would be overwritten by tomorrow"), and changing either would have moved a status code or a message that `tests/api/tools/test_chat.py` pins. The shared guards behind them are what the Discord door hits. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/chat.py` — the five deleted `note()`s | ⚠️ **The log rows do not change**: `kind_via("chat.knowledge_added", VIA_WEBSITE)` is `"web.chat.knowledge_added"`, byte-identical to what `note()` wrote. What changes is that there is now exactly ONE writer. The `details` shape DOES change for those five rows (the shared function's `{"id", "title", "via"}` wins over the route's `{"title", "via"}` / `{"section_id", "changed", "via"}`) — a visible difference on the Logs page, and the point of the exercise. `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_a_route_never_notes_an_event_its_shared_path_already_logged` is the guard; it fails the build if this is half-done. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/chat.py` — the five moved strings | `NO_SUCH_TROPE`, `MODE_NEEDS_A_NAME`, `TROPE_IS_OFF`, `TROPE_IN_USE` and `LAST_TROPE_ON` moved to `chat_panel.py` and were DELETED here rather than imported back: the shared function returns the sentence, so a copy in the router would be a second home for the same refusal (checklist 15). The route's three `clean_*` wrappers went with them — `add_note` cleans inside and returns the refusal with a 400. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:chat_panel_minutes` | The ONE key this build adds, in its own block after the voice block so the parallel wave-3 branches merge textually. Help text carries the KI-20 warning in the shape the other seven use. ⚠️ **No `KEY_MIN`/`KEY_MAX`** — no `*_panel_minutes` key has one. ⚠️ **And no second edit anywhere:** `CHAT_KEYS` (`cogs/content/chat.py`) is `startswith("chat_")` over `KEY_TYPES`, so the key appears on the Settings card, in `/chat settings`'s successor and in the `Limits…` modal for free. A reader will otherwise go looking for the edit that is not there; `test_the_chat_panel_key_is_picked_up_by_the_prefix_scan_with_no_second_edit` measures it rather than trusting it. |
| `tests/test_bot.py:LOGS_GROUPS` | Lost its `"chat"` entry — there is no `Group` with a `logs` child to find any more — and the children assertion went with it. `"chat"` STAYS in `STAFF_COMMANDS`: the one command keeps `default_permissions=STAFF_ONLY`, because every one of the nine subcommands was `require_staff` and there is no member half to reveal. `assert len(top) == 38` is **unchanged and re-measured** — a group was already one top-level slot. |


# Raidtrain panel (wave 3) — `/raidtrain` is one command, three audiences

> Written on `worktree-agent-aba5d44f8e27a8e28` against `4bb059c` and carried into `main` at the
> merge `2dd2689` (v76, 2026-09-04 16:56; a clean merge, so the keys still hold).
> ⚠️ Trust the anchor text over the line number — the conductor re-keys after every merge. ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live Discord**: no boot, no
> panel opened, no hour claimed, no DM sent, and **no raid train has ever run** — `raidtrain_mode`
> is still `off` everywhere. The import check
> (`black_bloc.raidtrain`, `cogs.content.raidtrain`, `api.tools.raidtrain`, `personas`, `panels`)
> plus `import black_bloc.bot` is the substitute for a boot, and the new
> `raidtrain → panels → settings_store` edge is exactly what it is there to catch. It is clean.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py` — the `panels` import | ⚠️ **The pure module now imports the panel library**, which is new for it and is the reason `import black_bloc.bot` is in the proof list. It buys three things that would otherwise be copied: `option_label`'s 100-character clamp, `panel_minutes`, and `SELECT_OPTION_LIMIT`. The edge is one-way — `panels` knows nothing about raid trains — and `settings_store` does not import `raidtrain`, which is what keeps it acyclic. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:548` (`card_buttons`) | §C's card table AS DATA, so the parametrised test can assert every state renders its row and no other. It takes `held` as the POSITIONS a member holds rather than a count, because the one-slot label carries the number (`Give back slot #3`) and a count could not produce it. The `if/elif` on `len(mine)` is what makes *Give back #N* and *Give an hour back…* structurally unable to coexist — P3 as an `elif`, not as a convention. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:537` (`card_selects`) | Split from `card_buttons` because the two selects are not buttons and the parametrised test needs to assert on them separately. ⚠️ `TAKE_OFF_SELECT` is gated on `status in (OPEN, LOCKED)` as well as on there being a taken slot — the design's table said only the latter, but a cancelled train keeps its holders, so without the status gate an organizer would still be offered a move on a train that is over. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:493` (`may_claim`) | The four conditions §C's claim select renders on, in ONE function, so the control and `claim_slot`'s refusals cannot drift. `require_link=False` makes `linked` irrelevant rather than the other way round — that is the shape `raidtrain_require_link` off actually means. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:601` (`slot_label`) | ⚠️ **Plain `%H:%M UTC`, not `<t:…:t>`.** The design asked for a Discord timestamp in the option; Discord renders NO markdown inside a select option's label, so a timestamp there would print as literal `<t:1789…:t>`. The viewer's own clock is still honoured where it can be — the card embed is `render_lineup`, which is full of real timestamps. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:33` (`SLOT_COUNT_MAX`) | 24, and the fact §D rests on: it is BELOW Discord's 25, so a slot select can never cap and `capped_placeholder` is needed on the train selects only. `test_a_slot_select_can_never_cap_because_a_train_is_shorter_than_the_ceiling` measures it rather than trusting the comment. The 24 is a 2000-character message limit, not a taste, so it can move — and if it ever moves past 25 that test is what fails. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:96` (`CLAIM_HERE`) | ⚠️ **The one string in this build the whole room reads**, on the lineup post, which is edited in place forever. It used to say "Take an hour with `/raidtrain claim`". Anything that names a subcommand here is a message a member will type and be told does not exist. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:26` (`Outcome`) | Moved here from `chat_panel.py` rather than copied into `cogs/content/raidtrain.py`. Two frozen dataclasses of the same name and shape in two modules is checklist 15 on arrival; `chat_panel` re-exports it so nothing that imported `chat_panel.Outcome` moved. `refusal()` came with it for the same reason — it is the only constructor for the failure case, so a new refusal cannot forget its status code. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:400` (`redraw`) | The lineup post is COSMETICS and goes last in every shared function, after the write and after the log row (checklist 12). It reaches the cog through `get_cog` and degrades to a no-op when there is none, which is what lets the web tests use a fake cog and what stops a missing cog turning a committed claim into an exception. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:420` (`claim_slot`) | ⚠️ **The caller holds `_lock(train_id)`; this function does not take it.** The lock and `take_slot`'s `WHERE … user_id IS NULL` are together the race guard (checklist 6) — the lock serialises two clicks in one process, the WHERE clause is what makes a lost race a worded refusal instead of a silent overwrite. `run_move` is the panel's single place that takes the lock, so a new move cannot forget it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:506` (`assign_slot`) | Takes `named` as a keyword because the two doors know the person differently: Discord has a `Member` with `display_name`, the website has an id and `resolve_one`. The `MEMBER_NOT_LINKED` check moved INSIDE, so both doors refuse identically — it depends on a value chosen after the control renders, which is why it is a worded refusal and not a hidden button (P9). It ignores the per-member ceiling on purpose: an organizer outranks it. |

# Hide commands when off — a turned-off feature takes its `/command` away

> Written on `worktree-agent-a6975647f681f9de9` against its own tip `ec9215e` (branched from
> `main` `46fba16`, before that branch's later TODO commits). ⚠️ **Trust the anchor text over
> any line number** — the conductor re-keys after every merge, and this section was keyed before
> the merge existed. ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live Discord**: no boot, no guild sync, no
> command actually vanishing from anybody's client. `pytest` (4539) and `ruff check` are the
> whole of the verification.
>
> ⚠️ **This section SUPERSEDES every earlier claim in this file and in the design docs that a
> particular feature's command does NOT vanish when its mode is off.** Fourteen do now — every
> mode key with an `off` except `chat_memory_mode` (see its row below). Named,
> so a reader landing on one of them is not misled — all are stale as of 2026-09-04:
> the role-menus section's `command_visibility.py:HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` row (`rolemenu_mode`
> "deleted"); the applications row further up (`applications_mode` "NOT in this table any
> more"); the go-live row (`HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` "already silent about `golive_mode` and stays that
> way"); the birthdays row's aside; and in `info/`: `automod-panel-design.md` §I and §J
> ("`/automod` does not vanish when the mode is off"), `chat-panel-design.md` §I and §J (the
> same for `/chat`), `applications-panel-design.md` fork I2, `role-menus-panel-design.md`'s
> design B. ⚠️ The two that reverse a DATED OWNER ANSWER are `applications_mode` and
> `rolemenu_mode`; `chat_memory_mode` keeps its answer — see its row below, which is the
> one the conductor decided at the merge.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:17` `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` | Fourteen entries, one per mode key whose choices contain the literal `"off"` (all but `chat_memory_mode`), each mapped to its ONE top-level command. Sorted by KEY, not by command, because the key is what a reader arrives holding (they turned something off on the portal and want to know which command went). `modmail_mode` is absent because its choices are `channel`/`thread` — there is no off to read; `golive_end_mode`'s `off` is the END behaviour, not the feature, so it is absent too. The names were verified against the real tree, not guessed: `tests/test_command_visibility.py:real_tree` loads every cog in `COGS` and asserts the table's fourteen names are a subset of the 36 it finds. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:17` — `"off"` and not `"shadow"` | The comparison is `== OFF` on the literal string. A shadowed feature keeps its command on purpose: shadow means "log what you would do", which is only useful if somebody can still reach the thing. The owner's own posture is the worked example — `youtube_mode` is `shadow` today and `/youtube` stays; he sets it `off` on the portal and it goes. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:35` `NEVER_HIDDEN` | Grew from `("settings",)` to four. `settings` is the load-bearing one — it is the door back, and since 2026-09-05 what a Lead does when the feature's own command is gone is `/settings` ▸ **Turn a feature back on…** (it was `/settings set-value <feature>_mode on` until the panel retired that subcommand; the select is built from `hidden_names`, the same function `/help` asks, so it cannot list a feature that is not hidden or miss one that is). `help`, `about` and `ping` are belt-and-braces: nothing maps to them, but a later table edit that did would break the server's only self-explanation. The guard is applied TWICE (in `hidden_names` and again in `apply`), which is deliberate: `hidden_names` feeds `/help`, `apply` feeds the tree, and a name that slipped past one would be a silent divergence between what `/help` lists and what Discord shows. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:56` `hiding_is_on` | Reads `hide_commands_when_off` and is the single gate. It also absorbs the `guild_id is None` case that `hidden_names` used to own, so a DM (`/help` with no guild) and a switched-off server take the same path and neither can hide anything. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:62` `hidden_names` | Returns the empty set the moment the switch is false — before reading a single mode. That is what makes the switch cheap and total: `/help` and the tree sync both derive from this one function, so there is no second place the switch could be forgotten. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:174` `self.restored` | New. `self.removed` is a LIVE dict of what is hidden right now, so by the time the sync runs it can no longer say what came BACK during this debounce window — a command shown again is popped out of it. `restored` accumulates those names and is drained at `sync_now` (`:184`, the tuple swap), so one sync leaves one row naming both halves. `_hide` discards from it (`:118`) so a flip-flop inside one window nets out honestly rather than claiming a command was both hidden and shown. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:195` `_record` | Checklist 34 in miniature: **one sync, one `commands.visibility` row**, never one row per command. `details` is now `{"commands": N, "hidden": [...], "shown": [...]}` — the count alone could not answer "which one went?", which is the only question somebody reading this row has. `shown` is a parameter rather than another attribute read, because `sync_now` has already drained it by the time `_record` runs. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:233` `install` | Registers the same callback for the fourteen mode keys AND for `hide_commands_when_off`, so flipping the switch takes the identical debounced path a mode flip takes — 5 s debounce, ≤1 sync a minute. Without that line the switch would have been true-only-at-boot, which is exactly the class of bug the "configurable both ways" rule exists to catch. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:36` — the import | `from .settings_store import HIDE_COMMANDS_WHEN_OFF`. `settings_store` imports `automod`, `chat_memory`, `config`, `emoji`, `groq`, `logkinds`, `personas`, `polls` and `storage.db` and none of them reaches back here, so this is not a cycle. The key NAME lives with the registry (one fact, one home, checklist 15); `SWITCH_KEY` is a local alias so the reader of this module does not have to hold two names. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2253` `HIDE_COMMANDS_WHEN_OFF` | The decision as a key rather than a constant (checklist 33). `bool`, default `True` — the owner asked for the hiding, so the hiding is the default and the switch exists for the server that would rather see everything. `KEY_TYPES` gives the `/settings` panel a control for free through `settings_panel.control_for`, and the Settings page reads the same registry over `/api/settings`. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2809` — the help sentence | Says the three things a non-technical reader needs: what disappears, that it comes back within about a minute, and ⚠️ **that shadow is not off**. The last clause is the one that stops a support round-trip — "I set it to shadow and the command is still there" is the predictable question. `tests/test_settings_store.py` asserts the words `shadow does not` are in it, so a rewrite that drops the clause fails. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3250` — the default branch | Sits with the panel-minutes branches at the foot of `default()` rather than in its own block, because `default()` is one long if-chain and a new stanza there is a merge conflict waiting for the next parallel branch. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:60` `HIDDEN_NOTE` | ⚠️ **A person must never see a control silently missing with no explanation** (global rule). `/help` already filtered on `hidden_names`; what it did not do was say WHY the list is short. The note names the count and both doors back — the dashboard's Settings page and `/settings` ▸ **Turn a feature back on…** (rewritten 2026-09-05 with the subcommand it used to name; it is the sentence a locked-out owner reads, so it is the single most important string in the sweep). It is italic and leading-newline'd so it reads as a footer inside whatever chunk `pages_under_limit` puts it in. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:323` — why only on an unfiltered list | A filtered `/help` is already a short list on purpose; adding "3 commands are not listed" to `/help filter:ping` would be answering a question nobody asked and would be read as "your filter hid three things". The count is also the count of ALL hidden commands, not of hidden commands matching the filter, so on a filtered list it would be wrong as well as noisy. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:17` — `chat_memory_mode` is NOT in the table | ⚠️ **The one deliberate exception, kept at the merge (conductor, 2026-09-05).** The build put it in because the 2026-09-04 ask named every feature; the conductor took it back out because the owner answered this exact shape on 2026-09-03 (fork I-M1) with **"open it"**, and `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` KI-14 tolerates the third-person-note risk *because* `/memory` is "the enforcement of last resort" — the panel where a member reads and drops every note held about them. Turning `chat_memory_mode` off does NOT delete stored profiles, and the website is staff-only and counts-only, so with `/memory` hidden a member would have no door to their own data; `hide_commands_when_off` false and `/settings` are staff doors, not member ones. Pinned by `tests/cogs/content/test_chat_memory.py::test_memory_is_the_one_off_feature_whose_command_never_hides`. Putting it back is one line here plus that test. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:35` — `rolemenu_mode` and `applications_mode` | The other two carve-outs this build reverses, both for reasons the switch now answers. `rolemenu_mode` ships **off** and the role-menus build removed it so hiding `/rolemenu` would not hide the only way back — but `settings` is in `NEVER_HIDDEN`, so `/settings` ▸ **Turn a feature back on…** is that way back and it cannot be hidden. `applications_mode` (owner, 2026-09-03: "Visible") also ships off; the same door applies, and unlike `/memory` no member's own data is behind it. |
| `tests/test_command_visibility.py:96` (`real_tree`) | Loads all of `COGS` and returns the 36 top-level names. It is the only thing standing between the table and a typo — `voice` not `tempvoice`, `event` not `events`, `apply` not `applications` are all names where the key and the command deliberately differ, and a wrong one would fail silently (`_hide` returns False on a name that is not there, so nothing would ever be hidden and no test would notice). |
| `tests/test_command_visibility.py:361` (`test_every_hidden_feature_can_still_be_turned_back_on_from_discord`) | The owner-facing invariant as a test: every key in the table is in `VALUE_KEYS`, `parse_value(key, "on")` works, and `settings` is in `NEVER_HIDDEN`. This is the test that would fail if somebody ever put a feature in the table whose only way back was the command they just hid. |
| `tests/test_bot.py` — the 36 pin is UNCHANGED | Hiding happens at SYNC time against a guild-scoped copy of the tree, not in the global tree `test_the_command_tree_stays_inside_discords_limits` counts. `commands synced` in the live log will read lower than 36 whenever something is off; the pinned 36 is the tree the bot builds, which is a different number and stays right. |


# Honeypot panel (wave 3) — `/honeypot` is ONE command

> Written on `worktree-agent-a7ea6b0dbeac7f753`, off `932f34e`. ⚠️ **Every key below is a
> `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line number**, so this section survives a merge without re-keying;
> trust the anchor text. The `honeypot` and `exempt` Groups and all seven leaf subcommands
> (`logs`, `setup`, `status`, `mode`, `forget`, `exempt add|remove`) are gone; the top-level
> count is **36, unchanged, measured** through
> `tests/test_bot.py::test_the_command_tree_stays_inside_discords_limits`. ⚠️ **Nothing here has
> met live Discord** — no boot, no sync, no panel opened.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/honeypot.py` — the file itself | New. The feature had no pure module at all: every function lived in the cog. This holds only what a test can read without a bot — the move table, the mode labels, the trap options, the exempt prefill and the diff. Unlike `black_bloc/automod.py` it may import `panels` at MODULE level, because `settings_store.py` does not import it, so there is no loop to close (automod build deviation 4 is the counter-example — do not copy its function-local imports here). |
| `black_bloc/honeypot.py:173` (`exempt_editable`) | ⚠️ **A data-loss guard, not a nicety.** Discord caps a select at 25 options and requires `min_values ≤ len(default_values) ≤ max_values`; `honeypot_exempt_role_ids` is unbounded. Show 25 of 30 and the submit DELETES the other five silently — an access-reducing write nobody asked for, from a control that looked like it was showing the whole list. So above the cap the picker is not rendered at all and the embed says why. `panels.capped_placeholder` is the WRONG tool: it is for a picker whose unshown rows are merely unreachable, not for one whose submission IS the whole set. |
| `black_bloc/honeypot.py:178` (`exempt_diff`) | The picker sends the WHOLE list, so "what changed" has to be derived rather than read off an argument. The pair it returns is both the sentence the staffer sees and the `added`/`removed` the one log row carries — without it the log would say "the list is now these nine roles" and nobody could tell which one moved. Order-stable and de-duplicating, so a reorder is not a change. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:349` (`live_traps`) | ONE home for the fact that decides both whether **Setup…** renders and whether `make_trap_channel` refuses. `make_trap_channel` used to inline the comprehension; it now calls this, which is the only edit inside a function this build otherwise leaves alone. If the two ever disagree, the panel offers a button that is refused the moment it is pressed — exactly what P3 forbids. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:689` (`arming_refusal`) | The mode picker and `set_mode` read the SAME answer, so the control offered and the function's verdict cannot disagree. Unlike automod there is only ONE blocker here (no resolved staff role); honeypot has no `STAFF_IS_THE_TEST_CHANNEL` gate. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:714` (`set_exempt_roles`) | ⚠️ **One write of the whole list, one log row.** It replaces `_change_exempt`, which wrote one role at a time and had a "was already exempt, so nothing changed" branch — a branch the picker cannot reach, because the list it sends IS the new list. A submit that changes nothing writes nothing and logs nothing, and says so. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` — `honeypot.exempt_set` | New, and it could NOT reuse `honeypot.exempt`: that kind is taken by the LISTENER (`_caught`) for the row that proves a moderator was spared. Anyone who "tidies up" by merging the two destroys the only evidence that the exemption worked. `honeypot.exempt_add` and `honeypot.exempt_remove` had to leave `ROUTINE` in the same commit as their emission, or `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_no_classification_entry_is_dead` fails. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:787` (`status_lines`) | The panel embed and what `/honeypot status` printed are ONE list, never two shapes. It takes the totals rather than the database, so it stays synchronous and testable. The three lines the panel ADDS are the arming blocker, a recorded id Discord no longer has, and the test-mode containment — each of which a command could once explain in prose and a panel cannot. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:1137` (`NumbersModal`) | ⚠️ Both fields are parsed BEFORE either is written, and a refused value writes nothing at all — not even the box that parsed. The 0–7 ceiling is `HONEYPOT_PURGE_MAX_DAYS`, rebuilt in the field label because a modal has no `Range`; the registry's `KEY_MAX` is what actually enforces it, through `coerce_value` inside `save_settings`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:1087` (`ExemptPick`) — `min_values=0` | ⚠️ **Whether a real Discord client submits an EMPTY multi-select is unproven in this repo** — three shipped designs flag it and none needed the answer, because clearing was always its own control. Here it is load-bearing, so **Exempt nobody** (fork F-H1) is the fallback that works whatever the client does. Both doors call `set_exempt_roles(…, [])`; if the empty submit turns out to work, a later pass can drop one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:1103` (`ForgetPick`) | Fork F-H2. `honeypot_channel_ids` is a LIST, and the state that most needs forgetting (a recorded id Discord no longer has) is exactly the state where two ids can be recorded — the live check only refuses a second trap while the first is ALIVE, so a trap deleted while the bot was offline leaves its id behind and a new one is made beside it. One spelling in every state beats one button plus one card. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:MODE_IS_OFF_WAY_BACK` (through `settings_lines`) | `honeypot_mode` STAYS in `command_visibility.HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` — the opposite of `/rolemenu` and `/raidtrain`, and for a measured reason: those ship with their mode `off`, so hiding the command would hide the only door back on the day it lands, whereas `honeypot_mode` defaults to **shadow**, so `off` is a deliberate "I do not want this" choice. The trade-off is said out loud on the Settings card rather than discovered: with the command hidden the mode picker is unreachable, and the ways back are `/settings` ▸ **A setting group…** ▸ honeypot ▸ `honeypot_mode` and the portal. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/honeypot.py` — what did NOT move | The listener (`on_message`, `_caught`, `_delete`, `_offer_ban`, `_lock`, `on_guild_channel_delete`), the ban path (`do_ban`, `_dm_before_ban`, `ban_hit`), the hit-recording half (`record_hit` … `hit_counts`) and `BanNowButton` are untouched, and their log kinds are untouched. `api/tools/honeypot.py` imports `ban_hit`, `make_trap_channel` and `recent_hits` **by name from the cog** and none of the three moved, which is why `tests/api/tools/test_honeypot.py` stays green with **no edit** — that unchanged file is the proof the refactor changed nothing. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:1206` (`LOG_LEVEL_COMMANDS`) — the `honeypot` row is gone | `log_level_help` renders *"and in `/honeypot logs`"*, and there is no such command any more. With no entry the help simply says the lines are kept on the dashboard, which is true. ⚠️ **Ten of the remaining rows still name a retired subcommand** (`pings`→`pingroles`, `tempvoice`→`voice`, `events`→`event`, `poll`, `birthday`, `golive`, `request`, `applications`, `rolemenu`, `chat`); only `mod` and `modmail` are correct. That wants one pass of its own. |

> (`932f34e` + this build's five commits); carried in at the merge onto `main` after the honeypot

> sibling wave-4 build was running beside this one and both touch `settings_store.py`,
> `logkinds.py` and `tests/test_bot.py`.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|

| `black_bloc/modmail.py:784` (`capped_lines`) | One function behind `blocked_lines` and `snippet_lines`. The cap is 25 to match the select beside it, and the overflow line names the **Modmail page**, not the Moderation page the design said — `blocksCard` and `snippetsCard` both live on `site/public/assets/page-modmail.js`, so the Moderation page would have sent the reader to the wrong tab. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1728` (`block_member`) (and `unblock_member`, `put_snippet`, `drop_snippet`, `point_at`, `forget_place`, `set_mode`, `set_enabled`) | One function per move, each doing ONE write and ONE `log_action` with `kind_via(...)`, each returning a `panels.Outcome` so the words are decided once and both doors read them. | `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1728` (`block_member`) — why the routes ignore its refusal | The Discord panel prints `ALREADY_BLOCKED` / `NOT_BLOCKED`; `POST /api/modmail/blocks` and `DELETE /api/modmail/blocks/{id}` deliberately do NOT raise on it and still answer `{"blocked": true}` / `{"unblocked": true}`. That keeps the routes' status codes byte-identical to what they were, which is what makes "the route tests are unchanged" the proof that no route moved. The visible difference is the log: a no-op now leaves no row, which is correct — nothing happened. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1768` (`put_snippet`) — the route now validates the NAME | `POST /api/modmail/snippets` previously accepted any non-empty name. # Mod cases panel (wave 4) (2026-09-05)

> Written on `worktree-agent-ab5740f777a3dfd80` (keyed at `9d23dbb`) and merged onto `main` 2026-09-05
> after the honeypot and modmail A panels. Every key below is a `path:name` anchor rather than a line
> number, so the standing merge-order re-key is this paragraph and nothing else.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:11` (`SCHEMA_VERSION`) — 28 → 29 | Six nullable columns on `mod_cases`: `note`, `note_by`, `note_at`, `voided_at`, `voided_by`, `void_reason`. They go in TWO places — the `CREATE TABLE` so a fresh database has them, and `ADDED_COLUMNS` so an existing one gets them from `_add_missing_columns` — and both are required. ⚠️ **No table rebuild**, unlike `_set_aside_mod_cases_with_a_required_user`: every column is nullable with no default, so `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` is enough. No new index either — `voided_at` is read per row on a page of ten and never filtered on. The safe direction is old-database + new-code, because `connect()` runs the ALTERs before the bot logs in; a **rollback** is also fine, because `SELECT *` returns the extra columns and `row_value` tolerates whatever it finds. ⚠️ **Rollback was NOT exercised**; the forward migration was, against a database built by the code at `97531cc`. |
| `black_bloc/modcases.py:413` (`warn_count`) — `AND voided_at IS NULL` | Owner fork **F-M2 = (a)**. This is the one place a void changes a number something else reads: `warn_member` compares this count to `automod_warn_threshold` and says so in the reply and in `mod.warn_threshold`. A voided warn is a warn staff have said was wrong, so counting it toward "this member is at three strikes" would make the void a lie. The cost is that the clause sits inside a function the automod path reads, which is why it has a test of its own asserting the count before the void, after it and after a restore. |
| `black_bloc/modcases.py:484` (`case_line`) — the strike-through | `~~…~~` around the WHOLE line, so a voided case reads as voided at a glance without leaving the list (owner fork **F-M1 = (a)**: an audit that hides its own erasures is not an audit). The live line is byte-identical to what `/cases` printed, which is what lets one test prove nothing else moved. |
| `black_bloc/modcases.py:168` (`case_embed`) — `note=` and `voided=` are keyword-only with defaults | So **every existing call site is byte-identical** — the modlog post, `record_case`, `rewrite_card` and the automod verdict all still read exactly as they did. A voided card also drops to `COLOURS["purge"]`, the grey already in the palette, so it reads as voided in the modlog too. |
| `black_bloc/modcases.py:226` (`voided_field`) | The `Voided` field names who, when and why, and then says in a sentence that cancelling undoes nothing. ⚠️ **That sentence is not decoration.** A voided ban is still a ban and a voided timeout is still running; `/untimeout` and `/unban` are what lift them. AND voided_at IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` — returning `True` only for the caller that won (checklist 6). This is `claim_case` read across a different column. | `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modcmds.py:922` (`build_root`) | The list goes through `panels.clamped` (`DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` 4000) as an embed description, not through `pages_under_limit`'s chain of 1900-character messages — the pager is what reaches row 11 now. ⚠️ **`pages_under_limit` STAYS in `modcases.py`**: `cogs/core.py` imports it for `/help` — and did for `/settings show` until that command retired (retired 2026-09-05). `_say_in_chunks` went with `/cases`. |

Discord does not render markdown in a select option label, so `case_line`'s backticks and bold would be shown literally; `panels.option_label` builds `#12 · warn · the reason as far as it fits`, plain text, clamped to 100. The 120-character `LINE_REASON_LIMIT` cut belongs to the embed line and stays there. Page size is `CASES_PER_PAGE` 10, well under Discord's 25-option cap, so `capped_placeholder` is not needed here. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/mod.py:257` (`_correct`) | One door for the four corrections: `writer`, `require_guild`, `require_db`, `actor_for`, the shared function with `via=VIA_WEBSITE`, and the outcome's own status/code/sentence on a refusal. ⚠️ **Not one of them calls `note()`** — the shared function logs — and `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_a_route_never_notes_an_event_its_shared_path_already_logged` is what proves it stays that way. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/mod.py:NO_SUCH_CASE` — imported, not defined | Checklist 15. The sentence was defined FOUR times with three different wordings, two of which named `/cases`. One home is `modcases.py`; the cog and the route import it. `cogs/moderation/automod.py`'s copy was a different sentence about a missing automod VERDICT, so it was renamed `NO_SUCH_VERDICT` and kept rather than merged — the name was the only thing making it look like a duplicate. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:1206` (`LOG_LEVEL_COMMANDS`) | ⚠️ **The `"mod"` row was REMOVED, not re-pointed** — `log_level_help` renders *"and in `/mod logs`"* and there is no `/mod logs` after this build; with no row the help says the lines are kept on the dashboard, which is true. This follows automod's deviation 9, which removed `"automod"` the same way. ⚠️ **REPORTED, NOT FIXED: the rest of the map is still stale** — `"pings": "pingroles"` names a command wave 2 retired, and `tempvoice`, `events`, `poll`, `birthday`, `golive`, `request` and `applications` all now name panels rather than `logs` subcommands. It wants one pass of its own. ⚠️ The mock's own copy (`site/mock/server.mjs:LOG_LEVEL_FEATURES`) had the same `mod` row and was nulled to match; **its `automod` row is still stale** and was left, being outside this build. |
| `black_bloc/api/settings_api.py:NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE` — `mod_panel_minutes` | Without the override the key's `mod_` head would open a namespace of its own on the settings API, and `tests/api/test_contract.py::test_the_moderation_settings_all_live_in_the_automod_namespace` fails by design — moderation's keys belong with automod's, the way `modlog_channel_id`, `mod_dm_on_action` and `mod_log_level` already do. The mock carries the same row. |
| `site/public/assets/page-moderation.js:editors` · `voidControls` | Inline boxes holding what is there now with one Save button each, rather than a browser `prompt()` — nothing else on the dashboard prompts, and `actionBar` on the same page is the shape this copies. Void keeps the existing `ask()` confirm and spells out in it that voiding undoes no punishment; Restore is one press, being the access-REDUCING half of the pair. |

| REPORTED, NOT FIXED — four | (1) `mod.purged` and `mod.purge_failed` are the last two mod kinds built WITHOUT `kind_via`; harmless today because `/purge` has no web door, and a `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` candidate.
