# Modmail panel (wave 4, Build B) — the sticky card, the relay gate and the practice ticket

> Written on `worktree-agent-a4bebd98196e3ca14`, 2026-09-05. ⚠️ **NOT merged and NOT deployed.**
> Every key here is a `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line number, so the standing merge-order re-key
> is the paragraph under this heading and nothing else. Design:
> [`modmail-panel-design.md`](modmail-panel-design.md) §§C–H, forks F-M1 and F-M3–F-M8 (all (a)).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:914` (`ADDED_COLUMNS`) — `modmail_tickets.card_message_id`, `.practice` | ⚠️ **Schema 29 → 30, and the migration was RUN, not reasoned about**: `main`'s own `db.py` built a schema-29 file, a ticket row was written into it, and this branch's `connect()` was then pointed at that file — both columns present afterwards, `schema_meta` reads `30`, the pre-existing row reads `card_message_id` NULL and `practice` 0. ⚠️ **`PRAGMA user_version` is 0 and always has been**: this project keeps its version in the `schema_meta` TABLE, not in the pragma, so a recovery runbook must read `schema_meta`. Without `card_message_id` the card cannot survive a restart — the next member message would post a second card and the first would never be deleted. `practice` is a flag on the ROW, not a convention about the channel name, because `send_reply` and `close_ticket` must both be able to ask "is this real?" without looking at Discord. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1036` (`bump_card`) | ⚠️ **Hooked to the WRITERS, never to `on_message`.** Posting the card is itself a message; a listener trigger would have to exclude the bot, which would also exclude the reply echo, and "ignore the card but not the echo" is one refactor away from an infinite loop. The four writers are `_relay_inbound`, `send_reply`, `add_note` and `on_member_remove`'s note — which covers the website too, because `send_reply` is what the route calls. It is module-level and takes `bot`, for exactly that reason. ⚠️ A bump that arrives while the card is mid-post does not return early: it sets the ticket's `dirty` flag and `_card_later` re-loops until a refresh ends clean (`ca67bb5`, the review's one defect — the old code dropped that write, so the card was not last). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1017` (`card_clock`) · `card_wait` | The debounce state is a dict on the **bot**, not on the cog, for the same reason `user_lock` is (a cog is reloadable; the tickets are not). `CARD_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS = 2.0` coalesces a burst of DMs into ONE delete+post; `CARD_MIN_GAP_SECONDS = 8.0` is the floor between two card posts in one ticket. ⚠️ **Neither number has ever been measured against a real Discord channel** — they are reasoned from the documented per-channel bucket (~5 sends per 5 s) and should be treated as a first guess. They are mechanism constants, not settings keys, on the `command_visibility.DEBOUNCE_SECONDS` precedent: checklist 33 is about decisions, and a rate-limit floor is arithmetic. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1100` (`refresh_card`) takes the ticket's `user_lock` | **Found by a test, not by reading.** The debounced task and the reconciler can both reach `refresh_card` for one ticket; without the lock they interleave — both read `card_message_id` as NULL, both post, and the first card is orphaned with nothing able to delete it. The lock is the ticket's own `user_lock`, which `close_ticket` already holds, so a card refresh that arrives during a close simply waits and then sees `status != open` and returns. `bump_card` only SCHEDULES, so nothing deadlocks. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1126` (`post_card`) — write the new id BEFORE deleting the old | Checklist 12. If the delete fails the ticket has two cards: ugly, and **both work**, because both carry the same ticket id in their `custom_id`. If the order were reversed and the WRITE failed, the ticket would have an orphan card nothing can ever delete. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1155` (`drop_old_card`) | **Deleting a MESSAGE is a side effect `guard.py` cannot see.** The guard patches `http.send_message`, `http.edit_message` and `http.delete_channel` — **not** `delete_message`. So this asks `guard.allows_channel` by hand and logs `modmail.would_replace_card` when refused (checklist 1), which is a DIFFERENT kind from `modmail.card_failed` (checklist 2 — a dry run and a failure never share a kind). A `NotFound` is success, not a failure: somebody deleted the card by hand and the reconciler will notice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1179` (`card_is_there`) · `Modmail._recard` | The reconciler's third job, beside the two it had: an open ticket whose `card_message_id` is null, or whose card message has gone, gets one. It runs at `cog_load`, at `on_ready` and on the five-minute loop — all three already existed. This is what makes "exactly one card, always last" survive a restart, a deploy and a staffer deleting the card by hand. A `fetch_message` that fails for any reason OTHER than `NotFound` is read as *still there*, so a transient API error never posts a duplicate. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:4769` (`TicketCardButton`) | A persistent `DynamicItem`, not a timed `View` — program §7 and P14: a post that belongs to the ROOM survives restarts, and a ticket outlives the process by design. ⚠️ **The `ui/view.py` timeout gotcha therefore does not apply to the card**: a dynamic item has no per-message view instance and no timeout, so nothing can fire late; what replaces the card is deleting its message. The `/modmail` panel is the opposite case and every re-render still calls `retire`. The template is built from `CARD_MOVES`, so an unknown action cannot match and `from_custom_id` cannot `KeyError`. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:4750` (`card_pressed`) re-asks `still_staff` | A `DynamicItem` in a ticket channel is reachable by anyone who can see the channel, and a ticket channel's overwrites grant `view_channel` to every staff ROLE — so the check is not theoretical the moment a role is demoted. `require_staff` is **not** reused here: it calls `interaction.response.send_message` directly and only works before a defer (the requests-panel F3 finding). Every card move opens a modal, so nothing is deferred at the button; the modal's `on_submit` defers first (checklist 24 — `send_reply` DMs and `close_ticket` uploads a file). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1211` (`add_note`) — `echo` is why it is ONE function | `/note` (retired) posted a `Private note` embed into the ticket; the `=` prefix branch did not, because the staffer's own message is already sitting there. Merging them without a flag would double-post every `=` note. `echo=False` is the typed branch, `echo=True` the card and the old command. ⚠️ The `=` branch now writes a `modmail.note` row where it wrote **none at all** before, which is the point: the same act, one kind, from both doors. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1712` (`reply_body`) | Extracted from `Modmail._body` so the card's modal builds the body `/reply text: snippet:` builds — the snippet's content, then a blank line, then the typed text. F-M7 (a) is *combine*, not *pre-fill*: a modal is submitted once and Discord cannot re-render it mid-edit, so the select's value is only known at submit. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:4227` (`snippet_picker`) | `vote_picker`'s rule (`polls.py`), not a second one: a `RadioGroup` while the set is small, a `Select` above ten. `required=False` on both, so "no snippet, just my words" is a valid submission. ⚠️ A `RadioGroup` answers with `.value` and a `Select` with `.values`, which is what `modmail.picked_values` exists to hide. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/modmail.py:picked_values` is a SECOND COPY of `polls.py:picked_values` | Deliberate, and it should not stay that way. It is a four-line adapter over discord.py's two spellings of "what did they pick", and the two homes are `cogs/community/polls.py` and `black_bloc/modmail.py`. It was not hoisted into `panels.py` because the design's §J says nothing is added to `panels.py` in this build and `tests/test_panels.py` stays unchanged; importing a community cog from a moderation cog would have been the first cross-cog import in the tree. **The right fix is one `panels.picked_values` with a test, in a follow-up.** |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:983` (`ticket_dm`) | ⚠️ **One place suppresses the DM for a practice ticket, not four call sites** (the design's expected deviation 4). It returns `None` for practice — meaning *delivered* — so `send_reply` logs no `modmail.dm_failed` and marks nothing undelivered. **A suppressed DM is not a failed one** (checklist 2), and claiming a delivery that was skipped would be checklist 10 in reverse. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1604` (`open_practice`) | ⚠️ **Creating a thread is invisible to the guard** (it patches sends, edits and channel deletes), so `practice_parent` asks `guard.allows_channel` on the parent explicitly before anything is made — checklist 1. There is no `would_open_practice` shadow kind because there is no shadow mode here: either the test channel resolves and the thread is made, or `NO_TEST_CHANNEL` is the refusal in words. The partial unique index `modmail_open_ticket` means a staffer with a real open ticket cannot also have a practice one; that is a correct constraint, so the button says so in words rather than raising `IntegrityError`. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1604` (`open_practice`) claims the thread; REAL tickets are not claimed | Fork **F-M6 = (a)**. `guard.own_channel(thread)` is what makes the card actually stick where the owner can watch it — without it `speak` redirects the card into the test channel and "watch the card move to the bottom" is unobservable. It is the narrowest possible widening: one thread, made by the bot, under the test channel, claimed for the life of the practice and disowned in `close_ticket`. **Widening where the bot may speak is access-INCREASING and is not made as a side effect of a practice button**, so a real ticket keeps today's redirect and every existing test-policy test stays green, unchanged in assertion. |
| ⚠️ The consequence, which will look like a bug | In the PRACTICE thread the sticky card behaves as it will in production. In a REAL ticket under `TEST_MODE` the card appears in `#blackbloc-logs` instead, because `speak` redirects every guarded send. That difference is the practice ticket's entire justification and the sweep row says so. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1573` (`disown_place`) | Called from `close_ticket` only when the row is practice, and AFTER `remove_place` — the archive-and-lock edit still needs the channel to be allowed, so disowning first would refuse it. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py:927` (`relays_typing`) — the gate, not a relay | ⚠️ **`modmail_reply_style` does not BUILD a relay; it gates the one that has always existed.** `Modmail._staff_message` already relayed a plain staff message and already recorded a `=` line as a note — the incumbent ModMail bot's behaviour, kept because staff muscle memory is the whole reason not to invent a new prefix. `typing` and `both` are today's behaviour to the byte; `buttons` is the new thing and it turns the relay OFF. Any build that writes a second relay path has duplicated `_staff_message`. The gate sits AFTER the note branch, so `=note` works in all three styles. |
| ⚠️ `buttons` needs no confirmation | It is an access-REDUCING posture and fails safe: with it on, a staff message that would have reached a member does not. The reverse — a guild on `buttons` flipping to `typing` or `both` — is the one worth a sentence, and `reply_style_sentence` writes it: *"from now on, anything staff type in a ticket goes to the member."* |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:1856` (`MODMAIL_REPLY_STYLES`) lives in `settings_store`, not `modmail.py` | The design put it in `black_bloc/modmail.py`. It cannot go there: `settings_store` owns `KEY_CHOICES` and `modmail.py` already imports `settings_store` (`CHANNEL_MODE`, `THREAD_MODE`), so the other direction is an import cycle. Same precedent as `MODMAIL_MODES`. `relays_typing` and `reply_style_sentence` — the behaviour — stay in `modmail.py`. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py:593` (`REPLY_STYLE_MOVE`) is on row 2 | The design's `Setup…` table lists it beside the other four pickers on row 1; that row was already at Discord's five (category, staff channel, transcripts, mode, Answer DMs). Expected deviation 1 — the card's rows are Discord's rows, not the document's groupings. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py:696` (`root_buttons`) — `Try a fake ticket` and the confirm | Row 1 with the practice button is `Setup… · Blocked… · Snippets… · Forget… · Try a fake ticket` = exactly five, which a parametrised test asserts. The confirm REPLACES the whole row set with `Yes, open one · No`, on the `snippet_buttons(confirming=True)` precedent, rather than adding a sixth control. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:933` (`speak`) gained a `view` kwarg | The only caller that passes one is `post_card`. The design's own §D pseudocode calls `speak(..., view=card_view(fresh))`, so this is required by it rather than a departure from it; nothing else about `speak` moved, and the guard is still asked exactly once, in the same place. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/modmail.py:98` (`ticket_row`) — `practice` | The dashboard's ticket LIST excludes practice rows (`tickets_by_status(..., practice=False)`), and every ticket row carries the flag so the one place a practice ticket is still visible — reading it by number — can say what it is. No route was added or removed: `check.mjs` reads 17 pages / 146 routes before and after. |
| ⚠️ `close_ticket` — the card delete is the ONLY thing added, and it is first | The order inside `close_ticket` is a documented contract (see the Phase 7 note above) and nothing in it moved. `drop_card` runs before `post_transcript` so the transcript carries ONE card, not two — and `remove_place` deletes the whole channel afterwards in channel mode, which makes the delete a no-op there and load-bearing in **thread** mode, where the place is archived and locked rather than deleted. |


# Settings panel (wave 4, Build 1) — the pure half, the writers and the two keys

> Written on `worktree-agent-a3e6ccbead5a90537`, 2026-09-05. ⚠️ **NOT merged and NOT deployed.**
> Every key here is a `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line number, so the standing merge-order re-key
> is the paragraph under this heading and nothing else. Design:
> [`settings-panel-design.md`](settings-panel-design.md) §§B–G, forks F-S1–F-S5 (all (a)).
> ⚠️ **Build 1 retires nothing.** `/settings show|set|set-role|set-value|clear` and `/presence
> apply` all still exist and still work; the top-level count is **30, unchanged and measured**.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2763` (`namespace_of`) · `CORE_KEYS` · `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE` | **Moved out of `api/settings_api.py`, and the move is not optional.** A pure module in the bot's import graph must not import from `api/`, which would drag FastAPI into every `import black_bloc.cogs.core`. The move keeps ONE grouping for the dashboard and the panel and adds no dependency in either direction. `settings_api` re-exports both names with the redundant-alias spelling (`from ..settings_store import CORE_KEYS as CORE_KEYS`) so ruff reads them as deliberate re-exports rather than dead imports, and `tests/api/test_settings_api.py` stayed **byte-identical and green** — that is the proof the move changed nothing. In the same pass `settings_api`'s own `CORE = "core"` was deleted and `logkinds.CORE` imported instead: two spellings of one string in two modules is checklist 15. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2112` (`SETTINGS_PANEL_MINUTES`) · `SETTINGS_CORE_KEYS_ADMIN_ONLY` are in `CORE_KEYS` | Without that they file under a **`settings` namespace of their own** — a 23rd group nobody asked for, because `namespace_of` takes the prefix before the first underscore. `tests/test_settings_store.py:test_both_new_settings_keys_file_under_core_not_a_group_of_their_own` pins the count at **22**, which is what keeps the panel's group select under Discord's 25-option cap with no `capped_placeholder`. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3749` (`is_stored`) | ⚠️ **New, and the panel cannot render correctly without it.** `Put the default back` is drawn only when `store.clear` would return `True`, and until now there was no way to ASK that without doing it — `get()` answers with the default when no row exists, so a row stored at its own default value is invisible to a value comparison. It reads `_cache` and raises the same `SettingError` an unknown key raises everywhere else. It is a read; nothing inside `set` / `clear` / `default` / `coerce_value` moved. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:83` (`set_key`) takes NO `via`, deliberately | Checklist 34 asks a web route calling a shared path to pass `via=VIA_WEBSITE`. Measured: the settings route does **not** call any shared function — it calls `store.set` directly and `note("web.settings.set")` itself. One write, one row, on each door independently. A `via` nobody passes is dead weight (automod deviation 2's lesson). ⚠️ Wiring `PUT /api/settings/{key}` through `set_key` IS the right next pass and is what closes **KI-21**; it is a settings-API change with its own test surface, and doing it here would double-log unless the route's `note()` went in the same commit. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:83` (`set_key`) — `details` is now `{key, value, via}` for every type | The three bare copies it replaces wrote three different shapes: `{key, channel_id}`, `{key, role_id}` and `{key, value}`. Measured before unifying — **nothing reads `channel_id` or `role_id` out of a `settings.set` row**: `api/settings_api.py:via_by_key` reads `details["key"]` only, and the Logs page renders the details blob whole. The unified shape is what lets ONE function serve all eleven control types. The `target=channel` argument the old `/settings set` passed is gone with it; the channel is in `value`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:101` (`clear_key`) returns an `Outcome`, not a bare `bool` | The design's §F table says `cleared: bool`. An Outcome carries the same fact in `.value` **and** gives the refusal a shape and words — an unknown key and a key with nothing stored are different answers, and a bare bool can say neither. Both writers then have one shape, which is what the panel's single answer path needs. `NOT_SET`'s wording survives as the 409: the button is not drawn in that state, but two panels open on one key is a real race and a bare success would be checklist 10 in reverse. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/presence.py:35` (`reapply_presence`) resolves the cog itself | It needs `Presence.apply_status`, so it asks `bot.get_cog("Presence")` and returns **`None`** when that is `None` — meaning *not running*, which the panel answers with `settings_panel.PRESENCE_NOT_RUNNING` (S8). Putting the lookup inside is what keeps ONE implementation: `presence_apply` now calls it too, so the command and the future button cannot drift. ⚠️ `tests/cogs/test_presence.py:FakeBot` gained a `get_cog`, and the `cog` fixture registers itself on the bot — **no assertion changed**, which is the proof the loop, the listeners and `loop_health` did not move. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:129` (`FEATURE_MODES`) is DERIVED from `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` | Plus exactly two hand-added rows (`chat_memory_mode` → `/memory`, `modmail_enabled` → `/modmail`), which are deliberately absent from that table. A second hand-maintained "which features have a mode" list is how the root's mode block and the hide table would silently disagree. Sixteen rows, measured. `modmail_enabled` is a **bool**, so its row carries a `words` pair and renders as *answering DMs* / *not answering DMs* — never as `True`, and never as `on`/`off`. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:47` (`CONTROLS`) · `control_for` | The §C type→control table AS DATA, so the eleven registry types resolve to ten controls and one absence. A parametrised test walks **every** registry key and fails if a key's type is not in the table — which is the guard that catches a new registry TYPE arriving with no editor, not merely a new key. `automod_rules` is the only key with no control, and that is asserted as an equality, not an inclusion. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:492` (`list_is_too_long`) | S7. Discord requires `min_values ≤ len(default_values) ≤ max_values`, so a `channels`/`roles` key holding more than 25 ids cannot be put in a picker at all — and a **capped** picker would silently drop the ids it could not show on the next submit. So the picker is not drawn, the card says so and names the site, and `Clear the list` stays (checklist 26: a list-typed key always keeps a way to empty it). `enums` is excluded from the too-long test on purpose — its ceiling is `KEY_CHOICES`, and the registry's only one has eight. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:520` (`needs_confirm`) · `confirm_lines` | Fork **F-S2 (a)**, and the measurement behind it: `staff_channel_id`'s default is `settings.test_channel_id` on **every** guild in every mode, not only under `TEST_MODE`. One press of *Put the default back* therefore re-points the staff channel at the test channel, changing who counts as staff and disarming automod's and the honeypot's arming gates, silently. Only that key confirms; every other reset stays one press, because a speed bump in front of undoing a mistake is a speed bump in front of the fix. The confirm UI is Build 2's; this is the data it renders. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:456` (`hidden_line`) | ⚠️ Three states that read alike and are not: **nothing hidden** (`HIDDEN_NONE`), **something hidden** (`HIDDEN_SOME`, S4) and **hiding switched off altogether** (`HIDING_OFF`, S6). `hidden_names` returns an empty set in the last case whatever the modes say, so a panel that only checked emptiness would tell a Lead "every command is showing" while `hide_commands_when_off` was false and features were off — true by accident, and read as a bug the moment he checks. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:536` (`back_on_options`) | `command_visibility.hidden_names` is the ONE source, so the select cannot list a feature that is not hidden or miss one that is — it asks the same function `/help` asks. It writes **`on`, never `shadow`** (`BACK_ON_VALUE`): `shadow` does not hide a command, so picking it would leave the feature exactly as unreachable as before and read as a no-op. At most 14 features can be hidden, so the select can never hit the 25-option cap. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:313` (`BACK_MOVE`) is ONE move reused with `_replace(row=…)` | Every sub-panel's Back is the same action; six separate `BACK_*` constants would make `PANEL_MOVES` carry six rows with one action and break the distinctness test that exists to catch a genuine collision. The key card's Back keeps the same action and only changes its label (`KEY_BACK_LABEL`). |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:599` (`root_buttons`) — row 2 is exactly five | `Roles & channels… · How Black Bloc looks… · Panels & commands… · Logs · Open on the site` is Discord's per-row cap, hit exactly. A test asserts it. Anything Build 2 wants to add goes on row 3, beside `Log levels…` and `Refresh`. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:582` (`toggle_label`) | P3 — ONE button that says what it will DO. The two keys with written pairs (`hide_commands_when_off`, `operator_read_log`) read as sentences; every other `bool` in the registry falls back to *Turn `<key>` on/off*, so a key card for any of the 34 bools can be drawn without a table entry. Labels carry no markdown, because a Discord button label renders none. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:424` (`editable_options`) | The `Find a setting…` filter is `value_keys`' substring match, kept: `needle in key`, on the key name only. `chat` at 28 keys is the only namespace over 25 — measured — so `capped_placeholder` fires exactly once in the whole app, and the filter is what reaches the other three. The cap boundary is tested at 24 / 25 / 26 by patching `keys_in`, so the test does not go stale the day a namespace grows. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:452` (`stored_count`) | Counts keys whose value differs from `default()` — the sentence is *"set away from Black Bloc's own default"*, which is what a Lead wants to know. ⚠️ It is deliberately NOT `is_stored`: a row written at the default value is stored but not *away from* the default, and saying "1 setting is different" about a setting that is identical would be a worse lie than under-counting. `is_stored` answers the other question, and the reset button uses that one. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py` imports `panels`, and `settings_store` must not | Automod deviation 4 measured it: `panels` imports `DB_UNAVAILABLE` from `settings_store`, so a module-level import the other way closes the loop and every `import black_bloc.settings_store` dies. `settings_panel` is a leaf and may import `panels`, `command_visibility` and `logkinds` freely; the `namespace_of` move went into `settings_store` precisely because it needs none of them. |

# Settings panel (wave 4, Build 2) — the panel itself, and the last Group in the estate

> Written on `worktree-agent-a56c7b5137d9a609d`, 2026-09-05, on top of Build 1's merge
> (`main` at `57a878d`). ⚠️ **NOT merged and NOT deployed.** Every key here is a `path:name`
> ANCHOR, never a line number, so the standing merge-order re-key is the paragraph under this
> heading and nothing else. Design:
> [`settings-panel-design.md`](settings-panel-design.md) §§B–H, forks F-S1–F-S5 (all (a)).
> ⚠️ **This build retires things.** `/settings show|set|set-role|set-value|clear` and the whole
> `presence` Group are gone; `/settings` is ONE `app_commands.command` that opens a panel, and
> the top-level count is **30 → 29 with ZERO `app_commands.Group`s left in the tree** —
> measured through `tests/test_bot.py::test_the_command_tree_stays_inside_discords_limits`,
> which now asserts both numbers.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:357` (`settings`) — a Group's slot and a command's slot are the same slot | Retiring the `settings` Group and adding the `/settings` command could not be two commits: a tree cannot hold both under one name, so they are one atomic change and the count does not move (30 → 30) until `/presence` goes in the next. That is why the brief's suggested layer 1 ("the panel, subcommands still present") is not what landed — it is not expressible. `default_permissions` moves from the Group's keyword to the `@app_commands.default_permissions(STAFF_ONLY)` decorator, which is what `tests/test_bot.py` compares against `STAFF_ONLY`, and `require_staff` stays in the callback body because `is_staff_command` reads the body's `co_names`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:467` (`SettingsPanel`) — `back` and `rerender` on the VIEW | Every card is a fresh view, so the two questions "where does **Back** go?" and "what do I draw again after a write?" have to travel with it. Each builder sets them (`view.back = render_group(group=…)`, `view.rerender = render_key(key=…)`) with `functools.partial`, so `MoveButton` needs no table of destinations and `BACK_MOVE` stays ONE move with one action — which is what Build 1's `PANEL_MOVES` distinctness test exists to protect. A control that writes calls `view.rerender`; a control that navigates calls a named render. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`opened`, imported) | ⚠️ **The cog-local copy was deleted by the confirm/opened fold, 2026-09-05 — `opened` comes from `panels` now.** `still_staff` → `defer` → `db_ready`, in that order, before **every** move including the reads (P8, pings deviation 10 — a demoted staffer browsing the registry is the same defect one step earlier). The gate is first because `still_staff` answers with `response.send_message` and cannot respond to an already-deferred interaction. ⚠️ **This is what closes design §J defect 5**: none of the five retired subcommands ever checked the database — `show` answered off `store._cache` while the db was down and the three writers called `db.conn.execute` straight into an exception. The defect does not survive its fix, because nothing else in `cogs/core.py` writes. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:1074` (`open_modal`) (module level) | A modal cannot be sent after a defer, so the modal path asks `still_staff` and `db_up` (the pre-defer spelling) instead of `opened`, and the SUBMIT interaction goes through `opened` like everything else. Two gates, not one, because the modal is two round trips and a staffer can be demoted between them. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:877` (`run_set`) — a refusal re-renders NOTHING | Honeypot's discipline, kept: an outcome that is not `ok` is answered and the card is left exactly as it was, so a refused value cannot read as a save. The alternative — re-render, then answer — flashes a card showing the OLD value beside a sentence saying it was refused, which is the same information arranged to look like a bug. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:845` (`core_keys_allowed`) | Fork **F-S3 (a)**. `Roles & channels…` is not drawn without `manage_guild` (P9), and the button's absence is not the enforcement — the four `CoreChannelPick` callbacks re-ask through `run_core_set`, because a Lead can be demoted while the card is open and the card is still on their screen. `manages_guild` reads `member.guild_permissions.manage_guild`, the COMPUTED permission (checklist 21), never an explicit overwrite. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:497` (`number_label`) — the bound is on the FIELD | Checklist 22, and the reason it is not `settings_panel.bounds_line`: that one is prose for the embed (*"It takes a whole number no larger than 10000."*) and a Discord `TextInput` label is capped at 45 characters, so a truncated sentence would have read *"A whole number — It takes a whole number no lar"*. The modal gets its own compact spelling (*"A whole number, no more than 10000"*) and the embed keeps the sentence. `coerce_value` is still the backstop and its refusal is answered **verbatim**, never re-worded. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:956` (`run_typed`) | `parse_value` then `set_key`, in that order and both refusing in words: `parse_value` catches "that is not a number at all", `coerce_value` inside `set_key` catches "that number is out of range". Two different sentences for two different mistakes, and neither writes. The panel-minutes key gets one extra clause — `PANEL_MINUTES_NEXT_TIME` — because the new number applies to the NEXT `/settings`, not to the panel the person is looking at, and without saying so it reads as a bug. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:751` (`editor_control`) | The one place a `PanelMove` becomes a control: the six picker editors become their select classes, everything else falls through to `MoveButton` (which covers the toggle and the three modal openers). Build 1's `key_card_buttons` decides WHICH moves exist; this decides what each one is made of. Keeping the split means the "which controls does this key card carry" test is a pure-module test with no discord.py in it. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:1278` (`ChannelMany`) · `RoleMany` — `min_values=0` | The selection IS the list, so adding and removing are one move (checklist 26), and an empty submit clears it. ⚠️ Whether a real client will submit an empty multi-select is the **same unproven edge** automod flagged and honeypot shipped around; **Clear the list** is the second door onto the empty case and is drawn whenever the list is non-empty. Above 25 stored ids neither picker is drawn at all (`list_is_too_long`) — a capped picker would silently drop what it could not show. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:1226` (`LevelKeyPick`) subclasses `KeyPick` | One select class holds "a list of keys, pick one"; the log-level list differs only in where it goes (the level card, not the generic key card). Subclassing one callback beats a flag on the parent, and it is why the panel-minutes picker and the group's setting picker are literally the same class — the design's requirement that every route lands on the SAME key card, not a second editor. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:1095` (`MoveButton.callback`) dispatches on `move.action` | One button class for every button on the panel, because the alternative is fifteen near-identical `discord.ui.Button` subclasses and the duplicate-implementation trap checklist 15 exists for. The actions are Build 1's constants; the prefixed ones (`edit:…`, `level_set:…`) are split on `:` at the point of use, which is also how `CORE_KEY_MOVES` carries its key. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` — the confirm is a CARD STATE, not a helper | Fork **F-S2 (a)** asked for a confirm on `staff_channel_id`'s reset only. §F suggested a fourth hand-rolled `open_confirm` to hand to the conductor; it was not needed — `build_key(..., confirming=True)` re-renders the same card with `CONFIRM_TITLE` + `confirm_lines` on top and `key_card_buttons(confirming=True)` below, which Build 1 already returned. **No new panels.py helper, and nothing to hand over.** `Leave it as it is` re-renders the card unconfirming; neither path writes. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/presence.py` — the cog keeps everything that is not a command | The `presence` Group and `presence_apply` are deleted; the 10-minute loop, `on_ready`, the join/leave debounce, `apply_status` and `loop_health` are untouched, because none of them is a command and the dashboard's Health page reads `loop_health`. `discord` is still imported (the listeners take `discord.Member`); `app_commands`, `STAFF_ONLY` and `require_staff` are not, which is the measurable proof the command half is gone. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/birthdays.py:434` (`clear_role`) calls `clear_key` | The fourth `settings.clear` emitter, and the one Build 1 reported without fixing. It wrote `details={"key": …}` with **no `via` at all**, so a birthday role cleared that way recorded neither Discord nor the website. It now calls the shared writer and keeps its own words: `ROLE_CLEARED`/`ROLE_NOT_SET` say the birthday-specific thing (*a role somebody already has for today still comes off tomorrow*) that `CLEARED`/`NOT_SET` cannot. One write, one row, one shape — checklist 34 — with the wording still local. ⚠️ `cogs/community/*` importing `cogs/core` is the first cog-to-cog import in the tree; it is a MODULE-level function, not a cog, so it does not break the "cogs never import each other" rule the way reaching for a `Cog` instance would. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:83` (`set_key`) · `clear_key` gained `via: str = VIA_DISCORD` | Build 1 argued (correctly, then) that a `via` nobody passes is dead weight. It is passed now — by `clear_role` implicitly, and the keyword exists so the website's `PUT`/`DELETE /api/settings/{key}` can reuse both writers in the next pass without a signature change. ⚠️ **That wiring is NOT done here**: the route still calls `store.set` and `note()`s `web.settings.set` itself, so the two doors still log once each independently. Doing it in this build would double-log unless the route's `note()` went in the same commit, and it is what closes **KI-21**. Report, not start — design §J. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:1206` (`LOG_LEVEL_COMMANDS`) — all seventeen features, correct names | Design §J defect 4, fixed. It held eleven rows and, after wave 4, **eleven of thirteen named a `logs` subcommand that no longer existed**; two were wrong independently of the panels program (`pings` → `pingroles`, `applications` → `applications`, neither of which is a command). It now maps every entry in `logkinds.FEATURES` to the command that actually exists, and `LOG_LEVEL_HELP`'s clause reads *and in `/x` ▸ **Logs*** — the spelling every panel uses. `core` is in it for the first time, because `/settings` grew a **Logs** button in this build; a test walks `send_logs` call sites in the AST and asserts every feature has one. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py:409` (`reachable_on_the_panel`) | Added to Build 1's `__all__` contract for the tests, not for the panel. Thirty-one assertions across `tests/test_settings_store.py` and `tests/test_command_visibility.py` read *"this key is reachable from Discord"* as `key in cogs.core.VALUE_KEYS`; that list is deleted, and the honest replacement is the panel's own reach — the key is in its group's list AND its card carries an editor. The set-equality form lives in `test_every_registry_key_is_reachable_from_the_panel_as_well_as_the_dashboard`. |
| ⚠️ `tests/test_bot.py:226` (`test_every_features_logs_is_a_panel_button_and_no_group_is_left_to_hold_one`) | The old `test_every_feature_group_has_a_logs_command` could not survive: `LOGS_GROUPS` was already `{}` on `main` (honeypot, modmail and `/mod` emptied it), so the test iterated nothing and its remaining assertions were four "this group is gone" checks. Rather than delete a guarantee, it is re-expressed against what replaced it — **zero** `app_commands.Group`s in the tree, and an AST walk of `black_bloc/` proving every one of the 17 `logkinds.FEATURES` is the argument of a `send_logs` call somewhere. The walk resolves module-level string constants (and `logkinds`' own) so `send_logs(interaction, FEATURE)` and `send_logs(interaction, CORE)` both count. Its sibling `test_a_logs_command_is_staff_only_and_ephemeral` iterated the same empty dict and asserted nothing at all; it is now a direct check that `send_logs` itself calls `require_staff`, which is where that gate actually lives. |
| `tests/cogs/test_core.py` — the `/help` half did not move | Design §G's strongest available evidence, kept: every `/help` test reads exactly as it did except the two assertions that named a retired path (`HIDDEN_NOTE`'s sentence, and `/settings show — …` in the real-tree listing, now `**/settings** — …`). `/help` reads the tree, so a Group becoming a command needs no code change at all — and the unchanged tests are the proof (P15). |

# Modmail leftovers (wave 4 follow-up)

> Written 2026-09-05 on `worktree-agent-ad2fc0f5aad473c19`, off `main` at `6212380`; merged and live as **v85**. Every key below is a `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line
> number. Scope: the seven `TODO.md` leftovers after Build B — the panel-side `A ticket…` select
> and its ticket card, `picked_values` folded into `panels.py`, four dead names deleted, and a
> `modmail.card_failed` row for the card task that used to fail in silence.
> Verified by `ruff`, `pytest` (**5020**) and `node site/mock/check.mjs`
> (**17 pages / 146 routes**, unchanged). ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord.**

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/panels.py:171` (`picked_values`) | Was two byte-identical copies (`polls.py`, `black_bloc/modmail.py`) of one three-line reader, which is checklist 15 exactly. It belongs in the library rather than in either feature because what it knows is a **discord.py 2.7.1 fact** — a `Select` inside a modal answers with `values`, a `RadioGroup` with `value` — and not a fact about polls or about modmail. Its tests moved with it into `tests/test_panels.py`; nothing else changed, which is why the poll and modal tests are unchanged and are the proof. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/modmail.py:881` (`panel_card_buttons`) — derived from `card_buttons`, never spelled twice | The panel's copy of the card needs `ModmailMove`s (the panel machinery's shape) while the card in the channel needs `CardMove`s (the `DynamicItem` shape), so the naive answer is a second table of four labels. It is instead **built from `card_buttons(practice=False)`**, re-homing each move to row 1 and marking it `modal=True`, so a label or a style can only ever be changed in one place. `tests/test_modmail.py` asserts the two lists are equal, and `test_every_move_the_panel_can_draw_is_in_one_table` was widened to `PANEL_MOVES ∪ CARD_MOVES` rather than given four new entries — the card table IS the one table for these four. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py:panel_card_buttons(open_ticket=False)` → `Back` alone | §E says a closed ticket "renders no move buttons" and the panel is where a closed ticket is read. A lone `Back` with no explanation reads as a broken card, so `build_ticket` puts `CARD_CLOSED_FOOTER` on the embed — the ONE place the panel's embed differs from the sticky card's, and the reason `ticket_card_embed` itself was not touched. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:3513` (`run_card_reply`) — `previous` is the whole panel/card difference | Both doors run the same function; the optional `previous` view says which one pressed it. `None` is the card in the channel and behaves exactly as it did (`card_opened`, an ephemeral defer, one sentence). A view is the panel: `opened()` instead (`still_staff` → defer → `db_ready`, P8's order), then `card_moved` redraws the panel's card and says the same sentence. **`send_reply`, `add_note` and `close_ticket` are untouched**, so one press is still one write and one `action_log` row (checklist 34), and `source` stays `card` from both doors — the panel's copy IS the card, and a fifth `SOURCES` value would be a vocabulary invented for one surface. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:4734` (`card_modal`) | Which move opens which modal, stated once, `await`ed because the reply modal has to read the snippets first. `card_pressed` and `MoveButton.open_card_modal` are then two gates onto one table, and the practice-only `SpeakAsMemberModal` stays reachable from the channel card only. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:3856` (`MoveButton.open_card_modal`) — the ticket is re-read BEFORE the modal | A modal cannot be sent after a defer, so this path asks `still_staff` + `db_up` (the pre-defer spelling) and then `card_ticket`, which answers `NO_SUCH_TICKET` / `TICKET_CLOSED` **in words**. The submit interaction goes through `opened_card` and asks again — two gates, because a modal is two round trips and a ticket can be closed between them. A `picked_ticket` that is somehow unset reads as ticket `0` and gets the same sentence rather than an exception. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:3172` (`build_root`) — the picker is drawn on ≥1 open ticket, not on S5 | Deviation 1 in the design's `## Follow-up deviations` foot, with the reasoning. The short version: `_status_lines` already lists every open ticket in S2 and S3, so the S5-only reading would print the list above a panel with no way to act on it, and none of the four moves needs `modmail_enabled` or a pointed place. It is hidden while the practice confirm is up, because that surface is a two-answer question. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1113` (`card_embed`) | Pulled out of `post_card` so the sticky card and the panel's copy cannot drift: one function, one `ticket_card_embed` call, the counts and the blocked flag read the same way for both. `ticket_member` beside it is the `guild.get_member` → `bot.get_user` fallback both of them (and `TicketPick`'s labels) need. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:1069` (`card_move_failed`) | The debounced card task is awaited by nobody, so the `WARNING` it used to log was the only trace a card move had failed — a silent failure that read exactly like a success (checklist 2, and the reason the item was on `TODO.md`). It now writes `modmail.card_failed` with the same details shape `post_card` and `drop_old_card` write, the exception clamped to `CARD_REASON_LIMIT`. ⚠️ **The logging itself is wrapped**: this runs in a fire-and-forget task, and a `log_action` that raised there would replace one invisible failure with another. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `NO_CATEGORY` · `NOT_A_CATEGORY` · `Modmail._post_transcript` · `Modmail._remove_place` deleted | All four unreferenced anywhere in the repo, tests included, and each is a trap of its own kind: the two strings are the **command-era** wording of a refusal §B S3 now makes through `_status_lines`, and the two methods are Build-A wrappers whose module-level functions every caller already reaches directly. ⚠️ `events.py` keeps its OWN `NO_CATEGORY` / `NOT_A_CATEGORY` — those are live, and the duplicate names are why the grep before deleting had to be repo-wide. |


# Self-test (wave 5) — the bot proving itself, and cleaning up after itself

> Written on `worktree-agent-a4aa5efd43f249ba6`, 2026-09-05, off `main` at `374b498`; merged onto
> `main` the same day (two foot-append conflicts in the docs, kept both sides) and live as **v86**. Every key here is a `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line
> number, so the standing merge-order re-key is the paragraph under this heading and nothing
> else. Design: [`selftest-design.md`](selftest-design.md) §§B–I and its `## Build deviations`
> foot; forks F-ST1–F-ST3 (all (a)). ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord.** The verification
> is `pytest` (5090), `ruff check` and `node site/mock/check.mjs` (17 pages / 149 routes).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:109` (`Check`) — `run(one: Run)`, not `run(bot, guild, actor)` | The design's signature could not post: a check has to write the message id down against the RUN before the next check goes, or a restart mid-run leaves messages nobody knows to delete. `Run` carries the bot, the guild, the actor, the via, the run id and `post()`, so a check gets all six from one argument and cannot post unrecorded. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/selftest.py:297` (`readable_routes`) — the APP's route table, never `contract.json` | The design said to reuse the contract test's inventory. It cannot: `Dockerfile` copies `black_bloc` and `site/public` only, so `site/mock/contract.json` **is not in the image** and a runtime read of it would work locally and fail on Fly. The family is derived from the running FastAPI app instead, which is also the better single home — a route added without a contract entry is still checked. `tests/live/test_reads.py` is where the contract inventory is used, because that one runs from the repo. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:281` (`walk_routes`) | FastAPI keeps an included router as ONE `_IncludedRouter` entry in `app.routes` rather than flattening its routes into the app. Measured: `len(app.routes)` was 25 for an app with 149 routes. The walk recurses through `original_router`, with an id-set so a router included twice is not walked twice. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:314` (`_needs_arguments`) | What decides a GET route is *readable*: every parameter has a default. It is what excludes `/api/auth/me` (it takes the `Request`) without hand-listing it, and it is why the endpoint can be called directly — bypassing FastAPI's dependency injection, and with it the staff gate, which is correct for a check the bot runs on itself. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:338` (`read_check`) — 200 and a shape, not "the documented keys" | With `contract.json` out of reach at runtime there is nothing to check the keys against, so the check is: the endpoint returns without raising, and not `None`, and not an object with no keys at all. An empty LIST passes — a guild with no birthdays is not a fault. The detail carries the top-level keys it did find, so a shape that changed is visible in the log even though it does not fail. ⚠️ **A LOOKUP (`_takes_a_query` — the endpoint has query parameters, all defaulted) answering `{}` or raising `Refused` for the empty pick also passes** (v87, from the first live boot run 2026-09-05 22:29Z: `/api/ref/names?ids=` answered `{}` and `/api/applications/roster?form=` refused `no_such_form` in words — both the door working, both counted as failures). A parameterless page read answering `{}` is still a fault, and a `Refused` from one still raises. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/selftest.py:run` is `begin` + `finish` | The website's door has to answer `{run_id, started_at}` before the checks have run, or the Health card has nothing to poll. `begin` opens the row, marks the guild busy and writes `selftest.started`; `finish` runs every check and always clears the busy flag in a `finally`. `run()` is both, and is what the boot and Discord doors call and wait for. ⚠️ **The flag clears in the same breath as `close_run`, BEFORE the `selftest.finished` row is logged** (v86 landing, 2026-09-05): with the clear only in the `finally`, a `GET /api/selftest/{id}` landing in the await between `close_run` and `log_action` saw `finished_at` set AND `running: true` — checklist: a status flag travels atomically with its value. Caught by the deploy's own suite run (`test_a_run_started_from_the_website_answers_its_id_and_then_its_result`, 1 in ~2 full runs); the `finally` stays as the safety net for a check that raises. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:162` (`running`) · `_mark` — the flag lives on the BOT | Not a module global: two bots in one process (a test suite has many) must not refuse each other's runs. It is a dict keyed by guild id under `bot._selftest_running`, so a second guild can run while the first is going. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:166` (`busy_sentence`) | Global rule, no bare status: the second start says which run is going, when it started and how far it has got. The website's door wraps it in a 409 whose BODY is that sentence; the `/settings` card answers it as a plain ephemeral line. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:508` (`checks_of`) — the checks come out of the ACTION LOG | Checklist 34, one write one row. A `selftest_checks` table would have been a second copy of what `selftest.check` already records, and the two would drift. `GET /api/selftest/{run_id}` and the `/settings` card both read them back out of `action_log` by `details.run_id`. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:800` (`purge`) — bulk first, one at a time second, 404 counts | `channel.delete_messages` takes `discord.Object`s, so no message needs fetching. Past fourteen days Discord refuses the bulk call; the fallback deletes one at a time through `get_partial_message`, and a `NotFound` counts as purged because gone is the outcome the purge wanted. ⚠️ A channel the bot can no longer SEE still clears its rows, or the table grows for ever against a channel nobody can delete from. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:783` (`_stamp_purged`) | `purged_at` is stamped only when the run's LAST message goes, and the `selftest.purged` row is written in the same breath with the count — one row per run, not one per chunk. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:716` (`on_boot`) — purge, then run, then log | Fork F-ST1 (a): the boot run posts like any other, because a boot that posts nothing proves nothing about sending. The purge runs FIRST so a run that died mid-way is cleared before new cards go up. The whole body is wrapped per guild: a self-test that throws must never stop the bot from starting. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:46` (`BOOT_LINE`) | The one line the conductor reads with `flyctl logs` to verify a deploy, plus one `FAILED` line per failure. It is why `boot_lines` is a pure function with its own test — the format is a promise to a person reading logs, not an implementation detail. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/logkinds.py:555` (`HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT`) · `black_bloc/actionlog.py:default_view_clause` | Owner, 2026-09-05: *"keep the logs on the website tho under test"* — kept, and out of the way. ONE place decides it, and the SQL is built from the feature list rather than a hand-written `kind NOT LIKE 'selftest.%'` in the route, so `/api/actions` and its CSV export cannot drift apart. It applies only when NEITHER a feature NOR a kind was asked for: a deep link to `kind=selftest.` still works. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:35` (`FEATURES`) gains `selftest`, labelled **Test** | Adding it to `FEATURES` is what gives it a log-level key, a Logs-page chip and a `/api/actions?feature=` filter for free. It also means `tests/test_bot.py::test_every_features_logs_is_a_panel_button…` demands a `send_logs` call site — which is why the `/settings` self-test card carries its own **Logs** button rather than leaving the rows reachable only from the website. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:12` (`VIA_BOOT`) | A fourth via word, *By the bot at boot*. Without it a boot run's rows would read as **Discord**, which is a lie about who asked. `via_of` only honours a recorded via that is in `VIA_WORDS`, so adding the word is what makes `details={"via": "boot"}` mean anything. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py` — the four self-test keys are **CORE_KEYS** | Including `selftest_log_level`, which is the only `*_log_level` key not in its own feature namespace. Left alone, `namespace_of` would have made a 23rd settings group holding one key, and the design put them under **core** with the panel-minutes keys. `mod_log_level` → `automod` is the precedent (`NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`). |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:3250` (`default`) — `selftest_log_level` returns `off` | The ONE feature that ships at `off` rather than `important`, and it is deliberate: the rows are kept on the dashboard under **Test** and none of them is repeated into the Discord log channel unless staff turn it up. The check is BEFORE the `endswith("_log_level")` fallback, and its exception is spelled out in `tests/test_settings_store.py`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:203` (`Core.purge_loop`) | §D's 60-second loop lives on the Core cog, not on a cog of its own: `/api/status`'s `loop_health` reads loops off `bot.cogs`, so a loop with no cog is a loop the Health page cannot see. `before_loop` waits for ready, `@purge_loop.error` records the failure (checklist 28), and `loop_health("purge_loop")` is what the page reads. The first tick runs on boot, which is §D's "leftovers before new ones" — `on_boot` also purges explicitly, because the loop's first tick and `on_ready` are not ordered against each other. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` — a **Self-test…** CARD, not two buttons on the root | The design put **Run the self-test** and **Purge now** on the settings root. Row 2 there is already at Discord's five-control limit and the feature needed a third door anyway (its **Logs**, per `FEATURES` above), so the root gains one button on row 3 and the moves live on their own card. Same moves, one press further in, and room for the state the card has to show. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:640` (`selftest_card_state`) | ONE read of everything the card says, so the embed and the buttons cannot disagree — `Purge now` is drawn from the same `waiting` count the embed prints. Reading them separately is how a card ends up offering a move it then refuses. |
| `black_bloc/api/selftest_api.py:54` (`start`) — a background task, and a set that holds it | `asyncio.create_task` keeps only a weak reference; a bare one can be collected mid-run. `keep_tasks(bot)` holds it until `add_done_callback` discards it. The POST answers `{run_id, started_at, checks}` and lets go, which is what makes the Health card's 15-second poll the right shape. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/selftest_api.py` — the operator token can READ this door and never START a run | `auth.py:operator_session` refuses every method but `GET`/`HEAD` **in words**, so the design's "operator token allowed" holds for the three reads and not for the POST. `tests/live/test_selftest.py` asserts exactly that, and the start → poll → purge test needs a staff session cookie (`BLACK_BLOC_LIVE_SESSION`) instead. Recorded in `docs/access/testing.md`. |
| `black_bloc/api/server.py:207` (`api_app`) | One app per bot, kept on `bot._api_app`, because `start_api` and the self-test's `read.*` family must walk the SAME route table. Building a second app would work and would quietly stop proving anything about the one being served. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/server.py:156` (`unknown_route`) | Found while writing `tests/live/test_refusals.py`: an `/api` path nothing served answered Starlette's `{"detail": "Not Found"}` — a bare status by another name, which the global rule forbids and which the MOCK had already been answering in words for months. It is an exception handler rather than a middleware on purpose: a middleware cannot tell a route's own `Refused(404, …)` from Starlette's, and would have flattened the better sentence. |
| `black_bloc/selftest_panels.py:36` (`PANELS`) — 18 doors, not 29 | The design said "every one of the 29 commands that opens a panel". Measured: the tree is 29 commands and **18** of them open a panel; the other eleven take an argument and act (`/ban`, `/warn`, `/purge`, `/reply`, …) or answer one line (`/ping`, `/about`, `/help`). ⚠️ **No `root_card` extraction was needed** — all 18 already had a module-level builder their command handler calls, and `tests/test_selftest_panels.py` walks the AST to prove the handler calls the one the table names. |
| `black_bloc/selftest_panels.py:33` (`PanelDoor.shape`) | Five shapes, because five builders take different arguments: `(bot, guild, actor)` for thirteen, `(bot, guild)` for automod and honeypot, `(bot, guild.id, actor)` for `/memory` (its "home" is a guild id), `(bot, guild, page=, user_id=)` for `/mod`, and `(bot, guild, cog)` for modmail. The alternative — changing five signatures so one table could be uniform — would have been a refactor of five cogs to save a five-line branch. |
| `black_bloc/selftest_panels.py:59` (`panel_actor`) | Whoever asked, when they are a member of this guild; the bot itself at boot. A card built for nobody is not a card a person sees, and `guild.me` is the one member always present. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/selftest_panels.py:166` (`send_pings`) — a PREFIX, not a card | Ping roles never post anything of their own; what they contribute to another feature's announcement is the role mentions in front of it. So `send.pings` renders `golive.ping_prefix` over the three configured roles and posts that. It is the honest shape of what that feature sends, and it is the one sender whose "announcement" is a fragment. |
| `black_bloc/selftest_panels.py` — every sender goes through the FEATURE's own renderer | `golive.announcement_embed`, `youtube.render`, `birthdays.render_description`, `events.build_card`, `raidtrain.render_lineup`. A synthetic record rendered by a copy would prove the copy. `tests/test_selftest_panels.py` asserts no `{placeholder}` survives, which is what catches a template that stopped rendering. |
| ⚠️ `tests/api/test_selftest_api.py:44` (`client`) overrides the shared fixture | `TestClient` used WITHOUT `with` gets a fresh event loop per request, so the run the POST started in the background is killed on the way out and never finishes. Cost about twenty minutes and one apparently-hung test run. The local fixture is context-managed; the shared one in `tests/api/conftest.py` is left alone because nothing else starts background work. |
| `tests/test_selftest_panels.py:131` (`live`) — a REAL bot with every cog loaded | The panel family is only proof if the builders are the ones the command handlers call, so nothing in that fixture is stubbed: `BlackBlocBot(settings)`, `load_extension` for all 19 cogs, a fake guild with a channel, roles and a `me`. The loops it starts complain to stderr about a client that was never logged in — the same noise `tests/test_bot.py` already makes, and not a failure. |
| `tests/live/__init__.py` — the one deliberate exception to "tests mirror the package" | It mirrors no module: it hits the deployed host. The docstring says so, which is the rule's own escape hatch rather than a silent one. `-m 'not live'` in `addopts` keeps it out of every default run; a command-line `-m live` overrides it. |

# Confirm/opened fold (2026-09-05)

> Keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` (2026-09-11); written keyed by NAME (`path:function`) against
> `worktree-agent-a1f44401815e31ccf`, branched off `main` at `739c521`. A refactor with NO behaviour change: every card renders the same embed,
> the same buttons in the same order with the same labels and styles, and leaves the same log
> rows. **5110 tests before, 5122 after — none lost, +12 for the two new helpers** (11 new
> tests plus one name added to the library's own `__all__` test); ruff clean; `python -m
> black_bloc` NOT run (no bot token in a worktree), and nothing was exercised against live
> Discord. ⚠️ **Five notes above were re-keyed in the same pass** because they named a copy
> this fold deleted: `cogs/core.py:opened`, `cogs/moderation/automod.py:opened`,
> `cogs/moderation/modcmds.py:opened`, `cogs/community/role_menus.py:ready` and
> `cogs/community/birthdays.py:open_confirm`.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/panels.py:130` (`confirm`) | ⚠️ **Eight features had built the Keep it / Yes card by hand, and the eighth (temp voice) was not even on the TODO item's list of copies — which is the argument for one home (checklist 15/17).** The helper is the four steps every copy shared in the same order: append the question as an `Are you sure?` field, add the items, `retire(previous)`, then `edit_original_response` with `AllowedMentions.none()`. `question` is OPTIONAL because three callers put the question in the embed itself rather than in a field — birthdays makes it the description, role menus and temp voice title the whole embed "Are you sure?" — and a helper that forced the field would have changed what those cards look like. `title` is a parameter for the same reason. The embed and the view are built by the CALLER, because every panel subclasses `Panel` differently and carries its own state on the view (`where`, `note_id`, `member_id`, `streamer_id`, `query`). |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:114` (`confirm_items`) / `:ConfirmButton` | The pair of buttons, and the reason no feature needs a Button class for them any more: `ConfirmButton` takes its move as a callable and hands the LIVE view to it (`self.view`), which is what every deleted `callback` did with `self.view`. Six features' twelve one-off classes are gone. ⚠️ **`items` stays a parameter of `confirm` rather than being replaced by `confirm_items`**: automod and role menus draw their confirm buttons from their own move TABLE (`automod.confirm_buttons`, `rolemenus.PanelMove`) through their own `MoveButton`, and a table is how those two features keep "never two spellings of one move" (P3). `yes_style` exists because role menus' seed-the-defaults confirm is `primary`, not `danger` — a lowest-common-denominator helper would have quietly restyled it. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py:92` (`opened`) | The `still_staff` → `defer` → `db_ready` triplet, in that order, that five cogs carried under this exact name with this exact docstring, that `role_menus.ready` was under another name, and that `cogs/content/chat.py` wrote out **fourteen** times inline. The order matters and is why it is one function: `still_staff` answers through `answer()`, which can reply before OR after a defer, but `require_staff` cannot (see the `still_staff` note) — and `db_ready` answers a followup, so it must come after the defer. `staff=False` is the one parameter: `/raidtrain` opens for three audiences and `/memory` for anybody, so those panels defer with no gate. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1264` (`opened`) | The one caller that keeps a local `opened` — a one-line delegation to `panel_opened(interaction, staff=False)` — rather than making its ~30 call sites pass the keyword. It is a delegation, not a copy: the triplet itself is gone. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py:533` (`open_confirm`) / `:open_card_confirm` | ⚠️ **`KeepItButton`'s `where == CARD_VIEW` branch is not lost, it is resolved.** The generic button chose its way back at CLICK time from the view's `where`; only these two sites ever built one, so each now names its own way back at BUILD time — `back_to_panel` from the root card, `open_card` from the streamer card. Same two destinations, decided one step earlier. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/role_menus.py:2045` (`confirm_panel`) | What was left of the local `confirm()` after the rendering moved out: carrying `where`, `menu_name`, `grant_id` and `member_id` from the card that raised the question onto the confirm card, so `Keep it` / `Leave them` / `Leave it` land back where they came from. That copying is the only feature-specific thing the old function did. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:799` (`open_cancel_confirm`) / `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:open_withdraw_confirm` / `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py` (withdraw) | ⚠️ **Deliberately NOT folded, and the reason is a defect they share, not their shape.** All three edit with NO `allowed_mentions=AllowedMentions.none()`, where `panels.confirm` always passes it (checklist 11); folding them would have been a behaviour change inside a refactor. They also carry no `Are you sure?` field at all — the card is the event/request/application card and the two buttons are the question — and their Yes button carries the row id rather than reading it off the view. The fix is the standing small finding "`requests.py` re-renders lack `allowed_mentions`" on `TODO.md`; once that lands, all three fold with `question=""` and one `confirm_items` each. |
# Engineering sweep (settings + self-test leftovers)

> Written on `worktree-agent-accb69989b295c889`, 2026-09-05, off `main` at `aa03a01` (v87 live).
> ⚠️ **NOT merged and NOT deployed at the time of writing** — the conductor lands the branch.
> Every key here is a `path:name` ANCHOR, never a line number, so the standing merge-order
> re-key is the paragraph under this heading and nothing else. Source: `docs/TODO.md`
> "🔧 Open engineering items" (the self-test leftovers 1–2 and the `/settings` leftovers 1–4),
> plus **KI-21**. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord or the live dashboard.**

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/selftest.py:690` (`finish_quietly`) · `close_after_crash` | A check that FAILS was always recorded (`run_one` catches it); a check RUNNER that raises was not. `api/selftest_api.py:start` hands `finish` to `asyncio.create_task` and nothing awaits it, so the exception died as asyncio's GC warning: the run row stayed open with `finished_at` NULL, no `selftest.finished` row was ever written, and the Health card polled a run that would never finish. `finish_quietly` catches it, appends one synthetic `Result` named `RUNNER_CHECK` carrying `RUNNER_FAILED` in words, records it as a `selftest.check` row (so `checks_of` — and therefore `GET /api/selftest/{id}` and the `/settings` card — shows the sentence), closes the run row with `failed` counting it, and logs the `selftest.finished` row with a `detail`. The busy flag was already cleared by `finish`'s own `finally`; `close_after_crash` has a `finally` of its own so a database that is also down cannot leave the guild marked busy for ever. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:run` uses `finish_quietly`, not `finish` | Deviation from the brief, which asked only for the website's door. All three doors go through it: the boot line then names the crash (`BOOT_FAILURE`), and `/settings` ▸ **Self-test…** ▸ **Run the self-test** answers the sentence rather than the tree error handler's generic line (checklist 8/10). `finish` is left raising, so a caller that genuinely wants the exception still gets it. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/selftest.py:508` (`checks_of`) — `json_extract`, not a Python loop | It selected EVERY `selftest.check` row for the guild and dropped the ones whose `details.run_id` did not match, so one run's detail page read one run's worth of rows more on every run. Now `AND json_extract(details, '$.run_id') = ?`. **Measured** on a synthetic log, 50 runs × 106 checks: 5,300 rows read and JSON-parsed per call → 106; **14.9 ms → 3.4 ms** per call. With 50,000 unrelated rows beside them (a realistic `action_log`), **19.6 ms → 8.5 ms**. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:action_log_by_kind` (schema **31 → 32**) | `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` showed `SCAN action_log` for the new query — `action_log` had no index at all. The index on `(guild_id, kind, id)` turns it into `SEARCH … USING INDEX`. ⚠️ **It is only worth it at real size, and the measurement says so both ways:** with 5,300 rows the index made the call SLOWER (3.4 → 4.2 ms, because it adds `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`); with 55,300 rows it made it faster (8.5 → 3.1 ms). The live log is the second case and gets bigger, so the index goes in. It is a `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` inside `SCHEMA`, which `connect()` runs on every boot, so no migration step is needed — the version bump is bookkeeping, not a trigger. |
| ⚠️ `tests/api/test_selftest_api.py` — never POST `/api/selftest` twice in one test | Cost ~10 minutes: a second `client.post("/api/selftest", …)` at the end of a test, after a first run had finished, hangs the `TestClient` portal for ever with no output. The assertion that the busy flag cleared is made against `selftest.running(web, guild_id)` and `GET /api/selftest`'s `running` field instead, which proves the same thing without starting a second background task. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:891` (`run_gated_set`) · `operator_log_allowed` · `OPERATOR_LOG_REFUSED` | The operator-read-log toggle is DRAWN only for `manage_guild` (`settings_panel.py:panels_commands_buttons`), but `MoveButton.callback` sent it through `run_toggle` → `run_set`, which re-asks staff and the database and nothing else. The core-key picks already re-asked, through `core_keys_allowed`; this one did not, so a Lead who lost Manage Server while the ephemeral card was open still had a live button. `run_gated_set` is `run_core_set`'s body with the gate as an argument, and both moves are one line on top of it — checklist 15, one home. The refusal is its own sentence rather than the card's `OPERATOR_LOG_IS_FOR_A_LEAD`, because after a PRESS a person has to be told nothing was changed; both live in `cogs/core.py` and answer different questions. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/settings_api.py:189` (`settings_set`) · `settings_clear` — through `set_key` / `clear_key` | KI-21's first half. The routes wrote with `bot.store.set` / `.clear` and then `note()`d `web.settings.set` themselves, which was the ONE settings write in the app that did not go through the shared writer. They pass `via=VIA_WEBSITE` now and note nothing; `cogs/core.py:set_key` and `clear_key` build the head with `kind_via` (checklist 34, the single inverse of `bare()`), so the kind is `web.settings.set` exactly as it was and `SETTINGS_KINDS` in the audit reader needs no edit. ⚠️ **`clear_key` REFUSES a key with no stored row** (`NOTHING_STORED`, 409) where the route has always answered 200 with `cleared: false` and the page reads that flag — so the route treats that one code as a 200 and lets every other refusal through as a `Refused`. |
| `black_bloc/api/settings_api.py` imports `cogs.core` | The second `api/* → cogs/core` edge (`api/tools/*` already import their cogs). No cycle: `selftest.readable_routes` is the only place that reaches back into `api.server`, and it imports inside the function. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/settings_api.py:78` (`gated_writers`) — KI-21's second half | The generic `PUT` validated against `KEY_CHOICES` only, so `automod_mode=on` landed from the dashboard past both of `/automod`'s arming refusals, and `honeypot_mode=on` past `/honeypot`'s. The table maps a key to the cog's OWN move, every one of them `(bot, guild, value, actor, *, via)` → `Outcome`; the route still runs `coerce_value` first, so the gate is asked **as well as** the validator and never instead of it (without it a junk `honeypot_exempt_role_ids` would have reached `set_exempt_roles` and raised a 500 — a bare status by another name). ⚠️ **The audit's answer, 2026-09-05: THREE keys, and that is all of them.** Every other `*_mode` in the registry (`golive`, `youtube`, `pings`, `tempvoice`, `events`, `birthday`, `poll`, `request`, `chat`, `chat_llm`, `chat_memory`, `rolemenu`, `raidtrain`, `applications`, `modmail`, `modmail_enabled`) has a `set_mode` that writes and logs with **no verdict to share**, so routing it would add a hop and change nothing. `honeypot_exempt_role_ids` is in the table for the other half of KI-21: the route rewrote it with no `honeypot.exempt_set` row at all. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/automod.py:741` (`set_mode`) returns an `Outcome` | It returned a bare `str`, so a refusal and a save were the same type and the website could not tell them apart — the sentence would have gone out as a 200. Honeypot's already answered an `Outcome`; automod's now matches, with `not_armable`/409 for the arming refusal and `bad_value`/400 for a value the registry does not know. Its one panel caller reads `outcome.message`, which is what it printed before. |
| ⚠️ `site/mock/contract.json` gains a `settings` block · `site/mock/check.mjs:checkSettings` | One home for the registry's bounds, the same shape the rest of the contract already has: `tests/api/test_contract.py` asserts the block equals `CORE_KEYS` / `KEY_MIN` / `KEY_MAX` **and** that the real router's `/api/settings` matches it; `check.mjs` asserts the mock's own does. Both directions are checked — a bound the mock invents fails as loudly as one the registry adds and the mock does not mirror. **What the mock actually had, measured 2026-09-05 against the running server:** fourteen `*_panel_minutes` rows claimed `max: 1440` **which the validator does not enforce** (KI-20 says that value is deliberately unclamped, so the mock was inventing a bound, not copying one); `youtube_poll_minutes` was missing its `min: 5`; `CORE_KEYS` was a nine-entry second copy of a twelve-entry list; and **sixteen registry keys had no row in the mock at all** (`bot_bio`, `status_prefix`, `operator_read_log`, `emoji_skin_tone`, `golive_embed`, `hide_commands_when_off`, the four earlier `*_panel_minutes` and six panel flags). All generated from the registry rather than typed. |
| ⚠️ `tests/test_bot.py:324` (`test_every_log_level_names_a_command_that_still_exists`) | The `LOG_LEVEL_COMMANDS` sweep on `TODO.md` was **already done** — the v84 build corrected all eighteen rows and rewrote `log_level_help` to say "`/<command>` ▸ **Logs**", and re-expressed the old group test as `test_every_features_logs_is_a_panel_button_and_no_group_is_left_to_hold_one`. What was missing is what let it go stale eight times: nothing failed when a wave renamed a command out from under a row. This loads the whole tree and fails **by name** on any row naming a command Discord no longer has, and asserts the help text still ends in the Logs-button form and never in "`… logs`". |

# Personality pool (Black Bloc half) — 2026-09-05, branch `worktree-agent-a9f7e266cd87f5c2c`, live as v90 `7c59eb1`

Design: [`personality-pool-design.md`](personality-pool-design.md) §5.2–§5.4. Runbook:
[`../access/personality-pool.md`](../access/personality-pool.md). Keys are `path:name`, not
line numbers — the standing re-key rule applies after the merge.

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/personality_pool.json` | ⚠️ **HAND-BUILT from GABI's `personality.ts`**, because the canonical `catalog-platform/apps/discord-worker/src/personality-pool.json` is a later build and does not exist yet. `synced_from: catalog-platform@03dcb91` names the commit its CONTENT was read from, not one that contains the file. The `slots` array is carried so each bot's test can prove it fills every slot without hard-coding the list. |
| `black_bloc/personality_pool.json` — the `warn` slot | GABI's `REGISTER` carries an internal `⚠️ ` before *"The wiggle…"*; nothing in Black Bloc's prompts uses that marker, and stripping it from her copy is a live prompt change nobody asked for. A slot is cheaper than changing either bot. The one thing that DID move is Black Bloc's missing comma in *"clearly playing along, you may lean in"* — two spellings of one sentence is the accidental drift this design exists to kill. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:57` (`read_manifest`) | Module-level, so a missing or unreadable manifest stops the boot with a SENTENCE naming the file and the fix command, rather than a `KeyError` five frames into building a prompt. `MANIFEST` / `POOL_*` / `DRIFT_*` / `INVARIANT` / `REGISTER` are all derived from its result. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:100` (`clause`) | `str.format(**COOKOUT_SLOTS)`; a `KeyError` becomes `PoolError` naming the clause and the slot. A slot the bot does not fill is a worded failure, not a silent empty string — `{warn}` filling to `""` is a deliberate fill, which is a different thing. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:278` (`built_tropes`) | The zip that makes the whole design work: the manifest's skeleton (order, labels, wings) × `VOICES` (this server's skin). | `black_bloc/personas.py:77` (`POOL_SOURCE`) | Now the manifest's `synced_from` (was a prose sentence naming `personality.ts`). `GET /api/chat/personality` still hands it to the page as `ported_from`, so the Chat page reads *"Ported from catalog-platform@03dcb91."* — `tests/api/tools/test_chat.py` asserts the prefix rather than the old `personality.ts` substring. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/personas.py:453` (`_update_trope`) — `enabled` is absent from the UPDATE | Deliberate, and the single most important line in the build: `enabled` is the column staff own (owner rule, staff final say). | `black_bloc/personas.py:478` (`sync_tropes`) — `full=False` | What the three website routes in `api/tools/chat.py` pass. They call the sync only so a never-seeded guild is not shown a blank Personality tab; a GET that quietly retired rows would be a write nobody asked for. Insert-missing-only is exactly the old `seed_tropes` behaviour, which is also what `personality_pool_sync = false` gets. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:478` (`sync_tropes`) — the retire loop skips `source != 'gabi'` | A row somebody added by hand is not the manifest's to retire. Only rows the manifest itself put there (`source='gabi'`) can be retired by it; already-retired rows fall out of the same test, so a second sync reports no change. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:512` (`sync_wanted`) | ⚠️ `personality_tropes` is GLOBAL (no `guild_id` — see the `storage/db.py` note), and `personality_pool_sync` is per guild, so the two do not line up. `all(...)` is the resolution: one server holding the sync off holds the update-and-retire half off for the shared table. With one guild it is invisible; it is written down because a second guild would make it surprising. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:523` (`sync_pool`) | Imports `log_action` and the two kinds INSIDE the function. `settings_store` imports `PERSONALITY_CHOICES` from this module, so a module-level import either way is a cycle. |
| `black_bloc/personas.py:523` (`sync_pool`) — two kinds, not one | `chat.pool_retired` is per NAME (IMPORTANT — a mood leaving the roster is something staff should see), `chat.pool_synced` is per RUN (ROUTINE, and only when something changed).
