| `black_bloc/selftest.py:377` (`check_pool`) — a missing peer field passes | Landing order (design §8): Black Bloc ships first, so until GABI publishes `gabi_personality_pool_version` the honest answer is *"GABI does not say its pool version yet"*, not red. Claiming a check that could not run would be checklist 10. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:433` (`checks_for`) | The pool check sits between the reads and the sends, as its own one-item family, so the config/panel/read/send arithmetic in the tests still adds up with an explicit `+ 1`. |
| `black_bloc/api/server.py:146` (`health`) | `personality_pool_version` beside `version`. It is the field GABI's side compares against; without it drift is only visible from one direction, which is no direction. |
| `pyproject.toml` `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` | `personality_pool.json` added. `COPY black_bloc` in the Dockerfile carries it into the image either way, but the image installs the PACKAGE (`pip install .`), and package-data is what decides whether the file is inside it. A test asserts the entry is there, because the failure mode is a boot crash on Fly and a green suite locally. |
| `scripts/sync_personality_pool.py` | Committed, unlike `scripts/scan/` — it makes the bot work rather than gathering information. It refuses (exit 1, in words) when the canonical is missing, is not JSON, or has no tropes: the CLI-quirk rule says never print success over a stale copy. It refused every time until the GABI half landed (2026-09-05 19:33, catalog-platform `de4ef63`); the first real sync stamped `catalog-platform@de4ef63`. |
| `scripts/sync_personality_pool.py:61` (`repo_of`) | Walks up from the source file to the nearest `.git` so `--from` a checkout anywhere still gets a real `synced_from` stamp, rather than assuming the sibling-directory convention this machine happens to have. |
| `scripts/sync_personality_pool.py:55` (`name_of`) (v91) | The stamp's repo name comes from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`'s parent, not the folder the file sits in: the GABI half was built in a worktree at `C:/lcw/pool`, and `repo_of` alone would have stamped `pool@sha`. The common dir is the main checkout's `.git` from any worktree. |
| `scripts/sync_personality_pool.py:82` (`stamped`) (v91) | Copies the canonical's own bytes and appends one key, rather than re-serialising through `json.dumps`. The first sync re-flowed every array onto its own line — a 113-line diff of nothing — and wrote CRLF. Now `git diff` between the two copies is the `synced_from` line and nothing else, which is the whole point of a synced copy. The `json.dumps` branch only runs if the canonical ever carries a `synced_from` of its own, which it should not. |
| `black_bloc/selftest.py:377` (`check_pool`) — roster by name (v91) | `gabi_personality_tropes` has been an ARRAY since 2026-08-18; the first cut did `int()` on it, which would have raised `TypeError` the moment GABI answered. Fixed by comparing the names in order against `POOL_NAMES` — stronger than a count, and the failure sentence (`POOL_ROSTER`) reads both rosters so the edited side is obvious. The `int()` branch stays for a peer that answers a bare number. |

That is why the BOT is shared and rewound rather than the app being rebuilt around a fresh one. `TestClient` itself measured **0.0 ms**, so it is not worth scoping anything for. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:take` · `put` — the rewind, and why it is rows and not pages | First written as sqlite's own `Connection.backup` into an in-memory template. It failed **37 times** with `sqlite3.OperationalError: destination database is in use`: the backup destination must have no open cursor, and the suite's helpers (`kinds_in`, `web_rows_in`) return rows from cursors nobody closes. A `DELETE FROM` + `executemany` on the live connection is an ordinary write and has no such rule. `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` around it, because the delete order would otherwise have to follow the foreign keys. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:490` (`reset_bot`) · `BASELINE` — the attribute reset is not housekeeping | The bot's `__dict__` is snapshotted at module setup and restored per test. ⚠️ **Three separate leaks were only reachable because the bot is shared**, and each was found by a failing test, not by reading: a test sets `web.db = None` to prove the unreachable-database sentence (it broke the next **18** tests in that module); `with_token(web)` writes `web.settings.operator_read_token` and `test_a_tier_with_a_key_and_the_mode_on_is_live` writes `web.settings.__dict__["anthropic_api_key"]` **in place**, so settings are REBUILT (`web_settings_now()`, 0.6 ms) rather than restored — putting the same object back hands the next test the write. The four rate-limit buckets (`_api_write_bucket` and friends, hung on the bot by `api/writes.py` and `api/auth.py`) go by construction, because they are not in the baseline. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:437` (`fresh_client`) · `fresh_web` · `fresh_web_db` | The old per-test chain, kept under distinct names for the entries that must not share a module's app. One caller today: `test_contract.py`'s `web.*` row count, which asserts what a handful of writes leave in `action_log` and would be meaningless against a log 149 routes had already written to. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:566` (`wf`) — now session-scoped | It is a `SimpleNamespace` of classes and module-level functions with no state; nothing in `tests/` assigns to a `wf.*` attribute. Module- and session-scoped fixtures can depend on it, which is the only reason it changed. |
| ⚠️ `tests/api/test_contract.py:720` (`contract_seed`) · `Seed.rewind` — one seed, still one clean start per entry | The brief allowed the 149 routes to share a seeded database and accepted that a route which writes could affect a later one. **They do not share one in that sense.** The seed is built once (~430 ms, 57 awaited writes) and each entry is handed it *rewound*, so every route starts on the seed exactly as written. The reason is not caution: the routes are ordered so that **mutually exclusive transitions run on the same seeded id** — `/end` then `/cancel` on poll 1, `approve` then `deny` on request 1, `/check` then `/sendback` then `/accept` on one review row. Sharing without the rewind failed **48** of 149, and the ids cannot be split apart because they come from `site/mock/contract.json`, which a test-only build may not edit. |
| ⚠️ `tests/api/test_contract.py:704` (`Seed.rewind`) — the three marks that are not rows | A rewind of the database alone is not a rewind. The seed also leaves **its three members**, **the message the role menu was posted as** (`WebChannel.send` gives it id 9000, and `/unpost` deletes it), and **its three cogs** (`Contract`, `YouTube`, `RaidTrains`) on the guild and the bot. Every other api fixture calls `reset_bot`, which clears all three, so the seed puts them back on each rewind instead of assuming it ran first in the file. `copy.deepcopy` of the guild was tried and is impossible: the posted message carries a `discord.ui.View`, and `TypeError: cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object`. The messages are replayed from their own captured `kwargs`. |
| `tests/api/test_contract.py:746` (`snapshot`) — the read guard, and what it caught | Every entry whose method is `GET` hashes each table before and after its request and fails naming the route and the tables it changed. ⚠️ **It earned its keep on the first run**: `GET /api/chat/personality` fills the trope pool the first time anybody reads it, so the seed now takes that first read. The guard is the mitigation promised for decision 1 and stays whatever the rewind does — a read that writes is worth naming either way. |
| `tests/api/test_contract.py:200` (`sign_in_staff`) | A module-scoped seed cannot request the function-scoped `sign_in` fixture, and `tests/conftest.py` is not importable by name. Ten lines: one `sessions` row and the signed cookie, both from `black_bloc.api.auth`. `record_session`'s sync `sqlite3.connect` detour is not needed here — the seed is already async and writes through the live connection. |
| ⚠️ `tests/conftest.py:23` (`pytest_collection_modifyitems`) — `BB_REVERSE=1` | Reverses the collected items. It is the guard on everything above: module-scoped fixtures are order-independent only if something checks, and this is the something. **It found all three of the leaks in the `reset_bot` row.** Keep it. |

# Fixture-scope sweep (half B) — 2026-09-06, branch `fixture-scope-half-b`

> Off `main` at `b366c2a` (v93 + half A), in a worktree at `C:/lcw/bb-fixtures-b`. Keys are
> `path:NAME` ANCHORS, never line numbers. Source: the owner's yes to decision **2** of
> `docs/info/test-suite-profile.md` — the per-file `db` fixture, module-scoped.
> **TEST-ONLY: nothing under `black_bloc/` or `site/` changed.**
> **5187 tests before, 5187 after — none deleted, none added**; `ruff check .` clean; full suite
> `-n auto` **55.00 s → 25.99 s**, full suite SERIAL **462.06 s → 109.90 s**, `tests/cogs`
> `-n auto` **29.03 s → 12.11 s**, all measured on this machine. Every figure and its command is
> in `docs/info/test-suite-profile.md`, "Half B — measured".
> ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord, the live dashboard or a real boot.**

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `tests/conftest.py:109` (`module_db`) · `module_db_blank` · `db` — one database per module, rewound per test | **35 files** each defined `Database(tmp_path / "x.sqlite3")` + `await database.connect()` as a function-scoped `db`; the profile measured `connect()` at **51.0 ms** and **3298** tests paying it. There is now ONE `db` in the root conftest: `module_db` connects once per module (`loop_scope="module"`, matching half A's `module_web`), `module_db_blank` takes the snapshot a freshly connected database holds, and the function-scoped `db` puts that back before each test. **All 35 local fixtures were the plain pattern — none pre-seeded rows, none read the file back, none subclassed `Database` — so all 35 were deleted and NONE was kept under a distinct name.** The bespoke behaviour that did exist was per-TEST, not per-fixture, and is the two rows below. |
| ⚠️ `tests/conftest.py:88` (`put`) — the rewind restores the SCHEMA, not just the rows | Half A's rewind copied rows. That is not enough once the whole tree shares one database: `tests/cogs/content/test_golive.py::test_the_per_user_lock_serialises_two_go_lives_without_the_index` **`DROP INDEX golive_open_session`** on purpose, and with a row-only rewind the next test in the file got a database with no unique open-session index — `test_a_second_open_session_is_refused_by_the_database` inserted a second open session and read `assert 2 is None`. `put` now compares `sqlite_master` against the snapshot and, only when they differ, drops what a test made and re-runs the stored DDL for what a test dropped. Rows are deleted BEFORE the schema is repaired, so a unique index is never rebuilt over the duplicates that were the reason it went. `sqlite_` names are skipped (`sqlite_sequence` may not be dropped). ⚠️ **`sqlite_sequence` IS in the row snapshot**, which is what resets `AUTOINCREMENT` — without it every id in the suite would keep climbing across a module and the tests that assert `id == 1` would fail. |
| `tests/conftest.py:125` (`db`) — the reconnect | **13 tests in 8 files call `await db.close()`** to prove the "cannot reach its own database" sentence, and two of them (`tests/cogs/test_core.py`) reconnect afterwards while the rest do not. The fixture reconnects when it finds the database closed, before rewinding it, so the cost of a rebuild is paid by the handful of tests that earn it instead of by all 3298. No test was edited for this. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:take` · `put` — moved, not copied | Both moved to `tests/conftest.py`; the api conftest does `from tests.conftest import put, take`. ⚠️ **This corrects half A's note that "a conftest is not importable by name"** — under `--import-mode=importlib` pytest registers the root conftest in `sys.modules` as `tests.conftest` BEFORE it imports `tests/api/conftest.py`, so the import resolves out of `sys.modules` and needs nothing on `sys.path`. Verified by a probe test: `sys.modules["tests.conftest"] is tests.conftest`. `take` now returns `{"schema": …, "rows": …}` instead of a bare row dict; it is opaque to both callers (`module_blank`, `test_contract.py:contract_seed`), which only hand it back to `put`. |
| ⚠️ `tests/conftest.py:35` (`cog_modules_stay_the_ones_the_test_files_imported`) — the reversed-order failure half A found and could not name | Half A recorded that `tests/cogs/test_presence.py::test_reapply_presence_says_so_when_the_status_could_not_be_set` and `::test_someone_joining_or_leaving_refreshes_the_count_once` fail under reversed SERIAL collection **at v93, before any fixture changed**. The cause: **`discord.py`'s `load_extension` does not check `sys.modules` — it builds a NEW module object and hangs it there.** `tests/test_selftest_panels.py:live` loads all 19 cogs, so after it runs, `sys.modules["black_bloc.cogs.presence"]` is a different object from the one `tests/cogs/test_presence.py` imported `Presence` and `reapply_presence` from at collection time. Reversed, that file runs first, and then `monkeypatch.setattr("black_bloc.cogs.presence.update_status", …)` patches a module the running cog no longer lives in — the patch silently does nothing and the real `update_status` answers. Fixed test-side by an autouse fixture that puts the collection-time module objects back after every test. **Nothing under `black_bloc/` was touched**; the production behaviour (a reload replaces the module) is `discord.py`'s and is correct for a real bot, which never imports a cog by name from outside. Found by bisecting the reversed order down to the file, then reading `load_extension`. |
| `tests/test_timezones.py` — the one file that lost an import too | Deleting its `db` fixture left `import pytest` unused (`ruff F401`); it is gone. Every other file kept its `pytest` import for other fixtures, and the now-unused `from black_bloc.storage.db import Database` was dropped from the files that had no other use for it. |
| ⚠️ Files that build a `Database` INLINE rather than in a `db` fixture — not touched, and worth a later pass | Eleven files still make one of their own: `tests/storage/test_db.py` (by design — it is the schema's own test and must connect, close and reconnect), `tests/test_actionlog.py`, `test_chat_llm.py`, `test_chat_memory.py`, `test_knowledge.py`, `test_llm.py`, `test_personas.py`, `test_selftest.py`, `test_selftest_panels.py`, `test_settings_panel.py`, `test_settings_store.py`. Decision 2 named the 35 `db` FIXTURES, so only those were changed. Reported, not fixed. (`tests/cogs/content/test_raidtrain.py` keeps its `Database` import for one `monkeypatch.setattr(Database, "is_connected", …)`, which is a class-level patch and needs no database of its own.) |

# Saved poll drafts — 2026-09-06, branch `poll-drafts`

> Off `main` at `9cd79d6` (v93), in a worktree at `C:/lcw/bb-poll-drafts`. Keys are `path:NAME`
> ANCHORS, never line numbers. Source: [`poll-drafts-design.md`](poll-drafts-design.md) and the
> owner's decision of the same morning — *"B but only save 1 draft per person max"*.
> Schema **32 → 33**, registry keys **187 → 189**. **5187 tests before, 5226 after** (43 added,
> 4 `draft` parametrisations removed, measured by diffing collected ids);
> `ruff check .` clean; full suite `-n auto` green forward AND `BB_REVERSE=1`;
> `node site/mock/check.mjs` **17 pages / 149 routes / 14 core settings** before and after.
> ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord** — no boot (no token in a worktree), no panel opened
> by a person, no DM delivered by a real client.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:poll_drafts` — the whole "one per person" rule | `PRIMARY KEY (guild_id, user_id)` is the enforcement; `polls.py:save_draft` upserts onto it, so a second save cannot leave two rows even if two clicks race. ⚠️ **The draft never enters `polls`**, which is what keeps checklist 34 true for polls: a saved draft consumes no poll id, leaves no orphan row and writes no `poll.created` line until it is actually posted. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/polls.py:87` (`STATUSES`) — `draft` is GONE from the state machine | It sat in `STATUSES` / `OPEN_STATUSES` / `TRANSITIONS` / `COLOURS` / `CARD_BUTTONS` and **nothing ever wrote it** (`polls-panel-design.md` §A). Now that a draft is a real thing living somewhere else, leaving the word in the poll state machine would have been two spellings of one idea. The constant `polls.DRAFT` stays — it is the word the *preview* wears in its Status field — and `tests/test_polls.py:test_the_draft_status_is_gone_from_every_table_a_poll_walks` pins the distinction. `cogs/community/polls.py:MOVE_FUNCS` lost its `"post"` entry with it: no card row could ever produce that action again. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/storage/db.py:polls.status` — still `DEFAULT 'draft'`, deliberately | SQLite has no `ALTER COLUMN`, so dropping a column default means rebuilding `polls` (37 columns, an index, four child tables). The design allowed exactly this: *"drop the `'draft'` default … only if SQLite allows it cheaply; otherwise leave the default and note it."* **Every writer sets `status` explicitly** (`create_poll` takes it as a required keyword), so the default is unreachable — it is a dead value in the DDL, not a state anything can enter. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:984` (`PollDraft`) — moved out of the cog, and it now serialises | The dataclass and `whole_or_text` were in `cogs/community/polls.py`; the cog re-exports `PollDraft`, so `polls_cog.PollDraft` still resolves and no test moved for it. `to_json`/`from_json` are the storage format. ⚠️ **`polls.py` still imports no database and no gateway** — the helpers take `db` as an argument (measured by walking its AST: `json`, `logging`, `dataclasses`, `datetime`, `typing`, `discord`, `.`). `json` and `dataclasses` are the only additions and neither reaches a connection. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/polls.py:1041` (`draft_value`) — why a stored value is type-checked, not just filtered | `from_json` drops unknown keys (a field added later must not break an old draft) AND replaces a value whose shape has changed with the field's default. Without that second half, a payload someone hand-edited — or a field whose type changed between builds — reaches `draft.hours.strip()` and raises inside a button callback, which is a permanent spinner (checklist 30). Every field is a `str`, a `bool` or an optional `int`, so the check is three lines. |
| `black_bloc/polls.py:1157` (`stale_drafts`) — 0 days is NEVER, not everything | The guard is in the helper, not in its caller, because `poll_draft_days = 0` reaching a `WHERE saved_at < now - 0 days` would delete every draft in the guild. The test asserts both directions at the boundary (14 days + 1 second is stale; 13 h 59 is not). |
| ⚠️ `cogs/community/polls.py:create_poll(from_draft=…)` — one transaction, not two writes | `Post it` from a resumed draft must not be able to post the poll and leave the draft, or delete the draft and fail to post. The `DELETE` is issued between the `INSERT` and the single `await db.conn.commit()`, so sqlite carries both in one implicit transaction. The `from_draft` flag rides `store_poll` down and lands in the details of the poll's own `poll.created` row — **no second log row** (checklist 34), which the test reads back out of `action_log`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2320` (`render_preview`) — how a resumed preview stays resumed | The flag lives on the VIEW (`PreviewView.resumed`), and every re-render reads it off the view being replaced (`getattr(previous, "resumed", False)`), so the channel select, the ping select, the thread toggle and `Start over` all keep it without it being stored on the draft. It is deliberately NOT a `PollDraft` field: the dataclass IS the payload, and a "am I being resumed" flag has no business being saved. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2105` (`build_panel`) — why `Resume draft` is on row 4 and not beside `Create` | The design put it in row 0. **Discord allows five components per action row and a staff panel's row 0 already holds exactly five** (`Create` · `Find #…` · `Refresh` · `Settings` · `Logs`), so a sixth is a `ValueError` at render time — the panel would not open at all for the one person most likely to have a draft. Row 4 is its own row with the site link, which moved from row 3 to make room for the staff `Saved drafts…` select. Empty rows are not drawn, so nothing else looks different. The same cap put `Save for later` and `Discard draft` on row 4 of the preview (row 0 there can already reach four). A test asserts row 0 never exceeds five. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2065` (`may_save`) — a control nobody can use is not drawn | `Save for later` and `Resume draft` render only when `poll_drafts` is on AND the person could post the poll (`may_create`). A member who saved a draft and then lost `poll_who_can_create` keeps the row — it is simply not offered until they can post again, which is the same shape as the panel's existing `Create`. The row is never deleted by a settings change; only `Discard`, `Post it` and the sweep delete one. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:3705` (`_expire_drafts`) — off means kept, not aged out | It rides the existing poll sweep (`run_due_polls`, right after `_archive`) — no second loop, and the loop's `db.is_connected` check is the one that was already there. It returns early when `poll_drafts` is off: the design promises that turning drafts off keeps existing rows *"(turning it back on restores them)"*, and a sweep that kept expiring while the feature was off would quietly break that promise a fortnight later. One `poll.draft_expired` row per drop, never one per sweep. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:2701` (`their_discard_moves`) — confirm, THEN the reason box | `Discard` (staff) opens the Yes/Keep it card, and **Yes opens the modal** rather than doing the delete: a `ConfirmButton` callback has not deferred, so it is the last point in the chain where `send_modal` is still legal. The reason is required and is DM'd verbatim, so a person is never told "your draft is gone" with no explanation. Staff are re-asked (`still_staff`) at the button, at the Yes, and again inside the modal's submit. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:362` (`DM_DRAFT_DISCARDED`) — the DM goes through `dm()`, like every other one | Which means the test-mode guard sees it exactly as it sees the approve/deny DMs; there is no second sending path. ⚠️ **It resolves the member from the guild cache** (`guild.get_member`), so an uncached member gets no DM and the staffer is told so in words (`DRAFT_DM_FAILED`) rather than the failure being swallowed. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` — `draft_discarded` is IMPORTANT, the other two are ROUTINE | `poll.draft_saved` and `poll.draft_expired` are things that happen to somebody's own work with nobody else involved. `poll.draft_discarded` is staff removing something a member wrote, so it sits with `poll.cancelled`. ⚠️ Note `draft_expired` would have matched the `.expired` IMPORTANT suffix by accident — `ROUTINE` beats a suffix (`is_important`), so listing it is the decision, not an oversight. All three kinds are passed to `log_action` as **string literals**, so `tests/test_logkinds.py:KNOWN_DYNAMIC` needs no entry; the table is only for kinds built at runtime. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py:3318` (`SETTINGS_TOGGLES`) — the tuple grew a row number | Row 0 of the settings card also held exactly five toggles, so `Drafts: on/off` goes on row 4 beside `Numbers…` / the two clears / `Back` (five, at the cap). `poll_draft_days` is the fifth field of the `Numbers…` modal, which is Discord's modal cap exactly — **there is no room for a sixth number without a second modal.** |

| ⚠️ Three cog tests that asserted "the Logs button did not re-render the panel" — the assertion, not the behaviour, was what broke | `test_polls.py::…answers_with_a_new_ephemeral_message`, `test_birthdays.py::…refuses_a_stranger`, `test_events.py::…keeps_its_own_staff_gate` each read a fake attribute (`interaction.rendered` / `.message` / `._edited`) that their harnesses set INSIDE `original_response()` as well as inside an edit. The panel is still not touched — the list is a message of its own — so each now asserts what that message CARRIES: the panel's buttons, and (in polls) that the view's `message` is the list rather than the panel. |
| `tests/test_logs_panel.py` vs `tests/test_actionlog.py` — where the `send_logs` tests went | The mirror rule puts `send_logs`' tests beside `actionlog.py`. | `tests/test_logs_panel.py` — the three guards broken on purpose | `buttons_for`'s condition forced to `True` (7 tests fail, naming the cap, the ran-out case and the empty log); the `still_staff` re-check forced to `False` (the demoted-staffer test fails); one cog's `send_logs(interaction, "request")` given a `count=5` (the AST guard fails with `Extra items in the left set: (2, ('count',))`). # Loop guard — 2026-09-06, branch `loop-guard`

> Off `main` at `16bd8c2` (v96), in a worktree at `C:/lcw/bb-loop-guard`. Keys are `path:NAME`
> ANCHORS, never line numbers. Source: [`loop-guard-design.md`](loop-guard-design.md) and the
> owner's decision of the same morning — *"Build it a"*. Closes KI-24. No schema change, no new
> registry key (checklist 33 asks nothing: nothing here is a decision).
> **5267 tests before, 5277 after**; `ruff check .` clean; full suite `-n auto` green forward AND
> `BB_REVERSE=1`; `node site/mock/check.mjs` **17 pages / 150 routes / 14 core settings**,
> unchanged. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord or the live dashboard** — `python -m black_bloc`
> was not booted (no token in a worktree).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/loops.py:11` (`wait_ready`) — why a helper exists for two lines of `try` | discord.py 2.7.1 awaits `before_loop` on line 210 of `discord/ext/tasks/__init__.py` and opens the `try` that dispatches to `@loop.error` on line 217, so a `before_loop` that raises kills the task *outside* the handler: no restart, no `last_error`, nothing on the Health tab, and the only trace is asyncio's `Task exception was never retrieved` at GC time, attached to nothing. All fourteen `before_loop`s hand the exception to their own error handler through this one function, so a failed wait takes exactly the path a failed body takes. `CancelledError` is never caught — a cancelled loop is not a failed loop, and swallowing it here would record an error every time `cog_unload` ran. |
| `black_bloc/loops.py:11` (`wait_ready`) — why it returns `bool` | Twelve callers ignore the answer. Two do not: `content/raidtrain.py:_before_sweep` and `content/youtube.py:_before_poller` call `self._retime()`, which reads a setting and can call `Loop.change_interval` — after a failed wait the loop is already being restarted, so that is work on a task that is going away. `if await wait_ready(...): self._retime()` is the whole of the difference. |
| ⚠️ `tests/test_loops.py:50` (`test_a_before_loop_failure_is_recorded_and_the_real_loop_restarts_and_runs`) — `restart()` from inside `before_loop` WORKS, and this is the measurement | The design allowed for it not to: the task calling `restart()` is the task `restart()` cancels. It works because `restart()` only *requests* the cancel, and the library hands it over at the next await — `await asyncio.sleep(0)` on line 220, which the library itself comments *"allows canceling in before_loop"*. The done-callback then calls `start()` again. Proved against a real `discord.ext.tasks.Loop` whose bot's `wait_until_ready` raises once: `last_error` recorded, `waits == 2`, body ran. A fake would have proved nothing about the library. |
| `tests/test_loops.py:248` (`test_no_before_loop_waits_on_the_gateway_by_itself`) — the guard is on the WHOLE package, not on the fourteen | It asserts that `wait_until_ready` appears in `black_bloc/loops.py` and in no other file at all. A per-method check would pass the day somebody adds a fifteenth loop with its own copy of the try/except in a helper one call deep; the file-level one cannot. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py:1445` (`_poller_stopped`) — the fourteenth loop had no error handler at all | Thirteen loops had one and this one did not: `poller`'s body wraps `poll_once` in its own `try/except Exception`, so nothing ever reached an error handler and none was written. That left the `before_loop` guard nowhere to hand a failure. Written in the shape of its siblings (record `last_poll_error`, `log.error`, `self.poller.restart()`) rather than giving one `before_loop` a private recording path. Checklist 28 for a loop that was quietly missing it. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:219` (`_purge_failed`) — it recorded, logged, and left the loop dead | Alone among the fourteen handlers, and contrary to both checklist 28 and KI-24's own claim that "every loop here satisfies it". Measured before changing it: nothing in the suite depended on the loop staying stopped. Without the restart the new guard would faithfully record a `before_loop` failure for the purge loop and still never bring it back — half a fix. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:192` (`Core.cog_load`) — the guard is alignment, not a bug fix | Every other db-backed loop's `cog_load` returns early on `not self.bot.db.is_connected` (`community/birthdays.py:cog_load`); `Core` started `purge_loop` unconditionally. The body already returned early on a missing database, so nothing was broken — but "started and immediately doing nothing" and "not started" are different things on the Health tab, and one shape across thirteen cogs is worth more than the exception. |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/tools/polls.py:407` (`poll_create`) — the gap `recurrence-web-create-design.md` reported and did not widen | `POST /api/polls` wrote a poll while `poll_mode` was `off`; the recurrence route beside it refuses, and so does `/poll`. Same three lines, same `POLLS_OFF` sentence, placed before `_asked_for` so nothing is written on a refusal. Proved by deleting the gate and watching `test_the_form_is_refused_in_words_while_polls_are_switched_off` fail — a 409 test that passes with the gate removed is testing nothing. |

# Operator bucket — 2026-09-06, branch `operator-bucket`

> Written on `operator-bucket` off `main` at `6216e97` (v97 live) keyed by NAME; **merged, and
> keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11.** `black_bloc/api/auth.py` gained one
> constant and its `operator_session` body moved at that merge; the `# Operator read token`
> section above was re-keyed in the same pass. What the first
> live run found, and why each half was decided this way, is the dated note at the
> foot of [`operator-read-design.md`](operator-read-design.md); it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/auth.py:309` (`operator_session`) — the compare is before the bucket, and that ORDER is the fix | It used to take a bucket token first, so a legitimate read spent one of the thirty and the live sweep of ~60 GETs died at thirty. Design decision 6 is *a guess costs something*: a wrong token is a guess, a right one is not. Only the mismatch branch reads `client_ip`, takes the bucket and refuses — so on a server nobody has guessed at, `operator_bucket_for` is never called and the bucket object is never built. `test_the_right_operator_token_never_costs_a_bucket_token` asserts exactly that, by attribute absence rather than by counting |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:309` (`operator_session`) — an empty bucket refuses with `429`, never `401` | Ordering the bucket check INSIDE the mismatch branch and before the `401` is what stops an attacker buying unlimited guesses by ignoring the limit: past thirty, every wrong token is `429` and the `401` is unreachable. `429` versus `401` tells him only that the bucket he emptied is empty; both mean *wrong token*, and a right one reaches neither, so the pair is not an oracle for whether the token matched |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/auth.py:309` (`operator_session`) — a right token passes while its IP is out of guesses | The bucket is per **IP**, so an office, a VPN exit or a Fly region is one key shared by many callers. Locking a real operator out because somebody behind the same address was guessing would price the wrong thing; a correct token is proof the caller is not guessing. Pinned by `test_a_right_token_still_reads_while_that_ip_is_out_of_guesses`, which also re-asserts the `429` afterwards so a right token cannot be shown to refill the bucket |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:110` (`OPERATOR_SLOW_DOWN`) — why the login sentence could not be reused | `SLOW_DOWN` says *more sign-in attempts*; there was no sign-in attempt, and a reader sent to check a locked account is sent nowhere. The new one names the real cause (wrong operator tokens from this address), says signing in still works, and points at the mint command — the house three-part shape, same as `BAD_OPERATOR_TOKEN` beside it. The `error` code stays `slow_down`: the code is what a script branches on and the sentence is what a person reads |
| ⚠️ `tests/live/conftest.py:43` (`same_site_headers`) — why the live write tests were watching the wrong gate | `POST /api/selftest` with a bearer answered `403 cross_site`, not `operator_read_only`: `server.py`'s `same_site_writes` middleware runs before any dependency (design Deviation 5 says so, and the live run proved it). Both are refusals in words, so nothing was broken — but the test's whole point is the OPERATOR gate, and it never reached it. It sends BOTH `origin` and `sec-fetch-site` because `same_site` accepts either and the branch could not verify that `BLACK_BLOC_LIVE_URL` matches `settings.origin` character for character |
| `tests/live/test_reads.py:14` (`rows_of`) — why the read sweep reads the contract by `shape` | The first live run against v98 failed 26 paths with *is missing [...]*: the test looked for a `list` route's row keys on the list itself, and `/api/settings`' keys on the namespace map. `site/mock/check.mjs:check` already reads `keys` by `shape` (`list` → each row, `map` → each value, `namespaces` → each namespace's rows, else the top level); `rows_of` is that reading in Python, and `conftest.spec_for` hands over the whole route entry so `shape`, `keys` and `namespaces` travel together. An EMPTY list passes here where the mock check fails it — a live server may genuinely have no rows, and the mock's job is to prove the shape |
| `tests/live/test_reads.py:11` (`NOBODY`) — why one `403` is a pass | `/api/requests/mine` refuses the operator identity (`who["id"] == "0"`) with `not_a_member` in words. That is right: the token is nobody's account, so a member-scoped read has nothing to show. The sweep accepts exactly that code and checks the sentence names membership, so a member route that stops refusing (or refuses for another reason) still fails |

# Operator read bound

> Branch `operator-read-bound`, off `main` at `571e581` (v98). v98 took the right token off the
> guess bucket entirely, which left an operator loop on a `staff_dependency`-only route bounded by
> nothing at all; this gives it the dashboard's own read bucket, keyed on the operator identity.
> The design, and the deviations from it, are at the foot of
> [`operator-read-design.md`](operator-read-design.md) and are not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/auth.py:279` (`read_bucket_for`) — why the read bucket lives in `auth.py` and not in `writes.py` | The import direction is one-way: `writes.py` imports `auth.py`, so `auth.py` cannot reach back for it. `operator_session` is where the operator is admitted and therefore the only place it can be charged exactly once, so the bucket had to MOVE rather than be reached for. `writes.py` imports the five names back and keeps them in its `__all__`, so every existing `from .writes import READ_RATE` still resolves — `test_the_read_bucket_lives_in_auth_and_writes_re_exports_the_same_one` asserts the two names are the SAME object, which is the only thing that would catch a second bucket growing back |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:266` (`_bucket`) — moved up from `writes.py`, and `operator_bucket_for` now uses it | `operator_bucket_for` carried its own inline copy of the same four lines (`getattr`, build, `setattr`). Writing `read_bucket_for` out longhand beside it would have left two implementations of *hang a bucket on the bot* in one package. `writes.py`'s `bucket_for` and `member_bucket_for` import it back and are otherwise unchanged |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/auth.py:309` (`operator_session`) — the take sits AFTER the method check and BEFORE `note_operator_read` | Both halves of that order are load-bearing. After the method check, because a write with a good token is refused `403` and must not also spend a read. Before the log row, because a refused read must leave NO `web.operator.read` line — the docstring promises one row per request and never one for a refused token, and a rate-limited read is a refused read. `test_a_right_token_reading_too_much_is_a_sentence_and_leaves_no_row` counts the rows, not just the status |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:309` (`operator_session`) — the read bucket's key is the IDENTITY, where the guess bucket's is the IP | They answer different questions (*is this caller guessing?* / *is this caller reading too much?*) and stay two buckets. Keying reads on `OPERATOR_WHO["id"]` means two operator terminals share one budget — which is the point, the budget belongs to the token — and that a staffer's 300 and the token's 300 never drain each other. Both directions are pinned, because asserting only one would miss a shared key. `test_a_read_the_bucket_refused_never_reaches_the_guess_bucket` asserts the guess bucket is never even built |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/api/writes.py:142` (`reader_dependency`) — the operator is skipped here, not charged twice | The routes that take `reader_dependency` run `staff_dependency` first, which runs `current_session`, which is where the operator was already charged. Without the skip, a read of `/api/ref/roles` would cost two tokens and a read of `/api/settings` one, so the same 300 would mean anywhere between 150 and 300 reads depending on the route mix. The comparison is against `OPERATOR_WHO["id"]`, never a literal `"0"` — one fact, one home. A signed-in staffer is charged exactly as before |
| `black_bloc/api/auth.py:121` (`TOO_MANY_READS`) — one clause added, no second constant | The sentence moved across unchanged except *"wait a minute and open the page again"* → *"…open the page, or send the read, again"*. A terminal reading through `scripts/read.ps1` has no page to open, and this is now the only `429` a RIGHT token can meet. One refusal, one sentence: a second constant would have been two places to keep true, and the dashboard reads the same words it always did |
| ⚠️ `tests/api/test_auth.py:649` (`drain_operator_reads`) — why the test drains instead of counting on the 301st | The design said the 301st read is refused. It is not: 300 `TestClient` requests take ~0.7 s and the bucket refills at five tokens a second, so three or four are back before the 301st arrives and it answers **200** — the first attempt at that test failed on exactly this. The test still makes all 300 real reads (that is what proves the bound is 300 and not 30) and still counts exactly 300 log rows, then drains the operator's key against a clock a minute ahead — the trick `tests/api/test_writes.py:drain_reads` already uses — so the refusal is deterministic rather than a race with the refill. Sweep row `RB-a` carries the same warning for a person typing the loop by hand |

# The "When?" picker — 2026-09-10, branch `when-picker`

> Written on `when-picker` off `main` at `ef54e60` keyed by NAME; **merged as v100 (`1f35f28`),
> and keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11.** `black_bloc/events.py` gained a block
> of draft helpers before `update_event` and `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` ~180 lines
> before `ProposeButton` at that merge; the two `# Events` sections above were re-keyed in the
> same pass. Why each half was decided this way is
> [`when-picker-design.md`](when-picker-design.md) and its `## Deviations` foot; it is not
> repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/when_picker.py:144` (`WhenDraft.chosen_day`) — the typed date WINS, and that is what makes the two doors one field | `later_text` and `day` are two ways of saying the same thing, so one has to lose. `DaySelect` clears `later_text` when a real day is picked and `take_later` clears `day` when one is typed, which means whichever was touched last is the one `chosen_day` returns — no third "which door did they use" flag to keep true. The unreadable case is why `later_text` is kept as TEXT rather than parsed on the way in: a date nobody can read still has to come back prefilled in the modal, which is the whole of §2 |
| `black_bloc/when_picker.py:180` (`resolve`) — it answers a STRING, not a datetime, on purpose | The cogs already own the DST-gap, ambiguous, past and duration rules through `checked_fields` and `read_numbers`, and those take `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`. Handing back the same string the modal used to carry means the picker added a door and changed no rule; `tests/test_events.py::test_the_draft_reuses_the_dst_and_past_sentences_rather_than_writing_new_ones` is the guard on that |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/when_picker.py:190` (`day_options`) — a typed date replaces the LAST day rather than being appended | 24 days plus `Later — pick a date…` is exactly Discord's 25. Appending a 26th is a silent API refusal at render time, which looks like a broken panel rather than a bug. The same shape is in `zone_options`, where a stored zone outside the choices takes the 24th slot — except when the list is SHORT, where it is appended, because there is room and dropping somebody's own choice to make room that exists would be worse |
| `black_bloc/when_picker.py:258` (`duration_options`) — the option VALUE is a duration `parse_duration` reads, not a number of minutes | An option carrying `90` would need a minutes→text conversion somewhere, and `describe_duration` is about display (`1h 30m`), not about what the parser takes. Making the value `1h30m` means the draft holds the same string the old modal's box held, so `checked_fields` is called with exactly what it was called with before. `duration_for` goes the other way for the ONE case that needs it — marking the option `events_default_minutes` names — and falls back to `{n}m`, which the parser also reads |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/when_picker.py:406` (`ZonePanel`) — the three callbacks are handed the PANEL as well as the interaction | Back has to retire the ZonePanel, and the closure that knows where Back goes is built before the ZonePanel exists. Passing `self` through `take_zone` / `take_other` / `go_back` is what lets one `open_zone_panel(interaction, previous, back)` serve three callers (`/event`'s **My time zone**, and both drafts' **Time zone**) with nothing but a different `back` |
| `black_bloc/when_picker.py:377` (`ZoneModal`) — one modal, two thin cog subclasses | `cogs/community/events.py:ZoneModal` keeps its `(cog, current, previous, back)` signature so all its existing tests construct it unchanged; `cogs/content/raidtrain.py:TrainZoneModal` is the same three lines for the train. The field is still called `zone`, which is why `test_a_timezone_black_bloc_does_not_know_is_refused_with_a_suggestion` and its neighbours never moved |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1063` (`draft_check`) — the title is asked for BEFORE the time, which is not the obvious order | `checked_fields` checks the title first, so a draft with neither would otherwise say two different things depending on whether the time happened to be complete. Asking the title first in both branches means the panel's sentence is the one `checked_fields` would have said, always. Pinned by `test_a_draft_with_no_title_says_so_before_it_says_anything_about_the_time` |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1095` (`draft_lines`) — the Still-needed line is DROPPED when it would repeat the When line | The design's card carries both a short parenthetical on **When** and a one-line **Still needed**, and while the only problem IS the time those are the same sentence. Comparing the two strings is cheaper than a second sentence that has to stay in step with the first, and `test_the_draft_card_says_what_is_missing_once_and_never_twice` is what stops one of them drifting |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1119` (`scheduled_name`) — it renders THEN clamps, and a long title eats its own suffix | Clamping the title first and appending would push the result past `EVENT_NAME_LIMIT` and Discord would refuse the whole scheduled event; clamping the rendered name means a 100-character title simply loses ` Feat. BaF`. That is the right trade — an event on the calendar under a plain name beats no event — and it is what the design asked for. The `except` is checklist 17: the template is staff-editable text, and a stored one that will not render falls back to `fallback` — the caller's own shipped default, `EVENTS_SCHEDULED_NAME_TEMPLATE` unless it says otherwise — with a log line rather than losing the event |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2686` (`default_minutes`) / `guild_zone` / `zone_choices` / `minute_step` — four one-line readers, not four `store.get` calls at the call sites | Each is read from two places (the cog's `build_draft` and something else — `create_scheduled_event`, `build_panel`, the train's `build_draft`), and a settings key spelled out at a call site is the shape that drifts. `DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES` stays as the module constant so `duration_minutes(row)` — a pure function with no store — still has a fallback |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/timezones.py:105` (`get_timezone`) — the fallback is re-validated with `is_known` | A guild's `default_timezone` is refused on set, so it was a real zone once; tzdata drops names between releases, and a container upgrade is exactly when a zone stops resolving. Falling through to `DEFAULT_TZ` there means the worst case is times read in Phoenix rather than a crash in a render. `events.stored_zone` does the same thing for the same reason |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2848` (`checked_zones`) — unknown names are DROPPED, an all-unknown list is REFUSED | The design says "each validated with `is_known`, at most 24 kept", and a silent strip is the shape the global rules warn about — so the sentence `set_key` echoes is `display_value` of what was actually STORED, which is the cleaned list, and the refusal only fires where silence would be worst (nothing survives, so the dropdown would have had no zones at all). One name that vanishes is visible in the confirmation; a whole list that vanishes is not recoverable from it |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2891` (`TEXT_CHECKS`) — the `text` kind gained per-key validators, which it did not have | `golive_template` and `birthday_template` are unvalidated on purpose (checklist 17 catches them at render), and this does NOT change that. The three keys here are different: a zone that does not resolve makes the picker useless rather than ugly, and `events_scheduled_name_template` is refused on set because the design asked for it in words. `UNKNOWN_ZONE` here is deliberately NOT `events.UNKNOWN_TZ` — that one says *nothing was saved* about a member's own zone, this one says *nothing was changed* about the server's default, and `settings_store` cannot import `events` anyway (the arrow runs the other way) |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2717` (`NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`) — the three timezone keys are filed under `events` | `namespace_of` splits on the first `_`, so `default_timezone`, `timezone_choices` and `time_step_minutes` would each have made a one-key namespace of its own and taken the Settings panel's group count from 23 to 26. They are read by `/event` and `/raidtrain` and edited beside the other event keys, so `events` is where a person looks for them |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:985` (`submit_draft`) — it re-checks everything the button already checked | `SubmitButton` only renders when `draft_check` passes, so on the face of it the re-check is dead code. It is not: the mode can go `off`, the clock can pass the start time, and the panel can sit open for `event_panel_minutes` between the render and the click — the same argument P8 makes for re-asking staff. `test_submit_is_refused_when_events_go_off_while_the_draft_is_open` and `test_submit_re_checks_rather_than_trusting_the_button_that_rendered_it` are the two halves of that |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1773` (`EventTextModal`) — every box is `required=False`, the title included | A required box that is empty is refused by DISCORD, before `on_submit` ever runs, and that refusal is exactly the failure the whole change exists to remove. The title is still required — by the panel, which says `(needed)` and holds Submit back — so nothing got easier, only later |
| ⚠️ `cogs/content/raidtrain.py:TrainModal` was removed, and it had never worked | It was constructed as `TrainModal(view, tz_name, minutes)` — a `RaidPanel`, not the cog — and its `on_submit` called `self.cog.submit_train(...)`, a method no class in the file defines. Nothing in the suite touched it, so nothing caught it; a real Start-a-raid-train would have raised `AttributeError` and shown the clicker `AnswersErrors`' apology. Found while deleting it, not by looking for it, which is the argument for the cog test that now drives the button |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:652` (`read_numbers`) — moved out of the cog with `BAD_NUMBER` and `OUT_OF_RANGE` | `draft_check` needs the bounds and lives in the pure half; leaving `read_numbers` in the cog would have meant the pure module importing the cog, or a second copy of the four constants. The sentences are byte-identical to the ones the modal said, which is why the four parametrised refusal cases in `tests/cogs/content/test_raidtrain.py` kept their expectations |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1731` (`MoveButton.callback`) — `START_TRAIN` moved OUT of `open_modal` | `open_modal`'s remaining job is the cancel note, which is genuinely a modal; Start now opens a panel, and a panel is a `defer` + `edit_original_response`, not a `send_modal`. Leaving it in the `else` branch would have meant `open_modal` deferring for one action and not the other, which is the shape that produces "This interaction failed" |

## The raid train's calendar name (branch `raidtrain-name`, off `main` at `d25f87c`; ✅ merged as
v104 `b320031`, keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11)

| Where | Why |
| --- | --- |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1119` (`scheduled_name`) — the `fallback=` keyword exists so the DEFAULT could stay what it was | Two features share this function and they do not share a default: `/event` falls back to `{title} Feat. BaF`, a raid train to the plain `{title}`. Making the keyword default to the events constant means `cogs/community/events.py` and every existing test call it unchanged, so the owner's "leave raid train as it is now" cost `/event` nothing. A shared `if this is a raid train` inside the function would have been the other shape, and it is the one that grows a third branch |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:286` (`RAIDTRAIN_SCHEDULED_NAME_KEY`) — reuses `checked_name_template` rather than copying it | The rules are the same rules (`{title}` present, no other placeholder), and a second copy is the thing that drifts when one of them gains a placeholder. What is NOT shared is the DEFAULT, which is why the key is a separate registry entry and not a posture flag on the events one |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2804` (`NAME_TEMPLATE_NEEDS_TITLE`) — it no longer says the example is "the one it ships with" | It was true while one key used the sentence. With two keys shipping two different defaults, `{title} Feat. BaF` is what the EVENTS key ships with and would have been a lie under the raid-train key, so the clause is now "is one that works". The `example` format field stayed, so a third key with a third default can pass its own |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:2325` (`_maybe_scheduled_event`) — the guard check still comes BEFORE the name is rendered | Nothing about the wording can make a scheduled event under TEST_MODE, and `test_test_mode_makes_no_calendar_event_however_the_wording_is_set` is what pins that ordering. The name is rendered inside the `try` with the rest of the call, so a template stored before the validator existed cannot stop the train being posted — it just falls back |

# The "Where?" picker — written on `where-picker` off `main` at `a47e43a`, 2026-09-10

> Written keyed by NAME because the branch was not merged and every line number in the four
> changed source files (`black_bloc/events.py`, `cogs/community/events.py`,
> `api/tools/events.py`, `storage/db.py`) moved at the merge. ✅ **Merged as v105 (`3205c0f`);
> keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11**, with the name kept beside each number. Why each half was decided this way is
> [`where-picker-design.md`](where-picker-design.md) and its `## Deviations` foot; it is not
> repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:266` (`read_where`) — a row with no `where_kind` and a `location` reads as `other`, which is what makes schema 34 need no backfill | Every event that existed before the two columns had its place in `location` and nothing else, and that is exactly the `other` kind. Reading it that way means the migration is two `ALTER TABLE`s and no `UPDATE`: the old rows are already right. It is also why `location` is still the home of the typed text rather than a fourth column — one fact, one home, and the fact did not change shape |
| `black_bloc/events.py:266` (`read_where`) / `cell` — the columns are read THROUGH a try/except rather than off the row directly | `card_for(row)` is handed rows from four places, and the tests hand it plain dicts that predate the columns. `sqlite3.Row` raises `IndexError` for a missing column, a dict raises `KeyError`, and neither is a reason to fail rendering a card. The cost is that a genuinely missing column reads as unset instead of exploding, which for a display path is the right way round |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:316` (`where_line`) vs `where_said` — two renderings of one fact, because a MENTION does not render everywhere | `where_line` is `<#id>`, which Discord resolves into a clickable channel on an embed. A button label is not markdown: `<#123>` on a button reads as the literal angle brackets, so `where_said` spells the channel out (`🔊 Raid Night`, `#general`) for `where_button_label` and for the website's `where_label`. They are deliberately NOT one function with a flag — the callers are display surfaces with different rules, and a flag would invite the wrong one |
| `black_bloc/events.py:316` (`where_line`) — the channel is rendered from the ID at display time, never copied into `location` | A channel that is renamed shows its new name on every card, and a card built a month ago is not stale. It is also the reason `location` stays NULL for the two channel kinds: a name stored beside an id is a second copy of the same fact, and the copy is the one that goes wrong |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1427` (`scheduled_place`) — the CHANNEL's live type decides voice vs stage vs text, not the stored `where_kind` | Discord refuses `entity_type=voice` with a stage channel and refuses either with a text channel, and a channel can be converted between the three after the event is proposed. Branching on what `guild.get_channel` hands back now means the calendar entry is always one Discord will accept; `where_kind` stays on the row for the website's dropdown and for reading a row without a guild in hand. `checked_where` normalises the same way on the way in, which is why a text channel sent as `voice` is stored as `text` rather than refused |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1427` (`scheduled_place`) — it is computed BEFORE the `try:` that wraps `create_scheduled_event` | It awaits `log_action` on the gone-channel path, and `log_action` can raise a network error of its own. Inside the `try` that failure would be recorded as `event.create_scheduled_failed` — a lie about which call failed, and checklist 2's whole point is that a failure and a dry run must be distinguishable at a glance |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1218` (`set_where`) — the staff card writes three columns, not through `update_event` | `update_event` takes `starts_at` and `finishes_at` as datetimes and rewrites the whole row; the card has a row whose start may be unreadable (the reconcile loop cancels those) and no business re-writing a time nobody touched. `set_where` sits beside `set_status`, `set_review`, `set_scheduled` and `set_announced`, which is the grammar this module already uses for one-fact writes. The website still goes through `update_event`, because there the whole row genuinely is being edited |
| `black_bloc/events.py:400` (`checked_where`) — the empty kind and the `other` kind both collapse to `WHERE_UNSET` when nothing was typed | Three ways of saying "nowhere" (no kind, `other` with an empty box, and `Clear`) would otherwise store three different rows, and a card that shows nothing would be one of `NULL`, `('other', NULL, NULL)` or `('other', NULL, '')`. Collapsing at the door means `read_where` has one shape to recognise and the website's `— nowhere in particular —` and the panel's `Clear` genuinely do the same thing |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1102` (`WhereSelect`) — a `ChannelSelect`, so there is no 25-item cap and no option list to keep in step | `zone_options` and the rest of the When picker build their 25 options by hand because Discord has no zone picker. It does have a channel picker, and `channel_types=[voice, stage_voice, text]` filters it server-side, so a guild with 200 channels works and a channel created a second ago is in the list. `min_values=0` is what makes deselecting mean *nowhere*, which is the same move as `Clear` — both land on `WHERE_UNSET` |
| ⚠️ `cogs/community/events.py:WhereSelect.default_values` — a bare `discord.Object(id=…)`, and NONE at all when the channel has gone | `_handle_select_defaults` treats a bare `Object` on a channel select as a `GuildChannel`, so the stored id is all the component needs and nothing has to be resolved to build it. But a default naming a channel Discord cannot find is a payload Discord may refuse, and a refused component render is "This interaction failed" on every press of **Where** — so `open_where_panel` asks `guild.get_channel` once and passes `known=False` when the answer is `None`. The picker then opens on nothing, with **Clear** still there, which is the honest rendering of a venue that no longer exists |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1053` (`open_where_panel`) — the panel is handed `on_pick` and `back`, and knows neither caller | The draft's button stores on `fields` and re-renders the draft; the review card's button writes the row and re-renders the card. Both are closures built where the thing being stored is in scope, exactly as `open_zone_panel` does it, which is what lets one panel serve two very different writers with no branch inside it |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1182` (`WhereModal.on_submit`) — it returns to the DRAFT, not to the panel that opened it | A modal submit is a fresh interaction and re-rendering the WherePanel would leave the person one press further from where they were going. It is also the modals-never-refuse rule: the box stores what was typed and the surface that judges it is the draft card |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:736` (`render_card`) split out of `open_card` | `open_card` calls `opened()`, which defers; `store_card_where` has already deferred through its own `opened()`, and a second `defer` on one interaction raises `InteractionResponded`. Splitting the render from the gate is the same shape `render_panel` / `back_to_panel` already have — and the same trap `finish_card` was written to avoid |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1677` (`CardWhereButton`) — staff only, and only while the event is still open | Staff final say means every stored decision has a staff move that reverses it, and this is Where's. It is gated on `is_staff` AND `status in OPEN_STATUSES`: a done or cancelled event has no venue worth changing, and `store_card_where` re-asks `still_staff` on the click rather than trusting the render that put the button there (P8) |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1701` (`store_card_where`) — it logs `event.edited`, the kind the WEBSITE's editor already uses | A new `event.where_changed` kind would need a classification, a mock entry and a row in the logs page's vocabulary, all to say what `event.edited` says. The details carry `where_kind`, so the Logs page shows which way it went. One write, one row — checklist 34 |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/events.py:91` (`event_row`) — `where_label` is computed server-side | The page has the cached `/api/ref/channels` and could resolve the id itself, but the queue table renders before that cache is warm and the detail card is read by a person, not by code. Sending the words means the row is complete on its own; the cached channel list is still what the EDITOR's dropdown is built from, because that needs every channel, not one |
| ⚠️ `page-events.js:whereControl` — the payload is built by a closure, not read off the DOM at save time | `Save` sends `...where.payload()`, which knows which of the three states the control is in; reading `select.value` at the call site would put the `— somewhere else —` sentinel into the same place a channel id goes. The typed box is `hidden`, never removed, so what somebody typed survives switching to a channel and back without a round trip |
| `black_bloc/knowledge.py:478` (`event_where`) — it imports `events` inside the function | `knowledge.py` already does this for `events_by_status`; the arrow between the two modules runs one way at import time and a top-level import would make it two. What it buys is that the chat's answer to "what's on?" names the channel for a channel-kind event instead of dropping the Where clause, which is what reading `location` alone would now do |

## Where follow-up — a channel AND a link (branch `where-link`, off `main` at `ebe0ead`; ✅ merged
as v106 `6c10b9d`, keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11)

> Written keyed by NAME because the branch was not merged and every line number in the three
> changed source files (`black_bloc/events.py`, `cogs/community/events.py`, `settings_store.py`)
> moved at the merge. Keyed by LINE since 2026-09-11, with the name kept beside each number. Why each half was decided this
> way is [`where-picker-design.md`](where-picker-design.md) § Follow-up and its
> `## Follow-up deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:266` (`read_where`) — `location` now holds the text for EVERY kind, and that is still no migration | The column the follow-up needed already existed; for the two channel kinds it was simply NULL. So schema stays **34**, there is no backfill, and a row written by v105 reads back identically (`location` NULL → `text` `""`). What changed is what the column MEANS beside a channel: not *the place instead* but *the link as well*. The `other` branch is untouched, which is why the pre-schema-34 rows still read as `other` |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:316` (`where_line`) / `where_said` — one join (` · `) in both, and the clamp still bites the TEXT only | The mention and the channel's name are not the thing that can run away; a typed link is, so `LOCATION_LIMIT` stays on `where.text` alone and the pair is assembled after. `where_button_label`'s 80-character clamp then trims the PAIR, which means a long link eats itself rather than the channel name — the channel is what the button is there to say. They are still two functions and not one with a flag, for the reason the row above in the Where section gives |
| `black_bloc/events.py:400` (`checked_where`) — the channel branch is `found._replace(text=typed)`, one line for two rules | Correcting the kind from the channel's live type (D4) and keeping what was typed have to happen together or a corrected kind would silently drop the link. Doing both in the return means they cannot drift. The three spellings of nowhere still collapse: text with no channel is `other`, an empty box is `WHERE_UNSET`, and `Clear` is `WHERE_UNSET` |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:426` (`described_with_where`) — the LINK wins the clamp and the description gives way | `DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` is Discord's, so something has to lose when both are long. The link is the entire reason the description was touched at all, so the body is trimmed to `DESCRIPTION_LIMIT - len(text) - 2` and the link is appended whole. If the body trims to nothing the result is the link ALONE — the join is applied only when `trimmed` survives, so a scheduled event never opens with two blank lines |
| `black_bloc/events.py:426` (`described_with_where`) — gated by an `appended=` keyword, not by reading the store | The pure half has no `bot` and no guild id, and a settings read inside it would have made every test build a store to check a string. `create_scheduled_event` does the one `store.get(guild.id, WHERE_LINK_KEY)` at the only place the key is consulted, which is also the only place a scheduled event is made |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1427` (`scheduled_place`) — deliberately UNTOUCHED, so a GONE channel now falls back to the LINK | Its last branch reads `clamp(where.text) or LOCATION_FALLBACK`, and `where.text` was always `""` for a channel kind before this build. It no longer is, so a channel that has been deleted between the proposal and the approval puts the typed link on the calendar entry instead of `Ask in the server` — and, because the kind is still `voice`, the description carries it as well. Both were left as they fell: a venue that has vanished is exactly when the link is the most useful thing on the event, and the duplication costs a reader nothing. `event.where_channel_gone` is still logged either way |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1121` (`WhereSelect.callback`) — the kept text is read off `self.view.where`, never off the item | `WherePanel` already holds the current `Where` and rebuilds its children on every render; a second copy stored on the select would be the one that goes stale. Picking a channel keeps the text, an empty selection keeps it as `other`, and both come from the same one read — which is why a person can pick, re-pick and un-pick without ever losing what they typed |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1135` (`WhereOtherButton`) — it takes the `Where` so its LABEL can change, and nothing else about it does | Two buttons (one for a link, one for a place) would have wanted two rows, two callbacks and a panel saying both things at once. One button whose words follow the channel picker is the same move `where_button_label` makes on the draft: the control says what it will do *now*, not what it can do in general |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1173` (`WhereModal.__init__`) — `beside` and the title are decided at CONSTRUCTION | The class-level `title=` is one string and the modal has two jobs, so the instance re-sets it to `WHERE_LINK_MODAL_TITLE` when there is a channel. Reading the panel's `where` again inside `on_submit` would be the shape that could disagree with the words the person was shown, and the panel is retired behind the modal anyway — nothing can change underneath it. An empty box beside a channel clears the LINK and leaves the channel, which is why `Clear` still exists |
| ⚠️ `page-events.js:whereControl` — the typed box is no longer hidden; its HINT changes instead | A control that disappears is precisely why the two facts could not be held at once before: the box was the `— somewhere else —` branch rather than a field of its own. It is now always rendered, always sent, and the `.field-help` paragraph swaps between *Optional beside a channel* and *Only used when it is somewhere else*. The payload still comes from the closure rather than the DOM, so the `__other__` sentinel can never reach `where_channel_id` |
| `settings_store.py:events_where_link_in_description` — the one decision this build made, so it is a key | Checklist 33: the owner chose *append it* in chat, which is a default and not a law. It is a plain `bool` with a default resolver beside `events_create_scheduled`, filed under `events` by `namespace_of` with no override needed, and carried in `site/mock/server.mjs` and `labels.js` — the latter because the total guard in `test_settings_store.py` fails by name for a key with no sentence |

## Where follow-ups 2 and 3 — links that look like links, and rooms that go on time (branch
`where-links`, off `main` at `8adbc75`; ✅ merged `ac43a20` as v107, keyed by LINE against
`1d090e5` since 2026-09-11)

> Written keyed by NAME because the branch was not merged and every line number in the four
> changed source files (`black_bloc/events.py`, `cogs/community/events.py`, `settings_store.py`,
> `knowledge.py`) moved at the merge. Keyed by LINE since 2026-09-11, name beside each number. Why each half was decided this way is
> [`where-picker-design.md`](where-picker-design.md) § Follow-up 2 and § Follow-up 3, and its
> `## Follow-up 2+3 deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:276` (`where_link`) — it guesses NOTHING, and that is the point | One token after `strip()`, starting `http://`, `https://` or `www.`, is a link; everything else is a place. A cleverer test (a dot and a TLD, say) would turn `the.bar at 8` into a button that goes nowhere, and a button that goes nowhere is worse than plain text. The `www.` case is the only thing invented — a scheme is put in front for the href, because `[www.x](www.x)` is a RELATIVE link on Discord and lands on nothing. A bare `https://` with nothing after it is NOT a link, or the masked form would carry an empty label |
| `black_bloc/events.py:306` (`where_shown`) — it bails out whole when the HREF carries a `)` | The label has its `]` and `)` stripped so the markdown cannot break, but the href cannot be edited — changing it would send the reader somewhere else. Discord's parser ends the destination at the first `)`, so a URL containing one (a Wikipedia article, say) renders as half a link plus loose text. Returning the bare url in that case is the honest fallback: Discord auto-links it and nothing is silently wrong |
| ⚠️ `events.py:where_line(linked=)` — one function with a flag, where `where_line`/`where_said` are two functions | The Where section above says two renderings of one fact are deliberately two functions. This is the opposite call for a reason: `linked` does not change WHAT is said, only whether the same text wears markdown, and the caller that wants it plain (`knowledge.event_where`) wants the identical channel-and-join logic. A second function would have been that logic copied. `where_said` stays separate because it says something genuinely different — the channel's NAME instead of its mention |
| `black_bloc/events.py:306` (`where_shown`) — the clamp bites the typed text FIRST, so the label can be shorter than `LOCATION_LIMIT` | `clamp(text, LOCATION_LIMIT)` happens before the scheme is stripped, so a 300-character link is cut to 100 and the label is that minus `https://`. Clamping the label as well is belt and braces. The masked form is longer than 100 characters overall, which is fine: it only ever lands in an embed description or an embed field, both bounded far higher |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:481` (`add_open_link`) — it counts `view.children` and can decide to add NOTHING | Discord caps an action row at five items and refuses the whole render when one is over, so a sixth button is not a cosmetic problem — it is “This interaction failed” on a card that used to work. Counting the rows already built is why it is called LAST in `build_card` (rows 1→4). `build_draft` does NOT call it — the conductor removed that at the merge, because on the draft the button would have shown only while the draft was incomplete and gone when Submit took the fifth slot; the masked line in the embed carries the link there, which is what § Follow-up 2 means by “A alone covers the draft” |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:481` (`add_open_link`) — the card offers it to EVERY viewer, unlike the Where button beside it | `CardWhereButton` is staff-only because it WRITES. A link button only reads, and the requester of an event is exactly the person most likely to want the stream it points at. It is `ButtonStyle.link`, so it carries no custom id and no callback — there is nothing for a permission check to guard |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:426` (`described_with_where`) — still the BARE url, and that is not an oversight | A scheduled event's description is not rendered the way an embed is; masked links there are unreliable, and a `[label](url)` that does not resolve shows the reader the raw brackets. Discord auto-links a plain url in a description, so the bare form is both safer and no worse. This is the one surface where follow-up 2 deliberately changes nothing |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:199` (`swept_anchor`) — the status decides the column, and the fallbacks are ordered by how much they know | A DENIED or CANCELLED event's `ends_at` is a time that was never going to happen: a proposal refused today for next month kept its review room until next month plus the retention. `decided_at` is the fact that matters for those two, and it is NULL on rows the reconcile loop cancels itself — so it falls back to `ends_at` and then to `created_at`, in that order, because each knows less than the one before. A row with nothing readable returns `None` and is LEFT ALONE, which is the old behaviour for an unparseable `ends_at` and is deliberately not “delete it now” |
| `black_bloc/events.py:199` (`swept_anchor`) — it reads through `cell`, like `read_where` does | The rows handed to it in tests are plain dicts, and `decided_at` is a column a fabricated row may not carry. `cell` turns a missing column into `None`, which the fallback chain already handles; raising there would fail a sweep over one malformed row and strand every room behind it |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2247` (`_sweep_finished`) — “test mode is on” is `guard is not None`, the same predicate the rest of the module uses | `events_category`, `card_channel` and `rename_channel` all ask `getattr(bot, "guard", None)` and nothing else; a second spelling of the same question is the thing that would drift, and the guard exposes no `enabled` flag to read. What the branch changes is only the WINDOW: `timedelta(minutes=…)` instead of `timedelta(days=…)`. The `would_delete_channel` branch below it is untouched — the guard still decides WHERE the bot may delete, and a room outside the test category is still logged and left standing |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2247` (`_sweep_finished`) — the log row carries `kept_minutes` OR `kept_days`, never both | The owner's verification method is reading the log, and two keys where one is always meaningless is how a reader learns to ignore both. The delete REASON flips with it (`SWEEP_KEPT_MINUTES` / `SWEEP_KEPT_DAYS`), so Discord's own audit log says what the action log says. Both sentences live in `events.py` beside the statuses, because the cog is not the home of any fact |
| ⚠️ `settings_store.py:events_test_retention_minutes` — a SECOND key rather than a unit on the first | `events_channel_retention_days` is a live setting with a 1–365 bound and a refusal sentence written about days. Making it dual-unit would have meant a mode flag beside it and two ways to spell five minutes. Two keys means test mode and live mode are set independently and neither refusal has to explain the other — and lifting TEST_MODE later needs no migration, because the days key was never touched |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:126` (`EVENTS_TEST_RETENTION_MIN_MINUTES`) — the floor is 1 because the SWEEP is what is coarse | `RECONCILE_MINUTES = 5`, so a room actually goes somewhere between the setting and five minutes after it; zero would read as “immediately” and deliver up to five minutes later, which looks broken. The refusal says so in words. The ceiling is 1440 — a day — with its sentence pointing at `events_channel_retention_days` for anything meant to last, so neither bound is a bare number |


## Where follow-up 4 — a shorthand becomes a link, and the link is tried first (✅ LIVE v108, merge
`73e2e44` of `where-smart`; keyed by LINE against `1d090e5` since 2026-09-11)

> Written keyed by NAME because the branch was not merged and every line number in the changed
> source files (`black_bloc/events.py`, `cogs/community/events.py`, `settings_store.py`, and the
> new `black_bloc/linkcheck.py`) moved at the merge. Keyed by LINE since 2026-09-11; `linkcheck.py`
> is 45 lines and its four keys were verified by eye (14, 15, 21, 34). Why each half was decided this way is
> [`where-picker-design.md`](where-picker-design.md) § Follow-up 4 and its
> `## Follow-up 4 deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:227` (`WHERE_HOST`) — the bare-host rule lives in `where_link`, not in `where_typed` | Shape 1 is judged when a line is DRAWN, not when it is saved, which is the whole reason it is here and not at the door: an event stored months ago with `twitch.tv/skyaiva` in its `location` renders as a link from now on with no migration and no backfill. The alias rule (shape 2) is the opposite — it runs ONCE, at entry, so the stored `location` is the finished href and nothing downstream needs the table |
| `black_bloc/events.py:227` (`WHERE_HOST`) — why the TLD is two-or-more LETTERS and not any word character | `8.30` is a time and `e.g` is an abbreviation; both are single tokens with a dot, and both would otherwise become links that go nowhere. Letters-only kills the first, two-or-more kills the second. `7.30pm` fails on the first label rather than the TLD, which is the same answer by a different road |
| `black_bloc/events.py:292` (`where_typed`) — `where_link` is asked FIRST, before the split | `twitch.tv/skyaiva` splits on `/` into `twitch.tv` + `skyaiva`, and `twitch.tv` is not an alias, so the answer would be right either way — but asking `where_link` first says out loud that a thing which is already a link is never rewritten, and saves parsing the table for every full URL |
| `black_bloc/events.py:292` (`where_typed`) — the handle is matched BEFORE the `@` is stripped | `WHERE_HANDLE` accepts one optional leading `@`, and `lstrip("@")` takes it off before the template is filled. That is why `yt @skyaiva` gives `youtube.com/@skyaiva` and never `@@skyaiva` — the template owns the `@`, the typist's is courtesy. A bare `@` fails the pattern, because the character class after it needs at least one character |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2863` (`where_alias_table`) — the parse lives in `settings_store`, the use in `events` | `events.py` imports `settings_store`, so the reverse arrow does not exist. Putting the one canonical reader beside the key it belongs to lets `checked_aliases` (the refusal) and `where_typed` (the use) share it instead of keeping two parsers that would drift. It is lenient on purpose — drop what cannot be read, keep the first spelling of a repeated alias — and `checked_aliases` is the half that refuses in words when nothing survives |
