| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2863` (`where_alias_table`) — why the placeholder test compares the whole list rather than counting | A template carrying `{who}` as well as `{handle}` would pass a count test and then raise `KeyError` inside `.format` at the moment somebody typed a shorthand — a settings value turning into a crash later, which is what checklist 17 exists to stop. Comparing every placeholder found to exactly `["handle"]` rejects strays and duplicates in one line |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2793` (`NO_LINK_ALIAS`) — the doubled braces | The sentence shows the reader `{handle}`, and it is also `.format`ted to carry the limit. Doubling the braces in the constant is how both survive; a single-braced one would raise inside the refusal itself |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/linkcheck.py:34` (`link_answers`) — 403 is `LINK_OK`, and that is not a bug | Cloudflare and friends answer 403 to anything that does not look like a browser. *Reachable but refuses robots* is the opposite of *not there*, and calling it missing would warn about every link on a protected host. Only 404 and 410 — the two statuses that MEAN gone — are `LINK_MISSING`; 5xx joins the timeouts as `LINK_UNREACHABLE`, because a server that is broken today may be fine in a minute |
| `black_bloc/linkcheck.py:15` (`USER_AGENT`) — a browser-shaped string, not `aiohttp` | A bare aiohttp UA gets WAF-blocked, which arrives as a 403 and (per the row above) reads as ok — so the check would be answering a question about the user agent rather than about the page. The global gotcha, applied |
| `black_bloc/linkcheck.py:34` (`link_answers`) — `fetch` is a parameter, not a patched import | The `groq.py` `request or self._aiohttp_request` pattern. `aiohttp_status` is a module-level function so the suite can take the fallback away wholesale (`tests/conftest.py:no_test_ever_opens_a_link`), and every test passes its own `fetch`, so no test can reach the network by forgetting |
| `black_bloc/linkcheck.py:21` (`aiohttp_status`) — the session is built and closed per call | One request every few minutes at most, from inside a modal. A kept session would be a lifecycle to own in a module that has none, for a saving nobody would measure |
| `black_bloc/linkcheck.py:14` (`HEADER_BYTES`) — the session's `max_line_size` / `max_field_size` are 65536, not aiohttp's 8190 | Measured 2026-09-11: `x.com` sends a response header longer than 8190 bytes (on its 200 for a missing handle and on the `twitter.com` redirect), so the default limit raised `ClientResponseError: 400, Got more than 8190 bytes` inside the GET and `link_answers` called a host that had answered `unreachable`. Raising the two limits is the whole fix; nothing else about the request changed |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:278` (`LINK_FETCH`) — a module-level hook, `None` in production | The modal has no constructor a test can reach — Discord builds it from the button — so the seam has to be somewhere a test can patch. A module attribute is the smallest one: `monkeypatch.setattr(events_cog, "LINK_FETCH", fetch)` in the autouse `link_check` fixture, and the modal passes it straight through to `link_answers`, whose own `fetch or aiohttp_status` decides |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1182` (`WhereModal.on_submit`) — the note is put on the PANEL, then copied to the draft | The modal knows the `WherePanel` (`self.previous`), not the `EventDraft`; the draft is only reached through `take_where` → `take_draft_where`. So `on_submit` writes `self.previous.where_note` and `take_draft_where` copies it onto the fields. The copy is unconditional, which is what makes the note clear itself: `WherePanel.__init__` sets `where_note` empty, so picking a channel, clearing, or typing a link that answers all write an empty note over the old one without anybody having to remember to |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1057` (`EventDraft.where_note`) — never on the row, never on the card | It is about the LINK that was just typed, not about the event, and the person who typed it is looking at the draft when it appears. Storing it would mean a schema change (34 stays 34), a column every reader has to ignore, and a stale warning on a card read a week later by somebody who cannot act on it |
| `black_bloc/events.py:365` (`where_refused`) — the two sentences name the link, what was kept, and the key | A person must never see a bare status. Each one says what happened (404 / no answer in N seconds), what that means for their draft (nothing saved, the old place kept), and the way out (a Lead can set `events_where_link_check` to warn). `where_note` is the same information in six words, because the draft line has no room for a paragraph |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py:189` (`WHERE_CHECK_MAX_SECONDS`) — the ceiling is 3 because DISCORD sets it | A modal that has not answered within three seconds is closed by Discord and whatever was typed into it is lost. The check has to fit inside that AND leave time to render the panel afterwards, which is why the default is 2 and the ceiling is not higher. Both refusals say so in words |
| `black_bloc/events.py:400` (`checked_where`) — the website's door normalises but does NOT check | It is synchronous, and its caller already answers in words; making it `async` to open a socket would change every caller of a function whose job is validation. The dashboard's Where box therefore keeps a dead link without complaint, which is a deliberate difference from Discord's box and is written on the sweeps rows |

## Where follow-up 5 — the sentence above the picker (branch `events-where-hint`, off `main` at `27f08f2`)

> Keyed by NAME, because the branch is NOT merged and every line number in `black_bloc/events.py`,
> `cogs/community/events.py` and `settings_store.py` moves at the merge — re-key with
> `scripts/scan/rekey_code_notes.py` then, as the standing rule says. Why each half was decided this
> way is [`where-picker-design.md`](where-picker-design.md) ▸ `## Follow-up 5` and its
> `## Follow-up 5 deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py` (`where_panel_lines`) — the hint is APPENDED, never inserted | It has to be the LAST paragraph of the embed description, because the ChannelSelect is row 0 of the view and Discord draws the components under the embed. Last line = directly above the picker. Anywhere else and the sentence is talking about something the reader has already scrolled past |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`where_panel_lines`) — a blank hint is not an empty line, it is no line | `if hint.strip()` before the append. A `""` joined in would leave a trailing newline in the description, which Discord renders as a gap under the words — an emptied key would look like a rendering bug rather than like a switch somebody turned off |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`where_hint`) — read at every render, never cached | `open_where_panel` and `build_draft` both call it on the way in. That is the whole reason the sentence is a settings key: a word changed on the Settings page is on the next panel that opens, with no restart and no posted copy to re-render |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`where_hint`) — clamped to `DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` | The two surfaces it lands on are embed descriptions that other lines also draw from. 1000 is an existing constant in this file and is ten times more than the sentence needs; the point is that a pasted essay cannot take the draft card over Discord's 4096 |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py` (`draft_lines`) — `hint=` defaults to `""`, and the note still wins | `draft_lines` is pure and has no store, so the cog hands it the words. The default keeps twenty-odd existing callers untouched — including `raidtrain.py`'s identically-named, entirely different `draft_lines`. The `elif` order matters: a `where_note` (the ⚠️ link-check warning) only exists when something was typed, so the two can never both apply, and the note is the one that would |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`draft_lines`) — the hint goes with ANY pick, not just a channel | The test is `where_line(draft.where)` coming back empty, which is exactly the case that prints `(not set)`. A typed place is something picked, and a sentence about scrolling a dropdown does not belong beside *the park* |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`WHERE_HINT_KEY`) — no `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE` row, on purpose | The namespace is derived from the `events_` prefix, so the key lands in the events group on the dashboard and in `/settings` for free. `tests/api/test_contract.py::test_the_mock_groups_a_key_the_way_the_registry_does` compares the mock's override table to the registry's, and a row added to only one of them is what that test exists to catch — adding one here would have meant adding it twice for no behaviour |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK`) — this is what makes the line hideable | `coerce_value` refuses empty text for every other `text` key. Membership here turns `""` into a stored `""` instead of a refusal, and it is also what `cogs/core.py` reads to decide whether the `/settings` key modal marks the field required — so the sentence can be emptied from Discord as well as from the site, which is what KI-28 was closed over for the go-live keys |

## Event rooms — the posts move into the room, and staff get a Delete button (branch `event-rooms`, off `main` at `bd0b31d`)

> Keyed by LINE against the branch's own tree; every number will move at the merge, so re-key by
> anchor with `scripts/scan/rekey_code_notes.py` then, as the standing rule says. Why each half
> was decided this way is [`events-rooms-design.md`](events-rooms-design.md) and its
> `## Deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:2175` (`make_review_channel`) — `own_room` is what moves the posts, not a guard change | `TEST_MODE` is untouched: the guard still refuses every channel Black Bloc did not make. The room simply joins `owned_channel_ids`, which `allows_channel` has always honoured, so `card_channel` stops redirecting to the test channel and `post_to_room` is allowed through. Every other channel-making feature already did this (`polls.py`, `tempvoice.py`, `modmail.py`, `raidtrain.py`); events was the one that did not, which is the whole reason "the event stuff" was landing in the spam channel |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2208` (`_recheck`) / `:1834` (`_sweep_finished`) — re-owning happens on RECONCILE, not only at creation | `owned_channel_ids` is in memory (`guard.py:23`), so a restart forgets every room. Reconcile runs on `cog_load`, on `on_ready` and every five minutes, and it re-owns both the open rows and the swept ones — a DONE room still has to be deletable by the button and still has to accept the ended line. `tempvoice.py:2368` does the same thing for the same reason |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:2208` (`_recheck`) — an OPEN row whose room is missing keeps its id | Only `_sweep_finished` calls `forget_room`. `_recheck` is the half that CANCELS after two consecutive misses (checklist 32), and it decides that from `review_channel_id` being set while the channel does not resolve; clearing the id there would send the row down the `never_got_a_channel` path instead and lose the two-miss rule |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1855` (`forget_room`) — one write, one log line, then `continue` | TODO finding (h): a denied event kept a dead `review_channel_id` for ever and the sweep passed over it in silence. The row is written once (the id goes, the message and card ids stay), so the next pass finds nothing to forget and `event.room_forgotten` is logged exactly once per room |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1760` (`post_to_room`) — `f"event.{kind}_room"` / `would_` / `_room_failed`, never one kind for two outcomes | Checklist 2. `events_mode != "on"` and a guard refusal are DRY RUNS (`would_`); a row with no room and a send Discord rejects are FAILURES (`_failed`). The owner's verification method is reading the log, so the two must be distinguishable at a glance. The three f-strings are enumerated in `tests/test_logkinds.py:KNOWN_DYNAMIC` |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1760` (`post_to_room`) — `ping` is a parameter, and the ended, cancelled and denied lines pass `False` | An announcement and a go-live ping are what the ping role is FOR; a line saying the thing is over, or off, or refused is not worth a notification to everyone who opted in. `mentions(None)` still pins `everyone=False` and `users=False`, so an event title carrying `@everyone` cannot ping from any of the four (checklist 11) |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1808` (`post_event`) — the fan-out returns the ANNOUNCE channel's message id and drops the room's | `set_announced` feeds `edit_announcement`, which rewrites a public post when the event is called off. The room's copy needs no such edit: the room is deleted with the event, so storing its id would be a column to maintain for a message that cannot outlive its channel |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:715` (`ROOM_QUIET_REASONS`) — four cancel reasons that do NOT write a line in the room | Three of them (`review_channel_gone`, `review_channel_deleted`, `never_got_a_channel`) are cancels BECAUSE the room is missing, so the post could only ever log a failure; the fourth (`room_deleted`) is the Delete button's own cancel, and a farewell posted into a channel that is about to be deleted is noise in the log and nothing on the screen |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/events.py:1904` (`delete_room`) — the cancel comes FIRST, and the whole function does NOT hold `event_lock` | Cancelling first is what stops `on_guild_channel_delete` settling the same event a second time with `review_channel_deleted`: the listener only acts on `OPEN_STATUSES`, and by the time Discord fires it the row is already CANCELLED. The design says to run steps 1–5 under `event_lock`; that would DEADLOCK, because `cancel_event` takes the same non-reentrant `asyncio.Lock` itself. The atomicity that matters is the status change, and `cancel_event` owns it |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1904` (`delete_room`) — the sentence carries the cancel even when the delete fails | The two halves can come apart: the event is settled, then Discord refuses the channel. Saying only "could not remove it" would leave the presser believing nothing happened while the host is being DM'd that their event is off. `extra` is appended to the refusal as well as to the success line, which is the "state what was NOT done" rule in one string |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1904` (`delete_room`) — `event.channel_deleted` is the SAME kind the sweep logs, with `by` | One event, one kind: a room going away is a room going away. `details["by"]` is what tells a reader whether a person pressed the button or the five-minute sweep came round, and `details["cancelled"]` says whether the event was settled with it. `kind_via` puts the `web.` head on for the route (checklist 34) |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1954` (`remove_this_room`) — `defer(ephemeral=True)` BEFORE anything, and the followup is swallowed | The channel the interaction came from is about to stop existing. Deferring first claims the interaction while the room is still there; the followup goes to the interaction webhook afterwards and is wrapped in `said_after_the_room` because a dead channel can take it down. The `action_log` row is the record either way |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1954` (`remove_this_room`) — the row is re-read and its room compared to `interaction.channel_id` | The button is persistent and its custom id carries only the event number, so a message that was moved, or a row re-pointed at another channel between the press and the submit, would otherwise delete the wrong room. Two reads, two answers: no room left at all is `ROOM_ALREADY_GONE`, a different room is `ROOM_NOT_THIS_EVENT` |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:239` (`DECISION_TEMPLATE`) — one template, three actions | `bot.add_dynamic_items(DecisionButton)` is registered once in `cog_load`; extending the alternation to `approve|deny|delete_room` means the Delete button is covered by that same registration rather than a second class with a second template to keep in step. `deny` is tried before `delete_room` in the alternation and does not match it, because the third character differs |
| ⚠️ `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:1846` (`ask_to_delete_room`) — `decision_context(..., staff=False)`, then THREE different sentences | The guard, database and row checks are the same ones Approve and Deny make, so they stay in one function with a flag rather than a copy. What differs is the gate: the approver role or staff open the box, the HOST is told to use **Call it off** instead (it is their event, and that is the move they want), and anybody else gets `store.staff_refusal`, which names the role and the channel. Four causes, four fixes — never a bare status |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1728` (`may_delete_room`) — staff pass whatever `events_room_delete_who` holds | Owner rule, 2026-09-03: staff always get the final say and the permission. `approver` WIDENS who may press the button; it never locks staff out. A blank `events_approver_role_id` in approver mode resolves to `None` and the answer falls back to the staff question, mirroring `applications_approver_role_id` |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:555` (`build_rooms`) — the four keys live on their own page, not under `ModeSelect` | The design asks for a second select on the settings view. There is no room: rows 0–3 each hold a select (a select fills its row) and row 4 already holds five buttons, which is Discord's cap. A **Rooms…** button takes the slot the settings page's duplicate site link had — the same link is one Back away on the panel itself, and it is on the Rooms page too |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py:315` (`room_notice_view`) — the notice is built by the COG and handed to `submit_event` | `events.py` owns no buttons; the cog owns them. `room_view` is passed the same way `review_view` already was, so the pure module can post the message without importing a view, and a caller that has no buttons to offer (none today) simply posts the text |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1829` (`post_room_notice`) — posted only when the card actually reached the room, and only a FAILURE is logged | If the card was redirected the room is not the bot's to speak in, and a Delete button on a message nobody can see would be a lie. The success is visible in the room itself, so logging it would be one more routine row per proposal; a send that fails is the case nobody can see, and that gets `event.room_notice_failed` |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1829` (`post_room_notice`) — `{when}` is read at POST time and never refreshed | A room made today says "7 days after it ends"; change the key tomorrow and the old message still says seven. That is accepted: the SWEEP is the truth, the message is a courtesy, and editing every notice in every open room whenever a number changes would be a fan-out for a sentence nobody re-reads |
| `black_bloc/events.py:2151` (`approve_extra`) — a `room` approval does not claim nothing was announced | The old sentence fired whenever the announce channel got no message, which with the new default is every approval — telling staff a thing failed when it was configured. The `where` argument makes the three values say three true things |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/events.py` (`event_room_delete`) — the route calls `delete_room` and `note()`s nothing | Checklist 34, the 2026-09-03 double-post. The shared function builds its kind with `kind_via` and records `details["via"]`, so one press of **Remove its room** leaves one `web.event.channel_deleted` row and one embed. A refusal comes back as `Refused(409, …)` carrying the same sentence the Discord button says |

# Guides (G1) (branch `guides-core`, off `main` at `ecb2bb6`)

> Keyed by **NAME**, not by line, so the merge does not have to re-key it. Why each call was
> made this way is [`guides-design.md`](guides-design.md) and its `## Deviations` foot; it is not
> repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py` (`SCHEMA`, `guides_one_published_command`) — the partial index carries `audience` | §C1 says `(guild_id, command)`. The conductor's own seed publishes `event-propose` (member) and `event-review` (staff) against `/event`, so that index refuses the seed on the first boot. Deviation 1. `/help` is still safe because `links_for` asks for `audience = 'member'` |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py` (`SCHEMA`, `guide_releases`) — `"commit"` is quoted everywhere | `commit` is a reserved word in SQLite and `CREATE TABLE t (commit TEXT)` is a syntax error. Measured, rather than renamed, so the column keeps the name §C1 gave it |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py` (`SCHEMA`, `guide_steps`) — no `UNIQUE (guide_id, position)` | A whole-guide sync reorders steps in place, and a unique position collides half-way through the loop. The order is the `position` column read with `ORDER BY position, id`; `put_steps` rewrites it from the array's own order |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`lint_step`) — returns a LIST and never raises | §C2 and §D.4: staff have the final say, so the linter is advice attached to a row that saved. `api/tools/guides.py:step_row` puts it on `warnings` for the editor to paint |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`AND_THEN`) — `\s+(and\s+then|then)\s+` catches `", then "` too | The comma is consumed by `\s+`'s predecessor, so *"Press A, then B"* warns the same as *"Press A and then B"*. Deviation 13 measures how often the shipped seed trips this rule's sibling |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`PROBES`) — every reader is imported INSIDE its own coroutine | `guides.py` is imported by `cogs/core.py` and by `api/tools/guides.py`; importing `cogs.content.golive` at module scope would put a cog in that chain. The local import also means a probe for a feature that fails to load cannot stop the module |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`probe_fact`) — a probe that throws answers `not readable` | Checklist 10: claiming a check that was skipped is a lie, and a guide whose Right now block is blank reads as a broken page. The warning names the probe and the exception |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`refused_setting`) — the four core keys come from `settings_panel.CORE_CHANNEL_KEYS` | One fact, one home (checklist 15). §C5 says "the four core keys behind `settings_core_keys_admin_only`", and that tuple IS them; a fifth added there is refused here without anybody editing this file |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`named_value`) — `<#500>` becomes `#general` through `api/names.resolve_one` | §C5: cache only, never a fetch. `display_value` is the panel's own renderer, so the guide and the Settings page cannot disagree about what a key says |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`reconcile_releases`) — a missing `release.json` returns `None` and writes nothing | That is the NORMAL case until G2 ships the deploy step, so absent must not look like an error or like "nothing changed". A release already in `guide_releases` also returns `None`, which is what makes the 5-minute loop idempotent |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`mark_stale`) — the rows are filtered in PYTHON, not in SQL | `shot_release < release` as a string puts `v99` after `v112`. `release_order` reads the first run of digits, so `v110 < v112` and anything with no digits falls back to its own text |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`refresh_seeds`) — `seed_do` / `seed_expect` only, and `seed_hash` is the guard | §C11: a later deploy never touches a staff edit. The hash is over the whole seed entry, so a reworded title still refreshes what **Put the original back** would restore without moving the title itself |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`save_media`) — the row is inserted with an empty `file`, then named `<id>.<ext>` | The id is the file name, so the insert has to come first. The `UPDATE` in the same transaction is what makes a half-written row impossible to serve |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`picture_size`) — three header readers rather than Pillow | Deviation 5: Pillow is not installed and §C1 says not to add a dependency for this. The JPEG walk skips the standalone markers and reads the first SOF; WebP handles `VP8 `, `VP8L` and `VP8X` |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`FEATURE_PATHS`) — one dict, and `features_changed()` beside it | §C4.2 asks for one home the deploy can map a `git diff --name-only` through. G2's `deploy.ps1` step calls `features_changed`; nothing else should grow a second table of paths |
| `black_bloc/api/writes.py` (`member_read_dependency`) — the same gate, a different bucket | Measured: `member_dependency` takes from the member WRITE bucket, `MEMBER_RATE = 10` a minute (`writes.py`), so four guide reads cost a member four requests and eleven reads locked them out of filing one. The twin takes from a read bucket at `READ_RATE` (300 a minute) and `_member_who` is the one home of the two refusals both share |
| `black_bloc/api/server.py` (`KEEPS_ITS_OWN_CACHE`) — the one `/api/` path that keeps its own `Cache-Control` | Deviation 6. Every other API response stays `no-store`; a guide screenshot is member-gated content that is meant to sit in that member's own browser for a day, with the sha as its ETag |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`_wanted`) — a hidden guide answers **404**, not 403 | F-G3. A 403 would tell a member that a staff guide exists and what it is called; the 404 sentence is the same one a renamed guide gets |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`_may_edit`) — read at SAVE time, never at render time | §C3 and the row-290 precedent: a Lead can lose Manage Server while the editor is open. The page's `may_edit` is only what to DRAW |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guide_save`) — one `web.guide.edited` row, and `note()` is correct here | Checklist 34: the website is the only door, so this route is the sole logger and there is no shared function that already logged. `diff_summary` is what makes the row worth reading — `steps +1 −0 ~2, faults +0 −1 ~0` |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guide_save`) — publish / unpublish leaves a SECOND row | They are different questions in the log: what the words now say, and who made it visible. The publish row is only written when the flag actually moved |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guide_media`) — the old picture is dropped AFTER the new one is saved | Checklist 12: do the irreversible thing in the order that fails safe. A failed upload leaves the old shot in place; a failed delete leaves a spare file on the volume, which is cheap |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guides_stale`) — `reader_dependency`, so the operator token reads it | §C4.3: the capture session reads its to-do list with `OPERATOR_READ_TOKEN` before it opens a browser. `reader_dependency` is the one dependency that lets the operator identity past |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`guides_loop`) — seeding lives here, not in `cog_load` | Deviation 3. `cog_load` has no guild list yet. The Health page finds the loop generically (`api/status.loop_health`), so `loop_health("guides_loop")` is all the wiring it needs |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`help_lines`) — the guide clause is appended AFTER the filter has run | §C7: the filter and the paging are untouched. `needle in heading.lower()` is asked of the plain heading, so typing `guide` into `/help`'s filter still matches nothing but a command that says it |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`AllTheGuides`) — `timeout=None`, and a link button has no callback | Checklist 30 is about components that DEFER; a link button never reaches the bot at all, so there is nothing to answer and nothing to time out |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`_guide_links`) — `guides_help_links` is asked here, `guides_mode` inside `links_for` | The mode is the feature's own switch and belongs with the rows; the link switch is a `/help` decision and belongs with `/help`. Either being off gives the same empty dict, so the button is not drawn either |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` (`FEATURES_WITHOUT_A_COMMAND`) — one tuple, read by two tests | Deviation 9. It is a fact about F-G1, so it lives beside `FEATURES` rather than being spelled `"guides"` twice in `tests/test_bot.py` |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py` (`KNOWN_DYNAMIC["black_bloc/api/writes.py::kind"]`) — the seven `web.guide.*` kinds | `note()` is not `log_action`, so the AST walk cannot see a route's literal. This table is where a website-only kind is declared, and `test_the_note_table_names_exactly_the_kinds_routes_still_write` fails the moment it and the routes disagree |

# Guides (G2) (branch `guides-pages`, off `main` at `cad1abc`)

> Keyed by **NAME**, not by line. Why each call was made this way is
> [`guides-design.md`](guides-design.md) and its `## G2 deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`right_now`) — the hub's strip, NOT read from `/api/status` | §C5 says "read from `/api/status` the rail already fetches". Measured: that route is `staff_dependency`, and `shell.js:paintShell` returns early for a member-only viewer without asking for it, so a member's hub would have had no strip at all. G2 deviation 1. `feature_modes` is imported inside the function, so `guides.py` does not pull `api.status` into the cog import chain |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`feature_mode`) — `None` when the feature has no `_mode` key | §C6's card wears a mode pill. `core` has no switch, and a pill reading "not set" would be a lie about a feature that has none. The page draws nothing instead |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`next_release`) — the number is read AFTER `by=deploy.ps1`, and only the first one | A `deploys.log` line is prose after that marker and several carry more than one `v<N>` (v109's line names v109 twice; v107's names v108). The first match after the marker is the release that line IS; a `max()` over the whole line would overshoot |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`release_payload`) — `release or commit` | §C4.2's fallback. `reconcile_releases` does `str(payload["release"])`, so a `None` would be recorded as the literal release `"None"`. Naming it after the commit is wrong-but-loud: `release_order` reads the digits out of the hash, so it sorts oddly and marks shots stale rather than silently marking none |
| `scripts/release_json.py` — an entrypoint, not logic | Thin-entrypoint rule. It reads argv and stdin and calls `guides.next_release` / `guides.release_payload`; every decision it makes is in `black_bloc/guides.py`, where the tests are |
| `scripts/deploy.ps1` (the release step) — it runs BEFORE the check-clean gate | The file has to be committed for the gate to pass and for it to ship inside the image. It stages ONE path (`git add -- $releaseFile`), never `-A`, so a concurrent agent's uncommitted work is not swept in; and the gate still refuses anything else dirty, two lines later |
| `scripts/deploy.ps1` (the release step) — refuses when column 3 of the last log line is not a commit | The silent alternative is an empty diff, which reads exactly like "nothing changed" and marks nothing stale. A one-line fix to `deploys.log` is cheaper than a release of screenshots nobody knows are wrong |
| `scripts/backup_db.ps1` (the shots block) — `NO SHOTS`, not a failure | `/data/guides` does not exist until the first upload, which is the normal state today. The snapshot is what decides the exit code; a missing tar is logged in words and never reported as a success |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`fact_choices`) — the API answers what the picker may offer | Checklist 15. The alternative was the page re-deriving "not the four core keys, not a `*_log_level`", which is `guides.refused_setting`'s rule spelled a second time in JavaScript. It is sent to staff only; a member gets two empty lists |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guide_confirmed`) — `reading_member`, not `writer` | §C8: it is the one guide write a MEMBER makes. It takes from the read bucket, writes one routine row, and touches no guide row — there is nothing for a member to damage. The `_wanted` call still hides an unpublished or staff guide behind the same 404 |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` (`HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT`) — `guides` is NOT in it, and `guide.confirmed` cannot be on its own | §C10 asks for that one kind to be hidden like the self-test's. Measured at G2: `hidden_by_default_patterns()` builds from `like_patterns(feature)`, which is every kind head of a FEATURE — adding `guides` would hide every guide edit from the Logs page too. G2 deviation 2 |
| `site/public/assets/shell.js` (`guidesIndex`) — memoised, and it RESOLVES rather than throws | Three callers want the same list: the rail (to hide the item when guides are off for a member), `page-guides.js` (the hub itself and a guide's related list) and the Ctrl K palette. One request, and a refusal is data rather than an exception, because two of the three only want to know whether it refused |
| `site/public/assets/shell.js` (`MEMBER_TABS`) — a list, and `MEMBER_TAB` is its first | `app.js:refuseFor` sends a member who lands on a staff page somewhere they may be; that is still one destination, but "may they be here" is now a membership test. The `shell.js:4` comment that said "the one page" is rewritten |
| `site/public/assets/palette.js` (`all`) — the entry list is module state, not a closure | ⚠️ Found in the browser, not in the code: `open()` captured `index()` once and `input.oninput` closed over it, so the guide titles that arrive a microtask later repainted the open list and were then thrown away by the next keystroke. Typing "house" found nothing. Every repaint now reads the module list, and the late arrival refreshes it |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`full`) — `data-span="full"` on five blocks | `layout.js:mountColumns` balances `#dash` into two columns once there are two blocks in a run. Measured in the browser: it halved the Right now strip, the card grid and both halves of a guide. `wide()` honours `data-span` before anything else |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`goTo`) — sets the hash and lets `hashchange` repaint | Setting the hash AND calling `refresh()` reloads the page twice for one press. Going back to the hub has no hash to change, so that branch uses `replaceState` and refreshes itself |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`factsCard`) — one `setInterval`, cleared by `stopFacts` at every load | §C5: "re-reads every 60 s while open". The timer also stands itself down when its own node has left the document, which is what happens when a guide is opened and then the hub is |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`pictureControls`) — an upload is refused while the save bar is showing | The media POST lands immediately and the page has to reload to show it, which would throw away every unsaved word. The sentence says exactly that. A step with no `id` yet gets its own sentence: the bot has nothing to file the picture against |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`plain`) — the alt text has the `**` taken out | §C4.7 makes the alt the step's `do_text`, which is written with bold markers. They are typography; a screen reader should not read them |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`warningsBlock`) — the linter's warnings are staff-only | §C2's rules are editorial. A member reading a guide cannot act on "no control is named", and an amber note under a step reads as something being wrong with the step |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`whereOf`) — a guide with a command is "in Discord" | §C6's filter chips. There is no column for where a guide is done, and one would be a second home for a fact the `command` field already carries |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`settingsLink`) — a fact's key links to `settings.html` only for staff | The global refusal rule: prefer not drawing a control somebody cannot use. A member sees the key as plain text rather than a link to a page that would refuse them |
| `site/public/assets/site.css` (`.guidecard-title`) — `font-family: var(--et-font)` | `site-restyle-design.md` §2 keeps the display face for the wordmark and page titles, 20–26 px, never in a control. A card title inherits it from the global heading rule unless it says otherwise |
| `tests/api/tools/test_guides.py` (`test_the_hub_carries_the_strip…`) — asserts against the fixture's own `web.settings.test_mode` | Not a literal `True`. A test that hard-codes the test-mode flag passes for the wrong reason the day somebody flips it |

# Settings editor — the false "1 change pending" (v112, 2026-09-16)

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `site/public/assets/ui.js` `settingRow` → `paint` | An empty text box reads back `null` while the stored value is `""` (`chat_memory_model`'s default), so `same()` said the row had changed on every load and the save sent `null`, which the validator refuses in words — every save from the page reported "1 refused" (found by the capture session, 2026-09-16). A blank read against a blank stored value is now not dirty. |
| `ui.js` `keepUnlisted` (used by `channelSelect` / `roleSelect`) | The worse twin: a stored channel or role id that the picker's list does not carry (deleted from the server, or a cold cache) read back as `null`, counted as dirty, and the next **Save Changes** would have CLEARED it — measured on the mock, whose `chat_visibility_role_id` names a role its fixture list lacks. Such an id is now kept as a selected option labelled *a role the server no longer has · id*, so it reads back as itself; a person can still pick "not set" on purpose. |


# Posts (branch `posts`, off `main` at `193dac9`)

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `render_message`.** The design (§C2) says it answers
`{"content": body}` or `{"embed": Embed}`. It answers BOTH keys every time instead, with the
other one `None`. The reason is the edit path: a post whose style a staffer changes from
`embed` back to `plain` is `message.edit(**payload)`, and an edit that does not pass
`embed=None` leaves the old embed sitting under the new content. One function, one payload,
both doors.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `refused_title`.** Titles are REFUSED over 256, never clipped.
The first draft clamped with `clamp(title, TITLE_MAX)` and then checked the cap, which made the
check dead code and silently shortened what a staffer typed — the "validators silently
stripping instead of rejecting" bug the verification-culture rule names. The embed wording
offers the way out (set the style back to plain); the plain wording does not, because there is
no bigger title.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `body_hash` / `changes_pending`.** The pill compares a hash of
(style, title, body) as the row reads NOW against the hash taken at the moment the message was
sent. It is deliberately not a timestamp: an edit that puts a word back where it was leaves the
row identical to what Discord holds, and the pill goes away, which is the truth.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `allowed_mentions_for`.** Checklist 11. Nothing pings unless the
body names a role AND either that role is `mentionable` or the actor holds Mention Everyone. It
reads the ACTOR's permissions rather than the bot's, because the attacker-controlled text here
is the post body and the person who typed it is the one being held to it.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `_pin`.** Checklist 12. The row and its `post.posted` line are
written before the pin is tried, so `post.pin_failed` can never undo a post that did happen.
`reconcile_posts` re-pins one a person unpinned; an unpinned post (`pin = 0`) is left alone.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `note`.** Every kind this module writes goes through one helper
that builds the kind with `logkinds.kind_via` and records `details["via"]`, so the API routes
never `note()` on top (checklist 34) and `tests/test_logkinds.py`'s AST guards stay green. The
two kinds that do NOT go through it — `post.mode` and `post.seed_channel_unknown` — are
written as STRING LITERALS at their single call sites, which is what keeps them out of
`KNOWN_DYNAMIC`.

**`black_bloc/cogs/community/posts.py` — `_reconcile_loop`.** The first tick is where the
seed happens, not `cog_load`: at `cog_load` the gateway has handed over no guild, so
`bot.guilds` is empty and `seed_posts` has nothing to resolve `#welcome` against. Same shape as
`cogs/core.py`'s `guides_loop`. The loop also carries the five-minute reconcile (checklist 25).

~~**`black_bloc/cogs/community/posts.py` — `ModeButton`.**~~ **Retired 2026-09-16 by the
shadow build: the button is a `ModePick` SELECT now — see `# Posts — shadow` below.** What it
said stays true of the key: `/posts` is hidden when `posts_mode` is **off** only, so the panel's
own control can never bring it back from there; that is `/settings` ▸ **Turn a feature back
on…** or the Posts page's own switch, the same shape every other `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` feature has.

**`site/public/assets/discordmd.js` — the order of the passes.** `escapeHtml` runs FIRST and
everything after it works on escaped text. That is why the mention patterns read
`&lt;#(\d+)&gt;` rather than `<#(\d+)>`: by the time they run, the angle brackets are already
entities, and there is no path by which raw markup reaches the output. Anything already rendered
(code, mentions, links) is parked behind a `\u0000N\u0000` marker so the span pass cannot reach
inside it and turn a URL's underscores into italics.

**`site/public/assets/discordmd.js` — links.** A masked link renders as `<span class="md-link"
title="…">` and never an anchor. A preview of text somebody else typed is not a place to click:
an anchor here would be a phishing surface on a staff-only page, and the `title` is enough to
read the address. §D.3 is the one line that flips it back.

**`site/public/assets/discordmd.js` — embed style.** `renderDiscord(..., {style: 'embed'})`
does not draw `#` headers, matching what Discord does with an embed description; `-#` subtext
still renders, because that one does. `renderPreview` adds the embed box around it.

**`site/public/assets/page-posts.js` — `refs()`.** The three `/api/ref/*` lists are read once
per page load and handed to every render, rather than re-read per keystroke. The preview is
re-rendered on a 60 ms timer so a fast typist does not run the renderer per character.

**`site/mock/discordmd.test.mjs`.** The renderer is the only part of this site with no Python
half, so its fixtures are a Node file rather than a pytest one. It reads
`black_bloc/posts_seed.json` directly, which is what makes "the seed still renders its header
and its three quotes" a real assertion rather than a copy of the text.


# Posts — shadow (branch `posts-shadow`, off `main` at `440c0c6`)

> Keyed by NAME, not by line: this branch moves most of `posts.py` and every number would be
> wrong at the merge. Why each call was made is [`posts-design.md`](posts-design.md)'s
> `## Shadow-mode deviations` foot; it is not repeated here.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `mode_of`.** An unknown value reads as **shadow**, not as `on` and
not as `off`. The registry refuses a fourth value, so an unknown one can only arrive from a
hand-edited row or a restore — and the safe reading of "I do not know what this says" is the
one that keeps the message off members' screens while still letting staff see it. `off` would
have been wrong for the opposite reason: it would silently hide `/posts`.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `shadow_channel_id` vs `shadow_channel_ids`.** Two functions on
purpose, and they are NOT interchangeable. The singular is where a rehearsal GOES: the guard's
own channel while it is installed, else `log_channel_id`. The plural is where a rehearsal
already IS, and it is a LIST because the cutover (`cutover-plan.md` P5) **lifts the guard**
between the rehearsal and the real post — resolve once at delete time and the copy in
`#blackbloc-logs` is stranded for ever with its id cleared off the row. Checklist 3: a thing
that was done must be undoable whatever the mode says at reversal time. `_shadow_message`
hunts the id through all of them; `_drop_shadow`, `take_down_post` and `reconcile_posts` all
go through it, and only `publish_post`'s send uses the singular.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `is_posted` now means "a copy is up SOMEWHERE".** It answers true
for a real message, a shadow copy, or both. That one change is what carries `changes_pending`,
`status_words`, `move_label` and `remove_post`'s "take it down first" refusal into shadow
without a second hash column: there is still exactly one `posted_hash`, and `posted_where`
(`"channel"` / `"shadow"` / `None`) says which copy it describes. The alternative —
`shadow_posted_hash` — would have been a second column, a second write path and a second way
for the pill to disagree with itself.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `forget_message` vs `clear_posted`.** `forget_message` drops ONE
id and only clears the posted stamp once neither id is left, because the stamp belongs to
whichever copy is still up. `clear_posted` is the take-down: everything goes at once. A 404 on
either copy goes through `forget_message`, so losing the rehearsal never blanks the hash that
describes the real message.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `_drop_shadow` keeps the id when the delete FAILS.** The real post
is already sent and written down (checklist 12), so the failure is logged as `post.post_failed`
with the reason and the function returns without clearing `shadow_message_id`. Clearing it
would strand a message nobody can now find; keeping it means the next **Post it** tries the
delete again. The success and the 404 are different kinds on purpose — `post.shadow_taken_down`
and `post.shadow_message_gone` — because the owner's verification method is reading the log.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `publish_post` refuses `off` from the MODULE, not from the cog.**
The panel already gated on the mode; the website's **Post it** did not, and only carried an
amber note. One gate in the shared move closes both doors and is what `post.mode` off means.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — shadow does NOT require the post's own channel.** `no_channel` is
only raised on `on`. Shadow never touches `channel_id`, so refusing for want of one would be a
refusal about something shadow does not do — and the whole point of the default is that a
staffer can see the message before deciding where it goes.

**`black_bloc/posts.py` — `SHADOW_LINE` / `SHADOW_LINE_NOWHERE` / `SHADOW_LINE_SAME`, and
their JS twins.** Three spellings because two of them would read as nonsense: a post with no
channel cannot be told "not #nothing", and a post already aimed AT `#blackbloc-logs` — which is
exactly what §C9's old workaround told staff to do — must not read `not #blackbloc-logs`. The
same three sentences exist in `page-posts.js` as `WILL_SHADOW*`, which is the base build's own
split (Discord's card is written in Python, the site's line is written live from the draft) and
is held together by a test on each side rather than by a shared payload.

**`black_bloc/logkinds.py` — why the four shadow kinds are not silenced.** `SHADOW` in that
module is the string `".would_"`, not the word "shadow", so `post.shadow_posted` is free to be
IMPORTANT. It should be: a shadow publish is a real message really sent, unlike a `would_` line,
which is a thing that did not happen.

**`black_bloc/cogs/community/posts.py` — `ModePick` sits at row 2, and the root lost a
button.** Three values do not fit a two-state button, so it is the golive-shaped select
(`cogs/content/golive.py` `ModePick`) with `Posts are: {mode}`. Discord allows five action rows
and one select each: root row 0 is the three buttons plus the site link, row 1 is **A post…**,
so the mode goes to row 2.

**`site/mock/check.mjs` — `seed()` turns `posts_mode` ON, and `checkPostsModes()` is separate.**
Every contract route and every `web.post.*` kind is the `on` shape, and the GUARDED entry for
`/publish` only means anything when the post's own channel is the target — in shadow it reaches
the channel the guard allows and answers 200. `tests/api/test_contract.py`'s seeded fixture does
the same thing for the same reason, and `tests/api/tools/test_posts.py` has an autouse fixture
that does it per test. All three are the same decision in three places because the three
fixtures are separate; shadow has its own tests in each.

**`tests/test_posts.py` — `FakeChannel(first_id=…)`.** Message ids no longer repeat across
the fake channels. A shadow copy is hunted BY ID through several channels, and with every
channel starting at 9000 the hunt found the ACTION LOG's own message in `#bot-log` and reported
the rehearsal alive. Discord's snowflakes are globally unique, so the fake was the thing that
was wrong — but it was wrong in a way that made a real bug look fixed.


# Modmail doors (branch `modmail-doors`, off `main` at `4d60f68`)

⚠️ **Keyed by NAME, not by line** — this block was written against a branch that had not merged,
so every key below is the construct's name in its file. `docs/info/modmail-doors-design.md`
`## Deviations` carries the fifteen places the build differs from its design.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `open_or_find` / `make_place` / `post_header` /
`record_inbound` came OUT of the cog, and that is the whole safety argument.** Three new doors
had to reach the path a DM takes. They were `Modmail._open_or_find`, `._make_place`,
`._post_header` and `._relay_inbound` — methods, so a module-level door could not call them
without a cog instance. They are module functions now and the methods are one-line delegates;
`_inbound` is unchanged in behaviour, and **every DM test in `tests/cogs/moderation/test_modmail.py`
passed unedited**, which is the proof the relay did not move.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `open_a_ticket` is the only door body.** The command,
the posted button and **Open a ticket with…** all call it: bot → off → blocked → already open →
`open_or_find` → the first message. The member doors write the paragraph as an INBOUND row
(`record_inbound`, the same three calls `_relay_inbound` makes); the staff door sends it as the
first staff reply through `send_reply`, so a staff-opened ticket's first line is already in the
member's DMs. Every refusal leaves one quiet `modmail.open_refused` row carrying the reason word.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `open_with_refusal` asks the three questions BEFORE
the modal.** A modal cannot be refused politely: Discord has already taken the paragraph by the
time `on_submit` runs. So the `UserSelect`'s callback asks bot / off / blocked / already-open
first, and only then sends the modal. The same checks stay inside `open_a_ticket` for the race,
and the refusal path re-renders the root with **Unblock them** on it (staff final say).

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `_repanel` and `_panel_shadowed`.** The reconciler's
third job: a posted ticket button somebody deleted by hand gets another. It logs `modmail.panel_gone`
only when it is actually about to re-post, and its `modmail.would_post_panel` is written ONCE per
guild per process, because a five-minute loop that cannot post would otherwise write that row
forever. The deliberate doors log every time — somebody is waiting for that answer.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `post_ticket_panel` writes the new id before deleting
the old message.** Checklist 12, the same contract `post_card` keeps: if the delete fails the
guild has two buttons and both work (the `custom_id` carries the guild id, not the message);
if the write failed first, the old message would be an orphan nothing could ever take down.
`drop_panel_message` asks `guard.allows_channel` by hand, because deleting a MESSAGE is a side
effect `guard.py` never sees.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `TicketButton`'s `custom_id` carries the GUILD id.**
`modmail:ticket:{guild_id}`, one button per guild, so re-posting it is free and a message that
survived a deploy still works. It is registered in `cog_load` beside `TicketCardButton`.

**`black_bloc/modmail.py` — `TICKET_SOURCES` is not `SOURCES`.** `SOURCES` is what a REPLY
carries in its log details; `TICKET_SOURCES` is which door a TICKET came in by. `command` is in
both and means the same thing in each. `ticket_source()` answers `dm` for any row older than the
column, which is right: the DM was the only door there was.

**`black_bloc/modmail.py` — `door_buttons` is the row the owner asked for.** *"basically for
modmail, anyone can make it, if youre a staff when you do a /modmail you see more than just
create"* (2026-09-16). One table, one row 0, and staff get the same first control a member does
plus **Open a ticket with…**. `root_buttons` re-rows its own moves to 2 and 3 so the select can
have row 1 to itself.

**`black_bloc/modmail.py` — `last_reply_missed` reads the NEWEST out row, not any of them.** A
ticket where one reply bounced a week ago and three have landed since is not a ticket that cannot
be reached. The card's ⚠️ line is about the last thing that was tried.

**`black_bloc/settings_store.py` — `modmail_panel_message_id` is `text`.** A message id is a
snowflake (~1.4e18) and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is 9.0e15, so an `int` key hands the dashboard a
mangled id — `api/settings_api.py` `as_json` already says exactly this about channel and role ids.
While it was `int` the settings row also sat permanently CHANGED with *"1 change pending"*, the
third instance of the family `# Settings editor — the false "1 change pending"` above records.

**`black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` — `/modmail` carries `extras={"staff_only": False}`.**
Dropping `default_permissions` is what Discord shows; `is_staff_command` is what `/help` reads,
and it answers True for anything whose callback mentions `require_staff` — which this one still
does, for the branch where `modmail_member_command` is off. The `extras` entry is checked first,
so `/help` stops calling a command anybody can run a staff command.

**`site/public/assets/page-modmail.js` — `panelSettings()` asks for the settings FRESH.** The
Ticket button card reads `modmail_panel_channel_id` out of the settings payload, and the two
routes write that key server-side without going through `saveSetting`, which is what usually
clears the cache. `settings(true)` is the one place that matters; without it the card says the
button is still where it was.

# Guides — mark all stale (branch `guides-stale`, off `main` at `c6a341a`)

> Keyed by **NAME**, not by line. Why each call was made this way is
> [`guides-design.md`](guides-design.md) and its `### Mark-all-stale` sub-list; it is not
> repeated here.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`mark_all_stale`) — no `reason`, and no row of its own | Its sibling `mark_stale` does not log either: the boot path's row is written by `cogs/core.py` (`_mark_stale_shots`) and this one's by the route. Checklist 34 is the hard edge — a shared path that logs makes the route's `note()` a double-post, and `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_a_route_never_notes_an_event_its_shared_path_already_logged` walks the AST for exactly that. `reason` has no column on `guide_media`, so it lives only on the row |
| `black_bloc/guides.py` (`mark_all_stale`) — `WHERE stale = 0`, and the count is what it CHANGED | Not `WHERE 1`. A second press must be able to answer "every screenshot was already marked", and re-stamping `stale_since` on a picture marked a week ago would reorder the capture session's to-do list (`stale_media` sorts by it) for no reason |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guides_stale_all`) — registered above `GET /media/{media_id}`, and so above every `/{slug}` route | FastAPI matches in registration order. Declared after `guide_one`, `POST /api/guides/stale/all` still would not collide (the third segment is a literal `all`, not `media`/`reset`/`confirmed`) — but the ordering is what makes that true by construction rather than by luck, and `test_stale_all_is_never_read_as_a_guide_called_stale` holds it |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guides_stale_all`) — `payload: dict[str, Any] \| None = None` | The sibling writes take a required `payload`. This one's only field is optional, so a press with no body at all is a legitimate press; a required dict would answer 422 with a bare FastAPI validation body, which is the one thing a person must never see |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/guides.py` (`guides_stale_all`) — three sentences, not one with a count | `1 screenshots` is the kind of thing that makes a person distrust the number beside it. `ALREADY_ALL_STALE` is the zero case; `ONE_STALE_SAID` and `ALL_STALE_SAID` are the same sentence in two numbers |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`loadHub`) — the stale section is drawn for staff whatever `payload.stale` says | It used to be `if (payload.stale)`. None-stale is precisely the state the cutover presses the button in, so the old guard hid the control at the only moment it was wanted. `count: payload.stale \|\| null` keeps the pill off a zero |
| `site/public/assets/page-guides.js` (`markAllCard`) — `keepSaying('guide', say)` BEFORE `refresh()` | The refresh redraws the whole hub and throws the notice away with it; `loadHub` opens with `sayAgain('guide', notice())`, which is where the sentence lands. Same pattern as **Make it** on the New guide card |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (`state.guideMedia`) — a second seed picture, on `house-rules`, `stale: false` | With one already-stale picture the mock could only ever answer the zero sentence, so no browser pass could exercise the move. `nextGuideMedia` moves to 3 with it, and `house-rules` step 3 now points at it |

# Pings remake — the streamer list, lazy roles, raid trains and onboarding (branch `pings-remake`, off `main` at `337d22a`)

Keyed by NAME rather than by line, so the merge that lands this does not have to re-key it.
Design: [`pings-remake-design.md`](pings-remake-design.md); its `## Deviations` foot carries the
eighteen things that were built differently and every number the build actually measured.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py` (`SCHEMA`, `streamers`) — `hidden_by` is the column that tells a person's hide apart from a staleness prune | The design gives the table one `listed` flag and one `hidden_by`, and needs three states out of them. `listed = 0` with `hidden_by` SET is somebody's decision, and `saw_streaming` never undoes it; `listed = 0` with `hidden_by` NULL is the 90-day prune, and one more go-live re-lists them. A fourth column would have been a second home for a fact these two already carry |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py` (`ADDED_COLUMNS`, `golive_fan_roles.unworn_since`) | §C2's "a role nobody wears for N days" needs a clock, and `created_at` is the wrong one — a role worn for a year then abandoned would have been deleted on the next sweep. The sweep stamps this the first time it sees the role empty and clears it the moment somebody wears it again |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`saw_streaming`) — returns `True` only on the FIRST sighting | The caller's only question is "is this a new streamer?", which is what decides whether `pings.streamer_seen` is written. Every later go-live is an UPDATE with `live_count + 1` and no log line, so the Logs page carries one row per streamer rather than one per stream |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`saw_streaming`) — `COALESCE(?, platform)` / `COALESCE(?, login)` | A presence-only go-live knows neither, and a later Twitch one knows both. Writing the NULL over a known login would lose it every other stream |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`drop_unworn_fan_role`) — re-reads `role.members` immediately before the delete | Both prunes and the member's own opt-out go through this one function, and all three are places where "nobody wears it" was decided earlier in the call. Reading it again here is what makes "never delete a role somebody wears" true by construction rather than by the caller being careful |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`days_old`) — an unparseable timestamp is never old enough | Checklist 5. A row whose `last_live_at` somebody edited by hand should sit on the list forever, not be swept on the next tick. `parse_ts` returning `None` is the same answer as "not yet" |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`prune_empty_roles`) — a role Discord no longer has is SKIPPED, not pruned | That is `pings.fan_role_missing`'s job and the card's **Make the role again**. Deleting the row here would take the repair away |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`follow_from_list`) — reads the LISTING first and the role second | The select is over the list now, so the stale case is somebody who came OFF the list between the render and the press. A role that was tidied away in the meantime is not stale at all — it is simply remade, which is what `ensure_fan_role` does when the row exists but the role does not |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`followable`) — leaves the caller themselves off | A streamer following their own role would wear it and then be pinged by their own go-live. There is no refusal for it because the option is never offered |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`following`) — over the ROLES worn, never over the list | **Stop following…** is access-REDUCING, so it has to work for somebody whose streamer has since been hidden, pruned or left the server. Reading the list here would make the way out disappear with the way in |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`all_feeds`) — the raid-train toggle is a third FEED, not a fourth kind of button | `set_event_pings`, `feed_role_id`, `FEED_WORDS`, `notification_lines` and `events_move` all took a feed already, for the split events/go-live case. Adding `RAID_FEED` to the same table got the toggle, its line, its refusal and its log row for nothing, and keeps `pings.events_on`'s `details["feed"]` the one place that says which |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`packed`, `free_slot`) — rows are computed, not constants | The busiest staff state is twelve buttons plus the site link, and `PanelMove.row` was fixed. The first attempt packed the staff block from its own index 0 and put six on row 2, which `discord.ui` refuses at construction time with `item would not fit at row 2` — a crash at render, not a warning. `free_slot` is what carries "how many are already on that row" across the two blocks |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`panel_buttons`) — a WORN feed renders its "off" half even with the mode off | The mode gates the `NOT_WORN` branch only. Same rule as **Stop following…** and **Take me off the streamer list**: an access-REDUCING move never needs a switch, and a feature switch that traps somebody in a ping is the wrong default |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`panel_state`) — `streamers`/`mine` are OPTIONAL arguments | The parametrised cog test and two older tests build the state without them, and so does anything that only wants the roles half. With `streamers` passed, `unfollowed` counts what the select will actually offer; without it, it keeps its old meaning |
| `black_bloc/pings.py` (`setup_raidtrain_role`) — the role name is a constant, not a key | §C7 adds no `pings_raidtrain_role_name` sibling to `pings_events_role_name`. Staff who want another name pick an existing role in the same `RolePick` the Events set-up uses, so the case is covered without a sixth key |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` — a module of its own, not more of `pings.py` | `pings.py` was already 987 lines before this build. The house rule is one behaviour per module; this one imports `pings` and nothing imports it back, so there is no cycle. The design calls it `pings.reconcile_onboarding`; it is `pings_onboarding.reconcile` |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`ours`) — ownership is EXACT TITLE, never a prefix | The design says "title prefix", which would have read as *"What should ping you? Which streamers?"* on a member-facing screen. The cost is that a foreign prompt titled exactly *Which streamers?* would be adopted; the staff sub-panel lists what the bot claims and **Stop managing onboarding** is the way out |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`as_shape` / `normalised`) — the diff compares TITLES and ROLE IDS, never Discord's objects | `edit_onboarding` re-numbers every prompt by its position on the way out (`p.to_dict(id=i)`), so ids change on a write that changed nothing else. Comparing ids would have made every sweep write, and writing every five minutes is exactly what §C5 says not to do |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`reconcile`) — passes `prompts=` and NOTHING else | Measured in `discord/http.py:edit_guild_onboarding`: the payload is built key by key and anything `None` is omitted, so a call that names only `prompts` sends only `prompts` and Discord keeps the default channels, `enabled` and `mode` as it had them. ⚠️ That is a fact about the library; what Discord does with a partial PUT is not documented anywhere the build could read |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`reconcile`) — refuses BEFORE reading Discord when there is nothing to say | Discord will not take a prompt with no options on it, so a guild with no Events role, no raid-train role and no fan roles must not be asked. `NOTHING_REASON` is a separate answer from `UNCHANGED_REASON` because the sub-panel says different words for each |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`take_over`) — idempotent by reading `menu["message_id"]` | There is no "have we taken over yet" key. The post is either up or it is not, and `unpost` returning `False` is what stops a second `pings.onboarding_took_over` row. That also means a staff member who re-posts the Notifications menu by hand gets it taken down again on the next sync, which is the honest behaviour |
| `black_bloc/pings_onboarding.py` (`last_sync`) — reads `action_log`, not a new key | One fact, one home. The sync already writes `pings.onboarding_synced`; a second timestamp key would be a thing to drift |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py` (`_note_streaming`) — called from `_go_live_once`, which is the ONE place both doors meet | `on_presence_update` → `_go_live` and `poll_once` → `_go_live` both land here, inside `self._lock(member.id)`, so "one upsert per go-live, never a second row" is true without a second lock |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py` (`_note_streaming`) — wrapped in a bare `except` | The streamer list is a side record. A DB hiccup while writing it must not stop the announcement it is standing beside; the log line says what happened |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py` (`_note_streaming`) — the call site is above the opt-out, the role filters and the cooldown | F-PR2 decided "anyone Discord shows streaming", and §C1 says the announcement opt-out "is a different thing". Below the cooldown, a throttled streamer's `last_live_at` would stop moving and the 90-day prune would lie about them |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` (`Pings.cog_load`) — the sweep starts here, not in `__init__` | `tasks.Loop.start()` wants a running event loop, and every cog test builds `Pings(bot)` synchronously. Same shape as `golive`, `raidtrain` and `posts` |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` (`sweep_guild`) — the stale prune runs BEFORE the role prune | Deliberate, and asserted: a streamer pruned off the list drops their unworn role in the same move, so the pair leaves ONE log row (`pings.streamer_pruned` with `role_deleted`) rather than that plus `pings.role_pruned` for the same role |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` (`onboarding_preview`) — builds a `Result` from the TABLES and never calls Discord | Opening the staff sub-panel must not write, and must not cost an API round trip inside the three-second interaction window. What Discord currently holds is a different question, and `Sync now` is the button that asks it |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` (`streams_now`) — being on the streamer list now counts | Before this build the only signals were a linked channel and a seen session. Somebody Discord showed streaming is on the list by definition, so **Start my own ping role** appears for them without a Twitch link |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/pings.py` (`NumbersModal.on_submit`) — every field is read before any is written | A modal that saved the first two and refused the third would leave the settings half-changed with no way to tell which half. `run_settings` then coerces them all through `save_settings`, so a number outside its bound is still one sentence and no write |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py` (`_post`) — gained a `mentions` override | Everything else this feature posts mentions the static ping role, which is what `_mentions` builds. The moved line mentions two roles, one of which changes per slot, so the caller hands the list down rather than `_post` learning the feature's rules |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py` (`moved_mentions`) — a separate function from the text | The same list is needed twice: once to render `<@&…>` into the line and once to build `allowed_mentions`. Deriving it twice is how the two drift, and checklist 11 is about exactly that pair |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py` — `rolemenu` is in `NEVER_HIDDEN` as well as absent from `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` | Belt and braces on purpose. `hidden_names` filters `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF`'s names through `NEVER_HIDDEN`, so the entry alone would do it; the `NEVER_HIDDEN` line is what stops a later session putting `rolemenu_mode` back in the map without noticing why it left |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py` (`EXTRA_MODES`) — gains `rolemenu_mode` | `FEATURE_MODES` is derived from `HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF`, so taking `rolemenu` out of the hide table would have taken its row off the Settings panel's mode block too. `chat_memory_mode` and `modmail_enabled` are there for the same reason |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/pings.py` (`pings_list_set`) — one route hides AND restores, on a `listed` body field | Two routes would have been two spellings of one decision, and the site's button is already one button whose label flips. The refusal for "already that way" is the shared function's, so both directions say the same kind of sentence |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/pings.py` — `POST /onboarding/sync` is NOT in `contract.json` | It answers 409 in words on any guild without `COMMUNITY`, which is every guild the contract runner can build, and the runner asserts 200. `tests/api/tools/test_pings.py` covers both of its refusals instead |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js` (`onboardingCard`) — no managed switch on the card | `modeSwitch` reads `spec.choices`, and `pings_onboarding_managed` is a bool with none, so the first attempt rendered an empty box. The switch lives once, in the settings block below, and the card names where |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (`onboardingPrompts`) — `community` is hard-coded `false` | The mock is not a Discord guild and never will be. Answering `false` is what makes the browser pass show the honest half of §C5: the refusal, the fallback sentence and the "Not written yet." line |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (`state.golive.streamers`) — four seeded rows, deliberately unlike each other | One listed with a role and followers, one listed with no role yet, one whose role was deleted by hand, and one hidden by their own press. Every column of the new table has a non-default value somewhere, so a browser pass can see whether each renders |

# Modmail — the Open-a-ticket-with hide toggle (branch `modmail-hide`, off `main` at `91bee8a`)

Keyed by NAME rather than by line, so the merge that lands this does not have to re-key it. The
decision and the three stale windows are `modmail-doors-design.md` `## Deviations` ▸ *Hide toggle
(v117)*; this table is only why each call was made the way it was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`door_buttons`) — a `open_with: bool` keyword, not a store read | The module is the pure half of modmail and every one of its callers hands it facts rather than a bot. Reading the registry here would make the one function that decides what the first row holds untestable without a fake store, and `tests/test_modmail.py` proves both ways with no fixtures at all |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`door_buttons`) — `staff and open_with and not picking`, in that order | `picking` still wins: a panel that is already showing the member select must not also show the button that raised it, whatever the key says. The key is an extra gate on that row, never a replacement for the existing one |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_with_on`) — one reader, beside `refuse_open` | Three places ask the same question (the render, the press and the door body) and a fourth would have been the modal. One function is what stops two of them drifting to `store.get(..., "modmail_open_with_button")` spelled slightly differently, and it lives next to the refusal it feeds rather than with the panel helpers |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_a_ticket`) — the toggle is checked FIRST, above `a_bot` | It is a fact about the door, not about the member; answering "that is a bot" to somebody whose door is switched off would be true and useless. It is also the gate a modal already on screen meets, so it has to hold whatever the member turns out to be |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_a_ticket`) — `refuse_open`, not a bare return | Every other refusal in this function leaves one quiet `modmail.open_refused` row with a reason word; `open_with_off` joins `a_bot` / `disabled` / `blocked` / `already_open`. A door that refuses silently is a door nobody can prove refused |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`run_open_with`) — a runner of its own rather than `open_root(picking=True)` | The press is the stale window the owner will actually meet: he turns the key off while a panel is open on his own screen. The runner re-renders the root (which then draws no button) and answers in words in the same interaction, so the panel and the sentence agree |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_with_refusal`) — the toggle is its first question too | It is the pre-modal half of `open_a_ticket`'s list and is documented as asking the same questions in the same order. A `UserSelect` left on screen is the second stale window; answering here is what keeps Discord from taking a paragraph it is going to throw away |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`OPEN_WITH_OFF`) — names the key AND both ways to it | The refusal rule: what happened, what it needs, how to get it. The key name is in the sentence because it is what somebody types into the Settings page's filter; `/settings` ▸ **A setting group…** ▸ modmail is the Discord half, and `/settings set-value` is deliberately not named (retired at v84) |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`MODMAIL_OPEN_WITH_BUTTON`) — in the doors block, and the default is spelled out | `default()` answers `None` for a bool it does not name, which reads as false and is right by accident. `if key == MODMAIL_OPEN_WITH_BUTTON: return False` is what makes it right on purpose, and what a reader finds when they ask which way round it ships |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` (`modmail_open_with_button`) — seeded at `false`, the same as its default | Every other seeded row in the mock differs from its default so the browser can see a stored value. This one is the state the owner is actually in, and the Modmail page's job here is to show the switch off and let it be turned on |
## Go-live once the stream is over — the past-tense rewrite (branch `golive-end`, off `main` at `fb1600b`; design `info/golive-end-design.md`)

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/golive.py:252` (`tidy`) — runs on every filled end wording | An empty `{duration}` or `{platform}` leaves a hole the reader sees: `streamed for .`, `was live on`, `()`. `tidy` closes the four shapes that hole takes — empty brackets, a dangling connector before punctuation or end of line, a doubled space, a space before a full stop — and nothing else. It is deliberately not a markdown pass |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:54` (`DANGLING`) — a fixed word list, not "the last word" | `for on in at — – ·` are the words a wording puts in front of a placeholder. Stripping any trailing word would eat a real sentence's last word the moment somebody writes one that ends in a placeholder-free clause |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:260` (`humanise_duration`) — minutes first, then hours | Anything under a minute reads "under a minute" rather than "0 min", and a negative span (clock skew, a row edited by hand) lands there too instead of "-3 min". A missing or unreadable stamp renders as the empty string, which `tidy` then cleans up — never a raise, because this runs inside the message edit |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:279` (`as_info`) — takes a `StreamInfo` **or** a session row | The edit happens long after the announcement, when the only record of the game and url is the `golive_sessions` row. One renderer serves both callers rather than the cog rebuilding a `StreamInfo` by hand |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:318` (`ended_render`) — falls back to `ended_text`, never to the default template | `render` falls back to `GOLIVE_TEMPLATE` because a live announcement with no wording is worse than the shipped one. The opposite is true here: the message already exists and says something true in the present tense, so an unreadable rewrite keeps it and appends the suffix (checklist 17) |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:318` (`ended_render`) — `keep_mention` governs the blank path too | §A reads "blank keeps the live sentence and appends the suffix as before" and §B reads "the mention prefix is stripped unless `keep_mention`"; those two disagree about a blank template. One rule is easier to explain and it is the one the owner asked for ("let's not tag a role"), so the key wins in both shapes. `golive_end_keep_mention` true is literally-as-before |
| `black_bloc/golive.py:343` (`ended_author`) — an author line that renders to nothing keeps today's | `set_author(name="")` is not a card anybody wants to look at, and a template of `{platform}` on a presence-only stream renders to exactly that |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py:1166` (`_mark_ended`) — takes `ended_at` from the caller | `end_session` has already written it, but re-reading the row costs a query for a value the caller is holding. Both callers (`_end_live`, `_close_session`) now compute `now_iso()` once and pass the same string to both, so the stored `ended_at` and the rendered length can never disagree |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2988` (`TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK`) — two keys may store `""` | Every other text key refuses blank, because a blank template is a silently broken feature. These two carry a MEANING when blank (keep the live sentence, keep "was live on"), which the design fixes, so the validator has to let them through. ⚠️ Emptying a settings row on the site does NOT store blank — `ui.js` clears the override and the default comes back; the Wording card's own button is the way to blank it |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/golive.py:203` (`preview_payload`) — calls `render`, `ended_render`, `ended_author`, `ended_footer` | The page had a second renderer (`fillTemplate` in `ui.js`), which was right for a preview that repaints as you type and wrong for "what does the bot actually send". The route is the answer to the second question, so nothing about the ending is spelled twice |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/golive.py:245` (`golive_preview`) — awaits the staff dependency a second time | The router-level dependency gates the route; awaiting it again is how a GET learns WHO is asking, so the sample carries the caller's own display name. `writer_dependency` would charge the write bucket for a read |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:973` (`botLine`) — reuses `.msg` / `.msg-head` / `.msg-body` | The modmail tab already draws a bot line in those classes and they live in `site.css`, which this branch does not touch |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:984` (`withRoleNames`) — replaces `<@&id>` for display only | The route returns exactly what Discord is sent, mention and all, because the whole point of the card is seeing the `@Events` disappear.
