Discord draws the name; this draws it too rather than showing the reader a number |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:991` (`shapeButton`) — one button, two directions | "Rewrite it" and "just add the ending" are one decision, so they are one control whose label flips, the way the streamer list's Hide/Restore button does. Blanking goes through `PUT` with `""`; going back is `DELETE`, which restores the shipped wording rather than guessing at it |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:1012` (`wordingPreview`) — a Refresh button beside the save hooks | The card repaints when the stream-end mode saves and when a settings row saves (the page reloads), but the wording editor above it saves through `templateEditor`'s own docked bar, which `ui.js` gives no `onSaved`. Rather than reach into a shared file for one hook, the card says what it reads and offers the press |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:3887` (`fillWording`) — a second, shorter renderer on purpose | The mock is a copy of every answer shape by design; it is checked against `contract.json`, not against the Python. Keeping it short is what stops it drifting into a competing implementation |

# Polls — shadow, a channel per poll, pinned while open (branch `polls-shadow`, off `main` at `905982b`)

Keyed by NAME rather than by line, so the merge that lands this does not have to re-key it. The
decisions and the two things the design measured wrong are `polls-shadow-design.md` `## Deviations`;
this table is only why each call was made the way it was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` — a module of its own, and `posts.py` is NOT pointed at it | The design said "if a shared helper falls out, put it in `black_bloc/shadow.py` and have both call it". Half of that landed: the module exists and polls calls it, but `posts.py` belongs to a build running in the same tree and was left alone. `tests/test_shadow.py::test_posts_and_this_module_answer_the_same_question_the_same_way` is the guard that stops the two copies drifting until somebody folds them |
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` (`guild_id_of`) — a guild OR an id | `fetch_poll_message` has a row and no guild, and a row carries `guild_id`. Posts' copy takes only a guild, so widening here is the one deliberate difference between them |
| `black_bloc/polls.py` (`mode_of`) — an unknown word reads as `on`, not `off` | The other two modes both change what a person sees. A typo in the registry that silently turned polls OFF would look exactly like the feature being broken, and the row that caused it would be invisible |
| `black_bloc/polls.py` (`shadow_note`) — catches `Exception`, falls back to the default line | Checklist 17. The note is staff-editable text with a `{channel}` placeholder; `"{nonsense}"` raises `KeyError` and `"{"` raises `ValueError`, and neither may cost the room its poll |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`post_poll`) — the copy's id goes in BOTH `message_id` and `shadow_message_id` | The §B fork. Votes, the reminder, the close, the results, the panel repaint and the gateway vote listener all already key on `message_id`; putting the rehearsal's id anywhere else would have made every one of them read "not posted". `shadow_message_id` is therefore a MARKER — "the copy this row has is a rehearsal, so look for it somewhere other than `channel_id`" — and never a second id to chase |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`where_it_went`) — one reader, seven callers | `channel_id` stopped being "where the message is" the moment shadow existed, and seven places asked it that question: the two guard checks around votes and voters, the close, the cancel, the live count, the card's move gate, the results and the last call. One function is what stops six of them being corrected and the seventh not |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`hunting_grounds`) — plural for the FETCH, singular for everything else | Deviation 3 of the posts build, met again: the cutover lifts the guard between the rehearsal and the real post, so a copy outlives the channel that resolution picks. Sending needs one answer; finding needs all of them |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`post_poll`) — the note is a PREFIX on the open line, not a replacement | `open_text` carries the ping role's mention and the creator's, and `mentions()` is what makes the ping legal. A shadow line that replaced it would have rehearsed a poll nobody was pinged about, which is the half of the rehearsal staff most want to see |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`post_poll`) — `poll.opened_shadow` carries BOTH ids | `channel_id` is where it would have gone and `shadow_channel_id` is where it went. One row that says both is what makes the Logs page answer "did the rehearsal point at the right place" without opening the poll |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`_pin`) — after the status is `OPEN`, never before | Checklist 12: the row is the important thing and the pin is the cosmetic one. A `Forbidden` here leaves `poll.pin_failed` and an open poll, which is what `test_a_pin_discord_refuses_is_a_log_row_and_the_poll_still_opens` proves rather than argues |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`_unpin`) — reads `message.pinned`, never `poll_pin` | Checklist 3: reversal must not depend on the setting at reversal time. Somebody turning `poll_pin` off while a poll runs must not strand the pin it already took |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`_post_results`) — the unpin is the FIRST line, above the guard's early return | The results card may legitimately not be posted (no channel, test mode); the pin still has to come off. Putting it after the return would have left every guarded poll pinned for ever |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`cancel_poll`) — unpins too, though the design only named close | A cancelled poll is not an open one. The design's §D says "pinned for its duration", and a cancel ends the duration |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`_drop_pin_notice`) — a five-message look-back matched on the REFERENCE | Discord's `pins_add` system message names the pinned message in `reference.message_id`. Matching on that rather than on "the newest system message" is what keeps a busy channel from having somebody else's pin notice deleted. Failure is one `log.info` and the notice stays, which is what the design asked for |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`CreateButton`) — `poll_channel_id` first, the current channel second | §C says the Where select defaults to `poll_channel_id`. The old behaviour (wherever `/poll` was run) stays as the fallback, so a server that has never set the key is no worse off than before |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/polls.py` (`PreviewView`, `picking`) — the select is not rendered for somebody who may not create | The permission rule read the other way: prefer not rendering a control somebody cannot use. The preview is reachable by a member whose server is staff-only for creating, and a channel picker on a poll they cannot post is a promise nobody keeps |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/polls.py` (`_refuse_outside_the_test_channel_id`) — takes the guild now | It has to ask `in_shadow`, and the mode is per-guild. The route already had the guild in hand; passing it is cheaper than reaching for `require_guild(bot)` a second time |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/polls.py` (`refuse_outside_the_test_channel`) — asks about `where_it_went` | Ending a rehearsed poll from the dashboard must reach the copy. Asking about `channel_id` would have refused every rehearsal in words, for a channel the poll never touched |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` — `poll.opened_shadow` is ROUTINE, beside `poll.opened` | `logkinds.SHADOW` is the string `".would_"`, so the shadow rule does not silence this one and the decision has to be made by hand. A rehearsal that really posted is exactly as loud as a poll that really posted, which is to say quiet; `poll.pin_failed` and `poll.unpin_failed` are IMPORTANT for free, by the `_failed` suffix |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`POLL_MODES`) — imported from `polls.py`, not declared twice | Checklist 15. `MODES` is the tuple the mode helpers read; the registry needs the same tuple, and two spellings of "off, shadow, on" is the shape that drifts |
| `tests/cogs/community/test_polls.py` (`FakeText.note_a_pin` / `history`) — the fake posts the notice the bot then deletes | Without it `_drop_pin_notice` would be a function no test ever entered. With it, `test_the_pin_notice_discord_adds_is_taken_away_again` asserts on what is LEFT in the channel, which is the thing a person would see |
| `tests/api/conftest.py` (`WebMessage.unpin`) — added beside `pin` | The website's end and cancel routes now reach `_unpin`. Without the method every one of them would have logged `poll.unpin_failed` and passed anyway, which is the silent-failure shape the log kinds exist to prevent |


# Blackmail — modmail and requests as forums, and the button under the rules (branch `blackmail-threads`, off `main` at `905982b`)

Keyed by NAME rather than by line, so the merge that lands this does not have to re-key it. The
design is `blackmail-threads-design.md`; its `## Deviations` holds what changed and why. This
table is only why each call was made the way it was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`forum_tags`, `tag_named`, `applied_tags`) — tags are looked up by NAME, never by a stored id | A `ForumTag`'s id is Discord's to hand out and changes if the tag is re-made. Keeping it in a key would give two homes for one fact and a dead id after any hand edit; the forum's own `available_tags` is the record, and a name that is not on it means no tag rather than a crash (`applied_tags` answers `[]`). It is the same reason the design said "never in a key" |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`THREADED_MODES`) — one tuple, not `mode in (THREAD_MODE, FORUM_MODE)` spelled twice | `open_or_find` decides `channel_id` and `thread_id` off it, and so does every reader that asks "does this ticket live in a thread". Checklist 15: a constant that exists in two modules is a bug, and this one nearly existed in two branches of the same expression |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`setup_buttons`) — the two forum moves are appended LAST and on row 3 | Discord allows five components a row. Rows 1 and 2 are already full (five and four), so the natural home would have overflowed the view and drawn nothing at all. Appending rather than inserting also leaves every existing row's order, which the door tests assert by label |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`make_forum_post`) — the starter message is `thread_invite`, and `post_header` then posts the dossier as message two | A forum post must be created WITH a first message, but `make_place` runs before the ticket row exists, so the header embed (prior tickets, roles, join date) cannot be built yet. Reusing thread mode's own staff line means one ping, in the one message that is guaranteed to exist, and the rest of the ticket machinery is untouched |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`make_forum_post`) — the post is `guard.own_channel`ed the moment it is made | A ticket post is a channel Black Bloc made itself, which is exactly what `guard.owns_channel` is for (the precedent is the practice thread and the temp-voice rooms). Without it `speak()` would redirect every relay to the test channel and the post would sit empty while the ticket looked fine |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`claim_forum`) — the sweep re-claims the forum, and only while `modmail_mode` is `forum` | A guard claim lives in the process that made it, so a deploy would otherwise break forum mode until somebody pressed **Make the forum** again. Requiring BOTH keys to point at it means widening test mode is a deliberate two-key act by a Lead, not something a stray channel id can do |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`FORUM_NOT_CLAIMED`) — names the sweep and its five minutes | The window it covers is real but short (boot with the database down, then a DM). Saying "try again in five minutes" is the honest instruction; saying "press Make the forum" as well covers the case where the mode is not `forum` yet and the sweep will never claim it |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`place_refusal`) — only the STAFF door gets the detailed sentence | A member who DMs must not be handed a Lead's setup instructions; `CANNOT_OPEN_DM` is what they see, unchanged. Staff pressing **Open a ticket with…** are the people who can act on "press Make the forum", so they are the ones told |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`may_remove`) — `or guard.owns_channel(parent_id)` | Archiving a forum post is an `edit_channel`, which the guard never sees, so `may_remove` is the by-hand ask. A post's parent is the forum, not the test channel, so without this every close would log `would_remove_place` and leave the post open and tagged `open` for ever |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`remove_place`) — the forum branch edits tags AND archives in ONE call | Two edits would be two rate-limited channel edits for one act, and a failure between them would leave a post archived but still tagged `open`. One `edit` is atomic from the reader's point of view |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`close_ticket`) — a forum ticket is disowned like a practice one | The owned set is in memory for the life of the process and would otherwise grow by one per ticket for ever. A closed post is archived, so nothing needs to write to it again |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`make_forum`) — reads `modmail_category_id` directly, NOT `ticket_category` | `ticket_category` deliberately redirects to the TEST channel's category while the guard is installed, which is right for a ticket channel and wrong for the forum: the design says the forum goes under Blackmail, test mode or not, because making a channel is not something the guard can see |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`make_forum`) — `dict(category.overwrites)` plus the bot's, rather than `ticket_overwrites` | The owner's ask was a channel with the same permission set as the rest of Blackmail. Building a fresh overwrite map from the staff roles would quietly diverge from the category the moment anybody edits the category by hand |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`FORUM_MADE_GUARDED`) — the reply says the forum is outside the test channel | Checklist 10: claiming a check that was skipped is a lie, and creation genuinely is not gated. The sentence is how a Lead learns that test mode did not stop this one, rather than finding out from the channel list |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`post_below_button`) — compares SNOWFLAKES, not fetch order | A Discord id counts up with the clock, so "is the rules message below the button" is one integer comparison against two stored ids. The alternative — reading the channel's history — costs an API call on every five-minute sweep and answers the same question |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`post_below_button`) — the shadow copy is checked too | `posts_mode` ships `shadow`, so on the day this is turned on the rules message in the guard's channel IS the one beside the button. Checking only the real copy would make the rehearsal the design asks for impossible to see |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`_repanel`) — `modmail.panel_below_post` is its own kind | Checklist 2: a button that somebody deleted and a button the rules overtook are different events with different causes, and the owner's verification method is reading the log. `panel_gone` would have said the message was missing when it is sitting there |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`on_post_published`) — a listener, not a call from `posts.py` | `posts.publish_post` is shared by `/posts`, the website and the boot seeder. `bot.dispatch` keeps posts ignorant of modmail, and the five-minute sweep is still the guarantee — the listener only makes it prompt |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`MODMAIL_PANEL_FOLLOWS_POST`) — `none`, not a blank string | `coerce_value` refuses empty text for a `text` key, and `clear()` puts the default (`welcome`) back, so "blank = never" was unreachable from the Settings page AND from `/settings`. A word both doors can actually type is what makes the decision configurable both ways (checklist 33) |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`FORUM_TAG_FOR`) — six tags, where the design named five | The design's list had no tag for `review`, so a request waiting to be checked would have worn **picked up** — the one state whose whole point is that it is NOT being worked on any more. `ready to check` is the sixth; `withdrawn` deliberately has none (see the Deviations) |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`post_title`) — `#<id> <what>`, capped at 100 | Discord bounds a thread name at 100 characters. Leading with the number means the forum's own list sorts and searches by the thing staff actually quote at each other, and the id survives a `what` long enough to be cut |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`thread_of`) — claims the post on the way out | Same reason as modmail's `claim_forum`, in the one place every writer already goes through. The requests cog has no sweep of its own, so the read IS the repair; the docstring says so rather than leaving a silent side effect |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`notify_move`) — the card is posted BEFORE the re-tag | Checklist 12: the card is the record staff read, the tag is decoration on top of it. Posting after the archive would also un-archive the post Discord had just closed |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`retag_post`) — archives but does NOT lock | Staff always get the final say (owner rule, 2026-09-03). An archived post reopens the moment anybody writes in it; a locked one needs a permission edit first, and there is no bot move that would reopen it for them |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`MakeForumButton`) — drawn only while there is no forum | The panels rule: a move is a button that renders only when it is valid, never a menu with two spellings of the same act. The refusal behind it still exists, because the website and a second staffer's open panel can both press it after the forum is there |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/modmail.py` / `requests.py` (`*_forum_make`) — call the cogs' own `make_forum` with `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and `note()` nothing | Checklist 34, the 2026-09-03 double-post defect: the shared path already logs, so one press leaves ONE `web.*.forum_made` row. The route's own job is the HTTP shape and nothing else |
| `tests/api/test_contract.py` (`seed_world`) — seeds `modmail_category_id` | Both **Make the forum** entries would otherwise answer 409 with a sentence about a key, which is correct behaviour and a useless contract check. The forum KEYS stay blank so each entry makes its own and neither meets the other's |

- `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` `forum_of` — claims the keyed forum for the test-mode guard on every read (v120): the key is the deliberate act that widens test mode for requests, as `modmail_mode = forum` is for modmail; without it every request under `TEST_MODE` was skipped (`blackmail-threads-design.md` § Found at the landing).
## Staff reach — every channel Black Bloc makes is the staff's to open and delete (branch `staff-reach`, off `main` at `4da192c`; design `info/staff-reach-design.md` §A)

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/spawned.py:12` (`staff_reach`) — one helper, called LAST by every builder | A builder that added the allow half-way through would have it taken back by whatever it did next (the `@everyone` deny, the owner's own overwrite, `apply_remembered_members`). Last is the only position where "a hidden room is still staff's" is true whatever the builder does afterwards. It mutates and returns the same dict so a builder can `return staff_reach(found, ...)` in place of `return found`. |
| `black_bloc/spawned.py:12` (`staff_reach`) — sets three flags and never clears one | `view_channel` / `manage_channels` / `connect` are written `True`; nothing is set to `False` or `None`, so a builder's own deny on a DIFFERENT permission (send, speak) survives, and a role that was already allowed keeps everything else it had. |
| `black_bloc/spawned.py:26` (`reach_roles`) — the key is read HERE, never in `staff_reach` | The helper is pure so it can be tested and reasoned about without a bot; the gate is one function the five call sites share, so the key cannot be honoured in four places and forgotten in the fifth. A `False` key returns `[]`, and `staff_reach` with no roles is a no-op — that is what "off leaves each builder's own permissions" means in code. |
| `black_bloc/spawned.py:26` (`reach_roles`) — takes `roles=` so the caller can hand in what it already resolved | `events.py` and `modmail.py` have already called `store.staff_roles(guild)` for the view+send allow; resolving them a second time would walk every role's computed permissions again for the same answer. tempvoice has no such list and passes nothing. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py:387` (`creator_overwrites`) / `:389` (`owner_overwrites`) — take `staff=` | The lobby and every spawned room. The roles arrive already gated by `reach_roles`, so neither builder reads a setting — they stay pure functions the parametrised tests can call directly. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py:720` (`join_roles`) — already returned the staff roles | ⚠️ **The design's §A measurement (*"temp voice rooms carry NO staff allow, so a hidden room is invisible to that role"*) was already false.** `join_roles` has returned `store.staff_roles(guild)` since `178fe69` (2026-08-26) and the caller passes it as `allow=`, so staff have had view + connect on the lobby and on every room all along. What §A actually adds for temp voice is **`manage_channels`**, and an allow that does not depend on the allowed-role plumbing. |
| tempvoice's lock / hide / ban / permit / hand-over paths — untouched | Every one of them is `channel.set_permissions(<one target>, …)` against `@everyone` or a member, never a whole-dict rewrite, so the staff allow cannot be taken back by any of them. The only path that re-writes the dict is `repair_creator_channel`, which builds it through `creator_overwrites` and therefore gets the allow back. |
| `black_bloc/events.py:1318` (`review_overwrites`) / `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:805` (`ticket_overwrites`) — `reach=` is a SECOND parameter beside `staff_roles` | The existing `staff_roles` allow (view + send) is what makes the room usable and is not the key's business; `reach` is the part the key governs. One parameter for both would have meant turning the key off also took staff's view of a ticket away. |
| Not in scope, deliberately: the honeypot trap (`cogs/moderation/honeypot.py:362`) and the two forums (`modmail.py:1774`, `cogs/community/requests.py:701`) | The trap is `@everyone`-visible by design — there is nothing to be shut out of. Both forums are created with a copy of the BlackMail category's own overwrites, which already allow the staff role (measured in the design's table: allow `117824`). §A names three builders and these are not among them. |

### §B — the BlackMail log gets a card when a ticket opens

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`log_open`) — reads the key, the channel and the guard in that order | The key first means a guild that has turned the card off never looks up a channel or writes a row; the guard last means the would-row carries the channel id, which is the one fact somebody reading it needs. It is the same four-step shape as `post_transcript` right below it, deliberately, so the two cannot drift. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`log_open`) — returns a reason string and never raises | It is called from `open_or_find`, inside a DM listener and inside three interaction callbacks. A raise there would leave a ticket that exists in the database with no card and an "application did not respond". Every exit is a log row: `modmail.log_open_failed` (which `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` classes as important, no registration needed) or `modmail.would_log_open` (the `would_` shadow prefix, same). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`log_open`) — a missing transcripts channel is a `log_open_failed` row, not silence | Mirrors `post_transcript`'s `no_log_channel`. A card that went nowhere should say so once per ticket rather than never; the alternative is a guild that quietly has no log and no way to notice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_or_find`) — `log_open` is the LAST thing the open does | Checklist 12: the ticket row, the place, the action-log row and the header all land first. The card is the cosmetic end of the open, so a Discord refusal there cannot cost anybody their ticket. `open_or_find` is also the ONE place all four doors meet (the DM through `_open_or_find`, and `/modmail` + the posted button + staff through `open_a_ticket`), which is what makes "once and once only" true without a call-count guard in four places. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`open_embed`) — footer `<name> | <user id>` | ⚠️ **Copied from the incumbent ModMail bot on purpose** (measured in `info/staff-reach-design.md`: six messages, all one shape, footer `<name> | <user id>`). Staff who have been searching that channel for two years keep finding tickets the same way. The rest of the card is ours; the footer is theirs. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`open_embed`) — `first_line(subject)` rather than the whole thing | The modal's subject box is one line by design, but a paste can carry more, and the card sits in a channel that is a list. The body is never on the card at all — it is in the ticket, which is where a member's words belong. |
| A practice ticket gets no card | `open_practice` has its own path and never reaches `open_or_find`. The incumbent's log holds real tickets only, and a practice ticket exists to be thrown away. |

### §C — three site items (the category on every picker, the ending's own editor, KI-28)

| Where | Note |
|---|---|
| `site/public/assets/labels.js` (`channelLabel`) — the channel label lives in `labels.js`, not in `ui.js` | It was a private function in `ui.js`, which cannot be imported outside a browser (`ui.js` reaches `document` through `api.js` at import time), so nothing could test it. `labels.js` is a leaf — no imports of its own — so `site/mock/labels.test.mjs` runs it under node, and `ui.js` re-exports it for the pages. Same rule as the key labels beside it: one home for what a thing is CALLED. |
| `site/public/assets/labels.js` (`categoryName`) — the field is `category_id`, not `parent_id` | ⚠️ The design says `/api/ref/channels` carries `parent_id`; measured, `api/names.py:channel_row` emits **`category_id`** (and `contract.json` lists it). Nothing was added to the route — the label reads the field that is already there. |
| `site/public/assets/labels.js` (`channelLabel`) — a category whose id is not in the list shows no suffix | The caller passes the same list the picker is drawn from, so a missing parent means the category is gone or filtered out. A name nobody can see is worse than no suffix, and `keepUnlisted`'s own `<said> · <id>` fallback is untouched. |
| `site/public/assets/page-events.js` (`whereControl`) — the Where picker lost its own two marks | It built the voice and text marks by hand inside its optgroups, which is a second copy of the one rule. It calls `channelLabel` now, so the categories arrive there too; the only visible change besides the category is a space after the `#`, which every other picker on the site already has. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` — the mock grew a **second** `modmail-log`, inside the `modmail` category | Every mock channel had `category_id: null`, so the mock could not show the thing this change is for. The new row is the owner's own confusion case (two `modmail-log`s, one at the top level and one under a category) and it is what the browser check looked at. |
| `site/public/assets/ui.js` (`templateEditor`) — takes a LIST of specs and an `onSaved` | Both wording keys belong to one decision, so they belong under one save bar; `settingsEditor` already accepted several specs and an `onSaved`, and `templateEditor` was passing neither. `paint(filled, key)` gained the key so one painter can serve several rows. ⚠️ A spec may carry `editorType` — `'text'` for the author's one-line input, `'longtext'` (the default) for the rest — which is how a one-line wording row is asked for without a second function. Checklist 35: this closes the gap `golive-end-design.md` deviation 8 recorded. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js` (`endWordingCard`) — an EMPTY box says what blank MEANS | Blank is a real, meaningful value for these two keys (`TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK`), not an unfinished edit: it means *keep the live sentence and add the suffix*. A preview that went blank with the box would read as broken. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js` (`WORDING_STALE`) — rewritten, not deleted | It used to tell the reader to press Refresh after saving the wording, which is now wrong — the card repaints itself. Refresh still earns its place for a change made on the Settings page or from Discord, and the line says which case is which. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` (`KeyModal.__init__`) — `required = key not in TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK` | KI-28, closed. The modal is shared by every typed key, so the flag has to be per key rather than per modal; `TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK` already existed as the registry's own answer to the same question (`coerce_value` reads it), so the modal asks the registry rather than carrying a second list. It is imported from `settings_store` and NOT re-exported through `settings_panel`, where it would have been an unused import. |

# Request posts carry the staff moves (branch `request-post-buttons`, off `main` at `f7cd19d`; design `blackmail-threads-design.md` §F)

Keyed by NAME as the Blackmail block above is, so the merge that lands this does not have to
re-key it; the `path:line` in each row is where it was at `1ad5ab0`. The design's `## Deviations`
holds what departed from §F and why; this table is only why each call was made the way it was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1435` (`PostMoveButton`) — a SECOND class beside `CardMoveButton`, which §F asked not to have | ⚠️ **Measured in `discord.py` 2.7.1, not assumed.** `ViewStore.remove_view` (`ui/view.py:970`) pops every dynamic TEMPLATE the view carried out of the global `_dynamic_items` registry, and `View.stop()` (`ui/view.py:650`) calls `remove_view` through `__cancel_callback`. The panel's card view is stopped on every re-render (`panels.retire`) and again on every timeout (`_dispatch_timeout`), so a `DynamicItem` living on the panel would DE-REGISTER the template for every forum post in the guild — the posts would go dead until something re-registered them, with nothing in any log. A timeout-bearing panel view therefore cannot host a dynamic item at all. `move_pressed` is what actually stops there being two implementations: both classes are ~10 lines and hold no behaviour. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1299` (`move_pressed`) — one function, two surfaces, an `on_post` flag | The panel and the post ask for the same DECISION and a different ANSWER: a component press on the panel defers with `deferred_message_update` and edits the message it came from, which on a post would overwrite the request card with a panel (Back button and all). `opened_here` and `finished` are the only two places the two diverge, and they are three lines each. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1189` (`opened_here`) — `defer(ephemeral=True, thinking=True)` for a post press | `thinking=True` is what makes discord.py send `deferred_channel_message` rather than `deferred_message_update` (`interactions.py`, `InteractionResponse.defer`), so `followup.send` writes a NEW ephemeral message and `edit_original_response` can never reach the post. Without it the press silently acknowledges and the staffer sees nothing. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:453` (`post_view`) — `card_buttons(status)` with `may_accept_here` left at its default | A forum post is ONE message for everybody, so there is no viewer to personalise for. `may_accept` is asked on the press instead, where it already lives: `apply_decision` answers `REVIEW_BY_SOMEBODY_ELSE`, which names who may accept. Rendering the button and refusing in words is the rule for a shared message; hiding it would hide it from the person who IS allowed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:453` (`post_view`) — the site link takes row 1 only when the moves fill row 0 | `review` draws five moves, which is Discord's whole row. Every other status draws two or three, and a link on its own second row there reads as a stray. `ROW_CAP` is the library's copy of the 5, beside the table that produces the moves. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:472` (`restyle_post`) — `thread.get_partial_message(id)`, never a fetch | The starter message's id is already on the row (`requests.message_id`, written by `open_forum_post`), so re-drawing the buttons costs one PATCH and no GET. A `PartialMessage` is enough because the edit replaces the components outright. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`notify_move`) — `restyle_post` runs BEFORE `retag_post` | `retag_post` archives the post at a decision, and editing a message inside an archived thread means un-archiving it first. Re-drawing the buttons while the post is still open costs nothing and leaves the archive the last thing that happens, which is also the order the card and the tag already went in. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:547` (`MOVE_BY_ACTION`) — one spec per ACTION, flattened out of `CARD_BUTTONS` | `from_custom_id` is handed an action and an id and nothing else, so an action has to mean exactly one button. It does: `decline` and `hold` repeat across statuses with the same label, style and modal flag, and every other action belongs to one status. `tests/test_requests.py::test_every_move_in_the_card_table_has_exactly_one_spec_to_rebuild_it_from` is what keeps that true when somebody adds a status. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:190` (`MOVE_TEMPLATE`) — built from `MOVE_ACTIONS`, not written out | Checklist 15. The alternative is a regex that silently stops matching a move somebody added to `CARD_BUTTONS`, which fails as "this interaction failed" on a post and nowhere else. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:837` (`site_button`) — extracted so `site_view` and `post_view` draw the same link | The channel/DM card still wants a view of its own; the post wants the button inside a view it also fills with moves. One builder, two callers, one URL shape. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:1602` (`Requests.cog_load`) — the cog's first `cog_load` | Registration has to happen where the cog is loaded, not where a post is drawn: a restart draws no posts at all, and the button must still answer. Same shape as `Modmail.cog_load` and `RoleMenus.cog_load`. |
| `request_post_buttons` defaults to **true** | §F says so, and the surface it turns on is the one the owner asked for. Off leaves the post exactly what v121 shipped — the card and the site link — so the key is a way back, not a way in. |

# A hand-made forum post becomes a request (branch `request-forum-adopt`, off `main` at `5e92e41`; design `blackmail-threads-design.md` §G)

Keyed by NAME as the two Blackmail blocks above are, so the merge that lands this does not have to
re-key it; the `path:line` in each row is where it was at `6c56f29`. The design's `## Deviations`
`### §G` holds what departed from §G and why; this table is only why each call was made the way it
was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`Requests.on_thread_create`) — the listener does the two cheap checks and nothing else | `db.is_connected` and `forum_adopts_posts` are a dict read and an attribute read; everything that costs an API call lives in `adopt_post`. Discord dispatches `on_thread_create` for EVERY thread in the guild, including every private modmail thread and every poll thread, so the common case must cost nothing. The forum comparison is inside `adopt_post` rather than the listener only because `forum_of` also CLAIMS the forum for the guard, which is a side effect the listener should not have when the feature is off. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`Requests.adopting`) — one `asyncio.Lock` on the cog, not one per thread | Checklist 6's read-decide-write. Adopting is rare (a person typing a post) and the whole critical section is three SQLite statements, so a single lock costs nothing and cannot leak a per-thread dict that never empties. It is a plain attribute rather than a private name because the tests read it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`made_by_the_bot`) — `thread.owner_id` OR the starter's author | Two answers to the same question, because either can be missing. `owner_id` is on the thread payload the gateway sends, so it is there even when the starter message is not cached; the author is what survives a `fetch_message`. ⚠️ This is the check that makes the race with `open_forum_post` harmless: the gateway can deliver `on_thread_create` before `set_thread` has committed, and then the row lookup answers "no row" for a post the bot itself made seconds earlier. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`starter_of`) — `starter_message` first, `fetch_message(thread.id)` second | A forum post's opening message carries the SAME id as the thread (Discord's own shape), which is why no search is needed. `starter_message` is populated only when that message is in discord.py's cache, so the fetch is the ordinary path on a bot that has just started. A refused fetch is logged at info and returns `None` — the post is still adopted, from `thread.owner_id`, with `ADOPTED_WHY` as the why. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`filer_of`) — the starter's author, else the thread's owner | The author is a `Member` with roles, which `store.is_staff` needs; `guild.get_member(owner_id)` is the fallback and can answer `None` on an uncached member, which is the one case that refuses to adopt at all rather than guessing. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`reply_in_post`) — goes through `post_line`, not a bare `thread.send` | `post_line` already owns the guard check, the missing-channel warning, `request.notify_skipped_test_mode`, `request.notify_failed` and `AllowedMentions`. A second sender here would have been a second place test mode could leak from. What the adopted reply adds is `set_message`, so `restyle_post` re-draws THIS message's buttons as the request moves — the same contract `open_forum_post` writes for a post the bot made. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`say_in_post`) — claims the thread before it speaks, and answers nothing when the guard still refuses | The refusal is the whole product of the "you may not file" path; a claim that happened only on the success path would have made test mode swallow exactly the message a person needs. It is a plain `thread.send` rather than `post_line` because there is no row to log against — `post_line`'s two log kinds both carry a `request_id`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`adopt_post`) — `set_thread` BEFORE the log row and the reply | The thread id is what makes the second `on_thread_create` a no-op, so it is written before anything that can await a Discord round-trip. `create_request` cannot take it (the id is not known to the INSERT's callers anywhere else), so it is the same two-statement shape `open_forum_post` uses. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`adopt_post`) — `retag_post`, not a hand-written `thread.edit` | One place edits a post's tags, and it already knows that `archives_at('open')` is false. A second tagger is exactly what KI-29's entry says this feature spent its care avoiding. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`adopted_fields`) — a pure function, clamping to `WHAT_LIMIT`/`WHY_LIMIT` | `checked_fields` is the modal's validator and RAISES on a blank what or why; a forum post always has a name and often has an empty body, so refusing it would have meant refusing the person's post. This is the same clamp with a stand-in instead of a refusal, and it is pure so `tests/test_requests.py` can pin the limits without a database. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`request_for_thread`) — `guild_id` in the WHERE, not just `thread_id` | Thread ids are globally unique in Discord, so the guild is redundant today; it is there because every other query in this module is scoped that way and a cross-guild read that happens to work is the kind of thing that stops working. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`create_request`, the `source` keyword) — a keyword with a default, not a positional | Every existing caller is untouched, which is what keeps the website and the modal writing `panel` with a zero-line diff. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` (`VIA_FORUM`) — a fifth via word | `actionlog.stamped` rewrites `details["via"]` through `via_of`, which trusts a recorded word ONLY when it is a key of `VIA_WORDS`. Without the entry, `{"via": "forum"}` is silently replaced by `discord` — the row still exists, so nothing fails, and the Logs page quietly tells the owner an adopted request was filed in Discord. `kind_via` needs no change at all: it puts the `web.` head on for `VIA_WEBSITE` and hands every other word back the bare kind, which is what a forum filing is. |
| `site/public/assets/logs.js` + `site/mock/server.mjs` (`VIA_WORDS`) — hand-copied, twice | `viaCell` draws a dash for a via it does not know, so a word added to Python only would have been invisible on the page that exists to show it. ⚠️ `boot` is still absent from both, which is a pre-existing gap this build did not close. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`tell_person`, the `to=` keyword) | The adopted filing owes the filer the DM every other door answers ephemerally. `person_told` is the MOVE table and `look_of` can return any status, so widening it would have changed paths this build never looked at; one keyword, defaulting to exactly what it did before, does not. |

# Temp voice in shadow — the lobby hidden from members, synced and un-hidden on the flip (branch `tempvoice-shadow`, off `main` at `c56962f`; design `info/tempvoice-shadow-design.md` §A–§F)

Keyed by NAME, as the two blocks above are, so the merge that lands this does not have to re-key
it. The design's `## Deviations` holds what departed from the brief; this table is only why each
call was made the way it was.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`TEMPVOICE_MODES`) — `shadow` sits BETWEEN `off` and `on` | The tuple is the order the `/voice` ▸ **Mode…** select draws and the order the Settings page lists, and it reads as a ladder: nothing, then working-but-hidden, then working-and-visible. The registry **default stays `on`** — a guild that installs Black Bloc fresh has no lobby to hide and no reason to start in a mode that needs a second step. The live value is set to `shadow` by hand after the deploy; a default of `shadow` would have made every future guild inherit this server's cutover. |
| `black_bloc/tempvoice.py` (`makes_rooms`) — one predicate, three call sites | Shadow only changes *who can see the lobby*; spawning, the panel's off-line and `_maybe_create` all have to treat it exactly as `on`. Three separate `!= "on"` tests were three chances to forget one, and the one that was forgotten would have been silent — a lobby that is visible to staff and spawns nothing looks like a Discord permissions problem, not a bug here. It lives in the pure module so `tests/test_tempvoice.py` pins it without a bot. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`hide_from_members`) — sets `view_channel = False` and NOTHING else | The deny MASKS the allow rather than removing it, which is why nothing about `creator_overwrites` or `allow_join` had to change: the allowed role keeps `connect = True` underneath, so the flip back to `on` is a re-allow and not a rebuild. It also means a role the owner allowed by hand, the staff reach and the bot's `manage_channels` all survive a sweep — the function never writes `False` to a permission it was not asked about and never touches a target it was not given. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`shadow_targets`) — `@everyone` AND the allowed role, resolved fresh every time | `@everyone` alone is not enough: `creator_overwrites` adds `tempvoice_allowed_role_id` through `allow_join`, and that allow beats the `@everyone` deny — which is exactly the v117 mistake (`voice-panel-design.md`, the corrected deviation). A role id that no longer resolves drops out rather than raising, the same way `join_roles` already handles it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`hidden_already`) — the compare is per TARGET, not a dict equality | Checklist: no edit that changes nothing. A whole-dict compare would have said "different" every sweep, because `category_overwrites` rebuilds each `PermissionOverwrite` and any unrelated hand edit would show up. The question the sweep actually asks is narrow — *do these two targets read `view_channel is False`?* — so that is what is asked, and one `tempvoice.lobby_hidden` row lands per lobby per hiding rather than one per five minutes forever. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`hide_lobby`) — builds from `category_overwrites(channel)`, the CHANNEL's own | The reconcile's job is additive: keep whatever the lobby says and add the mask. Rebuilding from the category (what `repair_creator_channel` does) would have thrown away every hand-made allow on every sweep, which is the opposite of *"with whatever rules it had before"*. `lobby_overwrites` is the other half — on Setup/repair the dict is being rebuilt anyway, so the mask goes on the end of that instead. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`show_lobby`) — TWO edits, deliberately, in this order | `edit(sync_permissions=True)` is Discord's own **Sync now** and cannot be expressed as an overwrites dict — it is a distinct field on the channel PATCH, and it is what the owner asked for in those words (*"do a sync of the permissions of the category"*). The second edit then reads `channel.category` and re-applies the allowed role, the bot's manage and the staff reach in ONE `edit(overwrites=…)`, so the lobby is never left mid-flip with the category's permissions and none of ours. A failure of either is `tempvoice.lobby_failed` naming which step failed, never a raise into the settings hook. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`apply_mode`) — a LAST-SEEN mode, not the hook's `value` alone | The hook is told the new value, not the old one, and only `shadow → on` may sync: `off → on` must change no permission (it never hid anything), and syncing there would silently flatten a lobby somebody had set up by hand. The memory lives on the bot (`mode_memory`) and is seeded by the reconcile, so a restart while the mode is `shadow` leaves the next flip detectable — and a flip that happens while the process is down cannot happen, because the setting can only be written by this process. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`apply_mode`) — called from the hook AND from `reconcile_channels` | Two triggers, one function, so they cannot disagree. The hook makes the flip immediate (the owner presses **on** and the lobby is visible before the panel re-renders); the reconcile is the convergence (`on_ready` + the five-minute loop, checklist 25) that puts back a deny somebody removed by hand and that seeds the last-seen mode after a restart. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`install_mode_hook`) — registered in `cog_load`, guarded by an attribute on the bot | `settings_store.on_change` appends, so a cog reload would have stacked a second callback and doubled every edit and every log row. The guard is a bot attribute rather than a module global because the tests build several bots in one process. `cog_load` registers it BEFORE the `db.is_connected` return, so a bot that starts with the database down still notices a flip once it is up. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`lobby_failed`) — one kind for both steps, with `doing` in the details | `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` classes `_failed` as important with no registration, and the two shipped kinds (`tempvoice.lobby_hidden`, `tempvoice.lobby_shown`) are ROUTINE because they are the bot doing what it was told. Checklist 2: a failure never shares a kind with a success, and `doing` says whether it was the hide, the sync or the re-allow without three near-identical kinds nobody would remember. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`ModePick`) replaces `MODE_OFF_MOVE` / `MODE_ON_MOVE` | A two-state button cannot express three modes, and cycling through them would be the *"status menu with two spellings of the same move"* the owner's panel rule forbids — from `on` you would press twice to reach `shadow`. One **Mode…** button opens a card whose select draws its options from `TEMPVOICE_MODES` with `MODE_MEANS` as the descriptions, so the registry stays the one home for the list and the helpers module the one home for the prose. `card_buttons` lost `mode_on` with them. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` (`status_lines`) — the shadow line is on the STAFF block | A member in shadow cannot see the lobby and has nothing to do about it; the person who needs the sentence is the staffer looking at `/voice` wondering why nobody is making rooms. The `**mode**` row above it already says `shadow`; the line says what that COSTS, which is the part a mode name does not carry. |
| The guard is not asked, and `may_act_in` is not asked | The test-mode guard patches `send_message` and `edit_message` only — `channel.edit` was never gated — so both edits go through under `TEST_MODE=true`. ⚠️ `may_act_in` would REFUSE: it accepts a channel the guard owns or one in the test channel's category, and the lobby is neither (`own_channel` is called on spawned rooms, never on the lobby, so the design's §C claim that the lobby is a place `may_act_in` accepts is wrong). Adding the check would have made shadow inert in exactly the state the owner is about to run it in; the design's conclusion — both edits go through — holds for the other reason. |

- `black_bloc/cogs/community/tempvoice.py` `_create_for` (the `mode_of(...) == SHADOW_MODE` line before `create_voice_channel`) — shadow's mask goes on the ROOM after `owner_overwrites`' allows, or the allowed role gets its view back on every spawned room (v125; `tempvoice-shadow-design.md` § Found at the landing).
# The front door (branch `front-door`, off `main` at `0cee997`; design `info/front-door-design.md`)

⚠️ **Keyed by NAME, not by line** — written against a branch that had not merged, so every key
below is the construct's name in its file. The design's `## Deviations` foot carries the places
the build differs from §A–§E.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` (`RequestDoor`, `EventDoor`) — subclasses of `requests.FileButton` and `events.ProposeButton` rather than new buttons | The brief's whole point is that a press OPENS the existing flow. A subclass inherits `callback` outright, so there is no second implementation to drift and no gate to forget: `request_mode`, `request_who_can_file`, `events_mode` and the DB check all still answer in their own feature's words. A test asserts `isinstance(item, FileButton)` — the claim is the type, not a copied sentence. |
| `TicketDoor` is NOT a subclass, and calls `open_ticket_modal(interaction)` with `previous=None` | Modmail's only button class is `MoveButton(TICKET_OPEN)`, which passes its own view as `previous`; `run_open_ticket` then calls `render_root(interaction, previous)` and would redraw the **modmail** root over the front door's panel. `previous=None` is the posted-button path and leaves whatever raised the modal alone. It also makes the ticket's stored `source` read `panel`, which is true of both of the door's faces. |
| `open_the_event` sends a one-button ephemeral card instead of opening the draft | ⚠️ **The one thing a posted door cannot do.** `ProposeButton.callback` → `open_draft` → `panels.opened` → `interaction.response.defer()`, which for a component is `deferred_message_update`, so `render_draft`'s `edit_original_response` edits **the message the button is on**. On the `/ask` panel that is right — the panel becomes the draft. On the PUBLIC posted message it would draw a member's half-filled event draft over the front door, for everybody. `EventHandoff` is a private message to raise the draft from; the ticket and request doors need none because a modal is already private. |
| `black_bloc/posted.py` — `message_is_there` / `drop_message` / `overtaken_by`, with modmail's three helpers now one-line delegates | Checklist 15. The ticket button and the front door want the same three answers (is it still there, take it down without the guard seeing it, has the followed post overtaken it) and the modmail copies were the only ones. `drop_message` takes the shadow kind as `would_kind` because the CALLER owns its own log vocabulary; `tests/test_logkinds.py` `KNOWN_DYNAMIC` names the three values it can take. |
| `drop_message` returns a bool where `drop_panel_message` returned `None` | `hide_ticket_button` clears `modmail_panel_message_id` only when the message really went. Under the guard the delete is refused and logged, and clearing the key anyway would tell modmail its button is down while it is still up — the next `on` would post a second one beside it (the KI-8 shape). |
| `frontdoor.door_takes_over(store, guild_id)` lives in the PURE module, and `Modmail._repanel` reads it | The two-line early return in `_repanel` is the whole of "one door per channel" working. Without it modmail's five-minute sweep re-posts the ticket button the door just took down, and the two reconcilers alternate forever. The pure module has no cog imports, so modmail importing it makes no cycle; the door importing modmail's `panel_where` is the other direction and already existed. |
| `hide_ticket_button` clears the MESSAGE key and leaves the CHANNEL key | So the takedown is reversible without storing anything new: `door_takes_over` stops answering the moment the door moves or comes down, `_repanel` stops early-returning, sees a channel with no message, and posts the button again on its own next sweep. `frontdoor_replaces_ticket_button` off makes `door_takes_over` answer `None` and nothing is ever touched. |
| `frontdoor_message_id` is a `text` key | `api/settings_api.py` already says ids leave as strings because a snowflake does not survive a JavaScript number; an `int` key also sits permanently CHANGED on the Settings page (`# Settings editor — the false "1 change pending"`). Same call, same reason, as `modmail_panel_message_id`. |
| The eleven keys are `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`'d onto `modmail` rather than making a `frontdoor` group | ⚠️ **Measured: `settings_panel.groups()` was already at 25 and `cogs/core.py:GroupPick` takes `sp.groups()[: sp.SELECT_LIMIT]`** — Discord's own cap. A 26th group would have silently dropped `youtube` off `/settings` ▸ **A setting group…**, with nothing to say so. Filing them with modmail is also where the website card lives and where the log kinds head. `modmail` is now a second group over 25 keys, which is what **Find a setting…** exists for. |
| `logkinds.HEADS["frontdoor"] = "modmail"` rather than a new `FEATURES` entry | A new feature would mean a `frontdoor_log_level` key, a `FEATURE_PAGES` row and a Logs-page filter for a surface that is three buttons. The door's rows belong beside the ticket button's on the Modmail page, and `modmail_log_level` governs both. |
| `DoorButton.from_custom_id` reads the KIND out of the match | One template, three buttons, one registration. A restart re-derives which door was pressed from `door:<kind>:<guild_id>` and nothing else — no state, no lookup — which is why the label it rebuilds with is the shipped default and never the stored one: the label only matters when the message is WRITTEN. |
| `DoorButton.on_click` re-asks `door_is_on` | A posted message outlives the setting. Checklist "a gate can close while a card is open": with the mode off the door is taken down on the next sweep, but a press in the five minutes before that answers `DOOR_OFF`, which names the key and both ways back to it, rather than opening a flow the owner switched off. |
| `FrontDoor._redoor` takes the door DOWN when the mode is off | §C's help text promises it (*"off … takes the posted door down"*), and it is the only reconcile branch that runs with no channel resolved. It uses `take_door_down`, so both keys are cleared and posting again names a channel — the same "down means down" `take_panel_down` has. |
| `_shadowed`, a set cleared on the first successful post | The sweep runs every five minutes, so a door pointed at a channel the guard refuses would write `frontdoor.would_post` twelve times an hour forever. Deliberate doors (the website route) log every time, because somebody is waiting for the answer. Copied from `Modmail._panel_shadowed`, for the same reason. |
| `frontdoor_panel_minutes` exists although §C's table has ten keys | `panels.Panel` takes a timeout, and KI-20 is why every one of the eighteen panels owns its own key at **10**: fifteen or more loses the "this panel has gone quiet" footer, because the footer is written through an interaction token that expires at fifteen. Reusing `modmail_panel_minutes` would make one number mean two panels. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs` carries its own `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`, and `tests/api/test_contract.py::test_the_mock_groups_a_key_the_way_the_registry_does` compares the two | Found in a browser, not in a test: the mock's `namespaceOf` splits on the first `_` with its own override table, so the eleven keys drew a **Front door** group on the mock Settings page while the real one files them under modmail. Nothing else compares the two tables. |
# The front door in SHADOW (branch `frontdoor-shadow`, off `main` at `58fb7d6`; design `info/front-door-design.md` ▸ `## Shadow mode (2026-09-18)`)

⚠️ **Keyed by NAME, not by line** — written against a branch that has not merged. Owner, 2026-09-18
16:1x, a minute after the `TEST_MODE` lift posted the real door in `#welcome`: *"i dont want it to
post in welcome yet"* → *"lets have that in shadow mode"*.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/frontdoor.py` (`door_is_on`) now means **the mode is not off**, so shadow answers `True` | All four callers want exactly that: `/ask` answers in shadow, a press on the rehearsal copy opens the real flow, the sweep must NOT take the door down, and `door_takes_over` still applies. A `door_is_live` beside it would have been two names for one question and a fifth place to forget one of them. Its three existing assertions in `tests/test_frontdoor.py` pass unchanged. |
| `black_bloc/frontdoor.py` (`door_mode`) casefolds and falls back to **off**, never to `on` | A mode is a word, not a truthy value (the existing test says so). An unknown word — a typo through `/settings set-value`, a value from a future branch — must not leave the door posting in a real channel; off is the only safe reading. |
| `black_bloc/frontdoor.py` (`panel_follows_the_door`) — the ticket button's mode is DERIVED, never stored | The brief said not to add a second mode key, and there is nothing a separate `modmail_panel_mode` could say that `frontdoor_mode` + `frontdoor_replaces_ticket_button` do not already: the button follows the door precisely when the door replaces it. Two keys that can disagree about one thing is the shape that strands a live button in a public channel. |
| `black_bloc/frontdoor.py` (`door_takes_over`) answers the AIMED channel in shadow, with no `frontdoor_message_id` set | It is the answer to *"which channel does the front door own outright"*, and in shadow it owns it by keeping everything out of it. Without this, `Modmail._repanel`'s existing two-line early return stops firing the moment the door's message id is cleared, and modmail's five-minute sweep posts the ticket button into `#welcome` — the exact thing the owner asked to stop. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` (`lower_the_real_door`) clears `frontdoor_message_id` and LEAVES `frontdoor_channel_id` | `take_door_down` clears both, which is right for *down* and wrong for *rehearsing*: the channel is where the door is AIMED. It is what `rehearsal_note` names ("this is where it would go: #welcome"), what the staff line names, and what the flip to **on** posts into with no second step from the conductor. The log row is `frontdoor.taken_down` with `rehearsal: true` in its details, rather than a fourth kind nothing else reads. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` (`start_rehearsing`) runs BEFORE `rehearse_door`, not inside it | `rehearse_door` is shared with the `TEST_MODE` path, where there is no real door to take down and the guard would refuse the delete anyway. Doing it in the caller keeps the shared path a zero-line diff and makes shadow's promise unconditional: the real channel is emptied even when the rehearsal home turns out to be unreachable and the copy cannot go up. |
| The posting decision is `door_rehearses(...) or (guard refuses)` in FOUR places, and nothing else moved | `post_door`, `FrontDoor._redoor`, `post_ticket_panel`, `Modmail._repanel` — one line each, inside the decision, never around `reconcile()`. The concurrent `boot-reconcile-once` branch wraps `reconcile()` in a lock helper in `loops.py`; keeping to the inner branch is what makes those two merge textually. |
| `hide_ticket_button` skips its `door_takes_over == this channel` check while `panel_follows_the_door` | One door per **channel** is the rule when the door is really posted. In shadow the rule is *nothing of ours is in a real channel at all*, so a ticket button aimed at `#help` follows too. `modmail_panel_channel_id` keeps its value, so the flip to **on** puts it back on modmail's own next sweep — the same reversibility moving the door away already has. |
| `rehearse_door` picks `DOOR_SHADOW_SAID` over `DOOR_REHEARSING_SAID` on the same path | The path is identical; the reason is not. Telling a staffer *"Black Bloc is in test mode"* while test mode has been lifted is the class of sentence that sends somebody hunting a switch that is already off. Same for `DOOR_NO_HOME` vs `DOOR_GUARDED` on the homeless refusal — ⚠️ **the refusal CODE is still `test_mode` for both** (design Deviations S3). |
| `shadow_words` / `staff_shadow_words` are NOT settings keys, and `/ask` draws the line as an embed FOOTER for staff only | The standing rule is that every word the bot POSTS is a key. This one is never posted: it is a status line on an ephemeral panel and on a dashboard card — the call `rehearsal-home-design.md` deviation 7 made for `posts.shadow_words`, for the same reason. A footer rather than a field keeps the card a member sees byte-identical, and `door_hash` cannot drift because the posted copy is built from `door_embed` directly. |
| `site/public/assets/page-modmail.js` (`panelSettings`) reads the `core` namespace for `shadow_channel_id ?? log_channel_id` | The bot's chain is `shadow_channel_id` → the guard's test channel → `log_channel_id` (`black_bloc/shadow.py`), and with `TEST_MODE` lifted the middle link cannot fire — so the card agrees with the bot in every configuration that exists. It is one `settings(true)` call either way; the namespace filter is applied twice, not fetched twice. |

## YouTube live — a quota-free `/live` probe feeding the go-live path (branch `youtube-live`, off `main` at `9c08936`; design `info/youtube-live-design.md`)

| Where | Why it is like that |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`READABLE`) — a THIRD marker beside `IS_LIVE` and `CANONICAL_WATCH` | The design named two facts, and two facts cannot tell *not live* from *the page changed shape*: both are "no `isLive`". Without this, `youtube.probe_unreadable` would fire on every offline channel on every probe, and the KI-30 alarm would be pure noise. `ytInitialData` or a `<link rel="canonical">` is present on a real YouTube page of ANY kind (measured against the live Lofi Girl `/live` page, 2026-09-17), and absent from a consent wall or an error page. A page with neither is `readable=False`; a quiet channel page is `readable=True, live=False`. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`read_page`, `live = IS_LIVE… and not upcoming`) | A scheduled premiere's page carries `"isUpcoming":true` and often `"isLive":false`, but the ordering of the two in a 1.2 MB blob is YouTube's business. Making `upcoming` win outright means a stream that has not started cannot be announced whatever else the page says. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`Probe.announceable`) — a property, not a field | `live` and `video_id` are two separate readings and the parser reports both honestly; the CALLER needs one answer — can this be announced? A live page whose canonical link we could not read is live and unannounceable, and that distinction is worth keeping in the row. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`stream_info`, `game=None`) | Deviation 1 of the design doc. The channel title in `{game}` renders as *"currently streaming **Lofi Girl**"*, asserting a category YouTube never gave. `golive.render` fills `GAME_FALLBACK` — *something* — which is what a Twitch stream with no category already gets, so the wording is one shape, not two. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`stream_info`, the thumbnail fallback) | `golive.YOUTUBE_THUMBNAIL` (`i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg`) is a public no-quota URL that has existed since the presence path was written. Reusing it means the keyless card still has art, and there is one home for the URL shape (checklist 15). |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`after_probe` / `is_over`) — two pure functions, not a class | Nothing is stored between probes except one integer per channel, and the arithmetic is the whole rule: a live read clears it, anything else adds one, and it ends at the setting. Pure functions are what let `tests/test_youtube_live.py` pin the boundary at every value without a bot, a database or a clock. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py` (`probe_live`) — `status != 200` RAISES rather than returning an offline `Probe` | A 403 or a 500 is YouTube refusing to answer, which is not the same claim as "they are not live". The raise becomes a `YouTubeError`, the cog records it as `last_probe_error`, and the miss counter is left alone — so an outage cannot end somebody's stream. Contrast `readable=False`, which IS treated as offline, because there the page answered and simply did not say. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py` (`confirm_live`) — returns `None` with no key rather than raising | Without a key nothing is claimed (checklist 10). The caller then announces from the probe alone, which is the keyless shape §A describes, instead of having to catch an exception it expects. `search_live` and `_title_of` are the same shape. ⚠️ **It used to say *mirrors `classify()` two methods down*; `classify` went with the uploads half on 2026-09-18.** |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py` (`health_lines`, `live=` keyword with a `None` default) | The live lines are appended AFTER the rest and the keyword defaults to `None`, so a caller that wants the health block without them still gets exactly what it got. ⚠️ **The caller that needed that — `setup_embed`, which sliced `health_lines(...)[:6]` — went with the uploads half on 2026-09-18; the shape is kept because `live_lines` is also called on its own and a two-line block with nothing after it is a valid reading.** |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`live_poller`) — the cog's ONLY loop since 2026-09-18 | It was built as a SECOND loop beside the uploads `poller` rather than a second job inside it: the two had different clocks (`youtube_poll_minutes` 10, `youtube_live_poll_minutes` 5), different modes and different failure meanings, so one loop would have made either half's error the other's. ⚠️ **That separation is why the uploads removal cost the live half a zero-line diff** — `poller` and its four helpers were deleted whole. `live_poller` keeps its own `@loop.error` restart and its own `wait_ready` (checklist 28), and `loop_health` now answers for it alone. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`probe_all`, the per-sweep `worked` / `failed` bookkeeping) | Setting `last_probe_error = None` inside the per-channel loop would let the last channel probed erase an error the first one reported. The sweep is the unit the health line describes, so the sweep is what writes it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`self.live_video`) — a dict of channel id → the video id last acted on | The design's "no open session exists" test alone is not enough: with `golive_mode` off, `_go_live_once` returns before opening a session, so *no open session* stays true forever and every probe would log and re-enter the go-live path. Remembering the broadcast we already acted on makes the transition the trigger, not the state. It is also what makes a confirm that says `actualEndTime` cost ONE unit rather than one per probe. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_live_now`, `self.live_video[...] = ` set BEFORE the `not confirmed.live` return) | Same reason: a broadcast the API has declared over is over. Re-confirming it every five minutes would burn a unit a probe for as long as the page kept saying live. |

| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_confirm`, `_spent()` BEFORE the call) | The unit is charged by Google when the request is made, not when it succeeds. Counting after a successful return would under-report exactly the case the owner cares about — a quota that ran out. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_unreadable`, the one-per-hour dict) | KI-30's alarm has to be loud enough to notice and quiet enough not to be filtered out. A page change makes EVERY linked channel unreadable on EVERY probe — at five minutes that is twelve rows per channel per hour. The throttle is per channel, so ten broken channels still say ten different things. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`live_health`) — module-level, reading the cog by `getattr` | It is called by the `/youtube` panel AND by `GET /api/youtube/status`. As a cog METHOD (which it was, briefly) the API's own `FakeCog` had to grow one, and any caller holding a cog-like object would have got the "feature missing" sentence instead of the numbers it plainly had. One function, one reading, both surfaces — the surfaces half of one-fact-one-home. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`LiveModePick`, `row=4`, rendered only when `not picking`) | Discord allows five action rows and the root panel uses all five the moment **Link for somebody…** is pressed (`WhoPick` takes row 4). Deviation 7 of the design doc. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`set_live_mode`, the `extra` sentence) | Switching the live half on while `golive_mode` is shadow or `golive_channel_id` is blank does nothing visible, and a switch that appears to work and does not is the thing the "never a bare refusal" rule exists to stop. The sentence names the key that is actually in the way. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py` (`go_live` / `end_live`) — two one-line public wrappers | The YouTube cog needed a door. Reaching another cog's `_go_live` by `getattr` would have made a private method part of a contract without saying so; these say so. The lock, the cooldown, the role filters and the streamer-list upsert all still live behind them, unchanged. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/golive.py` (`_still_live_on_youtube`) — `None` from the probe means LEAVE IT OPEN | Copied deliberately from the Twitch branch above it, which leaves a session open when Helix cannot be reached. Reconcile runs on `cog_load`, i.e. immediately after a deploy: the cheap wrong answer (a session left open a few minutes longer) is aged out by `golive_max_session_hours`, while the expensive wrong answer closes a live stream's announcement mid-stream and the cooldown then blocks the re-announcement for an hour. |
| `black_bloc/golive.py` (`EMBED_SOURCES`) — a dict replacing a two-branch conditional | `embed_footer` read *"twitch, else Discord activity"*, so `source="youtube"` would have printed *via Discord activity* on a card Discord had nothing to do with. A table takes the third word without a third branch. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` (`youtube.probe_unreadable` in `IMPORTANT`) | It matches no `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` entry — it is not a `_failed`, because nothing failed; YouTube answered and the answer was not the shape we read. It still has to reach the log channel at the default `important` level, because it is the only alarm KI-30 has. |
| `tests/fixtures/youtube_*_page.html` — hand-written, not captured | A real `/live` page is **1.2 MB** (measured 2026-09-17), which is not a fixture anybody will read or a diff anybody will review. Each of the three is under 2 KB and carries a comment naming the real page and the date its markers were checked against. ⚠️ They are a record of what YouTube served on one day, not a contract — which is the whole of KI-30. |
| `tests/cogs/content/test_youtube.py` (`golive` fixture) — the REAL `GoLive` cog, not a double | The thing worth proving is that a probe produces a `golive_sessions` row with `source=youtube` and a post in the go-live channel, with the cooldown, the opt-out and the role filters all in the way. A fake go-live cog would have proved only that the YouTube cog calls a method. |

- `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` `Core._seed_guides` — `seed_guides` runs on EVERY guides tick (it inserts only slugs the guild lacks), so a guide the shipped seed gains after the first seeding appears on the next boot (v127; `guides-design.md` § Found at the v125 landing).

## YouTube live, the datacenter fix — the `/live` page is a bot check from Fly (branch `youtube-live-fix`, off `main` at `ddd6fdc`; design `info/youtube-live-design.md` ▸ Deviations ▸ *The datacenter page*; KI-30)

| Where | Why it is like that |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`read_page`, `video_id` from `CANONICAL_WATCH` ALONE — the `VIDEO_ID` regex is deleted) | Measured from Fly 2026-09-17: the bot-check page carries ~180 `"videoId"` fields and the first belongs to a stranger's video, so the fallback would have announced the wrong stream under the streamer's name. The canonical link is the only field on that page that ever means *this* video. A reading that can be confidently wrong is worse than one that is absent. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`BOT_CHECK`, `Probe.botcheck`) — a reporting field that changes NOTHING | It is not routing: `live` still decides. It exists so the `/youtube` staff half, `/api/youtube/status`, the Go-live card and the `youtube.live_seen` details can all say *why* a card read *Live now* with no id. Matching on the sentence `Sign in to confirm` rather than a status code is deliberate — the wall answers **200**, which is how it fooled v126. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`LIVE_ID_UNKNOWN = "?"`) | `live_video[channel_id]` is the "already acted on this broadcast" memory, and a botcheck announcement has no id to put there. `None` cannot be stored (it is indistinguishable from absent, and absent means *not live*), and a sentinel that no eleven-character video id can collide with is the cheapest honest marker. Without it the 100-unit search would run on every probe. |
| `black_bloc/youtube_live.py` (`channel_info`) — a SECOND `StreamInfo` builder beside `stream_info` | The keyless bot-check card has no video id, so `WATCH_URL` and `YOUTUBE_THUMBNAIL` (both `{video_id}`-shaped) cannot be used at all. Rather than teach `stream_info` a None branch, the id-less card is its own three-line function: url = the channel's own `/live` page, no thumbnail, no title, so `golive` fills `EMBED_NO_TITLE` — *Live now*. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_probed`, `if probe.live:` where it read `probe.announceable`) | The whole defect in one word. `announceable` is *live AND an id*; on the wall the id is missing and the stream is real, so routing on it sent a live channel down `_not_live` and the feature went quiet with no error anywhere. `announceable` is kept — it is the honest two-part reading — but the cog is where the two facts are reconciled. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_searched`) — 100 units, guarded by `live_video` rather than by a rate limit | `search.list(eventType=live)` is 100 of a 10,000-unit day; the design ruled it out as a poller for exactly that reason (ten channels every ten minutes = 144,000). As a one-off on the TRANSITION it is 101 units for a whole broadcast, confirm included. The guard is not a timer but the same memory that already stops a second announcement, so "searched twice" and "announced twice" cannot come apart. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_searched`, a failed search falls back instead of giving up) | The channel IS live — that is the one fact the wall did not take away. A refused search leaves the announcement on the channel's `/live` URL, which is a working link, and writes `youtube.live_search_failed` (IMPORTANT by the `_failed` suffix) so the degraded card is explained rather than mysterious. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_spent(units)`, `self.confirms` counting UNITS) | The attribute feeds `quota_today`, which is labelled *quota used today*. A counter that ignored the 100-unit call would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. The name is left alone because `live_health`, the panel, the route and the mock all read it; only what it counts changed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`is_live_now`, `probe.live` not `probe.announceable`) | The reconcile asks *is this member still live*, and behind the wall the honest answer is yes-with-no-id. Left as it was, a restart inside a stream would have read the wall as offline and closed the session — the failure Deviation 8 exists to prevent, arriving through a different door. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`last_botcheck`, the LAST probe rather than a tally) | The health line answers "why did the id go missing just now", not "how often does this happen". A counter would need a reset rule and a window; a last-reading needs neither and cannot go stale in the way a total can. It is reset on every probe of every channel, so on a multi-channel guild it describes the last one probed — which is what the wording says. |

## YouTube live, the silent open-session path (branch `youtube-live-seen`, off `main` at `568c177`; design `info/youtube-live-design.md` ▸ Deviations ▸ *The silent open-session path*)

| Where | Why it is like that |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`live_seen_details`) — a module function, not a method | Two writers now make a `youtube.live_seen` row: the announcing path and the open-session one. The four facts a reader always wants (`channel_id`, `video_id`, `botcheck`, `mode`) come from one place so they cannot drift; each caller merges its own tail onto it. Module-level rather than a method because it touches no state — the tests build one without a cog. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_live_now`, `if known is None` inside the open-session branch) | The once-per-stream rule, and it is the SAME rule the announcing row has — `live_video` holding no entry for the channel IS the transition.
