A five-minute poll through a three-hour stream would otherwise leave 36 rows saying the same thing. ⚠️ A stream that swaps video id without ever reading offline writes no second row; that case falls through to the announcing branch and returns at the open-session check, exactly as before. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`_live_seen`, and the kind still a literal ternary at the `log_action` call) | `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_every_dynamic_kind_is_enumerated` reads the call site's AST and wants a string LITERAL; lifting `"youtube.live_seen"` / `"youtube.would_live_seen"` into module constants made it fail with *not a string literal and is not in KNOWN_DYNAMIC*. The wrapper exists for the two callers, the ternary stays where the guard can see it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`because: "open_session:<source>"`) | The row has to answer *why did a working probe announce nothing*, and the answer is another source already holds the session. The source travels with it because `twitch` and `presence` are different stories — one is a poller, one is a Discord status — and a reader six weeks later cannot tell them apart from "an open session". `UNKNOWN_SOURCE` covers a row with no source rather than writing `open_session:None`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`announced: true` added to the ANNOUNCING row) | The new row says `announced: false`; a key present on one kind of row and absent on the other is a field a reader has to guess the meaning of. Checklist 2 wants a dry run and a real one distinguishable at a glance, and two rows of the same kind that did different things are the same problem one level down. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`live_health`, `reading_live` beside `open`) | `open` counts go-live sessions whose source is `youtube`; it is the honest answer to *what did go-live announce* and it read **0** on the live bot while the probe was reading Pawpette as live. `reading_live` is `len(cog.live_video)` — what the PROBE sees — and the two disagreeing is now information instead of a silence. Neither is redefined in terms of the other, deliberately: one fact, one number. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` (`reading_live_channels`, sorted, in the health dict but on no surface) | Sorted so a test can assert a list rather than a set, and `str()`-ed because `live_video`'s keys are channel ids from a database row. It is not on the panel or the card: a list of `UC…` strings nobody can click is noise beside a number that answers the question. It is there for the next session that has to ask *which* channel. |

## Send to… — staff hand-offs between requests, events and tickets (branch `send-to`, off `main` at `8a27840`; design `info/send-to-design.md`)

| Where | Why it is like that |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` — one module for the vocabulary, the wording and the moves; the SURFACES stay on the cogs | The design's §A says *one helper, three surfaces*. Everything a hand-off decides (the trail cell, the log kind, the refusal sentences, the DM) lives here so the panel card, the forum post, the review room and the ticket card cannot disagree. What it must NOT do is import a cog at module level — `cogs/community/requests.py` imports `handoff` for its refusal text, so a module-level `from .cogs...` here would close the circle. Every cog import inside this module is therefore function-local, which is the same shape `black_bloc/modmail.py:ticket_label` already uses for `panels.option_label`. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`read_trail`) — ONE column carries three shapes | `moved_to` says `kind:id` once a thing has been filed, `asked:kind:<iso>` while a member is being waited on, and `yes:kind` when they have said yes but staff still owe a date. The design named three additive columns and exactly three; a fourth column for the pending question would have been a fourth. Anything unreadable reads as `None`, so a cell written by hand cannot crash a card. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`expired` / `waiting_on`) — the READ decides, nothing sweeps | *"No answer in `handoff_confirm_hours` (24) = no"* needs no loop: a press after the deadline is refused as gone, and a fresh staff press is allowed because `waiting_on` answers `None`. A sweeper would have been a second place that decides the same thing, and checklist 25's "reconcile on a loop" is about state that would otherwise be stuck — this state is not stuck, it is simply stale, and every reader asks the clock. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`set_moved_to`, `TABLES[kind]`) | The table name is interpolated into SQL, so it is looked up in an allow-list keyed by the three words, never taken from a caller's string. A kind nobody named raises `KeyError` at the lookup rather than reaching SQLite. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`MOVED` in `STATUSES`, absent from `STAFF_STATUSES`) | `STAFF_STATUSES` is derived from `TRANSITIONS`' *values*, and nothing transitions INTO `moved` — so `/settings`, the website and `wanted_status` all keep refusing it, and the hand-off is the only path that can write it. `TRANSITIONS[MOVED]` is empty, which makes it final and puts it in `FINAL_STATUSES` for free. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`CHANNEL_LOOKS`, `moved` left OUT of `REQUEST_CARD_MOVES`) | `moved` is a LOOK (it has a colour, a title and fields, so the post's card re-renders) but it is not a card the request channel posts: the hand-off writes one plain line, `→ event #N`, and a second card saying the same thing would be the duplicate-surface trap. `channel_moves`' no-key fallback had to drop it too, or a server that had never touched the key would get both. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py` (`moved_words`, a function-local `from .handoff import`) | The card renderer is the one place that has to read a trail cell, and `handoff` already imports `requests` for `refusal_for_request`. Local import, one direction at module level. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`post_line(..., content=)`) | `post_line` is the guarded send every request line goes through — the guard refusal, the `request.notify_skipped_test_mode` row, the `request.notify_failed` row. It only ever sent an embed, because every caller had one. The hand-off's trail line is text, so the parameter is one word rather than a second guarded sender. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`handoff_row`, reusing `opened_here`) | `opened_here(interaction, on_post)` already encodes the §F lesson — a panel press defers as `deferred_message_update` and edits the panel, a post press defers `ephemeral, thinking=True` and gets its own message. The Send to… move needs exactly that split, so it asks the same function instead of a second one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` — the draft opens over the EPHEMERAL, with no intermediate card | `front-door-design.md` deviation 1 had to answer a posted press with a one-button card because `ProposeButton` → `open_draft` → `panels.opened` → `interaction.response.defer()` is a `deferred_message_update` and would have drawn a member's draft over the public message. Deferring `thinking=True` FIRST makes `edit_original_response` point at the new ephemeral instead, so `open_request_draft` can call `render_draft` straight away. One press fewer, and the public post is still never touched. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py` (`HANDOFF_TEMPLATE` separate from `MOVE_TEMPLATE`) | Two `DynamicItem` templates that both begin `request:` would be a race between two regexes. The hand-off ids begin `handoff:request:` instead, and a test asserts neither template matches the other's custom id. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` (`open_request_draft` calls `render_draft`, NOT `open_draft`) | `open_draft` runs `panels.opened`, which defers. Every caller of `open_request_draft` has already deferred (that is the whole point of the paragraph above), and a second defer on one interaction is an `InteractionResponded`. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`submit_event(..., requester=)`) — one keyword, three uses | The design asks for the event to be filed in the MEMBER's name while the log's actor stays the staffer who pressed. `requester` decides `create_event`'s `requester_id`, the review room's name and overwrites (so the member can see it), and `log_action`'s `target`; `actor` is untouched. With nothing passed it is the actor, which is every existing door. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` (`submit_draft` skips the proposer DM on a hand-off) | *"Submitted on **{guild}**"* is addressed to whoever proposed it. On a hand-off that is the member, and they are already being sent the real sentence — *"your request #N is now event #M"* — by `request_to_event`. Sending the staffer a "you proposed this" DM as well would have been the second message about one act. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` (`HEADS["handoff"] = "request"`) | Matching `frontdoor → modmail`: the hand-off has no settings namespace of its own (the group select is at Discord's cap of 25), so its rows obey `request_log_level` and land on the Requests page, which is where both keys are. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` (`HANDOFF_MODE` / `HANDOFF_CONFIRM_HOURS` in `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`) | `settings_panel.groups()` is at **exactly 25** and `cogs/core.py:GroupPick` slices `groups()[:SELECT_LIMIT]`, so a 26th namespace would drop one group off `/settings` ▸ **A setting group…** with nothing anywhere to say so. `front-door-design.md` deviation 3 found this the hard way; `tests/test_settings_panel.py::test_the_settings_groups_fit_the_select` is the guard that now fails by name instead. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` (`CANCEL_WHY["handed_off"]`, `HANDED_OFF`) | Event → request uses the EXISTING cancel path, which is what the design asks for — the scheduled event, the announcement edit, the room notice, the channel rename and the DM all still happen. The only thing that had to be new is the sentence the member reads: the default is *"either you or a member of staff called it off"*, which is untrue and unhelpful when it became a request. The reason word is also what keeps it out of `ROOM_QUIET_REASONS`, so the room still hears the cancellation. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`event_to_request`, `why` falls back to `FROM_EVENT`) | `requests.why` is `NOT NULL` and the filing modal makes it required, so a description-less event would have written an empty string into a column whose whole job is to say why. *"(filed from event #N)"* is the same shape `ADOPTED_WHY` already uses for a forum post with no body. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` (`make_it_a_request` defers only AFTER `refusal_for_event`) | `decision_context` answers its own refusals with `interaction.response.send_message`, so it must run before anything defers; the mode/decided refusal is the same shape and joins it. The defer then comes before `event_to_request`, which writes a row, cancels an event, edits an announcement and sends a DM — comfortably past Discord's three seconds. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` (`say_in_the_room`) — a line in the room, not a field on the closed card | `close_card` replaces the review card with `card_for(fresh)` and no view, and that card now carries a **Now** field. The separate line is for the ROOM's history: a card that was edited in place says nothing about *when* it moved, and the room is where staff go back and look. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`moved_words`) — one renderer, three surfaces | The event card, the request card and both API rows all say *"request #12"* the same way. `requests.moved_words` and `events.moved_words` are one-line wrappers that bold the id for a Discord embed; the API and the mock take it plain. The mock's `movedWord` is the JS copy of the same three lines, which is the same arrangement `REQUEST_STATUS_WORDS` already has. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js` (`movedBlock`, the link goes to the PAGE not the row) | `events.html` has no per-event anchor (`REQUEST_ANCHOR`'s `#r-<id>` has no counterpart), so *"open it"* points at the events page. A `#e-<id>` that no page renders would be a link that silently does nothing, which is worse than one that lands a scroll away. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (the confirm card IS the storage — `confirm_embed` / `read_ask`) | The ticket path has to carry a title and a body across a DM round-trip that may take a day and survive a restart, and the design allows exactly THREE new columns. So the wording lives in the embed the member is looking at: Yes reads it back off `interaction.message.embeds[0]`, and so does **Make the event…** off its own line in the ticket. Nothing else stores it, which also means the member cannot be shown one thing and have another filed. A member cannot edit a bot's embed, and a press with no card at all answers *"no longer waiting"* rather than filing a blank. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`moved_to` holds `asked:kind:<iso>` and `yes:kind` as well as `kind:id`) | Three shapes, one column. `asked:` is the question in flight and carries its own deadline, so `expired()` decides on the READ and nothing has to sweep — a fresh staff press after the window simply works again, which is the *"no answer counts as no"* rule with no loop to get stuck. `yes:event` is the one state the design creates that is neither: the member has agreed and staff still owe a date. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`member_said_no` clears the cell rather than writing `no:`) | Staff always get the final say: after a no, the card draws both moves again and asking a second time is allowed. A `no:` state would have been a terminal one staff could not leave. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`run_answer` takes the guild off the TICKET ROW) | The Yes/No press arrives in a DM, where `interaction.guild` and `interaction.guild_id` are both `None`. `bot.get_guild(ticket["guild_id"])` is the only way back, and it is also the check that the guild is still one Black Bloc is in. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`still_the_question`) — three conditions, not one | A confirm card outlives its question. The press must be the ticket's OWN member (a card forwarded or seen in a shared inbox is not their say-so), still inside the window, and still about the same kind — staff may have asked for an event after a request expired. All three answer the same sentence, because a member does not need to know which of them it was. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`card_modal` handles the two new actions FIRST) | The two moves ride the existing `CARD_ACTIONS_ON_THE_PANEL` machinery, so the channel card and the `/modmail` panel's copy of it open the same modal through the same dispatcher — no second table of which button does what. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`handoff_refused` at BOTH doors) | A card in a ticket channel is one message for everybody and can sit there for days; the panel's copy is re-rendered but the press can still race. The refusal runs before the modal opens on each, because a modal already on screen is the third stale window `modmail-doors-design.md`'s hide-toggle deviation 2 records. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`panel_card_buttons` computes Back's row rather than fixing it at 2) | Four moves plus two hand-offs plus Back is seven, and Discord takes five to a row. The moves keep their own `row` from `card_buttons` (offset by `CARD_ROW`), and Back goes one below whatever the last one used — so the panel is unchanged when the key is off and grows a row when it is on. |
| `black_bloc/modmail.py` (`card_buttons(practice=True)` returns BEFORE the handoff branch) | Nothing in a practice ticket reaches a member, so there is nobody to ask for permission. Offering the move would be offering to DM a confirmation to somebody who is not there. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`open_a_ticket(..., check_toggle=False)`) | `modmail_open_with_button` hides the **Open a ticket with…** door on the `/modmail` root. The design says the request hand-off uses the door *regardless* of that key, because it is a staff decision about a request rather than a general door — so the gate is a parameter with a default of True, and the one caller that bypasses it says so at the call site. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` (`deliver_dm` / `ticket_dm` grew a `view`) | The confirm card's two buttons have to arrive in the DM. Every other DM this cog sends is an embed, so the parameter is threaded rather than a second sender being written; `**extra` keeps `send(content, embed=…)` byte-identical when there is no view. |
| `black_bloc/settings_panel.py` (`groups()`) — guarded by `tests/test_settings_panel.py::test_the_settings_groups_fit_the_select` | `cogs/core.py:GroupPick` slices `groups()[:SELECT_LIMIT]` because 25 is Discord's own cap on select options. A 26th namespace is therefore not refused — it is **silently dropped**, and every key in whichever group falls off becomes unreachable from Discord with nothing anywhere to say so. The front-door build measured `groups()` at exactly 25 and filed eleven keys under `modmail` to avoid it (`front-door-design.md` deviation 3); Send to… filed two under `request` for the same reason. The test is the one line that makes the next feature fail by name — and names the group that would have gone — instead of quietly breaking `/settings`. |
| `black_bloc/handoff.py` (`refusal_for_ticket` refuses a PRACTICE ticket) | `card_buttons` already returns early for practice, so the sticky card in a practice thread never draws the moves. The `/modmail` panel's copy is the hole: `build_ticket` calls `panel_card_buttons(open_ticket=…, handoff=…)` and that path has never known about practice (it does not draw **Speak as the member** either). Without this, a Send to… press on a practice ticket's panel card would have reached `ask_the_member`, where `ticket_dm` short-circuits to `None` for practice — the same value a delivered DM returns — and the move would have reported success while nobody was ever asked. The refusal is on the MOVE rather than on the panel's button table because that is the one place every door goes through. |

## The rehearsal home — one channel every shadow copy lands in (branch `rehearsal-home`, off `main` at `9c8c179`; design `info/rehearsal-home-design.md`)

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` | ⚠️ **This module may not import `settings_store`.** `settings_store` imports `polls`, which imports `shadow`, so the key NAMES live here (`REHEARSAL_KEY`, `NOTE_KEY`, `NOTE_DEFAULT`) and `settings_store` aliases them (`SHADOW_CHANNEL`, `REHEARSAL_NOTE`, `REHEARSAL_NOTE_DEFAULT`). One home for the string, the other way up from what you would expect. |
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` `channel_id` | The order is the whole feature: the key, then the guard's own channel, then `log_channel_id`. Blank is exactly the behaviour before v129, which is why nothing had to change in posts or polls. |
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` `channel_ids` | The key goes FIRST in the hunt too, because a copy may still be sitting in the previous home when the key moves. |
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` `find_copy` | Was `posts._shadow_message`, hand-rolled. It answers `(channel, message)` rather than the message alone, because the front door and the ticket button have to compare where the copy IS against where it SHOULD be. An `HTTPException` from one channel never stops the hunt; a `NotFound` moves to the next. |
| `black_bloc/shadow.py` `install` | Called from `bot.setup_hook` straight after `store.load()`. It seeds the guard from `store.stored_values` (guilds are not up yet, so there is nothing else to read) and then follows the key with a `store.on_change` hook — the shape `tempvoice` shadow used. With `TEST_MODE` off there is no guard and no hook is registered at all. |
| `black_bloc/guard.py` `rehearse_in` | ⚠️ A DICT keyed by guild, not a set: a key that MOVES has to un-allow where it was, and add/remove of a stale id cannot get that wrong. It widens `allows_channel` only — `allows_place` (deleting channels) and `allows_interaction` (running a slash command) are deliberately untouched. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` `stored_values` | The only public way to ask "which guilds have set this key", for a sweep that runs before `bot.guilds` is filled. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` `CORE_KEYS` | `shadow_channel_id` and `rehearsal_note` are core because `namespace_of` would otherwise invent a `shadow` and a `rehearsal` group, and `settings_panel.groups()` is at Discord's hard cap of 25 (the front-door build's near miss). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` `rehearse_door` | One function for both callers, and **the caller owns the would-row**: a person pressing hears the refusal every time, the five-minute sweep says it once (`_shadowed`). That is why it returns `refusal(..., "test_mode", ...)` without logging. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` `rehearsal_payload` | The note is the message CONTENT above the embed, never inside it, so the embed the mods are reviewing is byte-for-byte the one `#welcome` will get. |
| `black_bloc/frontdoor.py` `door_hash` | The fingerprint is note + heading + line + the three labels. Without it the sweep would edit the copy every five minutes; with it an edit only happens when something drawn has changed. `frontdoor_shadow_hash` is the persisted half, so a restart does not cause one pointless edit. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/frontdoor.py` `hide_rehearsed_ticket_button` | The rehearsal twin of `hide_ticket_button`. `door_takes_over` cannot serve both: in a rehearsal `frontdoor_message_id` is blank (there IS no real message), so `rehearsal_takes_over` asks about the copy instead. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` `_repanel` | ⚠️ The early return for `rehearsal_takes_over` is the same bug the real path had at v125: without it, modmail re-posts its rehearsal copy every sweep and the front door deletes it again, for ever, in a real channel. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` `rehearse_panel` | Deliberately a near-twin of `rehearse_door` rather than a shared generic. The two differ in their keys, their kinds, their sentences, their card builder and what "the post it follows" means; the one thing they genuinely share — where a rehearsal goes — is `shadow.py`, and that IS shared. |

- `black_bloc/panels.py` `opened` — defers only when the interaction is not already answered (v130): the event draft's zone picker (`zone_submit` → `back=open_draft`) opened the same interaction twice and the second `defer()` raised `InteractionResponded` for every member without a stored timezone — seen by the mods in `#welcome-test` on 2026-09-17.

## Meeting minutes (prototype, branch `minutes`, 2026-09-17)

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/minutes_audio.py` | ⚠️ **Nothing here imports the receive extension at module level.** `build_sink` imports `discord.ext.voice_recv` inside the function, so the bot still boots on a host without it and `extension_available()` / `opus_available()` are what a command asks before promising anything. The three tests that need the extension use `pytest.importorskip` — the repo's own venv does not have it. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_audio.py` `to_mono_16k` | The downmix happens on EVERY 20 ms frame, not at the chunk boundary. Doing 60 s at once is ~960k Python loop iterations on the event loop; doing one frame is ~320, and the buffer is six times smaller (1.9 MB a minute rather than 11.5 MB). The 3-sample box filter is a crude low-pass before decimating 48 kHz → 16 kHz; Whisper resamples to 16 kHz anyway, so sending it at 16 kHz mono is both smaller and exactly what the model wants. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_audio.py` `SpeakerChunker` | The lock is real: `feed` is called on the voice READER THREAD, and `flush` from the event loop. The callback is deliberately a plain callable rather than a coroutine for the same reason — the session hands it to the loop with `run_coroutine_threadsafe`. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_audio.py` `_cut` | The audio is deleted from the buffer in the same breath it is wrapped as a WAV, so nothing large ever sits around and nothing is ever written to the volume. |
| `black_bloc/minutes.py` `may_start` | The order is the order a PERSON meets the refusals, not the cheapest-first order: mode, then no voice channel, then what the host cannot do, then a meeting already running, then consent, then permissions. A person who is not in a channel should not be told about `libopus0`. |
| `black_bloc/minutes.py` `wearers_of` | `channel.voice_states`, never `channel.members` — review-checklist item 27. The cache can be incomplete and the opt-out is the one check that may not be wrong. |
| `black_bloc/minutes.py` `landing` | The one home for "where does this actually go". Under `TEST_MODE` a channel the guard refuses falls back to the rehearsal home (`shadow.channel_id`), and the sentence it returns is what the panel and the site both print — the owner's rule is that a moved message says where it went. |
| `black_bloc/minutes.py` `notes_client` | Cached on the BOT, not module-global, so a test can hand one in and two guilds share one client. Same shape as `chat_llm`'s tiers. |
| `black_bloc/minutes.py` `write_notes` | Takes `via` because both doors call it and checklist 34 says one web write leaves ONE `web.` row. A failure always leaves the transcript alone — the words are the expensive half; the notes can be rebuilt from them at any time. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_session.py` `_hand_off` | Called on the reader thread, so `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe` rather than `queue.put_nowait`. A `RuntimeError` here means the loop is gone, which is a meeting already ending — it counts the drop and says nothing. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_session.py` `_transcribe` | A failure is one `minutes.transcribe_failed` row and a dropped chunk, and the loop carries on. The meeting is the thing being protected: losing a minute of transcript is a cost, losing the meeting is a disaster. |
| `black_bloc/minutes_session.py` `stop` | Order matters: flush the chunker (so the tail becomes a chunk), leave the channel, drain the queue, THEN close the row. Draining before leaving would keep recording into a queue nobody is going to read. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/minutes.py` `sweep_guild` | Three jobs on one five-minute tick: `minutes_max_hours`, the transcript purge, and a row a RESTART left open (checklist 4 — the process holds the session in memory, so a redeploy strands the row). The stranded row is closed and written up rather than left to look live for ever. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/minutes.py` `on_voice_state_update` | Reads `voice_states` and ignores the bot's own id, so "everybody left" means everybody except Black Bloc. Without that the meeting would never end on its own. |
| `black_bloc/groq.py` `WhisperClient` | Its own client rather than a method on `GroqClient`: multipart rather than JSON, a 60-second timeout rather than 15, and nothing to do with the chat tiers' token ledger. The `request` seam is what lets the suite fake it. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py` minutes block | Every `minutes_*` key is `NAMESPACE_OVERRIDE`'d onto **events**, because `settings_panel.groups()` is at Discord's hard cap of 25. `MINUTES_CHUNK_SECONDS_*` are imported from `minutes_audio` rather than re-declared — the module that enforces the band owns it. |
## Errors — every failure on the site's Logs page, and a Try again that keeps the member's place (branch `errors`, off `main` at `e7093d7`; design `info/errors-design.md`)

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `record` | ⚠️ **It may never raise.** Everything is inside one `try`, and a second failure is one `log.warning` — an error handler that throws replaces a sentence the member can read with silence. It also returns early with no guild (a DM has no `action_log`), which is why the Python traceback stays the floor rather than the row. |
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `message_of` | ⚠️ `str(error)` for a `discord.HTTPException` is `400 Bad Request (error code: 50035): …` and can carry the request body back at you. Reduced to `code + text` — Discord's own words — and everything else cut to 200. This is the one line standing between the action log and a member's modal field. |
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `step_of` | Walks the traceback to the LAST frame under `black_bloc/`, not the first. The first is whichever button was pressed; the last is the line that actually broke. Frames outside the package (discord.py, the tests' own monkeypatches) are skipped, so `step` is always a file a reader of this repo can open. |
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `render_again_of` | Three places, in order: the surface itself, its `previous` (a modal's parent panel) and its `view` (an item's). A modal never has to define one — the panel that opened it already did. Nothing found means today's plain sentence, which is why a panel with no `again` is a graceful degradation rather than a hole. |
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `RetryView.press` (`self.again(self.origin)`) | The re-render goes through the interaction the member was ALREADY on, not the button press — `edit_original_response` on the origin reaches the card they are looking at, while on the press it would replace the error message. That is also why `error_retry_minutes` is capped at 30 and defaults to 10: Discord closes the origin's token at 15 minutes, and past that the button says so in words instead of failing. |
| `black_bloc/command_errors.py` `said` | Reads the key, falls back to the constant, and swallows everything. An error path that needs a working database to say "something went wrong" is not an error path. |
| `black_bloc/panels.py` `Panel.render_again` (a property, not an attribute) | `getattr(panel, "render_again", None)` has to answer **None** for a panel that cannot rebuild itself, so the lookup is one question rather than two. Assigning a bound method on every panel would make every panel claim it can. The settable half is `again`, a plain `Move` — the shape every `render_*` / `open_*` in this repo already has. ⚠️ Not named `rerender`: `cogs/core.py` sets `view.rerender` as `(interaction, view)` while `EventDraftPanel.rerender` takes `(interaction)` alone, and one name with two arities is how this would break quietly. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` `open_zone_panel` (`again=back`) | Try again on the ZONE panel goes where **Back** goes — the draft it was raised from, or the `/event` panel — rather than redrawing the zone panel. The member has already picked their zone by the time this fires (it IS stored); putting them back on the picker would ask them to pick it twice. This is the 17:15 crash's own path. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` `EventDraftPanel.reopen` | `open_draft`, not `render_draft`: it re-asks the database and defers only if the interaction has not already been answered (the v130 `opened` fix), so the retry is safe whether the failure happened before or after the defer. `self.fields` is the same object throughout, which is the whole promise — the title survives because nothing ever copied it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py` `render_surface` | Lifted out of `MoveButton.go_back` unchanged. Back, Refresh and Try again are the same question — *draw the surface this panel is on* — and the panel's `again` is now that one function rather than a fourth copy of the dispatch. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py` `SettingsPanel(again=again)` | `again` is the module function that calls `view.rerender(interaction, view)`, so Try again always redraws whatever card the panel is currently showing — the builders reassign `rerender` per card and this follows them for free. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py` `ERROR_KINDS` in `IMPORTANT` (listed, not a prefix rule) | `tests/test_logkinds.py::_classification` reads `IMPORTANT` / `ROUTINE` / `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` and nothing else, so a prefix rule would classify at runtime and read as UNCLASSIFIED to the guard. Four names in the set keeps the one table the test checks. |
| `site/public/assets/logs.js` `LOG_FEATURES`'s `{ kind: 'error' }` entry | `error.*` is headed `core`, so a feature chip could never isolate it. The entry carries `kind` instead of `feature` and `page-audit.js` sets `state.kind` for it — one filter list, two kinds of narrowing, rather than a second chipbar. `LABELS` now skips entries with no `feature` so `featureLabel` is unchanged. |

## Boot status (branch `boot-status`, design [`boot-status-design.md`](boot-status-design.md))

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/bot.py:56` | ⚠️ **The `Database` and the `SettingsStore` are built BEFORE `super().__init__`, and the order is load-bearing.** `boot_presence(store)` has to be evaluated as an argument to `super().__init__`, because discord.py copies `status` / `activity` into `ConnectionState` there and that is what IDENTIFY reads. Assigning `self.db` afterwards keeps every other reader unchanged. Construction stays **offline** — `Database(...)` opens nothing until `connect()`. |
| `black_bloc/bot.py:89` (`_apply_boot_presence`) | ⚠️ **`setup_hook` runs BEFORE the socket, which is the whole reason this works.** `Client.login()` awaits `setup_hook()` and only then does `connect()` open a gateway (measured against discord.py 2.7.1), so assigning `self.status` / `self.activity` here — the documented public setters — changes the payload IDENTIFY is about to build. `change_presence` is NOT available: `self.ws` is `None` until `connect()`. Without this the stored `boot_status_text` could never appear, because at first ready the sentence is replaced wholesale by the head count. |
| `black_bloc/bot.py:91` | `wanted.get("status") or discord.Status.online` — with `boot_status_mode` **off** the constructor has already put `dnd` into `ConnectionState`, so it must be CLEARED rather than skipped. The IDENTIFY that results carries `status: online, game: null` where today's carries no `presence` block at all; same rendering, not byte-identical. Named in the design's Deviations. |
| `black_bloc/bot.py:123` (`close`) | The shutdown flip is the **first** thing `close` does, before the API tasks are cancelled and long before the socket goes. Discord keeps a bot's presence only while it is connected, so this reads for at most the last second — it is the ask's floor, not its aim. ⚠️ Swallowed on any exception with one `log.debug`: a presence is cosmetic and a close that a cosmetic failure can delay is worse than no flip at all (checklist 12). A bot that never connected raises `AttributeError` here on every test that calls `close()`, which is exactly the path being swallowed. |
| `black_bloc/presence.py:68` | ⚠️ **`status=online` travels in the SAME `change_presence` call as the activity.** Two calls would show a green bot still saying *"restarting and booting"* for a moment, which is the one thing the owner's ask rules out. Anything that later splits this line reintroduces it and no test but `tests/cogs/test_presence.py::test_being_ready_is_what_turns_it_green` will notice. |
| `black_bloc/presence.py:77` (`_red`) | One builder for both sentences, so the boot one and the shutdown one cannot drift in shape. `{}` when the mode is off — an empty mapping splatted into `super().__init__` or `change_presence` passes nothing at all, which is why the mode reads as "today's behaviour" rather than as a second code path. The text is trimmed to `STATUS_LIMIT` for the same reason `status_text` is (`presence.py:31`). |
| `black_bloc/presence.py:73` (`_setting`) | `store.default(key)` when there is no guild id, `store.get(guild_id, key)` when there is. No guild objects exist during `setup_hook`, so `status_guild` cannot be used and `settings.dev_guild_id` is the only handle on which server's value to read. Black Bloc is a one-server bot, so in practice it is the server. |
| `black_bloc/presence.py:96` (`go_green`) | The path `update_status` does not cover: its two early returns send nothing, so a ready bot with no guild in the cache or no `member_count` would stay red and keep saying it is restarting for the life of the process. Online with no sentence is what that bot showed before any of this existed. ⚠️ Added by the build, not asked for — the design's Deviations says so. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/presence.py:81` | `if await self.apply_status() is None` — the fallback hangs off the value `apply_status` already returned, so the ordinary boot still makes exactly ONE `change_presence` call. Also reached by the ten-minute refresh loop, where it is idempotent. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2691` | The three keys are in `CORE_KEYS` rather than left to `namespace_of`, which would have opened a `boot` group AND a `shutdown` group. The `/settings` group select is at Discord's cap of **25** and a 26th namespace is dropped **silently** — `tests/test_settings_store.py` asserts the count. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:2909` | Both sentences are plain `text`, so neither may be blank: `coerce_value` refuses an empty value for any key outside `TEXT_MAY_BE_BLANK`, and these two are not on it. `_red`'s blank branch is therefore unreachable from either door today and exists so a future blank cannot kill a boot. |
| `tests/test_bot.py` — reading `bot.activity` | ⚠️ **`Client.activity` is not idempotent** — read it once into a variable. The why, the production edge and the incident live in [`gotchas.md`](gotchas.md) (*"`Client.activity` gives a different answer the second time you read it"*), which is the one home for it. |

# Events as a forum post under BlackMail (branch `events-forum`, off `main` at `a7399b0`; design `info/events-forum-design.md`)

> Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, not `path:N` — they survive a merge and the re-key pass has nothing
> to move. Nothing here has met Discord.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/forums.py` | The one home for what requests and events both need of a forum: `tag_named` (a tag is looked up BY NAME every time — an id in a key is the thing modmail and requests deliberately refused), `forum_tags`, `forum_overwrites` (the category's own plus the bot's five) and `AUTO_ARCHIVE_MINUTES`. `black_bloc/requests.py` and its cog now import them rather than carrying a second copy; `requests.forum_tags` keeps its name and its default so nothing that reads it had to change. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `ROOM` / `POST` / `PlaceWords` | ⚠️ **A room and a post are ONE code path with TWO vocabularies.** `PLACE_WORDS[kind]` carries the button label, the modal title, the four refusals, the audit-log reason and the `CANCEL_WHY` word, so `delete_room` works on either and no sentence ever says "room" inside a post. The room entries are the live constants unchanged, which is why no existing wording moved. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `review_kind` | Reads `events.review_kind` through `cell`, so a row written before schema 45 answers `room` rather than raising. Any value that is not exactly `post` is a room — an unknown word can only ever make Black Bloc look for a channel, which is the safe half. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `review_place` | ⚠️ **The one resolver.** Every site that used to write `guild.get_channel(row["review_channel_id"])` asks this instead, so a thread id is never handed to the channel cache. It is deliberately SYNC and does not `fetch_channel`: `thread_of` in the requests cog is the precedent, and making it async would have turned ten call sites — `build_card`, `event_line`, `rename_channel` — into awaits for a cache read. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `forum_of` / `post_of` | Both CLAIM for the guard on every read. This is the v120 lesson written down in `blackmail-threads-design.md` deviation 2: `owned_channel_ids` is in memory for the life of the process, so after a restart an unclaimed forum would have swallowed every card under `TEST_MODE` while the event itself looked fine. `post_of` only claims a thread whose parent IS the keyed forum, so a thread somewhere else can never be claimed by a re-pointed row. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `rename_channel` | A room says its status in its NAME; a post says it in its TAG. So the post branch delegates to `retag_post` and returns — renaming somebody's post would be a second surface saying what the tag already says, and it is not something this build had a mandate for (the §G precedent: *the adopted post keeps its OWN name*). ⚠️ It passes the `status` ARGUMENT, not `row["status"]`: `_finish` calls it with the row it read before `set_status`, so reading the row would tag a finished event **live**. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `retag_post` / `post_is_right` | Idempotent by comparison: a post already wearing the right tag and archive flag costs no API call. That is what lets `cancel_event` and `rename_channel` both call it on the `cancel_for` path without a second edit. ⚠️ It does NOT disown the post at the archive, where `requests.retag_post` does — a test post still has to be DELETABLE by the five-minute sweep, and `allows_place` reaches that through `owns_channel`. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `open_review_post` | Returns `(post, why)`. The why is what lets `submit_event` tell a person the difference between *Discord refused* and *the guard refused*; a bare `None` would have made one sentence cover both. The card and its buttons are the post's FIRST message because a forum post must be created with one — which is why this replaces `make_review_channel` AND `post_review_card` in forum mode, rather than sitting beside them. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `submit_event` | The forum check happens BEFORE `create_event`, so a refusal never leaves an orphan row for `_recheck` to cancel five minutes later. A post that could not be opened cancels the row it already made, exactly as `make_review_channel` does. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `make_forum` | Copied from `requests.make_forum` where it fits and sharing `forum_overwrites` and `forum_tags` where it did not. Lives in `events.py` rather than the cog because two doors press it — `/event` ▸ Settings ▸ Rooms… ▸ Forum… and `POST /api/events/forum` — and `make_review_channel` already showed that channel creation belongs in the module. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `FORUM_TAG_EMOJI` | ⚠️ **SIX tags, where the design named five.** `events.py`'s `STATUSES` holds `live` as well, and a status with no tag would wear the previous one through the whole event. `test_the_forum_carries_one_tag_for_every_status_an_event_can_hold` asserts the two lists are equal, so a seventh status cannot be added without a tag. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `_recheck` | ⚠️ **A post that is not in the thread cache is NOT a gone post.** A forum post auto-archives after 1440 minutes and discord.py drops archived threads from `guild.get_thread`, so an event proposed more than a day ahead would have been cancelled for being early. Deletion is `on_thread_delete`'s to report; the two-consecutive-misses rule stays exactly as it is for rooms. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `on_thread_delete` | The post twin of `on_guild_channel_delete`: Discord raises the thread event, not the channel one, when a forum post is removed. An open event is cancelled `review_channel_deleted`; a settled one is only forgotten, which is what keeps `delete_room`'s own delete from settling the same event twice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `_sweep_finished` / `_archive_post` | Retention is a ROOM rule. A settled post in a live server is tagged and archived and KEEPS its id — `event.post_archived`, never `event.channel_deleted`, because nothing was deleted and an auditor reading the log would have believed it was. Under `TEST_MODE` a post falls through to the same delete a test room gets, which is the design's own exception. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `build_forum` | A fifth sub-page, because a Discord view takes five rows and a select fills one: Rooms… already spends rows 0–2 on three selects. The mode select, the forum picker (forum channels only), **Make the forum** and the way back fit on three. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/events.py` — `event_forum_make` | Calls the module's own `make_forum` with `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and `note()`s nothing, so one press leaves ONE `web.event.forum_made` row (checklist 34). Declared before `/{event_id}` so no id can swallow the word `forum`. |

## Move an open event's room into the forum (branch `events-move-to-forum`, off `main` at `90252a6`; design `info/events-forum-design.md` §H)

> Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, not `path:N` — they survive a merge and the re-key pass has nothing
> to move. Nothing here has met Discord.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `remove_place` | ⚠️ **§H asked for a `settle=False` on `delete_room`; this is that, as an extraction rather than a flag.** A flag would have had to turn off TWO things, not one: the cancel *and* the `set_review(None, …)` that clears `review_channel_id` — which the move has just pointed at the new post, so clearing it would have thrown the post away. `remove_place` is the guard check, the delete, the disown and nothing decided about the row; `delete_room` keeps its own cancel, its own `set_review` and its own `event.channel_deleted` row, so its log and its sentences are byte-for-byte what they were. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `move_room_to_forum`, the ORDER | ⚠️ **The post is opened and the row re-pointed BEFORE the room is deleted, and that order is what stops the event being cancelled behind the move.** `on_guild_channel_delete` finds its row with `event_for_channel(review_channel_id)`; once the row points at the thread, the old room id matches nothing and the listener's `_cancel` never fires. Deleting first would have raced a cancel against the move. It also means a post that Discord refuses to open leaves the room exactly as it was — the refusal is answered in words and nothing is lost. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `move_room_to_forum`, the log | ONE headed row, `event.room_moved` with `from` and `to`, and no second `event.channel_deleted` — the room's removal is what `from` names. Checklist 34: the route passes `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and notes nothing of its own. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `move_room_to_forum`, a room that no longer resolves | `room_of` may answer `None` on a row whose id is stale. The move still runs: the post is opened and the row re-pointed, and the line and the delete are skipped. The alternative — refusing — would have stranded the event in a room that is not there. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `may_move_to_forum` vs the function's own refusals | Two different questions, deliberately. `may_move_to_forum` is what a DOOR renders on and includes the MODE (`events_review_mode` = forum); `move_room_to_forum` does not check the mode at all, so staff who reach the route with the mode still on `room` are allowed to move an event into a forum that exists (staff final say, 2026-09-03). §H lists four refusals and the mode is not among them. |
| `black_bloc/events.py` — `moved_line` | Checklist 17: the one staff-editable sentence this build adds catches `Exception` around `.format` and falls back to the default with a log line, because `events_moved_line` is typed by a person. `settings_store.checked_moved_line` refuses a stray placeholder at the door as well, so the fallback is the floor rather than the plan. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `moving_notice_view` | §H puts **Move to the forum** on the room's Delete card, and the card is posted at PROPOSE time — where forum mode gives a post, not a room. So the factory is honest (it asks the mode and the forum, exactly as §H says) and in practice always answers False today. The reachable Discord door is `build_card`; the deviation says so. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `build_card` | The `/event` panel's own event card is the only Discord surface that re-renders, so it is where a room made before v136 can actually be moved. Gated on `may_move_to_forum` AND `may_delete_room`, at `row=2` so it never crowds the moves on row 0. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/events.py` — `DecisionButton(row=…)` | The one thing the persistent template gained: a row for the panel card. `DynamicItem` proxies `.row` to the button it wraps, which is also why `has_item` in the tests cannot see the label and `offers_the_move` exists. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/events.py` — `event_move_to_forum` | Imports the cog's two view factories INSIDE the function, the way `handoff.py` imports the requests cog. A post opened with no view is a post with no Approve and no Deny, which would have been worse than no route. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs` — `checkEventsMove` | NOT a `contract.json` row: `checkRoutes` reseeds before every entry and a fresh seed has no forum, while seeding one would make the entry that MAKES the forum refuse as already-there. The bespoke pass makes the forum first and then walks the move, the second press and a settled event. |

## YouTube uploads removed — what is left, and what the empty spaces mean (branch `youtube-uploads-removal`, off `main` at `9bc1982`; design `info/youtube-uploads-removal-design.md`)

> Owner, 2026-09-18: *"the youtube uploader we should just fully trash"*. Keys are CONSTRUCT
> NAMES, not `path:N`. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord** — a worktree holds no token.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `settings_store` ▸ the seven gone keys | `youtube_mode`, `youtube_channel_id`, `youtube_ping_role_id`, `youtube_ping_fan_roles`, `youtube_announce_shorts`, `youtube_template` and `youtube_poll_minutes` are gone from the registry (**284 → 277**), and so are `YOUTUBE_MODES` / `YOUTUBE_TEMPLATE` / `YOUTUBE_POLL_MINUTES` / `YOUTUBE_POLL_MIN_MINUTES`. ⚠️ **Rows already stored in `guild_settings` for those keys are LEFT.** They are inert — nothing reads them — and a migration that deleted them would be a write against the audit trail for no gain. `SettingsStore.load` ignores a key it does not know. |
| `command_visibility.HIDDEN_WHEN_OFF` | ⚠️ **The feature's on/off is `youtube_live_mode` from now on.** `youtube_mode` was the key that hid `/youtube`; it no longer exists, so the entry moved rather than being dropped — dropping it would have left `/youtube` visible on a server that had turned YouTube off. |
| `settings_panel.MODE_LABELS` | `_hidden_when_off_modes` derives a label with `key.removesuffix("_mode")`, which turns `youtube_live_mode` into `youtube_live` — a namespace `FEATURE_LABELS` has no entry for, so the root panel would have printed the raw string. `MODE_LABELS["youtube_live"]` points back at `FEATURE_LABELS["youtube"]` rather than repeating the word, so the label still has one home. |
| `logkinds.FEATURE_LABELS` | `youtube` reads **YouTube**, not *YouTube uploads*. It is the label the Logs page, the log-level help sentence and the settings root all read, so it had to stop naming the half that went. |
| `logkinds.ROUTINE` | Six kinds removed: `youtube.announce`, `youtube.mode`, `youtube.poll_degraded`, `youtube.seeded`, `youtube.setup`, `youtube.skipped`. ⚠️ **A classification entry nothing emits is a table nobody maintains** — `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_no_classification_entry_is_dead` is what makes that a rule rather than a preference. Rows already in `action_log` keep the old kinds and read as unclassified, exactly as KI-19 describes for the modmail renames. `youtube.would_announce` and `youtube.post_failed` were never table entries (a shadow kind and a `_failed` suffix), so nothing had to be removed for them. |
| `youtube.YouTubeClient._title_of` | ⚠️ **The title used to come from the uploads FEED, free and keyless; it now costs one unit and only with a key.** `channels.list(part=snippet, id=…)` is the replacement, and without a key `resolve` answers `(channel_id, "")` — the panel and the links table already fall back to the id. The old free path was measured dead anyway: YouTube's feed endpoint answered 404 for every channel from every address on 2026-09-17 (20/20). |
| `cogs/content/youtube.set_link` | The INSERT no longer names `etag` or `seeded`; both columns keep their schema defaults (`NULL`, `0`). They are still in the table — schema is additive here — and nothing reads them any more, so no surface shows a permanent *not counted yet*. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.counts` | Down to `{"links": n}`. `videos` and `announced` counted `youtube_videos`, which is now orphaned; a count of a table nothing writes is a number that only ever goes stale. |
| `api/tools/youtube.youtube_status` | Nine upload fields gone (`running`, `last_ok_at`, `last_error`, `failures`, `fetches`, `unchanged`, `unchanged_ratio`, `videos`, `announced`) and `GET /api/youtube/videos` gone with the table it read (**187 → 186** routes). `api_key_set`, `links` and every live field stay, and `tests/api/tools/test_youtube.py` asserts the nine are ABSENT rather than merely zero — a zero would read as *the sweep ran and found nothing*. |
| `youtube.STAFF_MOVES` | **Setup** went with the sub-panel it opened. Everything that panel edited was an upload key except `youtube_panel_minutes`, which keeps both doors through the settings registry — the `/settings` panel's own key card and the dashboard's Settings page (checklist 33). |
| `selftest_panels.SENDERS` | The `youtube` sender posted a rendered upload sentence; there is no upload sentence any more, and the live announcement is go-live's card, which `send_golive` already posts. `send_pings` stopped naming `youtube_ping_role_id` in its prefix for the same reason. |
| `tests/fixtures/youtube_feed.xml` | Deleted with the parser it pinned. The five `youtube_*_page.html` fixtures are the LIVE half's and stay. |

## One reconcile at a time — the boot double-post (branch `boot-reconcile-once`, off `main` at `1177bce`; design `info/front-door-design.md` ▸ Deviations ▸ **14**)

> Written 2026-09-18 by the fix for the 16:08 incident. Keys are CONSTRUCT
> NAMES, not `path:N`. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met live Discord** — a worktree holds no token.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `loops.Reconciler` | Lives beside `wait_ready` because it is the same kind of fact — a rule about how a loop behaves, kept in one place so no cog grows its own copy. It holds ONE `asyncio.Lock` per cog instance; `asyncio.Lock()` binds no event loop at construction on Python 3.10+, which is why a cog built outside a running loop is fine. |
| `loops.Reconciler.run` | ⚠️ **`work` is a callable, not an awaited coroutine, on purpose.** The whole fix is that the reconcile's state read happens INSIDE the lock; handing `run` an already-started coroutine would read nothing earlier, but handing it a *value* computed outside the lock would. It returns True when it ran and False when the window said it had just run — `on_ready` reads that, the tests assert on it. |
| `loops.Reconciler.run` ▸ `stamp` | `on_post_published` re-posts ONE guild's door. It takes the lock (it posts, so it must) but passes `stamp=False`, because closing the skip window on a single-guild move would let the next `on_ready` skip a sweep that never ran. |
| `loops.RECENT_SECONDS` | 60. It exists to stop `on_ready` repeating what `cog_load` did milliseconds earlier; it is deliberately NOT a settings key, because it is a fact about one boot sequence rather than a decision anybody would want to change (checklist 33 is about decisions). |
| `FrontDoor.reconcile` / `Modmail.reconcile_tickets` / `Events.reconcile_events` | Each is now a two-line locked wrapper over a `_sweep` holding the old body, so every existing caller and every existing test is unchanged. The loop's tick calls them plainly; only `on_ready` passes `skip_if_recent=True`. |
| `Events._sweep` | ⚠️ **The lock is what stops the DOUBLED `event.room_forgotten` row**, not any change to `forget_room`. Two boot reconciles both read `events_by_status` while `review_channel_id` was still set and both forgot the same room. Serialised, the second re-reads and finds it already NULL. |
| `posted.duplicates_near` | The boot-time guard. It reads `channel.history` for the last `DUPLICATE_MINUTES` (5) and returns every OTHER message wearing a custom id starting with the family head — `door:` for the front door, `modmail:ticket:<guild_id>` for the ticket button. ⚠️ **It swallows every exception and answers `[]`**: a channel that will not be read must not stop a door being put back, so the guard fails OPEN and the lock is the real fix. |
| `frontdoor._redoor` ▸ `also` / `modmail._repanel` ▸ `also` | The check sits immediately before the post, never on the path that finds its door where it left it — so a healthy sweep costs no extra API call, and a duplicate beside a healthy door is invisible (deviation 14 says so out loud). Finding one writes `frontdoor.duplicate_seen` / `modmail.panel_duplicate_seen` and returns; ⚠️ **nothing is deleted**, because staff have the final say on what comes down. |
| `logkinds.IMPORTANT` | Both new kinds are IMPORTANT, not routine: a room holding two front doors is something a person has to decide about. `frontdoor.duplicate_seen` is a module constant, so `tests/test_logkinds.py` `KNOWN_DYNAMIC` gains its call site; `modmail.panel_duplicate_seen` is a bare literal like its neighbours and needs no entry. |
| `tests/…/yields_before_it_sends` | Two reconciles only race if something between the read and the write gives the other one a turn. A real `channel.send` is an HTTP call and always does; `FakeText.send` awaits nothing, so the tests wrap it. ⚠️ **Take the lock out and both concurrency tests fail with exactly the incident's rows** — that is what makes them regression tests rather than decoration. |
# The post editor's paste converter (branch `posts-paste`, off `main` at `0b4e7c4`)

> Keyed by CONSTRUCT NAME, not by `path:N` — nothing here can go stale on a line number.
> Why each call was made is [`posts-paste-design.md`](posts-paste-design.md)'s `## Deviations`
> foot; it is not repeated here. ⚠️ **No browser has run any of this.**

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `site/public/assets/clipmd.js` — no `DOMParser` | ⚠️ **Deliberate, and the reason the file is a tokeniser.** A DOM walk would have needed a fake node tree in the node test, which proves the WALK and leaves the PARSE — the half that actually meets Google's markup — unproven. A string in and a string out means the browser and the deploy gate run one code path over one input, and `site/mock/clipmd.test.mjs` needs no dependency (`jsdom` is not allowed and there is no `package.json` to hang it on). |
| `clipmd.marksOf` — why a style beats a tag | ⚠️ **Google Docs wraps the entire selection in `<b style="font-weight:normal" id="docs-internal-guid-…">`.** Read the `<b>` and every word of the paste is bold. So an explicit `font-weight` in the element's own style DECIDES, and only a missing one falls through to the tag or to what was inherited. The same one rule makes `font-weight:700` bold and `font-weight:400` — which Docs puts on ordinary words — not. `font-style` and `text-decoration:none` work the same way. |
| `clipmd` — `if (next.href) next.marks = { ...next.marks, u: false }` | Docs styles its own links `text-decoration:underline; color:#1155cc`, on a `<span>` INSIDE the `<a>` — which is why the override is applied to the inherited context rather than to the anchor element, so it survives into the span. Without it every pasted link would arrive as `__[words](url)__`. That underline is the editor drawing a link, not the author underlining a word. |
| `clipmd` — `start()`'s early return | A block inside an EMPTY `li` or heading fills the block already open instead of starting a new one. ⚠️ **Docs wraps each `<li>`'s words in a `<p>`**; without this every bullet would close its own list item, arrive as a bare paragraph, and the list would vanish. A SECOND `<p>` in the same item does start a new block — the item already has runs by then — which is the known limit. |
| `clipmd.headingFromRuns` — every run, not any run | A block is promoted to a heading only when EVERY run in it carries a font size and the smallest is over the threshold. `any` would turn a sentence with one big word into a heading; requiring a size on every run means unstyled HTML (where `pt` is `null`) can never be promoted by accident. Docs puts `font-size:11pt` on body words, which is what makes 13.5pt a safe floor. |
| `clipmd.HEADING_PT` | `20 / 16 / 13.5` points, keyed to Docs' **11pt** body default. ⚠️ **Library knowledge, not measurement** — a document written at a different base size may promote or fail to promote a heading. `ptOf` converts px at `0.75` and `em`/`%` against the same 11pt base. |
| `clipmd.parse` — a dropped element takes its contents | `script`, `style`, `head`, `noscript`, `iframe`, `object`, `svg` and `template` are not just skipped as tags: the scanner JUMPS past the matching close tag, so a stylesheet's `font-weight: 700` can never be read as words. A void or self-closed member of the same set (`<meta charset>`, which Docs leads with) is skipped WITHOUT the jump — hunting `</meta>` would have eaten the whole document. |
| `clipmd.parse` — a close tag that matches nothing | Ignored, never fatal. Clipboard HTML is whatever an editor felt like writing; a converter that throws on it would drop a paste on the floor, and `markdownFromPaste` would fall back to the plain paste with no sign that anything was lost. |
| `clipmd.wrapped` — spaces outside the marks | Leading and trailing whitespace is moved OUTSIDE the `**`/`*`/`__`/`~~`, because Discord does not render `** word **`. Runs merge first (`sameRun`), so a word split across three `<span>`s with identical styling is bolded once rather than three times. |
| `clipmd.lineOf` — a heading drops its bold | Docs headings are usually bold and `# **Rules**` draws literal asterisks in Discord, where a heading is already bold. Bold inside a paragraph is untouched. |
| `clipmd` — the blank line between two lists | Two `li` blocks are joined by ONE newline only when they are the same kind; a `<ul>` touching an `<ol>` gets a blank line, so Discord starts a second list instead of continuing the first. |
| `clipmd.linkOf` | A link whose words already ARE the address renders bare — masking it would say less, not more. The comparison strips the scheme and a trailing slash, so `example.com/x` pointing at `https://example.com/x` is the same address. A link with no words at all renders as NOTHING: its only content was an image, images are stripped, and emitting a URL where the doc showed a picture would add something the author never wrote. `LINKABLE` is why `javascript:` keeps its words and loses its href. |
| `page-posts.markdownFromPaste` — the two ways it says no | Empty `text/html` → the browser's own plain paste happens and nothing is intercepted. Markdown that EQUALS the trimmed `text/plain` → also nothing, because there is no formatting to keep and no reason to take the paste over or to show a note. Both `getData` and the conversion are wrapped: a refused clipboard read or a fragment the converter chokes on must degrade to an ordinary paste, never to a lost one. |
| `page-posts.insertAtCaret` — `execCommand` first | ⚠️ **`document.execCommand('insertText')` is what keeps Ctrl+Z working**, and the note under the box promises exactly that. It is deprecated and still the only way to write into a textarea inside the browser's own undo stack. `setRangeText` is the fallback for a browser that refuses it — and it is the fallback precisely because its undo behaviour is not guaranteed. ⚠️ Neither path has been observed in a browser (sweep `PP-c`). |
| `page-posts.PASTE_HINT` / `PASTE_KEPT` / `PASTE_DISMISS` | Page constants, **not settings keys**, on purpose. The standing rule (owner, 2026-09-17) is that every word THE BOT POSTS is editable on the site; these are the site talking to staff about the site and Discord never sees them. Three more registry rows would also push the `/settings` group select, already at its 25 cap. |
| `site.css` — `.postboxlabel` | `.postboxhead` is `justify-content: space-between`, so adding the hint as a third child would have pushed the counter into the middle of the row. The label and the hint are wrapped in one span instead, and the counter stays hard right. |

# Co-streaming — one announcement naming both platforms (branch `costream`, 2026-09-20)

> Design: `info/costream-design.md`. Owner, 2026-09-20 16:1x: *"It would be silly to suppress one of
> the live avenues someone is on"*. Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge cannot
> move them. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `golive.suppressed` — why the FILL wraps and the template never does | `<…>` is Discord's own preview-suppression syntax, and the owner's ask is that only the Twitch stream previews. If the `<>` lived in `golive_costream_template` instead, the first person to reword the sentence on the Settings page would take them out without knowing what they were for, and the YouTube link would grow a second preview card. `{url}` is filled BARE — measured against `render` (`golive_template` has never wrapped it) — so the Twitch side keeps exactly the shape it has today. An empty url fills as `""`, never `<>`. |
| `golive.costream_order` — platform, not arrival | `source`/`url`/`platform` record whichever platform came FIRST because that is the audit trail; the SENTENCE is ordered by platform, so Twitch leads whether it arrived first or second. Two platforms that are neither Twitch keep the order they arrived in — there is nothing to prefer. |
| `golive.costream_render` — no `tidy`, on purpose | It behaves exactly as `render` does (`format_map` over the tolerant `_Fields`, a warning and the default template on a bad one), because the design asks the two keys to behave alike. `ended_render` tidies because its `{duration}` and `{title}` are routinely empty; a co-stream always has two platforms and two urls, so there is nothing to tidy away. `costream_author` DOES tidy — it is an author line, and `ended_author` set that precedent. |
| `golive.again_render` vs `render` | `render` is for a POST and prepends `ping_prefix(...)`. `again_render` is for an EDIT and prepends whatever mention the message already carries (`mention_prefix(content)`). ⚠️ **That is the guard against a second ping**: an edit can never introduce a mention that was not already in the content, whatever the ping keys say now. |
| `golive.joins_session` — one home, two callers | The go-live cog and the YouTube cog both ask *does this second platform join the open session?* and must never answer differently. Mode on, `also_source` still null (one co-stream at a time), and a platform that differs from the open session's — an unnamed platform on either side answers no, because "different" cannot be established. |
| `cogs/content/golive.GoLive._costream_card` — `rebuilt` | The card is kept and restyled when the leading platform did not change, so the Twitch box art and thumbnail survive; it is REBUILT from `announcement_embed` only when Twitch arrives second and has to take the lead, because that is the one case where the richer `StreamInfo` is the incoming one and the row holds no art. A message with no embed at all (posted while `golive_embed` was off) is left with none — same rule as `_ended_embed`. |
| `cogs/content/golive.promote_also_platform` — game and title stay | Promotion copies `also_*` into `source`/`url`/`platform` and leaves `game`/`title` alone. A co-stream is one person streaming one thing to two places, so the game the Twitch side reported is still the right game for the YouTube side; blanking it would turn *"streaming **Celeste**"* into *"streaming **something**"* the moment one platform stopped. It is also why the row keeps no `also_game`/`also_title`. |
| `cogs/content/golive.open_session_on` — `source = ? OR also_source = ?` | Every end signal names ONE platform (`presence`, `twitch`, `youtube`). `open_session_for(..., source)` could only ever find the primary, so a co-stream whose Twitch half ended would have looked like no session at all and the announcement would have sat there claiming both. For a row with no `also_source` the two queries return the same thing, which is why today's single-platform behaviour is untouched. |
| `cogs/content/golive.GoLive._end_live` — drop before end | ⚠️ **The bug this exists to stop: closing a session because ONE platform ended while the other is still live.** A row with `also_source` set and a named ending source is a `drop_platform`, never `end_session`; only a row with one side left takes today's ended path, so the past-tense edit still happens exactly once, at the end of the last platform. |
| `cogs/content/golive.GoLive._side_live` — `platform=None` means "any" | `_still_live` passes `None` so a single-platform row keeps today's rule (ANY streaming presence proves it is live). A co-stream passes each side's platform, so a Discord presence that says YouTube cannot vouch for the Twitch half. `same_platform` returns True for `None` for exactly that reason. |
| `cogs/content/golive.GoLive.poll_once` — why the sweep still short-circuits | It calls `_go_live` when there is no open session **or** when `joins_session` says Twitch would join one. Calling it unconditionally would have been simpler and would have re-run `_note_streaming` — a `pings.saw_streaming` upsert — once a minute for the length of every stream. |
| `cogs/content/golive.GoLive.add_platform` vs `_add_platform_once` | The public door takes the per-member lock and re-reads the open session inside it (checklist 6 and 37: the read and the decision must be on the same side of the lock). `_go_live_once` is already holding that lock, so it calls the inner one — taking it twice would deadlock. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.JOINED_BECAUSE` | The `youtube.live_seen` row reads `announced: true, because: "joined_session"` — a detail on an existing kind, not a new kind. It is the one thing that distinguishes *the probe worked and a post was edited* from *the probe worked and nothing happened* (`open_session:<source>`), which is the silence KI-30's follow-up was about. |
| `cogs/content/youtube.GoLive door` — `_hand_off(…, door)` | The YouTube cog names the method it wants by string and gets the same missing-cog log and the same `youtube.live_announce_failed` row whichever door it is. Two copies of that seven-line fallback was the alternative. |
| `golive_costream_mode` ships **on** | The design's §B says so and the owner's ask is that suppressing a live avenue is the wrong default. It changes no posting behaviour on its own: with nobody co-streaming it is never consulted, and `off` restores the v135 hold-back exactly, which `test_with_the_mode_off_the_second_platform_is_held_back_as_before` and the two YouTube hold-back tests prove by name. |
| `settings_store.checked_costream` — one validator, two keys | The design asks the template and the author line to behave alike, so they share the placeholder set and the refusal sentence. It is why `{duration}` — legal on `golive_end_template` — is refused here: nothing fills it on this path, and a placeholder that renders as literal `{duration}` in a live announcement is worse than a refusal at set time. |
# The Go-live page rebuilt — one list of people (branch `golive-page`, off `main` at `948ff05`; design `info/golive-page-design.md`)

Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, not `path:N`, so nothing here can go stale on a line number.

| Where | Why |
|---|---|
| `golive-join.js` — the whole module | PURE on purpose: no DOM, no `fetch`, no import of `ui.js`. That is the only reason `site/mock/golive-join.test.mjs` can feed it the six traps under plain node with no dependency, exactly as `clipmd.js` is fed. Anything that needs a document belongs in `page-golive.js`. |
| `golive-join.liveByUser` — the `presence` preference | Two open sessions for one member resolve to ONE row, and `live` comes from the session whose `source` is **not** `presence`. Discord presence is the weakest signal there is (it says "this person is streaming somewhere"), so a session the Twitch or YouTube watcher opened outranks it. A co-stream session (`also_source` set) beats both and LOCKS the answer to `both`, because one session covering two platforms is a stronger fact than two sessions disagreeing. |
| `golive-join.joinStreamers` — the row set is a UNION of five payloads plus the open sessions | ⚠️ A member with a ping role and NO link at all must still have a row, or a whole role goes invisible and nobody can remove it. The same reasoning adds session users: somebody the *Live now* chip filters to has to exist in the list it filters. `streamers` (the fan-role table) overwrites `listing`'s role columns because it is the authoritative one; `listing` is read first so its `listed` / `last_live_at` / `live_count` survive. |
| `golive-join.routeTyped` — refuse, never guess | A value carrying BOTH a `twitch.tv` and a `youtube.com` marker is refused in words naming both shapes rather than routed by whichever regex ran first. A bare word is a Twitch login, because that is the one shape with no address around it; a bare `UC…` is a channel id, so the id test runs before the bare-login test. `javascript:`-style nonsense and `kick.com/x` fall through to the same refusal — it says what BOTH good shapes look like, so the sentence works for either mistake. |
| `golive-join.placeSettings` — the catch-all is the last drawer, not a filter | The partition is total by construction: a key that matches no drawer's `keys` list and no `holds` predicate lands in *Everything else*. That is what makes the every-key-lands-once test satisfiable, and it is why a settings key added next month appears on the page instead of vanishing. ⚠️ It is not permission to leave keys unsorted — the test also pins which drawer each of today's 36 lands in. |
| `page-golive.streamerRow` / `showStreamer` — the drawer, not an inline panel | The design asked for an inline panel; this is Moderation's construct instead (`page-moderation.caseRow` + `showCase`): a `<button class="grid-row">` ending in a `chevronRight`, opening `ui.js:openDrawer`. A real `<button>` gives Enter, Space, focus and the pointer for free, the chevron is what makes a row look clickable at rest, and `openDrawer` is a native modal `<dialog>` so Escape, the focus trap and the backdrop are the platform's job. `openDrawer` is called TWICE — a placeholder, then the awaited body — because the Ping-role group has to `await roleSelect()` and a drawer that opens empty for 200 ms reads as broken. Design ▸ Deviations ▸ **1**. |
| `page-golive` — *Live now* is BOTH a section and a filter chip, deliberately | Ruling 3, recorded here so nobody "fixes" it. They answer different questions: the SECTION answers *what is happening right now* (a card per open stream, glanceable, no interaction), the CHIP answers *show me only those rows* (navigation inside a 21-row list). One fact in two places would be the same number rendered twice; this is one fact serving two jobs. Remove either and the page loses something the other does not do. |
| `page-golive.unsection` | `logs.js:logsSection` returns a `section.sect`, and `layout.js:mountSections` collects sections with a DESCENDANT query on `#dash` — so three log blocks nested inside *Everything else* would have added three rows to the *On this page* rail and made "five sections" a lie. The class and the two `data-` attributes are stripped and the inner `details` forced open, because the chips above it own visibility now. ⚠️ `logs.js` is shared by nineteen other pages and is NOT forked. |
| `page-golive.logDrawer` — why **All** stacks three blocks | `logsSection` takes one feature and fetches `/api/actions?feature=…`; there is no multi-feature call and no combined route, and this build adds none. So *All* shows all three. The chip labels come from `logs.js:LOG_FEATURES` (**Go-live**, **YouTube**, **Ping roles**) rather than the mock's *Twitch*, because the `golive` feature's log carries both platforms. |
| `page-golive.drawer` — a page-local `<details>` rather than `ui.js:foldout` | `foldout`'s summary is an uppercase label and its count slot is mono, which turns ruling 2's sentence (*Ping roles · 11 settings · the shared roles · Discord onboarding*) into a shout. The page-local version is three CSS classes and no shared-module change. |
| `page-golive.warnCell` / `warningsFor` | Ruling 2's other half: the strip grows a pressable `.stat` when `golive_ping_role_id` is unset or onboarding is managed + community + never written, and pressing it opens the section, opens the Ping-roles drawer and scrolls to it. It is the only way those two setup cards are reachable without opening a closed drawer, which is what earns them the right to be in one. |
| `page-golive.SAMPLES` — the platform toggle is CLIENT-side | `/api/golive/preview` renders through the bot and takes no platform parameter, and this build adds none. So the chips change the sample the as-you-type previews are filled with (`{platform}` becomes Twitch or YouTube), while the *Wording* card below stays the bot's own rendering, labelled as such. Two previews with different jobs, not one fact twice. |
| `site.css` — `.grid-table.streamers` | The third column template on the shared grid, after Moderation's default and `.grid-table.members`. The construct was already built to be extended this way; adding a template is not the same as forking the row. |

# The boot run follows test mode, and `/test` (branch `selftest-boot`, off `main` at `74c25bf`; design `info/selftest-design.md` §K)

> Owner, 2026-09-20: *"now that we're no longer in test mode, we don't need to have black bloc post every
> panel in logs. Let's leave that as a default when in test mode and then a /test command that spews out all
> the panels for staff only."* Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge cannot move them.
> ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `settings_store.SettingsStore.default` — `selftest_on_boot` reads `self.settings.test_mode` | The old `SELFTEST_ON_BOOT_DEFAULT = True` is GONE rather than flipped to `False`, because a rehearsal that has to remember to switch the self-test back on is a rehearsal that proves nothing. The branch is a DEFAULT, so a stored row still wins either way and the key is still one bool in group `core` — which is what keeps checklist 33 satisfied (the Settings page and the `/settings` key card both reach it, both directions). ⚠️ It is read through `getattr(..., "test_mode", False)` because `default()` is also called from tooling that hands the store a bare settings stand-in; an absent flag means OFF, which is the safe side. |
| `selftest.Run.channel` vs `selftest_channel()` | The override is on the RUN, not on the setting, so `/test where:#x` never writes anything a later boot would inherit. `post()` falls back to `selftest_channel()` when it is `None`, which is exactly today's path — the boot and website doors pass nothing and behave as before. |
| `selftest.Run.keep_minutes` is mirrored onto `selftest_runs.keep_minutes` | ⚠️ **The row is the one that matters, and the in-memory field alone would have been a bug.** The purge is a 60-second `tasks.loop` in `cogs/core.py` that re-reads `selftest_messages` from scratch; the `Run` object is gone the moment `finish()` clears `_mark`, and gone twice over after a deploy. Without the column a `/test keep:60` run would have had its cards swept at the next tick by the global `selftest_purge_minutes`, which is 1 — so the option would have looked like it worked and then not. Schema 46 → 47, added by `ADDED_COLUMNS` (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`), NULL meaning "use the setting". |
