| `selftest._kept_for` — why it tolerates a row with no such key | `waiting_messages` is a LEFT JOIN now, so every row it returns carries `keep_minutes`; the `try` is there for the orphan case (a message row whose run row was deleted) and for any caller that hands in a plain dict. `int(asked or fallback)` also means a stored `0` reads as "use the setting" rather than "delete immediately" — the registry refuses 0 at set time, and this is the second line of that defence. |
| `selftest.purge` — the cutoff moved INSIDE the loop | It used to be one `cutoff` computed before the walk. It is now per row, because two runs waiting at the same moment can want different minutes. `now` is still computed once, so every row in one sweep is judged against the same instant. |
| `selftest.asked_for` — `where`/`keep` on the log rows only when asked | A row that always carried `where` would state the resolved channel as though somebody had chosen it, and the Logs page could not tell a `/test where:#x` from an ordinary run. Absent means nobody typed it. |
| `selftest.keep_asked` — `coerce_value(SELFTEST_PURGE_MINUTES, …)` | One set of bounds for the setting and for the option (1–1440), and the refusal a person reads is the registry's own `KEY_MIN_REASON`/`KEY_MAX_REASON` sentence. ⚠️ Deliberately NOT `app_commands.Range`: Range is refused by Discord's client with Discord's own wording, which is a bare-ish refusal the house rule forbids, and it would put the numbers in a second place. |
| `cogs/core.Core.test` — the gate is `require_staff` in the body, not the lock | `default_permissions(STAFF_ONLY)` only HIDES the command from members; `settings_store.is_staff_command` walks the callback's own names looking for `require_staff`, and `tests/test_bot.py::test_nothing_a_member_can_run_is_hidden_behind_the_lock` fails if the call is moved into a helper this one does not name. Same three guards as `/settings`, in the same order: guild, staff, database. |
| `cogs/core.selftest_on_demand` — the defer is AFTER both refusals | A bad `keep` and a missing channel are answered on the initial response, so the person gets one ephemeral sentence rather than a spinner that resolves into a refusal. Everything past that point can take a minute (107 checks, 24 posts), which is why the defer is there at all. |
| `cogs/core.selftest_body` | The counts sentence differs between the two doors (`/test` names the channel, the settings card does not) but the failure list under it must not, so the list is built once. |

# Spotlight — a Twitch channel with nobody here behind it (branch `spotlight`, 2026-09-20)

> Design: `info/spotlight-design.md`. Owner, 2026-09-20 16:5x: *"we have a twitch channel
> gamesdonequick, it 1 needs to be tracked even though its not in the discord."* Keys are CONSTRUCT
> NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge cannot move them. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord or
> Helix** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `spotlight_channels` / `spotlight_sessions` — why NOT a `golive_sessions` row | `golive_sessions` is keyed by `user_id` and its partial unique index is one open session per MEMBER. A spotlight has no member, so a row there would need a sentinel id, and every surface that joins on it — the Members page, the Streamers list, `pings.saw_streaming`, the fan-role path — would inherit that lie and have to special-case it. Its own two tables cost one more query per tick and let every one of those stay honest. |
| `spotlight.KEPT` / `spotlight.pin` — the owner's two meanings of "pin" | The ask uses *pin* for both *"certain reoccuring channels like GamesDoneQuick can be always in the list"* and *"pin those streams in the go live channel"*. Here a ROW is **kept** (`expires_at IS NULL`) or **expires**; a MESSAGE is **pinned** (the `pin` column). Nothing in the code or the wording uses one word for the other, which is why `until_words()` answers `kept` and never `pinned`. |
| `spotlight.next_bump_at` — `last_bump_at or started_at` | §A's *"measured from `started_at` then from `last_bump_at`"* is one expression, not two branches: the base is whichever exists. That is also why the first poll can never bump — at `started_at + 0` the base is the start and the due time is `hours` away — and why a bot restart does not double-bump, because `last_bump_at` is on the row, not in memory. |
| `spotlight.bump_render` — `tidy` on, and the default wording changed for it | `tidy`'s `DANGLING` regex strips a trailing `in` before a full stop, which is exactly what it exists to do when `{game}` is empty — and it silently ate the word in the design's *"{duration} in."*, rendering *"4 h."*. The default is *"{duration} so far."* for that reason. Keeping `tidy` is still right: a stream with no game must not read *"**{game}**"* or *"****"*. |
| `spotlight.is_expired` — an unreadable date is NOT due | A `expires_at` that will not parse returns `False` with a warning, so a typo or a schema surprise leaves the row on the list rather than deleting a channel the owner curated. Checklist 5 says a bad row must not block forever; here the failure that matters is the opposite one, and deleting on a value nobody can read is unrecoverable. |
| `Spotlight._seen` — the re-read inside the lock | Checklist 6. The poll reads the whole list, then acts on each row; between those two moments a route or the panel can have removed or extended it. `_seen` takes the row's own lock and re-reads by id, so the decision and the state it was made from are on the same side of the lock, beside the partial unique index that makes a second open session impossible anyway. |
| `Spotlight.reconcile_open_sessions` under `loops.Reconciler` | Checklist 37, and it is the same incident: `cog_load` calls it and `on_ready` calls it again, so without the lock both can read *this session's message is gone* before either writes the `ended_at`. `skip_if_recent=True` on the `on_ready` path only; `cog_load`'s call never skips, because it is the one that must run. |
| `Spotlight._end` — state first, messages second | Checklist 12. `end_session` and the `golive.spotlight_ended` row land before the unpin, the past-tense edit and the reminder cleanup, so a Discord failure at any of those three leaves the session correctly closed rather than open forever. The three that follow each say so in their own way: `_unpin` writes `golive.spotlight_unpin_failed`, the edit logs at info, the cleanup leaves the reminder and says which. |
| `Spotlight._unpin` — reads the MESSAGE, not the key | Checklist 3, the same rule as `polls._unpin`. The pin comes off because `message.pinned` is true, never because `row["pin"]` still says so — otherwise turning the pin off mid-stream would strand a pinned announcement nobody could unpin through the app. |
| `Spotlight._helix` — the go-live cog's client | One `TwitchClient` for the whole process: one app token, one `aiohttp` session, one thing to close. `cog_unload` here cancels the loop and closes nothing, because the client is not this cog's to close. The consequence is named in the panel and on the page: no key, nothing polls, and `words.NO_KEY` is the sentence. |
| `Spotlight._post` — where a rehearsal goes | `on` posts to `golive_channel_id`. Anything else resolves `shadow.channel_id` and prepends `shadow.note_line`, so the go-live channel never sees it. ⚠️ The go-live cog itself does NOT do this today — it logs `would_announce` and posts nothing — so the design's *"as go-live itself does today"* describes polls and posts, not go-live. This build follows the shadow-home pattern because a pin and a four-hour reminder are things you want to SEE rehearsed. |
| `golive.render(name=…)` / `announcement_embed(name=…)` | Additive keyword-only overrides. `display_name(None)` is `"Someone"`, and a spotlight has no member — the card would have read *"Someone is now live on Twitch!"*. A fake object with a `display_name` attribute would have been a lie in the shape of a member, and the first thing to call `member.id` on it would have found out. |
| `spotlight_channel` / `change_spotlight` / `forget_spotlight` / `bump_now` — one door each | Checklist 34: the panel, the route and the event card all come in here, the function does the `log_action` with `kind_via(...)` and `details["via"]`, and no route `note()`s on top. `bump_now` returns an OUTCOME rather than raising, so the panel can put it in a sentence and the route can pick a status code — and it tells *no row* from *not live* from *the cog is not up*, because answering "that row is gone" about a row that is plainly there is the bare-status failure in words' clothing. |
| `events.spotlight_login` — approved AND one twitch link | Both halves matter. An un-approved event must not be spotlightable (staff approve first, then set it up — that is the owner's order of operations), and `where_link` answers only when the typed Where IS one link and nothing else, so *"twitch.tv/gdq at 8pm"* is correctly not a channel. The button is not RENDERED when it answers None, rather than rendered and refusing. |
| `events.drop_spotlight` — a function-level import | `black_bloc/events.py` is imported by the cog, so importing the cog at module level would be a cycle. `cancel_for` is the one place both doors pass through, so the hook belongs there; it catches everything and logs a warning, because failing to drop a spotlight must never stop an event being called off. |
| `golive-join.spotlight` — a `spotlight:<id>` user id | The join keys rows by member id and a spotlight has none. The synthetic prefix keeps ONE sorted list (design §C test 3: one subject, one place), keeps `blankRow`'s shape intact for every other consumer, and is what `page-golive.memberCell` reads to print *channel only* instead of handing `nameNode` an id Discord has never heard of. A channel that IS a linked member's login merges onto the member's row instead — one row, the member's, carrying the spotlight facts. |

# Posts — version history instead of "Put the original back" (branch `posts-versions`, 2026-09-20)

> Design: [`posts-versions-design.md`](posts-versions-design.md). Owner, 2026-09-20 18:1x:
> *"for all post lets remove the put back original and add a version history so you can view and
> swap to any previous saved post."* Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge
> cannot move them. ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes,
> the mock and a browser pointed at the mock.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `storage/db.SCHEMA` — `post_versions` has `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and `connect` already sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` | A post's history is the post's, and `remove_post` is the one place a post goes. Doing it in the schema rather than in `delete_post` means the mock's own DELETE and any future door cannot forget; the test that proves it counts rows after `remove_post`, not after `delete_post`, because that is the path a person takes. |
| `storage/db.BACKFILL_POST_VERSIONS` — plain SQL in `db.py`, not a call into `posts.py` | `black_bloc/posts.py` imports `actionlog`, which reaches the bot; `storage/db.py` is imported by everything and stays leaf. The insert is `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM post_versions …)`, which is what makes it idempotent — it runs on every `connect`, and a third boot writes nothing. `saved_at` is `COALESCE(updated_at, now)`, so a backfilled row is dated when the post was last touched rather than when the migration happened to run. |
| `posts.record_version(bot, guild, …)` — NOT `(db, row, …)` as the design wrote it | The keep-limit trim reads `posts_versions_keep` off the store and writes a `post.versions_trimmed` row when it drops any, and both need the bot and the guild. Keeping the trim inside the one door is the point: a version written by a path that forgot to trim would quietly exceed the limit the owner set. |
| `posts.version_fields` — the comparison is FIVE normalised values, never the row objects | `channel_id` arrives as `int` off SQLite and as a `str` off the website's JSON, and `pin` as `0`/`1` or `True`/`False`. Comparing raw rows would have written a "new" version on every save that changed nothing, which is the one thing the owner's second sentence forbids. `as_channel_id` and `wanted_style` are the same normalisers `save_post` writes through, so the stored row and the comparison cannot disagree. |
| `posts.record_version(always=True)` — only **Use this version** passes it | A restore of a version whose words happen to match the latest one would otherwise write nothing, and the history would lose the step: somebody pressed a button and the list looks untouched. Save and publish never pass it, which is what keeps "a save that changes nothing writes nothing" true. |
| `posts.version_now` — what `post.saved` / `post.posted` put in `details["version"]` | The n the row READS AS, not the n that was written: a save that changed nothing carries the version it still matches. A row saying `version: null` would be indistinguishable from one written before the feature existed. |
| `posts.publish_post` — the version is recorded AFTER the send and before the `note` | Checklist 12, and the design's §A rule read literally: the version describes what went out, so it cannot be written before Discord has taken it. Shadow publishes record too — a shadow copy is a real message really sent, which is the same reasoning `logkinds.SHADOW` uses to keep `post.shadow_posted` out of the dry-run rule. |
| `posts.restore_version` — writes `post.restored` and NOT `post.saved` | It is one move and leaves one row (checklist 34). It also does its own `set_post_fields` rather than calling `save_post`, because `save_post` would write a `saved` version and a `post.saved` row on top of the `restored:n` one. The caps are not re-checked: the five fields were refused-or-accepted when they were saved, and the style travels with them, so the pair cannot fall out of step. |
| `posts.trim_versions` — `found[max(1, keep):]` | Two guards in one slice: `keep` of 0 never reaches here, and `max(1, …)` is what keeps the last row standing if a later change ever lets 0 through. The `n` sequence is deliberately NOT renumbered after a trim — `v7` stays `v7` for ever, so a log row naming a version still points at the same words. |
| `posts.is_shipped_version` — the `shipped` chip is EARNED, not assumed | The conductor's call (2026-09-20) moved *ships with the bot* off the list row and into the Versions list. A backfill row of a seeded post is only *shipped* while its title and body still match `posts_seed.json`; a post staff rewrote before this landed gets *what it said before*, which is the truth. Without the comparison the chip would say `shipped` about words Black Bloc never shipped. |
| `posts.when_words` — plain words, not Discord's `<t:…:R>` | A `SelectOption` label is text: Discord renders a timestamp in message content and in an embed body, and prints the raw `<t:…>` in a dropdown. One helper feeds both the sub-panel's lines and its options so the two cannot disagree; the page uses `ui.ago` for the same reason on its side. |
| `api/tools/posts.py` — `preview` is three fields, not a rendered string | `posts.render_message` answers a `discord.Embed`, which is not JSON. The site already owns a Discord-markdown renderer (`discordmd.js`) and the editor's own preview draws through it, so the route hands over exactly what that renderer takes — `style`, `title`, `body` — and **View** draws a version the same way the editor draws the draft. |
| `assets/postversions.js` — ONE module, imported by the page and by its preview | The surfaces rule: two copies of one list eventually disagree about what a chip says. The preview passes `wouldDo` handlers where the page passes real ones, and that is the only difference between them. |
| `assets/postversions.toneFor` — `null` for an ordinary save | `site.css` defines `.badge[data-tone]` for `ok`, `warn`, `danger` and `info` only (ux-audit finding 7), so a `quiet` chip renders identically to no tone at all while looking deliberate in the source. |
| `page-posts.js` — **Post it** saves a dirty editor through the SAME `saveDraft` the bar uses | Rule 3 of the owner's ask. One body builder means the save half of Post it cannot drift from Save changes, and `run()` puts either refusal in the same sentence beside the box. `changeCount(draft, was)` is the dirtiness test the save bar already had — no second idea of "changed". |
| `page-posts.js` — `WILL_POST_SAVED` / `WILL_UPDATE_SAVED` are whole sentences, not a prefix | *"Saves your changes, then "* in front of the existing line reads *"…then Post it sends this to…"*. Two more constants cost nothing, and the shadow lines are deliberately left alone because a shadow copy's sentence already says where it goes. |
| `page-posts.js` — the versions list is fetched in `loadPost`, and a failure is a NOTICE | The foldout is a second read; letting it throw would empty a page whose editor is perfectly usable. `history === null` draws one warn notice saying the history could not be read and that everything else still works — never a bare status, and never a silently missing section. |
| `cogs/community/posts.VersionsButton` is on row 1, beside `Back` | Discord caps a row at five components and the card's row 0 already holds Post it, Take it down, Edit…, Pin it and Delete this post. Row 1 was `Back` alone. |
| `cogs/community/posts.build_versions` — the select re-renders, the buttons act | *"Moves are buttons that render only when valid"*: nothing picked, so no View and no Use this version; the current version picked, so View but no Use this version. The picked n lives in the rendered view rather than on the cog, so two staffers on two panels never share a selection. |
| `logkinds` — `post.reset` is GONE from `ROUTINE`, not kept for history | The brief asked for it to be kept in case the live Logs page holds old rows. It cannot be: `tests/test_logkinds.py::test_no_classification_entry_is_dead` fails by name on a table entry nothing emits. ⚠️ **Measured, and this is why it costs nothing:** `is_important("post.reset")` is `False` either way — it is not in `IMPORTANT` and ends in none of `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` — and `feature_of` still answers `posts` off the `post` head, so an old row renders in the same place, in the same class, with the same words. |
# The go-live boot sweep — nobody is missed because the bot was restarting (branch `boot-sweep`, 2026-09-20)

> Design: `info/golive-boot-sweep-design.md`. Owner, 2026-09-20 17:5x: *"also for go live detection,
> have the bot check all the channels with status and taht are linked on start up and make sure the
> most recent post regarding them in the golive channel is accurate so we dont miss people during
> reboots"*. Keys are CONSTRUCT NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge cannot move them.
> ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `GoLive.cog_load` — `stamp=bool(self._guilds())` | 🔴 The finding this build turned up. `bot.py:setup_hook` loads every cog BEFORE IDENTIFY, so `self.bot.guilds` is empty at `cog_load` and the v141 boot reconcile iterated nothing — on the real bot it has been a no-op, and a session left open by a restart waited for `age_out_sessions` twelve hours later. The `on_ready` listener is the pass that has guilds; stamping the window from a pass over NO guilds would make `skip_if_recent=True` throw away the only one that matters. A pass over nothing never happened, so it does not close the window. |
| `GoLive._guilds` | One home for *which guilds a boot pass covers* — non-`unavailable` (checklist 32), in cache order. Both the stamp decision and `boot_pass` read it, so they can never disagree about whether there was anything to do. |
| `GoLive.boot_pass` — per guild, reconcile then sweep then the row | The design says the sweep runs "right after `reconcile_open_sessions()`"; the counts are per guild, so the unit is a guild, not a phase. `reconcile_open_sessions()` survives unchanged as the public name the older tests call — it is `boot_pass` minus the sweep and the row. |
| `GoLive.sweep_presences` — the SAME `_go_live` door | Discord replays no presence at boot: a member already streaming when the bot comes back raises no `on_presence_update`, and the reconcile reads activities only for sessions that already exist. The sweep walks `guild.members`, and everything it finds goes through `self._go_live(member, info, "presence")` — the identical door — so mode, opt-out, role filters, cooldown, co-stream joining and shadow all apply without a second copy of any of them. |
| `GoLive._go_live_once` — it returns a REASON now | `presence_skipped` has to say *why*, and the alternative was for the sweep to re-check the mode, the opt-out, the role filters and the cooldown before calling — four copies of decisions with one home (checklist 15), four chances to drift. Every caller that ignores the return value is byte-for-byte unchanged. ⚠️ A **shadow** announcement returns `announced`: the row's `mode` says which it was, and the count answers *"did the sweep act on this person?"*. |
| `golive.boot_swept` — written even when the key is off | §B's second gap is *"nothing records that the boot pass ran"*, and a row that disappears when the sweep is off answers nothing. `swept` carries the key's value, so an empty row and a switched-off one are told apart at a glance. `members_cached` is `guild.chunked` — a walk of a cache that was never filled must not read as a guild with nobody streaming. |
| `golive_boot_sweep` — in *How streams are spotted* | The drawer that already holds the YouTube probe cadence and the spotlight poll is where "how does Black Bloc find out somebody is live" lives. `announcementSection` renders a hand-picked set from the `golive` namespace, so a key placed there would pass the every-key-lands-once test while appearing nowhere; the drawer renders through `settingsPanel`, which is the surface that actually shows it. |
| `FakeGuild.members` in both content test files | Was a dict keyed by member id; `discord.Guild.members` is a LIST. The sweep would have walked integers, found no activities, and passed for the wrong reason. The members live in `by_id` now and `members` is a property over its values. |
| `Spotlight.cog_load` / `Spotlight._guilds` — the same fix, one cog over | The spotlight boot reconcile had the identical shape and the identical consequence: `cog_load` stamped the `Reconciler`'s window from a pass over zero guilds, so `on_ready`'s `skip_if_recent=True` threw away the only pass that could see anything, and an open spotlight session whose announcement had gone was never closed at boot. `stamp=bool(self._guilds())`, and the same non-`unavailable` guild source (checklist 32). ⚠️ `poll_once` and `_poll_minutes` still read `self.bot.guilds` directly — they run after ready, so the emptiness never bites them, and widening the change was out of scope. Falsified before it was kept: the guard fails on the un-fixed cog. |

# A ping role for a spotlight channel — GamesDoneQuick pings (branch `spotlight-pings`, 2026-09-20)

> Design: `info/spotlight-pings-design.md`. Owner, 2026-09-20 19:3x: *"i dont see how to add a role
> to the games done quick entry in streamers"* → *"yes design and build it"*. Keys are CONSTRUCT
> NAMES, never `path:N`, so a later merge cannot move them.
> ⚠️ **Nothing here has met Discord** — every claim is the suite's, against fakes, plus one headless
> pass over the mock's Go-live page.

| Construct | Why it is the way it is |
|---|---|
| `Database._set_aside_fan_roles_that_require_a_member` / `_restore_set_aside_fan_roles` | SQLite cannot drop NOT NULL with `ALTER TABLE`, and `golive_fan_roles.user_id` was NOT NULL *inside* `PRIMARY KEY (guild_id, user_id)`. The table is renamed before the bootstrap and copied back after, column by column over the INTERSECTION of the two shapes — a file that predates `unworn_since` migrates without naming it. The same two-step `mod_cases` uses. ⚠️ It runs once: the guard is `user_id`'s own `notnull` flag, so the second boot is a no-op. |
| `golive_fan_roles_one_member` / `golive_fan_roles_one_spotlight` | Two partial unique indexes instead of a primary key. SQLite would have allowed NULLs in `PRIMARY KEY (guild_id, user_id)` — a legacy quirk that a `STRICT` table or a later rebuild breaks silently — so uniqueness is stated per kind instead, where a reader can see it. |
| `pings.FAN_ROLE_SELECT` | One SELECT with a LEFT JOIN on `spotlight_channels`, so every read of the table hands back `spotlight_login` / `spotlight_name` and nothing has to look a channel up twice. The cost is that `all_fan_roles` now returns rows with a NULL `user_id`, which is why `member_fan_roles` exists. |
| `pings.member_fan_roles` — and who reads it | `prune_empty_roles`, `follower_counts` and `pings_onboarding.streamer_options` are members-only ON PURPOSE. A channel's role is not pruned after 30 unworn days, because it goes when the channel goes; and Discord's *Which streamers?* prompt is built from the streamer LIST, which a channel is not on. Reading `all_fan_roles` in any of the three is a crash on `int(None)` — that is how this was found. |
| `pings.spotlight_ref` / `spotlight_from_ref` | `spotlight:<id>` is the one spelling of "this select option is a channel", shared by `FollowPick`, `StreamerPick`, the card, `run_follow` and the page's synthetic row id. A Discord select value is a string and a member id is a number, so the prefix is what keeps them apart without a second select. |
| `pings.ensure_fan_role(spotlight=)` — `member` may be None | §A's "one path" taken literally: the same template, the same existing-role reuse, the same `staff` gate, the same log kind. The branch is three lines (which name, which row, which sentence) rather than a second function that would drift. |
| `pings.remove_fan_role(spotlight=, because=)` | `because` exists so `pings.fan_role_removed` says whether a role went because the spotlight expired, because staff removed the channel, or because staff took the role — three different stories that were one row before. |
| `Spotlight._mentions(guild_id, fan_role_id, pinging=)` | `pinging=False` is what makes a reminder's `allowed_mentions` `roles=False`. Without it a role id typed into `spotlight_bump_template` by hand would ping while the key says reminders are silent — the template is staff-editable, so this is not hypothetical. |
| `spotlight.drop_fan_role` / `give_fan_role` / `take_fan_role` | The three shared moves the `/golive` sub-panel, the `/pings` card and (for the first) the expiry sweep all come in by. They live in the cog module beside `forget_spotlight` because that is where a spotlight row is read; `black_bloc/pings.py` never imports the cog, so there is no cycle. |
| `_announce` — `update_channel(display_name=name)` | A row added by hand knows only the login, so its role would have been called *gamesdonequick pings*. Twitch's own `user_name` arrives with the first stream and is saved then, which is why the role, the drawer and the cell all read **GamesDoneQuick** after one announcement. |
| `api/tools/pings.streamer_row` — `kind` | A channel's row has `member_id: null`, and a page that reads `member_id` to key a row would silently collapse every channel into one. `kind` is the field to branch on; `member_id` being null is the consequence, not the signal. |
| `spotlight_listing_row` — `last_live_at: null` | `GET /api/pings/list` says a channel exists and what its role is; the streaming history lives on the Go-live page's spotlight payload, which already carries the sessions. One fact, one home — and `golive-join.js` skips a row with no member id, so the page never sees these. |
| `page-golive.js:spotlightOnly` | Was `String(row.user_id).startsWith('spotlight:')` written out three times, and the third was about to be a fourth. It also checks `row.spotlight` is really there, so a malformed payload draws the member shape rather than reading `row.spotlight.id` of null. |
| `golive-join.js:wearRole` | A row that is BOTH a member's login and a spotlight keeps the MEMBER's ping role in its cell (`if (!mine.role_id)`), so the one cell can never disagree with itself. Both roles still exist; each is mentioned by its own announcement. |
| `FollowPick(..., channels=)` — the cap is over the COMBINED list | Discord shows 25 options, and people and channels share them. A server with 25 followable people therefore shows no channels, and the placeholder says *25 of N*. Named because the fix (a second select) is a design call, not an oversight. |
| the mock's `SPOTLIGHT_FAN_ROLE_ID` and Frost Fatales' role | GamesDoneQuick's is a real `ROLES` entry worn by three roster members, which is what the page draws; Frost Fatales' points at a role id deliberately absent from `ROLES` — the deleted-by-hand half — and exists because `check.mjs` pins `{spotlight_id}` to row 3 and the DELETE entry has to find a role there. ESA Marathon has none, which is the **Add a ping role…** door. |
